sections.heading: The data booklet: what is given and what must be learned
paragraphs: Students are issued a data booklet in the examination, and a surprising number of them do not know what is in it. That has two costs. They waste revision hours memorising values that will be supplied, and they arrive in the hall unable to find the table they need quickly enough. Both are solvable in a single session and almost nobody does it.

What the booklet supplies, broadly, is reference data: the periodic table, physical constants, enthalpy and bond data, electrode potentials, acid and base constants, and the spectroscopic reference values used for infrared, mass spectrometry and proton nuclear magnetic resonance. What it does not supply is anything requiring judgement — definitions, mechanism conditions, reagents, qualitative test results, naming conventions and the reasoning that connects any of it.

The practical exercise is to sit the student down with the booklet their school issues and have them find, under time pressure, the five tables they will most often need. The spectroscopy section in particular rewards familiarity: structure-deduction questions combining infrared, mass spectra and proton nuclear magnetic resonance are among the most learnable mark sources in the course precisely because the reference values are given and the examined skill is interpretation.

A note on materials generally. We reference and link official sources at ibo.org and do not host, reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, data booklets, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; they are the board's copyright and some are unreleased. Your school issues the booklet and holds licensed access to papers, and a session works from those copies rather than from anything we supply.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: pathways, conditions and arrows
paragraphs: Organic chemistry decides more Higher Level chemistry grades than any other part of the course, and it is the part students most often learn at half depth. The usual pattern is a student who knows that an alcohol can be converted to a carboxylic acid and cannot say with what, under what conditions, or by what mechanism. The pathway alone is worth a fraction of the available marks.

Three things carry the marks. First, reagents and conditions, named specifically: the scheme does not accept a vague oxidising agent where a named reagent and a condition were required. Second, mechanism arrows, which must start at the electron source — a lone pair or a bond — and end where those electrons go. A correct product with arrows from the wrong origin scores partially at best. Third, at Higher Level, the distinction between substitution routes and the structural factors that decide which one operates.

The way to learn it is as a map rather than a list. Build a single diagram of functional groups with the arrows between them labelled with reagent and condition, have the student redraw it from memory each session, and test it by giving them a start and an end and asking for the route. On a shared screen that diagram can be built up over several sessions and kept, which works better than a page in a notebook that gets rewritten and lost.

Stereochemistry at Higher Level is the other recurring gap, and it is usually a visualisation problem rather than a knowledge problem. Students can state what an enantiomer is and cannot identify one in a drawn structure under time pressure. Drawing practice, not definition practice, is the fix, and it is another case where a screen beats paper because the same structure can be rotated and redrawn without starting again.

sections.heading: Past papers on a syllabus with a short history
paragraphs: The current Structure and Reactivity syllabus has only a few sittings behind it, which changes past-paper strategy in a way most revision advice has not caught up with. There is not an unlimited stock of papers on this specification, so they cannot be used the way a student uses IGCSE papers — front to back, generously self-marked, as a way of filling time.

The correct approach is to treat the available current-syllabus papers as scarce and expensive, and to spend them deliberately. Sit one section under real timed conditions. Mark it against the official scheme line by line. Sort every lost mark into content not known, precision lost, calculation slip, or ran out of time. Only then decide what the next fortnight is for. A paper burned without being marked properly has taught the student how it feels to sit a paper, which they already knew.

Specimen material and older papers still have uses, with a caveat. Questions on content that survived the restructuring are perfectly good practice, and the mark schemes from earlier series still show how examiners reward precision, which is the transferable lesson. Questions on content that moved or was removed are a waste of a student's evening and occasionally teach something now wrong. A tutor who knows the specification can separate the two quickly; a student cannot.

The materials themselves come from the school's licensed access or the board's own platform. We reference ibo.org and do not host, reproduce or distribute papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides, because they are copyright and some are unreleased. Where a student needs a paper, the right route is the school's chemistry department, who have it legitimately and usually have a view on which ones are worth sitting.

sections.heading: The chemistry investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: A fifth of the chemistry grade is an individual investigation marked on four criteria over 24 marks, with a 3,000-word limit on the write-up. In chemistry the recurring failure is not poor data collection. It is a research question that the chosen method cannot answer, a design fault that no quality of execution repairs and that is visible to the tutor in five minutes and invisible to the student for six weeks.

The classic version is a question about a rate or an equilibrium position with a method that measures something only loosely related to either, often because the equipment available suggested the method and the question was fitted to it afterwards. The order matters: question first, then method, then a check that the method produces data capable of answering the question. Reversing that order is the single most common way a chemistry investigation lands in the middle band.

The other reliable losses sit in evaluation. Chemistry investigations invite specific limitations — heat loss, incomplete reaction, impure reagent, a concentration assumed rather than standardised — and a student who writes about human error in general has written a sentence that scores nothing. Naming the limitation, its direction and its effect on the numerical result is what the criterion asks for.

The honesty line is firm. A tutor may discuss whether a question is answerable by a method, explain what each criterion asks for, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not design the experiment, produce or clean the data, write any part of the text, or edit it to completion. The declaration on the submitted work is the student's. One page ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments outright, which puts the student at risk rather than the seller.

sections.heading: What chemistry tuition costs, specialist band first
paragraphs: Begin at the top of the market, because chemistry is one of the subjects where the specialist band is genuinely doing different work. An IB specialist in Dubai runs AED 200 to 450 or more an hour, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table giving 200 to 450 plus. The premium end reaches AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650. All figures read in October 2026 and all belonging to whoever published them.

Below that, a qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online tutoring runs AED 45 to 150, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 500 including travel, with Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500.

What the specialist band buys in chemistry specifically is the ability to name the trap. Marking a mechanism for arrow origin, spotting that an investigation's research question cannot be answered by its method, knowing that a Higher Level question has quietly required extension content inside a core-looking stem — that is experience of the mark scheme rather than knowledge of chemistry. Plenty of people with chemistry degrees cannot do it, and the rate bands in this market broadly reflect that rather than reflecting prestige.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages published in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Ask any provider three things before booking: the session length behind the rate, whether VAT is included, and what happens if you stop after one lesson.

sections.heading: A subject made of drawings, taught on a shared screen
paragraphs: Chemistry is unusually well suited to video delivery, and the reason is not cost. It is that most of what a chemistry session produces is drawings: mechanisms, lattice structures, energy profiles, titration curves, orbital diagrams, structural formulae. A shared screen keeps the student's own attempt, the examiner's expected version and the correction visible together, and nothing has to be redrawn or turned around.

Marking works better too. The official scheme's wording sits beside the student's answer on one screen, both people reading the same line at the same time. That is how precision gets taught: not by being told that state symbols matter, but by watching a correct answer score two out of four in real time because they were missing. On paper, with one copy of the scheme between two people, that moment is diluted.

What video genuinely loses is presence. A tutor in the room notices drift faster and a parent can see the session happening, which matters more for a fifteen-year-old than for a seventeen-year-old. The market charges roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour extra for that, which across a two-year Diploma in one subject runs into several thousand dirhams. It is a real trade and worth making consciously.

sections.heading: Laboratory time, the mandatory subjects and a compressed week
paragraphs: Chemistry needs laboratory time, and laboratory time competes with everything else in a Dubai Diploma timetable. That competition is sharper here than most international comparisons allow for, because KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and those lessons sit inside the same week as six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge and CAS.

KHDA's published arrangements are specific. Instructional time for the mandatory subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction.

For a chemistry student that arithmetic has a practical consequence. A student who misses laboratory sessions — through illness, travel, or a timetable clash with a mandatory lesson — loses something an outside tutor cannot replace, because the school runs the practical programme and nobody else does. The right response is to protect laboratory attendance ahead of almost everything else and to put the investigation's data collection early, before the term gets crowded.

Where tutoring does fit is around the laboratory rather than inside it: preparing the thinking before a practical so the time at the bench is productive, and working on the write-up afterwards against the criteria. That division is worth being explicit about with any provider. Anyone offering to supply practical results or produce data for an investigation is offering something that is not tutoring and that puts the student's declaration at risk.

sections.heading: The chemistry grade and what it is for
paragraphs: Chemistry is the Diploma subject where a single grade most often changes an outcome, because medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, chemical engineering and most life-science degrees specify it, frequently at Higher Level with a minimum grade attached. That is why families in Nad Al Sheba treat a disappointing chemistry report with more urgency than a disappointing report in a subject with no prerequisite riding on it, and the urgency is rational.

The right way to use that is precision rather than panic. Read the published prerequisite for the specific programme at the specific institution, because requirements differ between universities and are revised. A student who needs a 6 and is predicted a 5 has a defined gap and roughly a known number of marks to find; a student who needs a 7 for a single competitive programme has a different conversation, including about whether to apply more broadly.

There is a separate UAE step that is often confused with admissions. Ministry of Education equivalency converts a school-leaving qualification into something UAE authorities recognise and governs applications to universities inside the country. The British-track rules are published: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 with Arabic and Islamic education excluded, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the American track, English requires IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 reading-writing, and mathematics requires SAT Math of at least 450.

No IB equivalency figure appears on this page, deliberately. The source that sets out those British and American requirements states no IB points threshold, so publishing one would be invention, and one ranking competitor already publishes the wrong subject count for the British track. Check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of equivalency, and tutoring is not a requirement for it — any suggestion otherwise is false urgency about a regulatory process.

faqs.question: Are the chemistry lessons given in Nad Al Sheba or online?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. Chemistry suits the format unusually well because most of a session produces drawings — mechanisms, energy profiles, titration curves, structural formulae — and a shared screen keeps the student's attempt, the examiner's expected version and the correction visible together, rather than redrawn in one notebook and passed back and forth across a table.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when their chemistry answers look right?
faqs.answer: Because chemistry schemes mark very specific wording, and the usual losses are precision rather than ignorance. An enthalpy value correct in magnitude and wrong in sign. An ionic equation without state symbols. A periodicity trend described instead of explained with nuclear charge and shielding. A mechanism whose product is right and whose arrows start in the wrong place. A half-equation balanced for atoms and not charge. Each costs one or two marks, every paper, and all of them are drillable habits rather than concepts.

faqs.question: What is actually in the chemistry data booklet?
faqs.answer: Reference data: the periodic table and relative atomic masses, physical constants, enthalpy and bond data, standard electrode potentials, acid and base constants, and the spectroscopic reference values for infrared, mass spectrometry and proton nuclear magnetic resonance. What it does not contain is anything requiring judgement — definitions, organic reagents and conditions, qualitative test results, naming conventions or reasoning. So organic chemistry is where memorisation effort belongs, and spending revision hours on values the booklet supplies is wasted time.

faqs.question: How is the IB chemistry grade divided between components?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 carries 44% in structured extended response. The scientific investigation carries 20% at both Standard and Higher Level. Standard Level courses run 150 teaching hours and Higher Level 240. Because a fifth of the grade is written coursework completed before the exams, it is the most controllable part of the course and the part most often treated as administration.

faqs.question: What goes wrong most often in a chemistry internal assessment?
faqs.answer: A research question the chosen method cannot answer. It usually happens because the available equipment suggested a method and the question was fitted to it afterwards, which is the reverse of the right order. That design fault is visible to an experienced marker in five minutes, invisible to the student for six weeks, and not repairable by careful data collection. The other reliable loss is evaluation written as generic human error rather than a named limitation with its direction and numerical effect.

faqs.question: How should my child learn organic chemistry pathways?
faqs.answer: As one labelled map rather than a list of reactions. Build a single diagram of functional groups with every arrow labelled with its reagent and its conditions, have the student redraw it from memory each session, then test by giving a starting compound and a target and asking for the route. Conditions and reagents carry marks alongside the product, and most students learn the pathway and not the conditions, which is why they score partially on questions they feel they knew.

faqs.question: Does the Higher Level extension content need separate revision?
faqs.answer: No, and treating it that way builds in a failure. The current syllabus examines Higher Level extension material inside the Structure and Reactivity themes alongside the core, so a single Paper 2 question can require both and often does. A Higher Level student cannot secure the core and add the extension later. Any revision plan or tutor that keeps them separate is working from the older options-based structure, which is a reasonable thing to check before hiring anybody.

faqs.question: There are not many past papers on this syllabus. How should we use them?
faqs.answer: Treat them as scarce. Sit one section under real timed conditions, mark it against the official scheme line by line, and sort every lost mark into content not known, precision lost, calculation slip or ran out of time before deciding what the next fortnight is for. Older papers are still useful where the content survived the restructuring, and their mark schemes still show how examiners reward precision, but questions on moved or removed content waste an evening.

faqs.question: Can online tutoring help with laboratory work?
faqs.answer: Not with the practical itself. The school runs the laboratory programme, the equipment and the supervised data collection, and no outside tutor replaces that. What a tutor can do is the thinking around it: deciding what the practical needs to produce before the student is at the bench, and working the write-up against the four criteria afterwards. Anyone offering to supply results or produce data is offering something that is not tutoring and that puts the student's declaration at risk.

faqs.question: What does paying for a specialist rather than a general tutor actually buy?
faqs.answer: In chemistry, the ability to name the trap. Marking a mechanism for arrow origin, spotting that an investigation's method cannot answer its question, recognising that a core-looking Paper 2 stem has quietly required Higher Level extension content — that is mark-scheme experience rather than chemistry knowledge, and plenty of chemistry graduates do not have it. Market bands run AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB specialist against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, read October 2026.

faqs.question: My child is strong at chemistry but slow. What can be done in eight weeks?
faqs.answer: Timing is one of the recoverable losses, so quite a lot. The drill is timed sections rather than whole papers, with a rule about when to leave a question and come back, and explicit practice at the end of Paper 2 where the heaviest questions sit and most students arrive with no minutes left. If the marked script shows the student writing paragraphs for two-mark questions, that habit alone is often worth a grade boundary and takes about three sessions to break.

faqs.question: How does the mandatory-subject timetable affect chemistry in Dubai?
faqs.answer: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and schools advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Those minutes sit inside a week already holding six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, which squeezes laboratory time. The practical response is to protect laboratory attendance and put investigation data collection early in the term.

faqs.question: Which spectroscopy questions are worth revising for?
faqs.answer: Structure-deduction questions that combine infrared, mass spectrometry and proton nuclear magnetic resonance. They are among the most learnable marks in the whole course, because the data booklet supplies the reference values and the examined skill is interpretation and combination rather than recall. Students avoid them because three techniques look like three topics. In practice it is one procedure applied in a fixed order, and two or three sessions of practice makes it reliable.

faqs.question: Does my child need chemistry at Higher Level for medicine?
faqs.answer: Most medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering programmes specify chemistry and many specify it at Higher Level with a minimum grade, but requirements differ between institutions and are revised, so read the published prerequisite for the specific programme rather than relying on a general rule. For universities inside the UAE there is a separate Ministry of Education equivalency step, and no verified IB points threshold exists to quote, so check moe.gov.ae directly rather than any tutoring site.

faqs.question: Will a tutor read my child's investigation draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, and give written feedback on it against the four criteria — whether the research question is answerable by the method, whether uncertainties are carried through, whether the conclusion compares numerically with an accepted value, and whether the evaluation names limitations with direction and effect. What a tutor will not do is design the experiment, produce or clean data, write any part of the text, or edit it to completion. That boundary is stated to the student at the start, because the declaration is theirs.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Higher Level chemistry tutor be arranged?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days for a Higher or Standard Level chemistry match, since it is among the better-subscribed Diploma sciences. Narrower requests take longer: a tutor with investigation-marking experience in a specific area, or one covering chemistry and Higher Level maths together. Where the match is not available in a given term you get a date or a straight no rather than a generalist with the right label, because a generalist is discovered in session three and the term is gone by then.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.closingHeading: Send a marked script, not a report card
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.closingBody: Chemistry marks disappear in nameable places, so the fastest way to use an IB chemistry tutor in Nad Al Sheba is to show where yours are going. Send the level, the theme the school is on and the most recent marked piece of written work. The first lesson is a free diagnostic spent marking the student's own answers strictly against the official scheme, which separates content gaps from precision losses — and in chemistry the second is far more common. You get a written note naming which, and the AED bands above are on the page with their sources so the comparison is yours to make.

intro.heading: What you are actually paying for when you hire a Chemistry tutor
paragraphs: Start with the arithmetic, because it is the part nobody publishes. A Higher Level Chemistry student in Year 12 who takes one weekly hour from October to the May session of Year 13 will sit through roughly sixty hours of tuition. At the budget end of the Dubai market, around AED 45 to 65 an hour as advertised by EdFlik, that is a commitment near AED 3,000. At a specialist rate of AED 270, the figure TutorChase publishes, the same sixty hours cost about AED 16,200. At the premium end BartyED quotes, AED 650, it passes AED 39,000. Those are four very different family decisions wearing the same words: a Chemistry tutor.

The honest answer is that the hourly number tells you almost nothing on its own. What matters is how many of those hours are spent on Chemistry a student cannot already do. A cheap tutor who re-teaches bonding because bonding is the topic they remember best is expensive at AED 45. A tutor who opens with a diagnostic on energetics and equilibria, finds that the student loses marks on enthalpy cycles rather than on definitions, and spends six weeks there is cheap at AED 270. The waste in this market is not overpriced hours. It is correctly priced hours aimed at the wrong topic.

Oud Metha sharpens this because of geography. The neighbourhood sits between Dubai Healthcare City, Al Jaddaf and the Bur Dubai school corridor, with the Red Line running through it and Al Garhoud Bridge carrying most of the Festival City traffic. A tutor who drives to an Oud Metha apartment at 5pm on a Tuesday is billing for an hour and spending close to two. Somebody pays for that difference, and in every in-home rate card published in Dubai it is the parent. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoting up to AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for the same qualified tutor working online.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a family in Oud Metha this is the cheaper arrangement and the better one on the academic merits. The pool is no longer every Chemistry graduate living within a twenty-minute drive of Al Nasr Leisureland. It is every Chemistry specialist who can teach at 5pm Gulf Standard Time, which is a different and much larger set, and it includes people who have taught the organic mechanism sequence thirty times rather than twice.

What follows is a cost page, not a brochure. It lists the AED bands with the source that published them, counts the two-year Diploma spend backwards from the May session, separates the parts of the Chemistry grade that respond to tuition from the parts that do not, and states plainly what a tutor may and may not do with an internal assessment. Every figure carries an attribution. None of them is an IB Gram price list, because IB Gram starts with a free trial lesson and a conversation about the student's actual mark profile rather than a rate card.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-oud-metha.programmesIntro: Chemistry does not begin in DP1. An Oud Metha student arriving at Higher Level has usually come through MYP Sciences or an IGCSE Chemistry course, and the cost of DP Chemistry tuition is largely set by how well that earlier stage was taught. These are the stages, and what each one costs a family to repair later.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no Chemistry. It has inquiry units that touch materials, change and matter, and it builds the habit of recording what happened rather than what was expected. Families rarely buy PYP science tuition and rarely need to. Where money is well spent at this stage it is on written English and on arithmetic fluency, both of which show up later as marks lost in Chemistry calculation questions.
programmes.countryNote: Swiss International Scientific School in Al Jaddaf, a short drive from Oud Metha over Oud Metha Road, runs the PYP, and several Bur Dubai families use it as the primary feeder before an IB continuum. KHDA inspects it annually on the six-band Outstanding to Very Weak scale, and the published report is the one document worth reading before paying for anything.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion C is where DP Chemistry trouble starts, because processing data and evaluating method is precisely what the DP internal assessment is marked on. A student who reaches MYP5 without a graph they built themselves will pay for it twice.
programmes.countryNote: MYP tuition in the Bur Dubai belt is usually bought in panic in MYP5, when the DP subject choice sheet arrives. Bought in MYP3 instead, at around AED 150 to 250 an hour for a qualified online tutor, it costs less in total and removes the need for the DP1 catch-up block entirely. That is the single largest saving available on this page.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: DP Chemistry is where the money goes. Under the syllabus first examined in 2025 the course is organised around structure and reactivity, with Paper 1 split into multiple choice and a data-based section, Paper 2 carrying extended response, and a scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. Higher Level adds depth rather than new headings, which is why HL students often cannot name what they do not know.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is a Diploma market in a British-curriculum city. KHDA's 2024-25 figures put 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula, with UK 37%, Indian 26%, US 14% and International Baccalaureate 7%. Confirm your child's exact paper structure and weightings with the school's IB coordinator and the current subject guide, since the figures above describe the 2025 first-examination course.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs DP courses with a career-related study and is offered by a small number of UAE schools. A CP student taking DP Chemistry sits exactly the same papers and the same investigation as a full Diploma candidate, so the tutoring need is identical and so is the cost. What differs is the surrounding load, which is lighter, and that usually means fewer hours are needed overall.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in Dubai is thin and families in Oud Metha generally choose between the full Diploma and a British A Level route instead. If the CP is on the table, ask the school which DP subjects it actually timetables before budgeting for Chemistry tuition, because a course listed in a brochure is not always a course running in September.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-oud-metha.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is rarely bought alone. Most Oud Metha students who need a Chemistry tutor need one because the HL block they chose is quantitatively heavy, and the cost of the whole block is the number that matters. These are the subjects we teach alongside it, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The reactivity sequence is where marks go: enthalpy cycles, entropy and spontaneity, equilibrium shifts under changed conditions, and the organic mechanism chains. Definitions are cheap marks and most students already have them. Tuition that stays on definitions is the most common waste in this subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Taken with Chemistry by nearly every medicine applicant in the Bur Dubai belt. The marks lost are in experimental design and statistical reasoning rather than recall, which means one tutor can often cover the method half of both subjects and halve the hourly spend.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Shares the uncertainty and significant-figure conventions with Chemistry, so the data-handling work transfers. Where it diverges is algebraic fluency: a Physics HL student who cannot rearrange confidently loses marks in every topic, which no amount of content revision fixes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The course most Chemistry HL students are also taking. Logarithms, exponentials and rates of change appear in both, and a student weak on logs will struggle with pH and with rate equations simultaneously. Fixing it once is cheaper than fixing it in two subjects separately.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics-heavy route, and the better fit for a Chemistry student heading into health sciences rather than engineering. Check the admissions pages of the universities on your child's list before switching, because some engineering faculties still ask for Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Counts in either the sciences or the individuals and societies group, which makes it the standard load-reducer for a student carrying Chemistry HL. The assessment rewards systems reasoning and the handling of real data, so the skills overlap with Chemistry more than the title suggests.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: A genuine science option for a student who wants the physiology without the Chemistry calculation load. Students who take it alongside Chemistry SL often find the biochemistry sections mutually reinforcing, which is a saving rather than a duplication.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The written component that quietly sets the ceiling on every science extended response. A Chemistry student who cannot structure a paragraph under time pressure loses Paper 2 marks that look like content gaps and are not.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by exhibition and essay. The exhibition is the component Chemistry students handle well, because an experiment is a ready-made object for a knowledge question. Support here is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafting.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A Chemistry EE is the highest-risk choice in the Diploma because a weak research question produces a weak essay however good the laboratory work. The tutor's job is to interrogate the question in week one and then review the student's own drafts, never to produce text.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-oud-metha.igcseSubjectsIntro: Several Oud Metha families arrive at DP Chemistry from an IGCSE Chemistry course at a Bur Dubai British-curriculum school. The transition gap is real and it costs money to close late, so these are the IGCSE science courses we also cover.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
igcseSubjects.description: Extended tier is the only sensible route into DP Chemistry. The mole concept, electrolysis and organic families are the three topics that decide whether DP1 begins smoothly or begins with a four-week repair block.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Pearson 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Pearson's International GCSE Chemistry sits in one tier with two papers. The practical content is examined within the written papers rather than separately, which changes how a student should revise method and apparatus.

igcseSubjects.name: Combined Science (Cambridge 0653)
igcseSubjects.description: Covers all three sciences at reduced depth. A student who took Combined Science and then chose Chemistry HL has a real content gap, and pretending otherwise is how DP1 goes wrong in October.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
igcseSubjects.description: Paired with Chemistry by most pre-medicine students. The marks lost are in genetics calculation and in extended-response structure, both of which transfer directly to DP Biology.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and waves dominate the lost marks. The unit-conversion discipline built here is the same discipline Chemistry calculation questions demand, so the two courses reward joint attention.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Higher tier is the prerequisite most Bur Dubai schools apply before allowing DP sciences. Standard form, ratio and algebraic rearrangement are the Chemistry-critical strands.

sections.heading: Four ways Oud Metha families waste money on Chemistry tuition
paragraphs: The first is paying for content a student already holds. Chemistry students are good at the parts of the course that can be read, and the parts that can be read are what an unprepared tutor teaches. A session that re-covers bonding and intermolecular forces because those are the first chapters feels productive and moves nothing. Ask for the diagnostic before you ask for the rate.

The second is buying hours instead of buying a target. A standing weekly slot with no stated end point runs for two years and costs between AED 9,000 and AED 36,000 depending on tier, and nobody involved has to decide whether it worked. A block with a named objective, such as recovering the data-based section of Paper 1 before the February mock, can be judged. If a block fails, you stop. If a standing slot fails, you keep paying.

The third is the travel premium bought by accident. Families in Karama and Al Mankhool often pay in-home rates because an in-home tutor was the first one who answered, not because the format was chosen. The published gap between an online qualified tutor and an in-home one, AED 150 to 300 against AED 180 to 500, is money that buys no additional teaching. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE at all, which removes the decision.

The fourth is leaving the investigation until February of DP2. The scientific investigation is a fifth of the Chemistry grade and the only component where a student controls the conditions entirely. Supported early, it is the cheapest grade movement in the subject. Supported late, it becomes a rescue job at exam-season rates while Paper 2 revision is also due.

sections.heading: What the Chemistry grade is made of, component by component
paragraphs: Before buying hours, know what they can move. Under the Chemistry syllabus first examined in 2025 the externally assessed papers carry eighty per cent of the grade and the scientific investigation carries twenty. Paper 1 is split between multiple choice and a data-based section; Paper 2 is extended response. Higher Level sits the same structure with longer papers and greater depth. Confirm the exact durations and weightings for your child's cohort with the school's IB coordinator and the current subject guide, because the IB revises these.

The useful consequence is that the three components fail for three different reasons, and therefore respond to three different kinds of teaching. Multiple choice is lost to misread stems and arithmetic slips under time pressure, which is drilled rather than taught. The data-based section is lost to uncertainty handling and graph interpretation, which is a method problem. Paper 2 is lost to structure: students who know the chemistry write two sentences where the mark scheme wants four steps.

A tutor who treats all three as one subject will spend your money on content. The right sequence for most Oud Metha students is to fix Paper 2 structure first, because it is the largest single weighting and the fastest to move; then the data-based section, because it shares its skills with the investigation and so pays twice; then multiple choice, which needs volume rather than insight and can be done in the last six weeks.

sections.heading: The travel premium, priced for this part of Dubai
paragraphs: An in-home Chemistry tutor serving Oud Metha is solving a routing problem as much as a teaching one. The practical catchment from a Bur Dubai base is Karama, Al Mankhool, Oud Metha, Al Jaddaf and perhaps Al Garhoud before the bridge becomes the limiting factor. A tutor who accepts a 5pm in Oud Metha and a 7pm in Al Qusais is committing to a drive that can take forty minutes in either direction, and the rate card absorbs it.

That is the arithmetic behind the published monthly packages. AED 799 a month for eight online sessions is close to AED 100 a session. AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions is AED 200 to 225 an hour before anyone has taught anything. The teaching in both cases can be identical; one of them includes a car.

The consequence for a Chemistry student specifically is a narrower choice of teacher. HL Chemistry with strong organic mechanism teaching and real experience of the scientific investigation is a specialism, not a general science competence. Within a twenty-minute drive of Oud Metha the number of people who hold it is small, and smaller again once you filter for somebody free in the one window your family can actually use. Across the pool of tutors who can teach at 5pm Gulf Standard Time it is not small at all, and that difference is what the online format actually buys. It is not a compromise on the in-home option; it is the reason to prefer it. A family paying the travel premium is paying for a shorter shortlist.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry, energetics, and the two topics that eat a budget
paragraphs: Ask a Chemistry teacher where a Diploma cohort loses marks and the answer narrows quickly. Organic chemistry is first, not because the content is hard to read but because it is a sequence: reagent, condition, mechanism, product, and a student who has learned the products without the conditions answers half of every question. The repair is mechanism-by-mechanism practice with the arrows drawn by the student, which takes weeks and cannot be compressed into the fortnight before a paper.

Energetics and thermodynamics is second. Enthalpy cycles, bond enthalpies, entropy and the spontaneity condition are all arithmetic sitting on top of a sign convention, and the sign convention is where it collapses. A student who is confident on the definitions and wrong on the signs looks like a student who needs more content. They need twenty worked cycles and someone watching the signs.

Equilibrium is the third, and it is the one most often mistaught cheaply. Le Chatelier's principle can be recited in a sentence, which makes it feel covered. Applying it to a changed condition in a real system, and then connecting it to the equilibrium constant quantitatively, is a different skill, and it is the skill Paper 2 asks for. Students who can state the principle and cannot calculate with it typically score the first mark of a five-mark question and stop.

These three topics between them account for most of the hours an Oud Metha family will usefully buy. A tutor who proposes to start anywhere else should be asked why, and the answer should be a mark breakdown rather than a syllabus order. There is one honourable exception: measurement, uncertainty and significant figures. That work is dull, it is quick, and it pays in two places at once, because the same discipline is assessed in the data-based section of Paper 1 and in the analysis criterion of the investigation. It is the best-value fortnight on the whole course.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: what a tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: The Chemistry investigation is worth a fifth of the grade and is marked against criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The student signs a declaration that the work is their own. A tutor who drafts text, builds the graphs or rewrites the evaluation has created an academic-honesty breach that sits on the student's record, not the tutor's, and under IB rules the consequence can reach the whole Diploma.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial, and families are often surprised by how much of it there is. The research question can be challenged hard before any data exists, which is where most weak investigations are saved. The method can be interrogated for uncontrolled variables and insufficient range. Uncertainty treatment can be taught as a skill. The student's own draft can be read and returned with written feedback naming what a criterion is asking for and where the draft does not answer it.

This boundary is also a commercial point worth stating plainly, because this search result contains providers who cross it. One operator found during research for this project sells completed internal assessments outright at AED 3,750. That is not expensive tutoring; it is a malpractice trigger for the student and the end of the Diploma if it is detected. IB Gram does not write, complete or supply assessed work in any subject, and no reputable tutor in Dubai will either.

There is a budgeting point buried in the boundary. Because the permitted work is front-loaded, the investigation is cheapest to support early and most expensive to support late. Challenging a research question takes one session. Rescuing a finished investigation with a weak question takes several, produces less, and lands in the same weeks as Paper 2 revision at the highest intensity of the two years. An Oud Metha family that books two investigation sessions in DP1 term three usually spends less in total than one that books six in DP2 term two, and the earlier version is the one that moves the mark.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects sit on top of the Chemistry timetable
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school, whatever curriculum it is licensed for, teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies. KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidance states these requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a DP Chemistry student this is not a footnote. It is timetable time that cannot be given back, and it changes how much homework space exists on a Tuesday.

The organisational rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run shorter than twenty-five minutes.

Two practical consequences follow for a family budgeting Chemistry tuition in Oud Metha. First, schools must ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, which is a credential a parent can ask about directly. Second, for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so Arabic support has to work with the school's own material rather than around it. Budget for it separately from Chemistry; the two needs rarely share a tutor.

sections.heading: Counting the Diploma spend backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session, and the whole two-year budget should be built backwards from it rather than forwards from September. IB exam and results dates are not restated here: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a parent acts on must come from the school's IB coordinator or ibo.org directly. What can be planned without a date is the order of the work.

Working backwards, the final eight weeks before the session are for timed papers and multiple-choice volume, at the highest hourly intensity and therefore the highest cost. The term before that is for Paper 2 structure and the remaining content gaps. The investigation should already be submitted internally by then, which means the investigation window belongs to DP2 term one at the latest and ideally DP1 term three. DP1 is for the three topics named earlier and for the measurement discipline that feeds both Paper 1B and the investigation.

For IGCSE siblings in the same household the dates are available and sourced. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series; the February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply to UAE candidates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 Pearson results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, since it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and what a parent can verify before paying
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow for an Oud Metha parent. The permit is free, so a tutor who cites a permit fee as a reason for a higher rate is mistaken. And individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you either. Ask to see the permit. It costs the tutor nothing to hold and nothing to show.

On the regulatory side, Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there; Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which IB Gram does not hold and does not claim; IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge, and any provider telling you otherwise should be asked for the permit number.

process.title: Tell us the mark profile, not just the subject
process.description: A request that says Chemistry HL, lost marks concentrated in Paper 2 and organic, mock grade 4, is matched in a fraction of the time a request saying needs help with Chemistry takes. Send the most recent mark breakdown if you have one. It is the single most useful thing in the first message.

process.title: Free trial lesson, no payment discussed
process.description: The trial is a diagnostic. The tutor sets Chemistry problems across a few topics, watches where the method breaks rather than where the recall does, and reports what they found. If the match is wrong, you say so and nothing is owed. This is where the overpaying problem is solved, before money moves.

process.title: A written plan with a stated end point
process.description: After the trial you receive a short plan: the topics, the order, roughly how many sessions, and what the block is meant to achieve. A plan that cannot name its objective is a standing weekly slot in disguise, which is the most expensive way to buy tuition in this market.

process.title: A fixed weekly slot on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Lessons run live over video at a time chosen around the Bur Dubai school run, usually between 4.30pm and 7pm on a weekday. Ramadan timings shift to post-Iftar slots on request. Nobody drives anywhere, so a session that starts at 5pm starts at 5pm.

process.title: Review against the plan, then stop or continue
process.description: At the end of the block you get the mark evidence and a recommendation, including the recommendation to stop. A tutor who always recommends continuing is selling hours. Reviewing against a stated objective is what turns tuition from a subscription into a purchase.

whyPoints.title: The AED figures are published, with sources
whyPoints.description: Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and one asks the price in its own FAQ and declines to answer it. Every band on this page carries the name of the provider that published it and the month it was read. You can check them.

whyPoints.title: Specialist by paper, not by driving distance
whyPoints.description: An HL Chemistry student needs somebody who has taught the organic sequence and the scientific investigation repeatedly. Online delivery means the shortlist is drawn from everyone free at 5pm Gulf Standard Time rather than everyone within a twenty-minute drive of Oud Metha.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, challenges and gives feedback on the student's own work. IB Gram does not write, complete or supply an investigation, extended essay or any assessed coursework, in Chemistry or anything else. In this search result that is a real distinction rather than a slogan.

whyPoints.title: A trial before any payment
whyPoints.description: One free lesson, used as a diagnostic, with a written report on what the tutor found. If the match is wrong you say so and nothing is owed. The condition is simply that it is one lesson per student.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what is not available
whyPoints.description: If no Chemistry HL specialist is free in the window you need, we say so and tell you when one is, rather than filling the slot with a general science tutor. Availability transparency is absent from every competitor page researched, and it is the fastest way for a family to waste a term.

whyPoints.title: Regulatory claims we can actually stand behind
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, Ministry of Education, IB or Cambridge approval and claims none. What we do is explain what each body governs and point you to its own pages, so you can verify a school, an inspection band or a tutor permit yourself.

faqs.question: What does an online IB Chemistry tutor cost per hour in Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to 300 per sixty-minute session, reviewed October 2026. Unitors publishes from AED 200 for IB and from AED 150 for IGCSE; TutorChase publishes AED 270 for specialist support. Budget-tier online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, is advertised from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya. Premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. IB Gram starts with a free trial lesson and sets pricing after the diagnostic, because an hourly quote given before anyone has seen a past paper is guesswork.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to use an online Chemistry tutor or hire one who comes to our apartment in Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: Online is cheaper, and the gap is almost entirely travel. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors advertise up to AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for an equivalently qualified tutor teaching online. The advertised monthly packages make it plainer still: AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case, because every lesson is delivered live over video; home visits are an India-only service.

faqs.question: How many hours of Chemistry tuition will my child actually need?
faqs.answer: For a Higher Level student starting in DP1 with one weekly hour through to the May session of DP2, around sixty hours is realistic. That total is less important than its distribution. Most of the usable movement comes from three blocks: organic mechanisms and energetics in DP1, the scientific investigation across DP1 term three and DP2 term one, and timed paper practice in the final eight weeks. Families who buy a standing weekly slot for two years often pay for more hours and get less movement than families who buy three defined blocks with stated objectives and stop between them.

faqs.question: Which Chemistry topics do Dubai students lose the most marks on?
faqs.answer: Three, consistently. Organic chemistry, because it is a sequence of reagent, condition, mechanism and product, and students who learn products without conditions answer half of every question. Energetics and thermodynamics, because enthalpy cycles and entropy sit on a sign convention that collapses under pressure. Equilibrium, because Le Chatelier's principle is easy to recite and hard to apply quantitatively to a changed condition. Periodicity and bonding, which students expect to be the problem, are usually already secure. A tutor who proposes to begin with bonding is beginning with the content your child can already read.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the IB Chemistry scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a firm boundary. A tutor can challenge the research question before any data is collected, which is where most weak investigations are rescued. They can interrogate the method for uncontrolled variables and insufficient range, teach uncertainty treatment properly, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts against the assessment criteria. What a tutor must never do is write text, build the graphs or rewrite the evaluation. The student signs a declaration that the work is theirs, and a breach falls on the student's record. IB Gram does not write or supply assessed work in any subject.

faqs.question: How much of the IB Chemistry grade does the investigation carry?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, with the externally assessed papers carrying the other eighty under the syllabus first examined in 2025. Paper 1 is split between a multiple-choice section and a data-based section and carries 36 per cent; Paper 2 is extended response and carries 44 per cent. Higher Level sits the same structure with longer papers and greater depth. Confirm the exact durations and weightings for your child's cohort with the school's IB coordinator and the current subject guide, since the IB revises assessment structures between syllabus cycles and a figure read online can be a cycle out of date.

faqs.question: Does Chemistry HL cost more to support than Chemistry SL in Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, but through hours rather than rate; the published AED bands do not separate the two levels. HL adds depth inside the same topic headings rather than a long list of new ones, which is why HL students frequently cannot name what they are missing. The extra spend concentrates in organic chemistry, energetics and the quantitative treatment of equilibrium, and the papers are longer so timed practice takes more time. A student comfortable at SL moving up usually needs a method upgrade rather than a content sprint, which is a shorter and cheaper block than families expect.

faqs.question: My child is coming from Combined Science. Can they cope with Chemistry at Diploma level?
faqs.answer: It is possible but the gap is real and pretending otherwise is how DP1 goes wrong in October. Cambridge Combined Science covers all three sciences at reduced depth, so a student arrives without the full mole treatment, without electrolysis in detail and with thin organic coverage. The repair takes roughly four to six weeks of focused work and is far cheaper done in the summer before DP1 than in February of DP2. Ask the school's Chemistry department what entry profile they expect, then budget for the gap deliberately rather than discovering it in a mock.

faqs.question: Does the tutor permit add anything to what we pay in Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: No, because it is free. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Since the permit is free, ask to see it.

faqs.question: Which schools near Oud Metha offer the IB Diploma in Chemistry?
faqs.answer: The Diploma provision within reach of an Oud Metha address sits mainly across the Creek and in Al Jaddaf. Swiss International Scientific School in Al Jaddaf runs a full IB continuum; Deira International School and Universal American School in Dubai Festival City both offer the Diploma, reached via Al Garhoud Bridge. Within Oud Metha and Bur Dubai itself the provision is largely British and Indian curriculum, including St Mary's Catholic High School and The Indian High School. Check the current KHDA inspection report and the school's own subject list before assuming DP Chemistry is timetabled; a course in a brochure is not always a course running.

faqs.question: What time can a Chemistry session realistically start for a family in Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: For families whose school run stays inside Bur Dubai or Al Jaddaf, 4.30pm is workable and 5pm is comfortable. For families collecting from Dubai Festival City, Al Garhoud Bridge is the variable: a 3.15pm pickup can be home by 3.45pm or by 4.30pm depending on the day, so 5.30pm is the safer booking. Because lessons are delivered live online, no travel time is added at the tutor's end either, which is the practical reason a 5pm slot actually begins at 5pm. Ramadan sessions can move to post-Iftar timings on request.

faqs.question: Do tuition rates in Dubai go up closer to the exams?
faqs.answer: The published hourly bands do not generally change, but what families spend rises sharply because intensity rises. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at budget level and AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, while specialist exam-year support is estimated at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month. The increase is hours, not rate. The way to avoid it is to move the investigation work and the organic and energetics blocks into DP1, so the final eight weeks are timed paper practice rather than a content rescue at peak intensity.

faqs.question: Is Arabic or Islamic Education going to affect my child's Chemistry timetable?
faqs.answer: It affects the timetable, yes. Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of its licensed curriculum, and KHDA's guidance required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for April-start schools. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit and KHDA advises no mandatory-subject lesson runs under twenty-five minutes. Schools must also organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Budget Arabic support separately; it rarely shares a tutor with Chemistry.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level Chemistry specialist is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we tell you when one is. The alternative, filling the slot with a general science tutor and hoping, costs a family a term and is the most common quiet failure in this market. No competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all. If the window you need cannot be covered, the honest options are to shift the slot, to start with a defined block on the components that any strong science teacher can move such as measurement and uncertainty, or to wait. We will say which of the three we think applies.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers, mark schemes or IB syllabus documents?
faqs.answer: No, and no reputable provider should. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright material, and reproducing or distributing them is infringement. What a tutor does is work with material the student legitimately holds through their school, cite the official source, and link you to it: ibo.org for the Diploma, cambridgeinternational.org for Cambridge qualifications and qualifications.pearson.com for Edexcel. Your child's school and its IB coordinator are the proper route to current subject guides and released papers.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-oud-metha.closingHeading: Start with the diagnostic, then decide what to spend
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-oud-metha.closingBody: The useful sequence for an Oud Metha family is small. Book the free trial lesson and let the tutor set Chemistry problems across organic, energetics and equilibrium rather than talk about method. Read what they report back about where the marks are going. Then choose a block with a stated objective and an end date, at a rate you can compare against the AED bands published on this page. Sessions run live over video on Gulf Standard Time, timed around the Bur Dubai school run. If the match is wrong after the trial, say so and nothing is owed. If no Higher Level specialist is free in your window, we will tell you that too.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-palm-jumeira.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach Diploma Chemistry at Higher and Standard Level. Each works to a named subject guide rather than to a generic syllabus summary, and sessions run live over video with students across Palm Jumeirah, Al Sufouh and the Jumeirah coast.

intro.heading: Is there anybody near this island who knows the current Chemistry course?
paragraphs: The honest answer is that proximity was never the useful filter, and on Palm Jumeirah that is unusually obvious. The island has no secondary school. Every child on the fronds, along the Shoreline or in the Golden Mile already travels off it each morning, usually to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim or the Jumeirah beach strip. A parent who searches for a tutor nearby is therefore filtering a pool that was never built around their address in the first place. The question worth asking instead is whether a particular tutor knows this course.

That matters more in Chemistry than in most subjects, because the Diploma Chemistry course was restructured. The present guide is organised around two sets of themes rather than the old topic list: a structure strand covering models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter; and a reactivity strand covering what drives chemical reactions, how much, how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Higher Level content sits inside those same themes rather than in a separate appendix, and the old third paper has gone. A tutor working from memory of the previous structure will teach good chemistry against the wrong map.

The second thing that changed is the internal assessment. There is now one scientific investigation, carrying 20% of the final grade, assessed inside the school against published criteria and externally moderated. Students who were taught to a different internal-assessment pattern, or whose tutor was, arrive at the design stage with the wrong expectations about scope and about what the criteria reward. This is the most common place a competent Chemistry student loses a grade, and it has nothing to do with chemistry knowledge.

So the test of a tutor is not distance and not a rate card. It is whether they can say which guide and which first-examination year they are teaching to, which theme a given topic now sits in, how Paper 1A and Paper 1B differ in what they demand, and exactly where the line falls between coaching an investigation and interfering with it. Four questions, answerable in ten minutes, and they filter the market faster than any amount of searching by neighbourhood.

What IB Gram provides is one-to-one Chemistry teaching delivered live over video to Palm Jumeirah addresses, timed to Gulf Standard Time around the commute back onto the island. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE - that is an India-only service - and there is no office or centre in the emirate. The rest of this page is the detail a parent needs to interrogate any Chemistry tutor, including ours: the theme map, the component weightings, the Higher Level divergence, the honest availability position, and the questions to ask first.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-palm-jumeira.programmesIntro: A Chemistry question looks different depending on which IB programme the student sits in, and Palm Jumeirah families are spread across all of them. The notes below describe what each programme actually demands of a chemistry learner rather than summarising the programme itself.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Chemistry sits in Group 4 and runs at Higher or Standard Level across two years. Assessment is two written papers plus one scientific investigation. Paper 1 has a multiple-choice section and a data-based section; Paper 2 is structured and extended response. The data booklet is supplied in the examination, so recall of constants matters less than knowing what is in it and how to use it under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's Diploma cohort is a minority of a very large private-school market, so a school may run a single Higher Level Chemistry class and no second specialist. For a Palm Jumeirah family this is the practical reason paid support gets bought: not weak teaching, but no spare capacity for one-to-one attention on a specific mechanism or a specific investigation design.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sciences in the MYP is taught as one subject across chemistry, physics and biology, assessed on four criteria rather than by percentage. A student can hold strong chemistry content and still score modestly because the inquiring and designing criterion, or the evaluating criterion, was never taught as a separate skill. The gap is in method rather than in knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools reachable from the island run MYP to year 5 and then the Diploma, while others move to IGCSE at 14. An MYP student entering Diploma Chemistry has usually met less quantitative work than an IGCSE student has, and the shortfall appears in moles, titration arithmetic and energetics rather than in conceptual understanding.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Where a CP student takes Chemistry as one of their Diploma courses, the assessment for that course is identical to the Diploma version, including the scientific investigation and its 20% weighting.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools offer the Career-related Programme, and fewer offer Chemistry inside it, which makes tutoring availability for this combination the thinnest of all. It is one of the cases where disclosing a coverage limit in advance matters more than quoting a rate, because a family can plan around a known constraint and cannot plan around a surprise.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-palm-jumeira.subjectsIntro: Chemistry requests from this part of Dubai arrive in recognisable clusters, usually driven by a university target rather than by interest. These are the subjects most often needed alongside it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two written papers and one scientific investigation. Marks are most often lost on mechanism arrows drawn imprecisely, on energetics sign conventions, on equilibrium questions answered qualitatively where a calculation was wanted, and on data-based questions where the student explains the chemistry but never interrogates the data's reliability.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The usual partner for a medicine or life-sciences target. Shares the investigation structure with Chemistry, which means one tutor can often coach both internal assessment processes even where content teaching needs two people. Mark schemes here punish loose terminology much harder than Chemistry's do.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Taken with Chemistry by engineering and physical-sciences applicants. The shared skill is uncertainty and graph work in the data-based sections; a student who learns it properly in one subject usually picks up marks in the other without extra teaching.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic fluency Chemistry calculations depend on lives here. Rearranging, logarithms for pH work, and handling proportionality under time pressure are mathematics problems that present as chemistry problems, and diagnosing which is failing saves a term of misaimed tutoring.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Workable alongside Chemistry, with heavier statistics and a graphical-calculator expectation. Students on this route sometimes need deliberate algebra support for equilibrium and energetics work that the Analysis route would have covered incidentally.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Occasionally taken with Chemistry where a student wants two Group 4 subjects without Physics. Content overlaps on biochemistry and energy systems, and the investigation has the same evidence standards, so study habits transfer.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Counts as Group 3 or Group 4, which makes it a timetable solution for students who need Chemistry plus a humanities slot. Chemistry students usually find the data interpretation familiar and the systems vocabulary unfamiliar.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Named here because Chemistry students regularly lose Paper 2 marks to writing rather than to chemistry: explanations that assert instead of reasoning, and conclusions that restate the question. Work on precise written reasoning transfers directly into extended-response marks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Compulsory, with an exhibition and an essay. Chemistry students have unusually good material for it - models, evidence, the status of a theory - and often the least appetite. Support is about argument structure and counterclaim rather than content.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Chemistry
subjects.description: An independent research essay with a strict word limit, supervised inside the school. Where it is taken in Chemistry the practical constraints of school laboratory access shape what is answerable, and that constraint should be discussed before a question is fixed rather than afterwards.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-palm-jumeira.regionsTitle: Where the students on this page actually study
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-palm-jumeira.regionsIntro: Because the island has no secondary provision, a Palm Jumeirah Chemistry student is defined by the school they commute to rather than by the frond they live on. These are the destinations that matter, with what each one implies for Chemistry support.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The closest school cluster to the island and home to some of Dubai's longest-established selective provision. Students here are usually on an IGCSE-then-A-Level or IGCSE-then-Diploma path, so the Chemistry course at 16 depends on a choice made two years earlier.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: Where much of the IB Diploma and American provision sits. The furthest routine commute from the Palm and the cluster that generates the most Diploma Chemistry enquiries, often from students in a single Higher Level class with no second specialist available in school.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: A dense belt of schools along the beach road. Chemistry students here frequently combine a Diploma timetable with competitive swimming or sailing, which compresses the week and makes a fixed evening session more valuable than a flexible afternoon one.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1 and Jumeirah 2
regions.note: Mixed provision inside low-rise villa districts, including schools running Indian and British curricula alongside IB. Some Palm families keep primary-age children here and move them off-island for secondary, so the Chemistry question arrives later than the family's first tutoring enquiry.

regions.name: Jumeirah 3 and Al Manara
regions.note: Quieter residential streets inland of the beach road, with a handful of smaller campuses. Students travelling back to the Palm from here cross the trunk-road junction at the worst part of the afternoon, which in practice rules out a session before 5:00pm.
