sections.heading: What the current Diploma Chemistry course actually contains
paragraphs: Diploma Chemistry is now organised around two strands rather than a numbered topic list. The structure strand covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. The reactivity strand covers what drives chemical reactions, how much, how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Higher Level material is embedded inside those themes rather than appended, and the course is assessed by two written papers plus one scientific investigation.

That reorganisation has a practical consequence a parent can test. Ask a prospective tutor which theme a familiar topic now sits in. Enthalpy and entropy belong to what drives chemical reactions. Rates and equilibrium belong to how much, how fast and how far. Nucleophilic substitution and electrophilic addition belong to the mechanisms theme. A tutor who answers in the vocabulary of the previous syllabus is probably a good chemist teaching from an out-of-date map, and the student will spend sessions translating.

Paper 1 is split in two. Section A is multiple choice, and rewards fast, secure single-concept work. Section B is data-based and rewards something different entirely: reading an unfamiliar dataset, judging reliability, and reasoning about what the numbers do and do not support. Students who revise content thoroughly and never practise Section B lose marks that have nothing to do with how much chemistry they know. Paper 2 is structured and extended response and carries the largest single share of the grade.

Because guides and first-examination years change, nothing in the table below should be taken as final for a particular student. Ask the school's Diploma coordinator which subject guide is in use and which examination year applies, then check it against the table. A tutor who cannot name the guide they teach to has failed the first question on this page.

sections.heading: Why a twenty-minute radius is the wrong filter for a Chemistry tutor
paragraphs: Searching by distance works for a piano teacher and fails for Diploma Chemistry, because the pool it selects is defined by geography rather than by subject. The number of people within a comfortable weekday drive of a frond villa who can teach Higher Level mechanisms, read the investigation criteria accurately and mark an extended response against a published scheme is small. Widen the search by format rather than by distance and the pool is defined by what the tutor teaches instead.

Palm Jumeirah makes this concrete. One trunk road connects the island to the mainland, and every frond is a gated cul-de-sac off it. The monorail serves the hotel strip, not the residential fronds. A tutor travelling to a weekday session at 4:30pm queues at the junction, drives the frond spine, clears a gate, teaches, and repeats the journey afterwards. All of that time sits inside an in-home rate. Nothing about it improves the chemistry.

The counter-argument for in-home tutoring is real but specific. A younger child who needs an adult physically present learns better with one. A student who will not engage with a screen is not helped by being matched to a brilliant distant specialist. For a 17-year-old eight months from a written series, working through mechanism notation on a shared screen with a specialist, those considerations do not apply, and the geography argument collapses entirely.

So the search a Palm Jumeirah parent should run is not for a Chemistry tutor near them. It is for a Chemistry tutor who can name the guide, locate a topic in the right theme, explain how Paper 1B differs from Paper 1A, and state the internal-assessment boundary without being prompted. IB Gram answers that search with live one-to-one video teaching timed to Gulf Standard Time. It does not sell home visits in the UAE, and no UAE centre exists.

sections.heading: Higher Level and Standard Level Chemistry are not the same course
paragraphs: Families often treat Higher Level as Standard Level with extra topics bolted on. It is closer to the truth to say that Higher Level assumes complete Standard Level fluency and then asks questions that would be unanswerable without it. The written papers are longer, the extended-response demands are heavier, and the mechanisms theme in particular expands into territory a Standard Level student never meets.

The decision matters for two reasons beyond workload. The first is university prerequisites: some medicine and chemical-engineering routes specify Chemistry at Higher Level, and a Standard Level pass can close a door that cannot be reopened in the final year. The second is grade risk. A student who would reach a strong Standard Level grade may land in the middle bands at Higher Level, and for most university offers a secure 6 at Standard Level is worth more than a fragile 4 at Higher.

The practical tutoring consequence is sequencing. A Higher Level student with gaps in the structure themes should not be buying mechanism hours yet, because the mechanism questions assume bonding fluency the student does not have. This is the most common misallocation in Chemistry support: hours spent on the hardest visible content while the foundation that content rests on stays weak. A diagnostic session that reads a marked paper against the criteria usually makes the right order obvious.

sections.heading: Where Chemistry marks are actually lost, topic by topic
paragraphs: Students rarely lose Chemistry marks evenly. The losses cluster, and the clusters are predictable enough that a marked paper usually diagnoses them in one reading. Mole-based calculation chains lose marks to premature rounding and to units dropped midway. Bonding questions lose marks because the student names an intermolecular force correctly and never explains how it produces the property being asked about. Both are precision failures rather than knowledge failures, and both respond quickly to teaching.

Energetics is where sign conventions do the damage. A student who can define enthalpy change and still writes it with the wrong sign will lose the mark every time, and because the error is systematic it compounds across a paper. Entropy and free energy questions add a second trap: arguing spontaneity without reference to temperature. Teaching here is almost entirely about forcing a consistent written routine rather than about explaining the concept again.

Equilibrium, rates and acid-base work generate the largest single category of avoidable loss, because students answer qualitatively where a calculation was required. The question says calculate and the answer says the equilibrium shifts to the right. Related to it is the data-based section of Paper 1, where the chemistry is often correct and the student never interrogates the reliability of the data, which is precisely what the section is testing.

Mechanisms are the Higher Level pressure point. Arrows drawn from the wrong origin cost mechanism marks even where the overall product is right, and nucleophilic substitution questions are frequently answered with the correct outcome and an incorrect pathway. This is the area where a specialist is genuinely hard to replace, because the marking is precise and a general science tutor will usually accept an answer an examiner would not.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: the boundary, in plain words
paragraphs: One scientific investigation carries 20% of the Chemistry grade. The student designs it, carries it out, and reports it, and the school certifies that the submission is the student's own. That certification is why the boundary on tutoring matters so much: a breach is a malpractice finding against the student, not an administrative problem for the tutor.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial. They can teach the chemistry the investigation rests on. They can press hard on whether the research question can be answered with the apparatus the school actually has, which is where most weak investigations are decided. They can explain how the published criteria are applied, using the examiner's own vocabulary. They can model uncertainty treatment on a different dataset. And they can read a draft the student wrote and say where the reasoning does not hold up.

What a tutor cannot do is contribute anything that ends up in the submitted file. No supplied data. No written sections. No template that becomes the report. One operator in this market openly advertises finished internal assessments for sale; that is an academic-integrity breach with consequences for the student, and the price being asked is irrelevant to how bad an idea it is.

For a Palm Jumeirah family the practical move is to buy the hours early. Two or three sessions in the week the research question is being chosen achieve more than ten in the week before submission, cost less, and leave nothing ambiguous about authorship. Ask any prospective Chemistry tutor what they will and will not do with investigation work before the first session. The answer tells you how to read everything else they say.

sections.heading: The ten-minute interview: what to ask any Chemistry tutor
paragraphs: A parent does not need to understand Chemistry to test a Chemistry tutor. Four questions do most of the work, and all of them are answerable in a first conversation. Ask which subject guide and first-examination year they teach to. Ask which theme a named topic now sits in. Ask how Paper 1A and Paper 1B differ in what they demand of a student. Ask what they will and will not do with the scientific investigation.

Good answers sound specific and slightly impatient. A tutor who teaches this course will name the guide without hesitating, place enthalpy in the theme about what drives chemical reactions, explain that Section B tests data interrogation rather than recall, and state the internal-assessment boundary before being pushed on it. Weak answers are general: talk about building confidence, about covering the syllabus, about years of experience, with nothing that could be checked.

There is a fifth question worth asking about the student rather than the subject. Ask what they would do in a first session with a student who is scoring in the middle bands and cannot say why. The useful answer involves looking at marked work and finding error patterns. The unhelpful answer involves starting at the beginning of the course, which is how twenty hours get spent re-teaching material the student already knows.

Finally, ask about availability honestly and expect an honest reply. A provider who promises any specialism at any time has not checked. A provider who says Higher Level Chemistry at 4:30pm on a Tuesday is tight, and explains what happens if nobody is free, is describing a real service. That distinction is worth more than any rate comparison.

sections.heading: Starting Chemistry support from the island
paragraphs: Begin with a conversation that costs nothing. Useful material: the most recent marked Chemistry paper, the current and predicted grades, whether the student is at Higher or Standard Level, which subject guide the school is using, and the date of the next internal assessment or school examination. A marked script is far more useful than a report, because it shows which errors repeat.

Then take the free trial lesson. One session, with the student doing the work rather than watching, is the only reliable test of whether a tutor can teach this student this course. Watch whether the tutor asks the student to explain their reasoning, whether they name the theme and the component being worked on, and whether anything concrete gets fixed inside the hour.

Then agree a plan with the sequence written down. For most Chemistry students that means structure themes before mechanisms, a dedicated block on data-based work, investigation process coaching timed to the design stage, and timed-paper practice in the final terms. Sessions are scheduled around the commute back onto the island and shift to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan. The plan exists so that it can be reviewed against marked work at the end of a term.

Two things will not be claimed at any point. IB Gram holds no accreditation, approval or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and does not describe itself as having one. And no tutor will promise a grade. Chemistry grades come from a student's own work on papers and an investigation; what tutoring can offer is accurate teaching, honest diagnosis, and a boundary that keeps the student's work their own.

faqs.question: Who on Palm Jumeirah actually teaches the current IB Chemistry course?
faqs.answer: Nobody teaches it on the island itself, because Palm Jumeirah has no secondary school. Every student there commutes off the island, usually to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim or the Jumeirah strip, so the pool of Chemistry teachers relevant to a Palm family was never local to begin with. That is why searching by distance is the wrong approach here. The useful filter is whether a tutor can name the subject guide they teach to, place a topic in the right theme under the current structure, and explain how the data-based section of Paper 1 differs from the multiple-choice section.

faqs.question: Has IB Chemistry changed since my child started school?
faqs.answer: The Diploma Chemistry course was restructured, which matters when choosing a tutor. Content is now organised around a structure strand covering the particulate nature of matter, bonding and structure, and classification of matter, and a reactivity strand covering what drives reactions, how much, how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Higher Level material sits inside those themes rather than in a separate section, and assessment is two written papers plus one scientific investigation. Confirm the exact guide and first-examination year with your child's Diploma coordinator, because the details differ between guides.

faqs.question: What does the Chemistry data-based question test?
faqs.answer: It tests whether a student can interrogate data they have never seen, not whether they remember chemistry. A typical item presents results from an unfamiliar experiment and asks what they support, how reliable they are, what the uncertainty implies, or what a graph's shape means. Students who revise content thoroughly and never practise this section lose marks that have nothing to do with knowledge. It is also among the cheapest sections to improve, because the skills are explicit and teachable in a small number of hours, and the same skills then pay off in Paper 2 and in the investigation.

faqs.question: My child cannot do organic reaction mechanisms. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Usually, and faster than families expect, because the problem is almost always notation rather than understanding. Marks in mechanism questions are allocated to where arrows start and end, so a student can identify the right product and still lose most of the marks by drawing an arrow from the wrong origin. The fix is a drilled routine: identify the electron-rich site, identify the electron-poor site, then draw. It needs a specialist, though, because a general science tutor will often accept an answer an examiner would not, which leaves the habit uncorrected.

faqs.question: Is IB Chemistry HL worth the extra teaching hours over SL?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the university target. Some medicine and chemical-engineering routes specify Chemistry at Higher Level, and a Standard Level pass can close those doors in a way the final year cannot reopen. Where the target does not require it, a secure Standard Level 6 is worth more to most offers than a fragile Higher Level 4. Check the stated requirements of the actual courses being considered before the level is fixed. A diagnostic session that reads marked work against the criteria is a cheaper way to judge fit than a year at the wrong level.

faqs.question: Which Chemistry topics does HL add that SL never sees?
faqs.answer: Rather than a separate appendix, the current structure extends the same themes in depth, with the heaviest expansion in the mechanisms theme and in energetics. Higher Level questions also assume complete Standard Level fluency, so the difficulty is as much cumulative as it is additional. The practical consequence for tutoring is sequencing: a Higher Level student with gaps in bonding and structure should not be buying mechanism hours yet, because mechanism questions rest on that foundation. Confirm the specific additional content against the subject guide your child's school is teaching.

faqs.question: What should I ask a Chemistry tutor in the first ten minutes?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which subject guide and first-examination year do you teach to? Which theme does enthalpy now sit in? What does the data-based section of Paper 1 test that the multiple-choice section does not? And what will you not do with my child's scientific investigation? Specific, slightly impatient answers indicate someone who teaches this course. General answers about building confidence and covering the syllabus indicate someone who does not. A fifth question is worth adding: what would you do in a first session with a student stuck in the middle bands?

faqs.question: How far should I search from Palm Jumeirah for a Chemistry specialist?
faqs.answer: Distance is the wrong axis. Searching within a comfortable weekday drive of a frond villa selects a pool by geography, and the number of people in it who can teach Higher Level mechanisms and read the investigation criteria accurately is small. Searching by format instead selects by specialism. The island's single trunk road means any in-home visit carries the junction queue twice inside the rate, and none of that travel improves the chemistry. For a student in an examination year, who teaches the course matters more than where they sleep.

faqs.question: What if no UAE-based IB Chemistry tutor is free at our preferred time?
faqs.answer: You are told before booking, not afterwards. Higher Level Chemistry is a narrow specialism and early-evening weekday slots are the tightest, so availability for a specific person at a specific hour is never assumed. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the alternative offered is a specialist from the wider network teaching on Gulf Standard Time at an agreed time, with the same format, the same guide and the same written feedback. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE parents abroad without saying so.

faqs.question: Can a Chemistry tutor look at my child's investigation before submission?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the chemistry involved, question whether the research question can be answered with the school's apparatus, explain how the published criteria are applied, model uncertainty treatment on other data, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply data, text or analysis that ends up in the submitted file, because the school certifies the work as the student's own. Buying hours at the design stage is both more useful and completely unambiguous; help sought days before submission is neither.

faqs.question: How do online Chemistry sessions handle practical work?
faqs.answer: The practical work for the scientific investigation happens at school, with school apparatus, under school supervision, and that is where it should happen. Online sessions handle everything around it: designing an investigation that the available equipment can actually support, planning what data to collect and how much, processing results, treating uncertainty properly, and evaluating reliability. In written examinations, practical skills are assessed through the data-based section rather than in a laboratory, so the preparation that moves those marks is analytical work, which transfers to a shared screen without loss.

faqs.question: Does my child need to memorise the data booklet for Chemistry?
faqs.answer: No. The data booklet is provided in the examination, so recall of constants and values is not what is being tested. What matters is fluency with it under time pressure: knowing what it contains, finding the right page without hunting, and choosing the correct value when two look plausible. Students who have never used it in timed conditions lose minutes they cannot spare and sometimes select the wrong quantity entirely. Practising with it during past-paper work is a small, specific habit that returns marks across both written papers.

faqs.question: How many Chemistry sessions a week is sensible in the final year?
faqs.answer: One weekly session suits most students, with short concentrated blocks added where a specific need appears: a dedicated run on the data-based section, a few hours at the investigation design stage, and timed-paper technique work in the final terms. Two sessions a week is usually a sign that the plan is reactive rather than sequenced, and in a final year competing with five other subjects it is rarely sustainable. Anyone quoting a standard number of hours for a Chemistry grade is guessing; the honest answer comes from reading a marked paper first.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Chemistry and Biology for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it works best for investigation coaching, because both subjects share the same assessment structure and the same evidence standards. For content teaching it depends on the levels: one specialist covering Chemistry at Higher Level and Biology at Standard Level is realistic, while two Higher Level sciences usually need two specialists to be taught properly. Where two tutors are used, the scheduling is coordinated so the week stays workable and each subject gets its own written progress note rather than a combined summary that hides which subject is moving.

faqs.question: What separates a Chemistry 5 from a Chemistry 7?
faqs.answer: Rarely more knowledge. Usually precision and command-term discipline. The student at 5 names an intermolecular force and stops; the student at 7 explains how it produces the property asked about. The 5 answers an equilibrium question qualitatively; the 7 notices the question said calculate. The 5 gets the right product in a mechanism and loses the arrow marks; the 7 draws from the correct origin every time. Those are habits, not talent, and they are what a specialist can teach. No tutor can promise a particular grade, whatever a provider's marketing suggests.

faqs.question: Does a Chemistry tutor in Dubai need a work permit to charge fees?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted. Ask directly, and check the official MoHRE service page.

intro.heading: Why this particular subject is hard to source locally
paragraphs: A parent on Pearl Jumeira asking who nearby can teach IB Chemistry at Higher Level is asking the right question and will probably get a misleading answer. The listings will be long. The number of people in them who have actually taught the Higher Level course, marked the investigation criteria and drilled organic mechanisms to a mark scheme will be small. This page is about how to tell the difference, because the cost of getting it wrong is a term.

Three forces produce the gap. The first is that the International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25, out of 387,441 students across 227 schools, against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum. The teaching workforce follows the enrolment, so the overwhelming majority of chemistry tutors in this city have taught IGCSE and A Level rather than the Diploma. Those are respectable qualifications and they are not this one.

The second is that demand in chemistry is concentrated at Higher Level in a way it is not in most subjects, because medicine and dentistry applications generally require it. That produces a cohort of students who need a specific grade for a specific course, competing for a thin supply, which is why Higher Level chemistry is among the tightest points in the Dubai tutoring market. Price does not solve this, because general and specialist chemistry tutors quote similar figures, and the parent has no way to read the difference off a rate card. It is also a market where the mismatch stays hidden for months: an A Level chemist will teach moles, energetics and equilibrium perfectly well through the first term, and the gap only becomes visible when the Higher Level procedures arrive or the first investigation draft is written against criteria nobody has explained.

The third is geography. Pearl Jumeira is reclaimed land off the Jumeirah 1 shoreline reached by one causeway. A visiting tutor has to be free at a fixed hour, prepared to cross Al Wasl Road at the end of the school day and queue onto the island, and in possession of the Higher Level experience. Those conditions multiply rather than add, and applied together they frequently leave nobody. What happens next is the predictable thing: a capable A Level chemist arrives at a Diploma rate, and the mismatch surfaces when the first investigation draft is written without reference to the criteria it will be marked against.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with mechanisms drawn on a shared screen and kept. The reason that answers the question rather than sidestepping it: dropping the distance condition is what makes the Higher Level condition satisfiable, and the Higher Level condition is the one that affects the grade.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-pearl-jumeir.subjectsIntro: The list below is deliberately weighted towards Higher Level content, because that is the part a tutor either has or has not taught. Use it as a checklist in a conversation.

subjects.name: Buffer solutions and weak acid pH
subjects.description: Calculating the pH of a weak acid and of a buffer, and recognising which method a question calls for. The commonest Higher Level error is applying the strong-acid method to a weak acid, which is a procedure-selection problem rather than a conceptual one.

subjects.name: Standard electrode potentials
subjects.description: Combining half cells, predicting feasibility and handling the sign convention. A tutor who has taught A Level electrochemistry knows the chemistry; the Diploma expects a specific presentation of the working that has to be learned.

subjects.name: Entropy and Gibbs energy
subjects.description: Spontaneity, temperature dependence and the arithmetic of combining enthalpy and entropy terms. Units and sign conventions produce most of the lost marks, and those are drilled rather than explained.

subjects.name: Equilibrium constant calculations
subjects.description: Setting up an expression from initial and equilibrium quantities. Students manage qualitative shifts at Standard Level and stumble on the setup, which is the single most diagnostic question to ask a prospective tutor about.

subjects.name: Organic reaction mechanisms
subjects.description: Nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and the reasoning that selects a pathway. The marks are in the curly arrows drawn to convention, starting from a bond or a lone pair rather than from an atom.

subjects.name: Spectroscopy for structure determination
subjects.description: Using mass spectra, infrared and nuclear magnetic resonance data together to deduce a structure. Rewards a fixed reading order, which most students have never been given and which a Diploma-experienced tutor will have one for.

subjects.name: Transition metals and complexes
subjects.description: Colour, ligands, geometry and naming. Recall volume rather than difficulty, which makes it a frequent late-stage loss when it is met close to the examinations without rehearsal.

subjects.name: Moles, limiting reagents and yield
subjects.description: The arithmetic everything rests on. Multi-step problems lose marks through sequencing rather than chemistry, which is why a marked script separates a technique problem from a content one in minutes.

subjects.name: Energetics and enthalpy cycles
subjects.description: Bond enthalpies, Hess cycles and calorimetry, with sign conventions as the reliable trap. Secure at Standard Level, these are the foundation the Higher Level entropy work assumes.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: Both levels, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: Four criteria worth 24 marks within a 3,000-word limit. A Diploma-experienced tutor knows these criteria by name and knows that chemistry investigations fail at method feasibility rather than at chemistry.

sections.heading: Demand and supply in Dubai chemistry, set side by side
paragraphs: The gap this page describes is not an impression. It follows from three measurable things about the Dubai market, which the table below sets against each other.

On the demand side, Higher Level chemistry is required by medicine and dentistry pathways, and those are among the most commonly pursued competitive applications from Dubai schools. That concentrates a large share of total chemistry tutoring demand into one subject at one level, with a cohort of students who need a particular grade for a particular course and a timeline they cannot move.

On the supply side, the International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25, against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum. Teaching experience follows enrolment with a lag, so the proportion of chemistry teachers in this city who have taught the Diploma is small, and the proportion who have taught it at Higher Level is smaller. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new International Baccalaureate schools among seven new private schools and 16,846 new places, which widens the gap rather than closing it, because places arrive faster than experienced teachers do.

A fourth point sits underneath the other three and is easy to miss. Because the gap is structural, it does not resolve by waiting. A family that cannot find Higher Level chemistry depth in October will not find more of it in February, when the same thin supply is additionally committed. The useful response is to change a condition rather than to keep searching under the same ones, and the condition worth dropping is the geographic one. The third factor is that the market does not price the difference. Published rates for a qualified online subject tutor run AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB rates from AED 200 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work, and in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500 with travel included per Bestimate and independent tutors. Those figures, read in October 2026, belong to the providers named. Nothing in that range reliably signals whether a person has taught Higher Level chemistry, which is why the checklist in the next section does more for a family than a rate comparison.

sections.heading: The Higher Level checklist, and how to use it in a conversation
paragraphs: The most reliable test of whether somebody has taught Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level is to ask about content that exists only at Higher Level. You do not need to understand the answers chemically; you need to notice whether they arrive immediately and specifically or generally and warmly.

The four to ask about are buffers and weak acid pH, standard electrode potentials, entropy with Gibbs energy, and equilibrium constant calculations. Each is Higher Level content, each has a characteristic student failure that anybody who has taught it will name without prompting, and none of them can be bluffed in detail. A tutor who has taught the course will say something like: students apply the strong-acid method to a weak acid, or the sign errors come when half cells are combined, or the difficulty is setting up the expression from initial amounts rather than doing the algebra. A tutor who has not will talk about the importance of practice.

Then ask about organic mechanisms, which is the most discriminating single question in chemistry. The answer you want concerns drawing convention: where a curly arrow starts and where it points, and the fact that an arrow beginning on an atom rather than on a bond or a lone pair loses the mark even when the mechanism is understood. Somebody who has marked Diploma chemistry says this immediately because they have written it on scripts hundreds of times.

Finally ask what the investigation criteria are called and what the word limit is. Four criteria, 24 marks between them, a 3,000-word limit. A tutor who cannot produce that has not supervised one, which matters because the investigation is 20 per cent of the grade and the failure modes are predictable only to somebody who has seen them. Ask these five things before paying for anything; the conversation takes twenty minutes and it is the highest-value thing available to a family in this market.

sections.heading: Where the Higher Level extension actually sits
paragraphs: Chemistry Higher Level is not a deeper version of Standard Level spread evenly across the syllabus. The additional content clusters in identifiable places, and knowing where changes both the conversation with a tutor and the planning of a year.

Three of the extensions are new calculation procedures, and they tend to arrive in the second year together: buffer and weak acid pH, standard electrode potentials, and entropy with Gibbs energy. Each sits on top of Standard Level material the student has already met, so the characteristic risk is not misunderstanding but confusion between methods. A student who applies the strong-acid route to a weak acid has not misunderstood acids; they have failed to notice which procedure the question called for, which is a different and more trainable problem.

The other extensions add recall volume rather than procedure: organic mechanisms in greater depth, transition metal chemistry and complexes, and more demanding spectroscopy. These reward frequent short testing and repeated drawing rather than explanation, and they are the part of the course most often met too late because they sit near the end of the teaching sequence.

Underneath both groups is an assumption worth naming. Every Higher Level extension assumes fluency with the Standard Level material it builds on. A student still hesitant about setting up an equilibrium expression will experience electrode potentials as two problems rather than one. That makes the first Diploma year the cheap year in chemistry and the second year the expensive one, and it is the strongest argument for a standing weekly hour from September of Year 12 rather than a rescue in January of Year 13.

sections.heading: Organic mechanisms: the single most discriminating competence
paragraphs: If a family can only test one thing, test this. Organic mechanism teaching separates Diploma chemistry experience from general chemistry competence more sharply than any other topic, and it carries a large share of the available Higher Level marks.

The reason is that the chemistry and the marks are not the same thing. A capable chemist can explain nucleophilic substitution clearly and completely. What a Diploma-experienced teacher adds is the convention: an arrow must originate from a bond or a lone pair, not from an atom; it must point to where the new bond forms; intermediates must be drawn with charges shown; and the expected steps must appear in order. Students who understand the mechanism perfectly lose these marks through drawing habit, and the correction takes seconds to make and has to be made repeatedly across weeks before it holds.

That has a practical consequence for how sessions should run. Mechanism work needs to be drawn, marked and redrawn weekly rather than explained thoroughly once. It is a retrieval and habit problem, which means frequency matters more than session length, and it is why a tutor who proposes a single long block to cover organic chemistry has misread the task. Short repeated drawing beats comprehensive explanation every time in this part of the course.

It also happens to be the part of chemistry teaching that benefits most from a shared screen. Every mechanism drawn in a session is kept with the corrections visible, which means a student revising in the spring can reopen their own November attempt and see where the arrow was wrong rather than trying to recall the conversation. That is a material advantage over a photographed whiteboard, and in this specific subject it is the strongest practical argument for the format.

sections.heading: The investigation: criteria by name, and what feasibility means in chemistry
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is 20 per cent of the Chemistry grade, marked against four criteria worth 24 marks between them, inside a 3,000-word limit. A tutor who cannot state those numbers has not supervised one, and the reason that matters is that chemistry investigations fail in a specific place that only experience predicts.

They fail at method feasibility. A student chooses a reaction that is chemically interesting, then discovers the rate is either too fast to time reliably or too slow to observe within a laboratory session, collects a handful of points with no repeats, and writes a long and often well-argued evaluation explaining why the data was poor. That evaluation cannot rescue the data analysis criterion, because there is nothing adequate to analyse. The failure occurred weeks earlier, at the point where the method was chosen.

An experienced supervisor therefore spends the first session on four questions, before any chemistry is selected. Can the quantity be measured with the equipment actually available? Can the variable be changed across a range wide enough to reveal a trend? Can enough repeats be completed in the laboratory time the school allocates? Is there a reasonable accepted value to compare the result against? A research question surviving all four is most of the way to a strong investigation, and one failing any of them will produce data that no amount of careful writing recovers.

The boundary on help is firm and stated in plain words. A tutor explains what each criterion rewards, teaches the chemistry involved, shows how uncertainty propagates through the particular calculation, and gives feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write, draft, redraft or supply any part of it, and will not hand over a research question for adoption. At least one operator ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments; submitting purchased work is a malpractice risk carried by the student rather than the seller.

sections.heading: Coverage, match time and the honest answer about availability
paragraphs: Because this page argues that Higher Level chemistry is a tight market, it would be inconsistent to imply unlimited availability. None of the competitor pages reviewed for this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE families to contact numbers outside the country without saying so, which makes a plain statement worth making.

The position is this. Standard Level chemistry is well covered and matched quickly. Higher Level chemistry is covered, and a specific weekday slot may involve a wait, because this is one of the tightest supply points in the city for the reasons set out earlier. Where a particular slot cannot be filled, the answer given is a stated match time rather than a reassurance, and nothing is taken on account against a match that has not been confirmed. Where no suitable tutor is available, that is said.

There is a second limit worth naming, because families on this island often need several years of support. A tutor who has taught IGCSE chemistry is not automatically suitable for the Diploma, and the reverse applies as well. Where a change of tutor is the right answer at a transition point, saying so is part of the job rather than an admission. Asking about both stages at the outset makes that easier to plan.

The third is about scheduling honestly. School days in the Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim cluster end between about 2:45pm and 3:30pm, the causeway approach and the drive home take thirty to forty-five minutes, and activity programmes run to roughly 6pm. That leaves an early slot around 4:45pm on activity-free days and a dependable one from 6:45pm. A provider offering any hour you like has not thought about the week, and in a subject where the available specialists are few, slot flexibility is the thing most likely to be constrained.

sections.heading: Checking the permit, and what a tutor may not claim
paragraphs: The verification conversation has a second half that is shorter and entirely factual. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years.

Because there is no fee, lacking one is a choice rather than a barrier. Eligibility covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so an amount quoted at you cannot be substantiated.

Two restrictions on who may teach whom are worth knowing. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Separately, an operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

There are also claims nobody should be making. No tutor or platform holds regulator or examination board accreditation for private tutoring in the sense the phrase implies, and describing anyone as approved by a board or an authority is a claim worth challenging. Examiner status should not be asserted where it cannot be evidenced, and should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or unseen paper content. And no grade, score or improvement can honestly be guaranteed, which means any such promise tells you something about the rest of the claims around it.

sections.heading: What this costs, and why the island premium does not help
paragraphs: The rate question matters here mainly because of what it fails to tell a family, so it belongs at the end rather than the beginning.

The published figures, read in October 2026 and belonging to the providers named: in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500. Online qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work. Premium examiner-branded providers at AED 500 to AED 650, with BartyED at AED 650. Budget online options from AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik.

On a single-causeway island the in-home premium is largely a travel premium. A tutor crossing Al Wasl Road at the end of the school day and queueing onto Pearl Jumeira spends thirty to fifty minutes each way, and that is inside the rate. None of it improves a session on electrode potentials, and more importantly, paying it does not make a Higher Level chemist appear. It narrows the field to people who can reach the island, which is the opposite of what a family needing a tight specialism requires.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with mechanisms drawn on a shared screen and kept, and recordings available. The rate carries no travel and the match is made on Higher Level content. Some families will still prefer a person in the room, which is a legitimate preference; the recommendation here is only that the Higher Level checklist is run on whoever is reachable before that preference is paid for.

faqs.answer: Three reasons compound. The International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25 against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum, so most local chemistry experience is A Level rather than Diploma. Demand concentrates at Higher Level because medicine and dentistry pathways require it. And the island is reached by a single causeway, so a visiting tutor must also be free at a fixed hour and willing to make the approach. Those conditions multiply rather than add.

faqs.question: What Higher Level chemistry topics should I ask a tutor about?
faqs.answer: Four that exist only at Higher Level: buffer solutions and weak acid pH, standard electrode potentials, entropy with Gibbs energy, and equilibrium constant calculations. You do not need to follow the chemistry. You need to notice whether the tutor names the characteristic student failure in each without being prompted, such as applying the strong-acid method to a weak acid, or sign errors when half cells are combined. Somebody who has taught the course answers immediately and specifically.

faqs.question: What is the single best question to test a Diploma chemistry tutor?
faqs.answer: Ask about curly arrow convention in organic mechanisms. The answer you want concerns where an arrow starts and where it points: from a bond or a lone pair rather than from an atom, towards where the new bond forms, with charges shown on intermediates. Anyone who has marked Diploma chemistry says this immediately, because they have written it on scripts hundreds of times. A capable chemist who has not taught the course will explain the mechanism beautifully and not mention the convention.

faqs.question: Can an A Level chemistry tutor teach the IB Diploma course adequately?
faqs.answer: They will teach the chemistry competently and may miss how it is assessed, which is where the marks are. The content overlaps substantially; the assessment does not. Diploma Chemistry has a specific presentation of working in electrochemistry, a particular organic drawing convention, and an investigation marked against four named criteria within a 3,000-word limit. A good A Level chemist who has read the Diploma guide can get there; one who assumes the courses are interchangeable will not, and the gap shows up at the first draft.

faqs.question: Why does Higher Level chemistry feel harder in the second Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Because three new calculation procedures arrive together, each sitting on top of Standard Level material: buffers and weak acid pH, standard electrode potentials, and entropy with Gibbs energy. The risk is not misunderstanding but confusion between methods, since the question has to be read for which procedure it calls for. It also compounds: every Higher Level extension assumes fluency with the Standard Level work underneath, so a shaky equilibrium foundation makes electrode potentials two problems rather than one.

faqs.question: How should organic chemistry sessions be structured?
faqs.answer: Short, frequent and drawn rather than long and explained. Organic chemistry at Higher Level is a retrieval and habit problem: which reagent, which conditions, which product, which mechanism, drawn to convention. A student who draws a nucleophilic substitution weekly for eight weeks can draw it under exam conditions; one who has it explained thoroughly twice cannot. A tutor proposing a single long block to cover organic chemistry has misread the task, and frequency matters more than session length here.

faqs.question: What are the four chemistry investigation criteria and the word limit?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, worth 24 marks between them and 20 per cent of the grade, within a 3,000-word limit. A tutor who cannot produce those numbers has not supervised one. The reason it matters is that chemistry investigations fail at a specific point: the reaction chosen cannot be measured well enough in a school laboratory, so the data analysis criterion has nothing adequate to work with regardless of how well the piece is written.

faqs.question: How is a chemistry research question tested for feasibility?
faqs.answer: With four questions asked before any chemistry is chosen. Can the quantity be measured using equipment actually available at the school? Can the independent variable be varied across a range wide enough to show a trend? Can enough repeats be completed within the laboratory time allocated? Is there a reasonable accepted value to compare the result against? A question surviving all four is most of the way to a strong investigation. One failing any of them produces data that careful writing cannot rescue.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have a chemistry tutor who can come to the island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with mechanisms drawn on a shared screen and kept, and recordings available. For this subject the reasoning is supply rather than preference: requiring somebody to cross the causeway on a weekday afternoon removes most of the few people who have taught Higher Level chemistry.

faqs.question: Will paying a higher rate get us a Higher Level chemistry specialist?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, which is the uncomfortable part. Published online rates for a qualified subject tutor run AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase AED 270, while in-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel. Nothing in that range signals whether a person has taught Higher Level chemistry, because general and specialist chemists quote similar figures. On an island, the in-home premium also narrows the field rather than widening it, since it adds a geographic condition.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match a Higher Level chemistry tutor here?
faqs.answer: Usually quickly for the subject, with a possible wait for a specific weekday slot, because this is one of the tightest supply points in the Dubai market. Where a particular slot cannot be filled we give a stated match time rather than a reassurance, and nothing is taken on account against a match that has not been confirmed. Where no suitable tutor is free, that is said plainly rather than filled with a capable A Level chemist at a Diploma rate.

faqs.question: My child needs Chemistry HL for medicine. Does that change the plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the margin rather than the method, and it raises the cost of a mismatch. Students applying for medicine or dentistry from Dubai schools generally need Chemistry at Higher Level, and for most of them the deciding marks sit in the organic and recall half of the syllabus rather than in the calculations. That argues for protecting weekly mechanism work rather than adding calculation hours. No tutor can promise a grade or an admission outcome, and nobody honest will offer to.

faqs.question: Should a tutor claim to be accredited by an examination board or a regulator?
faqs.answer: No, and the claim is worth challenging wherever it appears. No private tutor or tutoring platform holds regulator or examination board accreditation in the sense that phrase implies. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific thing issued to training institutes with premises, obtained with initial approval first and renewed annually. Examiner status should not be asserted without evidence, and should never be used to suggest access to marking, grade boundaries or unseen paper content.

faqs.question: What times work for a chemistry session for an island family?
faqs.answer: An early slot around 4:45pm on activity-free days, or a dependable one from 6:45pm after food. School in this cluster ends between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, the Al Wasl Road crossing plus the causeway queue takes thirty to forty-five minutes, and activity programmes run to about 6pm. In a subject where the available specialists are few, slot flexibility is the thing most likely to be constrained, so a provider offering any hour you like has probably not checked availability.

If not, a travel premium is narrowing your options rather than widening them. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a free trial lesson first.

intro.heading: A chemistry grade is doing more work than a chemistry grade
paragraphs: Chemistry occupies an unusual position in a Diploma. Unlike most subjects, where a grade is one of six contributing to a total, chemistry frequently functions as a condition: medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary science and chemical engineering commonly require it, often at Higher Level and often with a stated minimum grade. That turns a subject into a gate, and it changes how a family should think about the hours they buy.

The practical consequence is that the margin matters more than the average. For a student whose other five subjects are comfortable, a chemistry grade one point below a condition closes a route that everything else was aimed at. That is a different risk profile from a subject where a weaker grade simply reduces a total, and it justifies attention earlier in the course than families usually give it.

It also makes the entry requirements themselves part of the work. The routes that gate on chemistry do not all gate in the same way: some specify Higher Level, some accept Standard, some require a second science, and the minimum grade varies by country and institution and changes between cycles. None of that should be taken from a tutoring page, including this one. It should be read from each university's own published course page, in Year 11.

Remraam shapes the delivery rather than the stakes. It is a low-rise apartment community in Dubailand, built as the Al Thamam and Al Ramth clusters with its own park and retail, reached from Al Qudra Road and Emirates Road. South View School sits close by and takes students through Year 11, so Diploma students have generally moved outward to Dubai Hills, Al Barsha South or The Sustainable City, which lengthens the afternoon considerably.

The second comparison families in this corridor make, usually at the same time as choosing a school, is between Diploma chemistry and A Level chemistry. Several schools within reach of Remraam run A Levels after Year 11 while others run the Diploma, so the two decisions arrive bundled and the subject question gets obscured by the school question. Separating them is worth doing explicitly, because the right answer depends on how a particular student works rather than on which school is more convenient.

Both comparisons are easier once chemistry is seen as four distinct clusters rather than one syllabus: notation that runs through everything, calculation work that fails for two different reasons, organic mechanisms, and the option topic that only the school can tell you. Each fails in a characteristic way and each responds to a different kind of work on a different timescale, and treating them as one body of content is the main reason revision in this subject so often produces no visible change.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. The practical belongs to the school and its laboratory, which this page states rather than skirts, and what a session does is prepare the design and interrogate the write-up. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and nothing here should be read as an offer to arrive at a Remraam address.

sections.heading: Chemistry as a condition rather than a grade
paragraphs: Most Diploma subjects contribute to a total. Chemistry, for a student aiming at a health-science or chemical-engineering route, does something different: it functions as a condition that either is or is not met. That asymmetry is worth naming because it changes how risk should be managed across a two-year course.

In a totals model, a weak subject can be offset by a strong one. In a conditions model it cannot. A student with five comfortable subjects and a chemistry grade one point below a stated requirement has not reduced their total; they have closed the route the whole timetable was built around. Families discover this in the spring of Year 13 and the discovery is unrecoverable, which is why the subject deserves disproportionate attention from the first term.

The practical response is not more hours. It is earlier hours and a clearer read of where the grade is actually coming from. Chemistry splits cleanly into mechanical losses, which are fast to repair, and the Higher Level extension content, which needs proper teaching over weeks. A student who clears the mechanical losses in Year 12 arrives at Year 13 with the extension content as the only remaining problem, which is a manageable position.

The other half of the response is administrative and free: reading what the intended routes actually publish. Some specify Higher Level chemistry, some accept Standard, some require a second science, and minimum grades differ by country and institution and move between cycles. That list belongs on paper in Year 11, assembled with the school's careers office from each university's own course page.

sections.heading: Routes that gate on chemistry, compared
paragraphs: The routes requiring chemistry do not require it in the same way, and the differences matter when a combination is being assembled. Medicine and dentistry commonly want chemistry plus a second science, frequently biology, often at Higher Level and with a stated minimum. Pharmacy usually names chemistry specifically. Veterinary science typically wants chemistry and biology together. Chemical engineering wants chemistry with mathematics, and often physics alongside.

Beyond the subject list, three further conditions recur and students miss them. Some courses state a minimum total points score as well as subject grades. Some require admissions tests sat in the autumn of the final year, which collide with coursework and mocks. And some set English language requirements separately, which for a student educated in English is usually satisfied by the Diploma itself but should still be checked rather than assumed.

For UAE universities there is an additional layer, which is Ministry of Education equivalency. The British-track rule is published and specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the IB, no points threshold should be taken from any tutoring page without being read on the Ministry's own site.

sections.heading: Diploma Chemistry Higher Level against A Level Chemistry
paragraphs: Both are accepted for medicine and engineering applications worldwide, so the comparison is about fit rather than standing. The structural difference is familiar: the Diploma asks for six subjects plus a core, A Levels for three or four studied further, and chemistry behaves differently inside those two shapes.

A Level chemistry typically goes deeper in individual topics, with organic chemistry in particular developed further than at Diploma Higher Level. Diploma chemistry covers comparable ground with slightly less depth per topic and distributes a steady calculation load across the course rather than concentrating it. For a student who prefers depth over breadth, that is an argument for A Levels; for one who likes several things at once, the reverse.

The internal element differs too. Diploma chemistry carries a marked investigation worth roughly a fifth of the subject grade, assessed on design, analysis and evaluation against published criteria. A Level chemistry usually involves a practical endorsement assessed differently and contributing differently. A Diploma student therefore has a coursework deadline inside the course that an A Level student largely does not, which is both a risk and an opportunity.

The parallel-deadline point is the one that decides most cases. A Diploma chemistry student is also managing five other subjects, each with its own internal component, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. A student who juggles badly finds that harder than the chemistry itself, and choosing the Diploma for its reputation while being that kind of student is a predictable route to underperformance.

sections.heading: The four content clusters and how each is examined
paragraphs: Chemistry is easier to plan once it is seen as four clusters rather than a long syllabus, because each cluster fails in a characteristic way and each responds to a different kind of work. Treating the subject as one undifferentiated body of content is why revision often produces no visible change.

The notation cluster runs through everything: balanced equations, state symbols, units, significant figures and, in organic chemistry, arrow direction. These are mechanical, which means they are assessed constantly and repaired quickly. Ten minutes of drilling in every session, regardless of the topic being taught, closes most of them inside a month and recovers marks the student had already earned conceptually.

The calculation cluster covers moles, energetics, equilibrium and kinetics, and fails for two different reasons that must be separated. Sign conventions and Hess cycle direction cause errors that look like carelessness and are actually convention problems, fixable with short context-free exercises. Logarithms and rearrangement cause errors that are mathematical, and no amount of chemistry teaching repairs them.

The mechanism cluster is organic chemistry, where the failure is memorising reactions as pairs of starting material and product rather than learning mechanisms. The remedy is grouping by mechanism type and drilling arrows under time, because the recall a paper demands is partly motor. The fourth cluster is the option, which only the school can tell you, and which no revision resource bought blind can be trusted to cover.

The practical use of the four-cluster view is sequencing. Notation and conventions first, because they are cheap and fast. Mathematical repair next, where a script shows it. Mechanisms after that, since they need weeks of timed drilling. And the option confirmed before any of it, because a plan aimed at the wrong option wastes whatever else it gets right.

sections.heading: What a 5 and a 6 look like in marked work
paragraphs: For a gated route the difference between a 5 and a 6 is often the difference between an offer and no offer, so it is worth describing what separates them in practice. It is rarely a body of content that one student has and the other lacks. It is a set of small, repeated behaviours visible across a script.

The 5 produces a correct calculation and leaves the equation unbalanced. It draws a plausible mechanism with an arrow starting from a positive centre. It answers an evaluate question with two advantages and no judgement. It gets the right number and omits the unit, or carries significant figures inconsistently. Each of those costs one mark, and across a paper they total more than any single topic the student has not learned.

The 6 does the same chemistry and does not leak. Equations balance with state symbols where the scheme requires them. Arrows start from lone pairs or bonds. Evaluate questions end with a judgement. Units and significant figures are consistent. The difference reads as care and is actually habit, which is why it responds to drilling rather than to explanation.

Above that, the gap to a 7 does usually involve content: the Higher Level extensions in equilibrium, energetics and organic chemistry handled securely under time. That is a longer piece of work and needs teaching rather than repair. The useful consequence for a family on a gated route is that the cheaper intervention comes first, because clearing the leaks often moves a grade on its own.

sections.heading: The option, the school and the laboratory
paragraphs: Three facts about chemistry depend entirely on the school, and all three change what a tutoring plan should contain. The first is the option topic, chosen by the department, which means two Diploma chemistry students in Dubai can sit the same core and different option questions. A revision guide bought online may cover material the student will never be examined on, and a group class drawn from several schools cannot teach any single option.

The second is the practical programme, which constrains the investigation. A research question requiring apparatus the department does not hold is a dead end regardless of its quality, and a reaction too fast or too slow to time reliably with school equipment cannot be rescued by effort. Asking for the practical calendar and a realistic list of available apparatus early is the cheapest planning available in the subject.

The third is the internal deadline structure. Draft dates and submission dates are set internally, so they differ between the schools students from this corridor attend and cannot be looked up in a general guide. A family that asks for them in writing at the start of Year 12 avoids most of the trouble the investigation causes.

What online tutoring can and cannot do follows from the second of those. It cannot run an experiment, and this page says so rather than implying otherwise. It can interrogate the research question before the laboratory and examine the data, the graph choice, the uncertainty propagation and the evaluation afterwards, which is where most of the criterion marks sit.

sections.heading: Remraam practicalities and thin Higher Level supply
paragraphs: Remraam is comparatively well served at IGCSE level and not at Diploma level, and the asymmetry is worth understanding before a family starts searching. South View School sits close to the community and takes students through Year 11, so the IGCSE years involve a short run. There is no IB provision beside the community, so Diploma students travel to Dubai Hills, Al Barsha South or The Sustainable City.

That longer afternoon matters for scheduling. A Diploma student home towards five has a different evening from the Year 11 version of themselves, and a session either sits early and short or later and longer. Because the lesson arrives over live video, the slot can move within the evening at no cost, which is the practical argument for the format quite apart from the subject-matching one.

On supply, Higher Level chemistry is among the thinnest specialisms in any tutoring market. IB programmes accounted for 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25 against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum, and within Dubailand most schools run IGCSE and A Levels, so the local pool is thinner still. The tutors advertising along this corridor, based around Dubai Investment Park, Dubai Sports City and Motor City, sensibly cover several sciences at IGCSE level.

Removing the distance filter changes the pool entirely, and for a gated route that is not a marginal improvement. The honest limit is that some combinations stay thin everywhere, including Higher Level chemistry with a less common option, and where that applies a family should be told with a timescale rather than matched with a generalist.

sections.heading: What chemistry tuition costs, and when to buy it
paragraphs: For a gated route the timing question matters as much as the rate. The efficient sequence is a short conditions conversation in Year 11, notation repair through Year 12 so the leaks are closed before the extensions arrive, a block on the Higher Level extensions when they are taught, and a final-stretch block in Year 13. That is less total spending than a continuous weekly hour across two years and better aimed.

Chemistry sits at the specialist end of the published bands, because credible Higher Level coverage is scarce. Named IB and IGCSE specialists publish roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai cost table giving AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 500 to 650, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Below that, a qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52, which suits routine practice rather than Higher Level extension teaching. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the price.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with packages seen including AED 799 for eight online sessions. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. These are market figures with their sources named, not IB Gram prices.

sections.heading: Permits, boundaries and the questions to ask
paragraphs: The investigation is assessed and must be the student's own, authenticated by the teacher. A tutor may teach the chemistry, explain what each criterion rewards, say that a reaction is too fast to time reliably or that a concentration range will not produce a measurable difference, work uncertainty propagation through the student's own data, and mark a draft the student wrote against the published descriptors. A tutor may not draft, rewrite, edit to completion, supply text, or provide data the student did not collect.

That last prohibition deserves emphasis in chemistry specifically, because a failed experiment near a deadline creates exactly the pressure under which the offer arrives. Failed experiments honestly evaluated score better than families expect, and the right response is to analyse what exists and name the systematic error rather than to obtain numbers from elsewhere. One provider in this market sells completed internal assessments outright.

On the legal side, an individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule.

A business with premises needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit instead, renewed annually. IB Gram has no UAE premises, holds no such permit, and does not attach a regulator's name to its tutors. The questions worth asking a chemistry tutor are narrow: which level and option, how many cohorts, how do you teach uncertainty propagation, and what will you refuse to do with a draft.
