dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-tecom.programmesIntro: Four stages matter for a chemistry plan, and the right work differs sharply between them.

programmes.name: Diploma Chemistry, Year One
programmes.description: Where the calculation spine is either built or not. Moles, concentration, titration arithmetic, empirical formula, limiting reagents and the start of energetics. A student who leaves DP1 without automatic mole handling will struggle through every later topic, because each one assumes it. This is the cheapest and most important chemistry year to get right.
programmes.countryNote: Barsha Heights students arrive into DP1 from campuses across Al Barsha, Al Barsha South and Al Sufouh, on either an IGCSE or a Middle Years route. IGCSE students usually arrive with decent quantitative habits and little experience of designing an investigation; Middle Years students arrive with the opposite profile.

programmes.name: Diploma Chemistry, Year Two
programmes.description: Equilibrium, kinetics, acids and bases, electrochemistry and organic chemistry, with the Scientific Investigation deadline underneath. The content is cumulative and the deadlines collide, which is why a plan for this year is mostly a sequencing problem rather than a question of how many hours.
programmes.countryNote: Internal school deadlines for the investigation arrive well before anything the International Baccalaureate sets, and in Dubai they commonly land in the same weeks as other subjects' internal assessments. The Diploma coordinator publishes them, and any tutoring plan should be built backwards from that list.

programmes.name: The Scientific Investigation
programmes.description: Twenty per cent of the grade, marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. In chemistry the research design criterion is the hardest to satisfy, because a question has to be measurable with school apparatus, chemically interesting enough to produce a trend, and safe enough for a school laboratory to permit.
programmes.countryNote: That three-way constraint is why so many chemistry investigations end up being rate-of-reaction studies on the same handful of systems. A better question is usually available, and finding it is a conversation worth having before any apparatus is booked rather than after a first attempt fails.

programmes.name: What Chemistry Is Required For
programmes.description: Higher Level chemistry is the most commonly specified science requirement for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering, and the grade rather than the experience is what an application uses. For many students in Dubai this is the single most consequential subject on their timetable, which is worth knowing before deciding how to prioritise an evening.
programmes.countryNote: Requirements are set by each institution and vary. Most medical programmes in the United Kingdom specify chemistry at Higher Level, often with a minimum grade; UAE institutions including Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, the American University of Sharjah and Zayed University each publish their own, and the programme page is the authority rather than any tutoring provider.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-tecom.subjectsIntro: Diploma chemistry breaks into areas that fail in very specific ways. These are the ones Barsha Heights students most often need, with the error that actually costs the marks.

subjects.name: Stoichiometric relationships
subjects.description: Moles, molar mass, concentration, gas volumes and limiting reagents. The foundation of everything else in the subject. Students who convert correctly but slowly become students who run out of time in Paper 2, and students who guess which reactant is limiting lose the whole question rather than part of it.

subjects.name: Titration arithmetic
subjects.description: Concentration from titre volume, back titrations and dilution factors. Appears in papers and in nearly every practical write-up. Marks go on dilution factors forgotten and on significant figures carried wrongly through a multi-step calculation, both of which are habits rather than concepts.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, calorimetry, Hess cycles and bond enthalpies, with entropy and Gibbs energy at Higher Level. Sign conventions are the standing error: a correct magnitude with the wrong sign earns little, and students who learn exothermic as a word rather than as a negative enthalpy change make it repeatedly.

subjects.name: Chemical kinetics
subjects.description: Rate measurement, collision theory and, at Higher Level, rate expressions, orders of reaction and the Arrhenius relationship. Determining order from data is the Higher Level separator, and students report a gradient without saying what it means, which is the error the mark scheme is built to catch.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.description: Le Chatelier's principle qualitatively, and at Higher Level the equilibrium constant with its calculations. Students explain a shift by restating the principle rather than reasoning through it, and they treat the constant as a number to compute rather than a quantity whose magnitude means something about position.

subjects.name: Acids and bases
subjects.description: pH, strong and weak behaviour, and at Higher Level buffers, titration curves and the dissociation constants. The densest calculation area in the whole subject and the one where a weak mole foundation finally becomes unmanageable. Worth attacking only once the earlier spine is secure.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half-equations, electrolysis and, at Higher Level, cell potentials and the Gibbs energy link. Half-equations that do not balance for charge as well as atoms are the recurring loss, and students routinely omit electrons entirely and still expect the equation to be accepted.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.description: Homologous series, reaction types and, at Higher Level, nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and the rest drawn with curly arrows. The arrows carry marks: they must start at a lone pair or a bond and end where the electrons go. This is the clearest case on the course for working on a shared drawing surface.

subjects.name: Structure, bonding and periodicity
subjects.description: Models of bonding, intermolecular forces, periodic trends and, at Higher Level, more depth on orbitals and transition metals. Marks go on explanations that name a trend rather than accounting for it through nuclear charge, shielding and atomic radius, which is a command-term problem.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and data processing
subjects.levels: SL and HL, central to the investigation
subjects.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, significant figures and error bars. Examined in Paper 1B and worth a large share of the investigation's data analysis criterion. Compact enough to teach in two or three sessions and worth a disproportionate number of marks.

subjects.name: Using the data booklet
subjects.description: A data booklet is provided in the examination, which changes what is worth memorising and what is worth practising finding quickly. Students lose time hunting for a value they could have located in seconds, and occasionally lose marks by using the wrong table. Deliberate practice with it is cheap and rarely done.

subjects.name: Higher Level extension content
subjects.description: Additional depth within each theme rather than a separate unit, with the heaviest load in equilibrium, acids and bases, electrochemistry and organic mechanisms. Higher Level grades are decided here, so a Higher Level student buying help with shared material is paying for the wrong half of their course.

sections.heading: The gap between the laboratory and the write-up
paragraphs: This is the specific thing a chemistry tutor in this community is usually solving, and it is worth describing precisely because it is not a teaching failure. Laboratory time in a Dubai school is timetabled, finite and shared with a class. The practical is performed under supervision, with apparatus that has been booked and a method that has been handed out. Then the raw data go home, and everything that carries marks happens there: processing, uncertainty, graphing, the conclusion and the evaluation.

In Barsha Heights the home end of that process is compressed. There is no large campus in the community, so students are bussed outward and return on multi-stop routes between a quarter past five and six. A write-up requiring uncertainty propagation and a reasoned conclusion is not work that goes well at half past eight after a full day and an hour in a vehicle. What tends to happen instead is that the processing gets done quickly, the uncertainty gets estimated rather than calculated, and the conclusion restates what the textbook says should have happened.

That pattern costs marks in two separate places, which is what makes it expensive. It costs marks in the school's own internal assessment of practical work, and it costs marks in Paper 1B, the data-based section of the examination paper, because Paper 1B tests exactly those skills. A student who never learns to propagate uncertainty properly will meet the same weakness in an examination hall where no one is available to help.

The useful intervention is therefore not more chemistry teaching. It is a session that takes the student's own raw results and goes through the processing properly once, then twice, until the student can do it unaided. Three or four of those sessions across DP1 generally settles the skill for the rest of the course, and it is the cheapest piece of chemistry support available because it pays into two components at once.

sections.heading: The calculation spine, and why order matters more than topics
paragraphs: Chemistry is the Diploma science with the longest unbroken sequence of dependent calculations, and that is the single most useful structural fact for planning tutoring. Most subjects can be attacked topic by topic in any order. Chemistry cannot, because each calculation type assumes the previous one is automatic. A student who is hesitant with moles will fail at buffers, and buffer teaching will not fix it.

The spine runs in a specific order. Moles and molar mass. Concentration and dilution. Titration arithmetic, including back titrations and dilution factors. Limiting reagents and percentage yield. Enthalpy changes through calorimetry and Hess cycles. Rate expressions and orders of reaction at Higher Level. Equilibrium constants. pH, weak acid dissociation and buffers. Cell potentials. Every one of those uses the output of an earlier step as its input.

The practical consequence for a family is that a diagnosis has to find the earliest broken step rather than the most recently taught topic. Students almost always present with the latest thing: buffers are hard, equilibrium calculations do not work. The tutor's job in the first session is to walk back down the spine until the arithmetic becomes fluent, and then start teaching from there. That is often three topics earlier than the complaint, and it is why the first session should be a diagnostic rather than a lesson on the stated problem.

It also explains a common and expensive mistake. A family buys five sessions on acids and bases because that is where the test went badly. The sessions are competently taught and the next test goes badly too, because the student was converting concentrations slowly and unreliably the whole time. Five sessions on mole fluency would have fixed both. Finding the earliest broken step is the whole value of a diagnostic in this subject.

sections.heading: What each chemistry component rewards
paragraphs: Diploma chemistry is assessed through Paper 1, worth 36% and divided into Paper 1A multiple choice and Paper 1B data-based questions, through Paper 2 at 44%, and through the Scientific Investigation at 20%. Higher Level adds extension content within each theme rather than a separate paper. Confirm these against the current subject guide with your school's Diploma coordinator, since the International Baccalaureate revises its guides.

The table below is organised around what each component actually rewards rather than around its weighting alone, because that is the information that decides how an hour is spent. Paper 1A rewards recognition of the misconceptions the syllabus builds its distractors from, which is coachable from past papers at low cost. Paper 1B rewards uncertainty, graphing and method evaluation, which is the same skill set as the investigation and therefore double value. Paper 2 rewards worked calculation and explanation with the reasoning visible.

One chemistry-specific point changes revision strategy and is often missed. A data booklet is provided in the examination. That means certain values do not need memorising, and that locating the right table quickly is itself a skill. Students lose minutes hunting for a constant they could have found in seconds, and occasionally lose marks by reading from the wrong table. Twenty minutes of deliberate practice with the booklet is among the cheapest marks on the course.

The other chemistry-specific point is drawing. Organic mechanisms carry marks in the arrows, not only in the products. An arrow has to start at a lone pair or a bond and end where the electrons go, and a mechanism with the right products and misplaced arrows scores poorly. That is a drawing discipline, and it is the reason a shared digital surface, where tutor and student can both draw on the same structure, is a genuine advantage rather than a substitute for paper.

sections.heading: Designing a chemistry investigation that can actually work
paragraphs: The research design criterion carries six of the investigation's 24 marks and is decided before any data exist, which makes it the highest-leverage conversation in the component. In chemistry it is also harder to satisfy than in physics or biology, because a research question has to clear three constraints at once: it must be measurable with school apparatus, chemically interesting enough to produce a trend worth analysing, and safe enough for a school laboratory to permit.

Most failed chemistry investigations fail on one of those three, and they fail before data collection rather than during analysis. A question that cannot be measured precisely enough produces a flat result with uncertainty bars larger than the effect. A question that is safe and measurable but chemically trivial produces a trend nobody can analyse interestingly. A question that is interesting and measurable may involve a reagent the school will not issue to a student. All three are foreseeable in a single conversation.

That is why a design session held before apparatus is booked is worth more than three sessions of rescue afterwards. The session tests the question against each constraint, names the independent and dependent variables and the controls, and predicts the expected trend. Predicting the trend is the step students skip and the one that matters most, because if the expected effect is smaller than the achievable precision, the investigation is already finished and nobody has noticed.

On the limits of what a tutor may do here: the design must be the student's. A tutor may explain the criteria, ask whether a variable is genuinely controlled, point out that a reagent is unlikely to be available, and question whether an expected trend exceeds the measurement precision. A tutor may not choose the research question, design the method, process the data or write any part of the submission. The student and the school declare the work authentic, and a breach is a malpractice finding against your child.

sections.heading: Organic mechanisms and why the drawing surface matters
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is where able Diploma students most often lose marks they believe they have earned, and the reason is almost always the arrows. A mechanism question is marked on the electron movement, not only on the final products. An arrow must begin at a lone pair or at a bond and must end where those electrons actually go. A student who draws the right products with arrows starting from an atom rather than from its lone pair has drawn something chemically wrong, and the mark scheme treats it that way.

That is a drawing discipline rather than a memory problem, and it is taught by drawing. Explaining a mechanism verbally produces a student who can recite it and cannot draw it. The teaching that works is the student drawing, the tutor correcting stroke by stroke, and the student drawing it again. Repeated across a handful of mechanisms, the discipline generalises, and it generalises because the rules about where arrows start and end are the same in every mechanism on the course.

It also helps to group the content by mechanism rather than by functional group, which is not how most textbooks arrange it. Nucleophilic substitution behaves the same way whether the substrate is a halogenoalkane in one question or another in the next. Electrophilic addition follows one pattern across alkenes. A student who has learned twelve reactions as twelve separate facts has a memory problem; a student who has learned four mechanisms has a system.

This is the clearest case on the whole chemistry course for the shared digital surface an online session provides. Two people drawing on the same structure, each able to add an arrow, is practically better than two people with one pen reaching across a single exercise book. We mention it because families reasonably assume that practical-looking subjects suffer online, and for mechanism work the opposite is true.

sections.heading: What chemistry support costs, and what a good trial and a good invoice contain
paragraphs: Two checks protect a family in this market more than any review page: what the free trial actually produces, and what the invoice actually says. Both are checkable before money moves, and both are where the difference between a specialist and a general tutor becomes visible. Before that, here is the published market, every figure credited to the provider that published it and read in October 2026, none of it IB Gram's price list.

Budget online and university-student tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International Baccalaureate from AED 200. Specialists across IB, IGCSE and A Level run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors, travel included.

A good trial session, whoever provides it, produces a written output rather than a feeling. It should name the earliest broken step on the calculation spine rather than the most recently taught topic, because in chemistry those are usually different. It should say how many sessions the fix realistically needs. And it should be spent with the student working rather than watching, because a diagnosis made from a conversation is a guess. If a trial produces only reassurance, you have learned something about the provider.

A good invoice states the session length, the rate for that length rather than an hourly rate applied to a different duration, and the VAT position. A ninety-minute session billed at an hourly rate is one and a half times the quoted figure, and a price with no stated tax treatment is not a price. Ask for all three in writing before the first paid session. Every provider who answers plainly has made the comparison with others easier, which is the point.

sections.heading: Chemistry for medicine, and what that means for priorities
paragraphs: A large proportion of Dubai Diploma students taking Higher Level chemistry are taking it because a medical, dental, pharmacy or chemical engineering application requires it. That is worth naming because it changes how a family should prioritise a crowded evening. If one subject on the timetable is the gate for the whole application, it is reasonable for it to get the protected hour rather than the leftover one.

The requirements themselves belong to the institutions and not to us. Most medical programmes in the United Kingdom specify chemistry at Higher Level, frequently with a stated minimum grade and often alongside a second science or mathematics. UAE institutions, including Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, the American University of Sharjah and Zayed University, publish their own admissions requirements, as do universities elsewhere. The published programme page is the authority, and no tutoring provider should be substituting a general claim for it.

There is a second, quieter requirement that catches Dubai families later, which is Ministry of Education equivalency for students who go on to apply to UAE universities. The sourced British-track rule, for students on that path, is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. No International Baccalaureate points threshold has been verified from an official source, so none is published here.

Two cautions belong with that. IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation, does not guarantee any outcome in it, and nothing here should be read as our doing it on your behalf: the process belongs to the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority, and you should verify the current rules with them. And nobody, including us, should suggest that tutoring is required for university admission or for equivalency. It is not, and a claim that it is would be a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Honesty boundaries, copyright and what we decline
paragraphs: Chemistry is one of the subjects where the market around Dubai crosses lines, because write-ups and investigations are discrete documents that somebody could simply produce. Research for this project found a provider selling completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price. That is not tutoring; it is an academic-integrity breach whose malpractice consequences fall on the student rather than the seller.

The legitimate boundary is easy to apply. A tutor may teach content, explain the assessment criteria, work through a calculation method, question whether a variable is controlled, check whether uncertainty has been handled correctly, ask whether a conclusion follows from the data, mark the student's own draft, and correct a mechanism the student has drawn. A workable test is whether your child's own teacher could do the same thing openly in a lesson.

A tutor may not design the investigation, process the raw data on the student's behalf, write any section of a write-up or report, dictate answers for transcription, or edit prose until the words are no longer the student's. Nor may anybody legitimately distribute International Baccalaureate subject guides, past papers, mark schemes, data booklets or grade-boundary documents as downloads, because those are the IB's copyright. We reference them, link to the official source and work from them inside a session.

On status: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified or licensed by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, and claims none of those relationships. We run no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Private tutoring here is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule.

sections.heading: Booking, timing and the limits we state first
paragraphs: Send the level, the component causing the problem, and either a marked paper or a recent write-up with its raw data. The write-up is often the more useful document in chemistry, because it shows whether the uncertainty was propagated or estimated and whether the conclusion was argued or asserted, neither of which a marked multiple-choice section reveals. The first session is free and is spent on that material with the student working.

You then receive a short written note naming the earliest broken step on the calculation spine, which is frequently several topics earlier than the complaint, together with a realistic session estimate. We do not quote an hour count before that, because a figure produced before anybody has seen the evidence is invented. If the honest answer is four sessions on mole fluency rather than a term on acids and bases, the note will say so.

Scheduling follows the bus. Barsha Heights students return on multi-stop routes between a quarter past five and six, so the workable slots are 17:30 and 18:00, and those are the most heavily demanded tutoring hours in the Dubai year with demand peaking in the second term. Securing one in term one costs nothing extra. Investigation and write-up work often moves to weekend mornings, which suits sustained processing better than a weekday evening after a commute.

Two limits worth knowing. Higher Level chemistry specialists for a specific weekend hour are among the thinner combinations we staff, and we will give you a date rather than take a booking and hope. And if no UAE-based tutor is free for your combination, we will say whether a tutor based elsewhere can cover your hour in Gulf Standard Time, and you may decline. IB Gram runs no home visits in Dubai; every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar slots for families who want them there.

faqs.question: Why does my child struggle with chemistry write-ups rather than lessons?
faqs.answer: Because the two happen in different places. Laboratory time in a Dubai school is timetabled, finite and shared with a class, so the practical is supervised and the processing is not. The raw data go home, and the uncertainty, graphing, conclusion and evaluation get done in an evening that in Barsha Heights starts near six because the bus collects from several communities first. The lesson was probably fine. What is missing is the unsupervised half, which happens to be the half that carries the marks.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topic should we actually start with?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly an earlier one than the topic that went badly. Chemistry has the longest chain of dependent calculations of the three Diploma sciences, running from moles and concentration through titration arithmetic and limiting reagents to energetics, equilibrium, buffers and cell potentials, with each step assuming the previous one is automatic. A student failing at buffers is usually converting concentrations slowly and unreliably. Five sessions on buffers will be competently taught and will not help, which is why the first session has to be a diagnostic.

faqs.question: What does Paper 2 reward in IB chemistry?
faqs.answer: Worked calculation and explanation with the reasoning visible. It carries 44% of the grade, the largest single component, and marks are distributed through the steps rather than sitting on the final answer, so a correct result with no working forfeits most of them. Explanations are judged against command terms: a question asking you to explain a periodic trend wants nuclear charge, shielding and atomic radius, not a restatement of the trend. Confirm the weightings against the current subject guide with your Diploma coordinator.

faqs.question: How do organic mechanism marks actually work?
faqs.answer: They sit in the arrows. An arrow must begin at a lone pair or at a bond and must end where those electrons go, and a mechanism with correct products but misplaced arrows is chemically wrong and marked as such. This is a drawing discipline rather than a memory exercise, which means it is taught by the student drawing and the tutor correcting stroke by stroke. Grouping the content by mechanism rather than by functional group also helps: four mechanisms is a system, twelve reactions is a memory problem.

faqs.question: Can organic chemistry really be taught over video?
faqs.answer: Better than on paper, for mechanisms specifically. The work requires two people drawing on the same structure, each adding and correcting arrows, which a shared digital surface does well and a single exercise book with one pen does badly. We mention it because families reasonably assume that practical-looking subjects suffer online. For mechanism work the opposite holds, and for calculation work the ability to keep a worked example on screen while the student attempts the next one is a genuine advantage.

faqs.question: What makes a good chemistry investigation question?
faqs.answer: One that clears three constraints at once: measurable with school apparatus, chemically interesting enough to produce a trend worth analysing, and safe enough for the school to permit. Most failed chemistry investigations fail on one of those before data collection rather than during analysis. The step students skip is predicting the expected trend and comparing it to the achievable precision. If the effect is smaller than the measurement uncertainty, the investigation is finished before it starts and nobody has noticed yet.

faqs.question: How much of the chemistry grade is the investigation worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Research design is fixed before any data exist, which is why a single design conversation held before apparatus is booked saves more time than any amount of rescue work afterwards. The criteria being equal in weight also means evaluation cannot be a closing paragraph, and in most first drafts we read, that is exactly what it is.

faqs.question: Does the data booklet change how my child should revise?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in a way most students never think about. A data booklet is provided in the examination, so certain values do not need memorising and locating the right table quickly becomes a skill in itself. Students lose minutes hunting for a constant they could have found in seconds, and occasionally lose marks by reading from the wrong table altogether. Twenty minutes of deliberate practice with the booklet, done once, is among the cheapest marks available anywhere on the course.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level chemistry add?
faqs.answer: Additional depth within each theme rather than a separate paper, with the heaviest extension load in equilibrium, acids and bases, electrochemistry and organic mechanisms. The component weightings stay the same. The practical consequence is that Higher Level grades are decided in the extension content, so a Higher Level student paying for help with the shared material is paying for the wrong half of their course. Secure the shared content cheaply first, then buy specialist help for the extension depth.

faqs.answer: Most medical programmes in the United Kingdom specify chemistry at Higher Level, frequently with a minimum grade and often alongside a second science or mathematics, but requirements belong to the institutions and the published programme page is the authority. UAE institutions including Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, the American University of Sharjah and Zayed University each publish their own. Do not accept a general claim from any tutoring provider, including this one, in place of reading the requirement yourself.

intro.heading: What you are buying at the top of the Chemistry market
paragraphs: Dubai's tutoring market has a visible ceiling and Chemistry sits close to it. Premium named tutors are advertised in the emirate at AED 500 to 650 an hour. Subject specialists for the Diploma, IGCSE and A Level are quoted from about AED 200 to 450 and upwards. Qualified subject tutors working online sit between roughly AED 150 and 300, and budget or university-student tutors from AED 45 to 150. Those are published market figures from Dubai rate cards and Bestimate's 2026 cost table for the emirate, not IB Gram prices.

A family in The Greens comparing the top and the middle of that range deserves a concrete answer rather than a reassurance. Three parts of Diploma Chemistry genuinely reward someone who has taught the course repeatedly. Organic mechanisms at Higher Level, where a curly arrow in the wrong place loses the mark even when the product is right. Paper 2 extended responses, where the command term dictates what counts as an answer and an explanation that stops one step early scores nothing. And the scientific investigation, which is assessed out of twenty-four marks across four criteria, only one of which is really about chemistry.

Everything else in the course is taught well at the middle of the market. The mole, reacting masses, bonding, energetics and equilibrium are standard content with abundant practice material, and a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 an hour covers them properly. A student who is behind on Structure 1 does not need a premium hour; they need twenty of the ordinary kind, used in order.

The 2023 Chemistry guide changed where the money should go, and many quotes have not caught up. The course is now organised around two themes, Structure and Reactivity, each with three topics, and the assessment from 2025 runs on Paper 1 at thirty-six per cent, split into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, Paper 2 at forty-four per cent, and the scientific investigation at twenty per cent. The old habit of buying hours to drill recall fits an assessment model that no longer exists.

The practical scheme of work is the other thing families do not budget for. Standard Level carries forty hours and Higher Level sixty, and ten of those hours go to the collaborative sciences project, an interdisciplinary piece of work every Diploma science student completes. It is not separately graded, so it consumes time without producing a mark, which makes the weeks around it the worst possible moment to start tutoring from scratch.

What follows prices each of those components, says plainly which band of the market covers it, and ends with the number of hours the whole thing realistically takes. Every AED figure is the market's. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits in Dubai, because home visits are an India-only part of the service.

programmes.description: Criterion-assessed integrated science, which measures something different from a timed chemistry paper. Students arriving in Year 12 with strong Middle Years Programme science grades can still be unprepared for the arithmetic density of Structure 1, because criterion-based marking rewards process and the Diploma papers reward accuracy under time.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-the-greens.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is one subject on the timetable and a dozen separately priceable skills in a mark scheme. These are the areas Greens families end up paying for, with the band of the Dubai market that covers each one adequately.

subjects.name: The mole and reacting masses
subjects.description: Moles, concentrations, limiting reagents, percentage yield and the ideal gas law. It is arithmetic-dense rather than conceptually hard, which means it responds to practice rather than to explanation, and the middle of the market teaches it entirely adequately.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and electron configuration
subjects.description: Isotopes, mass spectra, ionisation energies and orbital filling. Marks go missing on the explanation questions, where a student describes a trend correctly and omits the shielding or nuclear charge reason the mark scheme requires.

subjects.name: Bonding, structure and intermolecular forces
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic models, shapes of molecules and the hierarchy of intermolecular forces. The recurring loss is being asked to explain a physical property from a structure and answering with the structure alone, which earns half the marks at best.

subjects.name: Periodicity and classification
subjects.description: Periodic trends, functional groups, and the spectroscopic identification of compounds. The spectroscopy questions reward reading an unfamiliar spectrum rather than recalling a rule, and they are one of the components a generalist tutor tends to avoid.

subjects.name: Energetics: enthalpy, entropy and Gibbs energy
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess cycles, bond enthalpies and, at Higher Level, entropy and spontaneity. Signs and states are where the marks are lost, almost never the concept, and the fix is a drawing habit rather than more theory.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.description: Le Chatelier reasoning at both levels and equilibrium constant calculations at Higher Level. The Higher Level algebra defeats more students than the chemistry does, which makes it one of the places a specialist hour genuinely earns its premium.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and buffers
subjects.description: pH, strong and weak behaviour, titration curves and, at Higher Level, buffer calculations and indicator choice. Titration curve interpretation is high-yield and under-practised, since school practical time rarely allows enough repetitions.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half-equations, electrolysis and, at Higher Level, cell potentials and the Nernst-style reasoning the course expects. Half-equations in acidic and alkaline conditions are a reliable source of lost marks and a reliable thing to fix.

subjects.name: Kinetics and rate laws
subjects.description: Collision theory and rate graphs at both levels, with rate laws, orders of reaction and activation energy determination at Higher Level. Deducing an order from data is a data-handling skill, so it improves alongside the Paper 1B work rather than separately.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and reaction mechanisms
subjects.description: Functional group reactions at both levels; nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and the arrow-pushing conventions at Higher Level. This is the component where the gap between a specialist and a generalist is visible in a single session, because the conventions are either known precisely or not at all.

subjects.name: Uncertainties, data and graphs
subjects.levels: SL and HL, assessed in Paper 1B
subjects.description: Significant figures, absolute and percentage uncertainty, error bars and gradient uncertainty. It is taught thinly in most schools, appears in both Paper 1B and criterion B of the investigation, and is among the cheapest marks available in the whole course.

subjects.name: Paper 2 extended response technique
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 44% of the grade
subjects.description: Reading the command term, answering at the depth it requires, and stopping at the right point. Students lose more marks to writing the wrong kind of answer than to not knowing chemistry, and this is trainable in a handful of sessions with marked scripts.

modes.description: The realistic plan for Higher Level in the second year, with one hour on organic mechanisms, equilibrium and electrochemistry and one on timed Paper 2 practice. sections.heading: What the premium end of the market actually contains
paragraphs: Start at the top and work down, because that is the order a worried parent in The Greens receives quotes in. The table below sets out each published band in the Dubai market, who charges it, what the hour plausibly contains, and the specific circumstance in which the premium is defensible. The point of reading it downwards is to notice how quickly the honest justification runs out.

At AED 500 to 650 an hour, what is being sold is usually scarcity and reputation. That is not fraudulent, and a tutor with a long waiting list may well be excellent, but the hour contains the same sixty minutes as one at AED 300. The test is whether the tutor can name the component they are being hired for before the first session. If the answer is general revision, the premium is buying a name.

At AED 200 to 450, the specialist band, the content of the hour changes in ways you can verify. A specialist will talk about curly-arrow conventions rather than about organic chemistry in general, will name command terms rather than describing exam technique, and will refer to the four investigation criteria by letter. Those three habits are what the premium over the middle of the market actually buys, and they map directly onto the components where marks concentrate.

Below that, at AED 150 to 300, is where most of Diploma Chemistry should be bought. The mole, bonding, energetics and Le Chatelier reasoning are standard content with abundant practice material and clear right answers. Paying specialist rates to drill them is the single most common overspend in this subject among families in the Emirates Living cluster. Every figure quoted here is a published Dubai market rate rather than ours.

sections.heading: The 2023 Chemistry guide, and what it changed about the bill
paragraphs: The current Chemistry course is organised around two themes rather than a list of options. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Higher Level material is integrated into those six topics rather than sitting in a separate section.

That integration matters commercially. Under the previous structure a parent could buy help with a named option and leave the rest alone. Now the additional Higher Level depth appears inside equilibrium, acids and bases, electrochemistry and organic mechanisms, so a tutor working with a Higher Level student has to know where each topic deepens. A tutor who last taught the earlier guide will cover the right subject and the wrong depth.

The table below maps the six topics and, for each, names the place students most often need help. Read the right-hand column rather than the middle one if you are deciding where money goes. Five of the six entries are about applying chemistry under specific conditions rather than about recall, which is why hours spent on memorisation produce so little movement in a mark.

One practical note on sources. The IB's own site is not reliably readable by automated tools, so nothing on this page states an IB examination or results date, and nothing here reproduces syllabus text, past papers or mark schemes. Those belong to the board. Take session dates and the current guide from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly, and treat any tutoring page quoting a Diploma date without a source with caution.

sections.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2: where the money goes
paragraphs: The assessment model from 2025 puts forty-four per cent of the Chemistry grade in Paper 2 and thirty-six per cent in Paper 1, which itself splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. The scientific investigation carries the remaining twenty per cent. Those three numbers should drive a tutoring budget, and in most households they do not, because the hours get allocated by topic rather than by component.

Paper 1A, the multiple-choice section, rewards speed and arithmetic reliability. It is the cheapest component to improve because the fix is volume: enough timed questions that the common distractors become recognisable. A budget or mid-market tutor supplies that perfectly well, and a premium hour spent on it is money spent on supervision.

Paper 1B, the data-based section, is the opposite. It asks for significant figures, absolute and percentage uncertainty, error bars and gradient interpretation, and most schools teach those thinly because practical time is short. It is also the skill set criterion B of the investigation assesses, so hours spent here count twice. For a family wanting a single high-yield purchase, this is usually it.

Paper 2 is where the premium belongs. Extended responses are marked against command terms, and a student who writes a good explanation of the wrong kind scores nothing for it. Training that requires marked scripts and someone who knows what the criteria accept, which is precisely the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 an hour. Four to eight sessions on Paper 2 technique is the best-value premium purchase in the subject.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry, the topic families pay for twice
paragraphs: Organic chemistry arrives late in the course and is examined as though it arrived early. At Standard Level the demand is largely functional-group reactions and naming. At Higher Level it becomes mechanisms: nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition, and the arrow-pushing conventions that show where electron pairs move. Those conventions are not a style preference. A curly arrow starting in the wrong place loses the mark even when the product written underneath is correct.

That is why families pay twice. The first purchase is a generalist who teaches the reactions as transformations to memorise, which produces a student who can predict products and cannot draw mechanisms. The second purchase, usually in the spring, is a specialist who has to undo the memorised version before teaching the conventional one. Buying the second one first costs less in total than buying both.

The diagnostic is quick and a parent can run it. Ask the student to draw the mechanism for the reaction of a halogenoalkane with a hydroxide ion and say which species is the nucleophile, where the arrow starts and what happens to the leaving group. A student who narrates the product confidently and cannot place the arrows has been taught the memorised version, and that is a specialist job rather than a practice job.

There is a scheduling point too. Organic mechanisms usually land in the second year, in the same months as the investigation deadline and the start of serious revision. A Greens family who front-loads the investigation into Year 12 arrives at that term with capacity. One who leaves both to the spring is buying specialist hours at the busiest point in the Dubai tutoring calendar, for two jobs at once.
bullets: Standard Level rewards functional-group reactions; Higher Level rewards mechanisms

sections.heading: The investigation, the collaborative project and the honesty line
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is assessed out of twenty-four marks across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The report runs to no more than three thousand words. Note what that distribution means. Only one of the four criteria is primarily about chemistry; the other three assess how a scientist designs, interprets and criticises work. Strong chemists lose marks on evaluation more than on anything else, because a limitations section written as an apology scores far below one written as analysis.

The collaborative sciences project sits alongside it. It is an interdisciplinary piece of work taking around ten hours of the practical scheme, which is forty hours at Standard Level and sixty at Higher Level. It carries no separate grade. Families should know it exists because it consumes time in a term where time is already short, not because it needs tutoring.

The boundary on investigation support is explicit. A tutor may challenge a research question until the student narrows it to something measurable, teach uncertainty propagation using other data, explain each criterion by letter, read a draft the student wrote and say where it falls short, and press on limitations the student has not noticed. No tutor at IB Gram will write the investigation, produce a draft for submission, or edit a report until the words stop being the student's.

That line protects the candidate. Submitting work a student did not produce is malpractice under the board's rules and the consequence falls on the candidate, not on the provider. Operations in this market do advertise finished assessed work at fixed prices; what they sell is risk, transferred to a sixteen-year-old. Any provider offering to supply a completed investigation should end the conversation.

sections.heading: Higher Level or Standard Level: what the step up costs in hours
paragraphs: The step from Standard to Higher Level Chemistry is not a proportional increase. Papers lengthen, with Paper 1 going from ninety minutes to two hours and Paper 2 from ninety minutes to two and a half. The practical scheme rises from forty hours to sixty. And the additional depth sits inside the same six topics, which means it is met continuously rather than as a block that can be scheduled.

In tutoring terms the difference is roughly double, and it concentrates in the second year. Students on Standard Level who are keeping pace typically need one weekly hour plus an investigation block. Higher Level students usually need one weekly hour in the first year, the same investigation block, and two hours a week from September of the second year once equilibrium algebra, electrochemistry and organic mechanisms are all live at once.

There is a decision here that is worth making on evidence rather than ambition. A student aiming at medicine or chemical engineering may need Higher Level for admission, and that settles it. A student taking Higher Level because it sounded better will spend two years and a substantial tutoring budget on depth they do not need, in a subject where the Standard Level grade would have served the application equally well.

A tutor's job in that conversation is to supply evidence rather than an opinion: here are the marks the student produces on Higher Level questions under time, here is where the losses concentrate. The decision belongs to the student and the school. Nobody should be promising a particular grade at either level, and a provider who does is making a claim they cannot stand behind.

sections.heading: Why a Greens family should not buy Chemistry on travel distance
paragraphs: The Greens sits beside a metro station with Sheikh Zayed Road on one side and Al Khail Road on the other, so a tutor can reach it more easily than most Dubai addresses. That convenience is exactly what makes the in-home option tempting and exactly why the arithmetic deserves a look. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and advertised monthly packages of four two-hour visits run at AED 1,599 to 1,799.

Set that against the online rate for the same qualification level and the premium is visible. The extra is transport. For Chemistry specifically there is a second cost, because the usable weekday window in this community runs from about four o'clock, once buses and clubs are accounted for, until roughly half past seven. Mechanism work and graph interpretation need the student alert, and a session pushed to the back of that window by somebody else's drive is a worse session.

There is also a supply argument. Restricting the search to tutors who can reach Al Thanyah by half past four shrinks the pool to whoever is free in western Dubai at that hour. Removing the travel requirement widens it to everyone who teaches Higher Level organic mechanisms, which is the variable that actually changes a Chemistry grade. In a subject where the specialist skill is this narrow, that trade is clearly worth making.

To be unambiguous about the model: IB Gram has no office or centre in Dubai, and no tutor is sent to a UAE address. Home visits are an India-only service. The in-home rates quoted on this page belong to other providers and are shown so the premium can be seen rather than assumed.

sections.heading: Chemistry for medicine and engineering: what admissions actually asks
paragraphs: Higher Level Chemistry is a common requirement for medicine and for chemical and biomedical engineering, and it is frequently assumed to be a requirement for far more than that. The honest position is that the requirement belongs to the individual programme and the individual intake year. Check the published entry requirement for the specific course rather than relying on a general rule, because these change and because they differ markedly between jurisdictions.

Separately there is Ministry of Education equivalency, which recognises a foreign school certificate for use in the UAE. The published requirements differ by curriculum. On the British track a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. On the American track, mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test and English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section.

No equivalency threshold for the International Baccalaureate is published on this page, because none has been read from a Ministry of Education source. One ranking competitor in this market states a GCSE subject count that does not match the Ministry clarification reported by Gulf Today; inheriting that error would be worse than publishing nothing. Take the Diploma figure from moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority.

Equivalency is not something a tutoring company performs, guarantees or accelerates, and tutoring is not a requirement for it, for university admission or for school progression. IB Gram describes the process and points to the official channel; the application is between the family and the authority.

sections.heading: How many Chemistry hours, and when to buy them
paragraphs: A straight answer is more useful than a range. Standard Level, for a student keeping pace, runs on one weekly hour across two years plus a six-session investigation block, which is roughly sixty to seventy hours in total. Higher Level runs on one weekly hour in the first year, the same investigation block, and two weekly hours from September of the second year, which comes to roughly ninety to a hundred and ten hours.

At the published Dubai specialist band of AED 200 to 450 an hour, Higher Level therefore sits in the high tens of thousands of dirhams across the Diploma, and Standard Level at roughly half of that. Those are market figures rather than ours, and the range is wide because the Dubai market's spread is wide. A sensible plan mixes bands rather than paying one rate for everything: mid-market hours for Structure 1 and bonding, specialist hours for mechanisms, Paper 2 technique and the investigation.

Timing changes the total more than negotiation does. The investigation bought in Year 12 is a one-off block at a quiet point in the calendar. The same work in the spring of Year 13 competes with revision and with organic mechanisms, at the busiest point in the tutoring year, and usually costs two or three times as much for a worse result. Front-loading is the only reliable discount available in this subject.

Six weeks out from a session, what a block can buy depends entirely on what already exists. Sound content with weak Paper 2 technique moves with marked scripts and timed practice. A genuine gap in equilibrium or mechanisms closes partly. The investigation cannot be touched at all, because a fifth of the grade was settled when the report went in. That asymmetry is the argument for the earlier purchase, made with numbers rather than urgency.

process.title: Say which level and which component
process.description: Send four facts: Higher or Standard Level, the school, whether the scientific investigation has started, and which of the six topics the last school report flagged. Those four decide which band of the market you need and stop you paying specialist rates for work the middle of the market covers.

process.title: Use the free session as a diagnostic
process.description: One full session, free, with no card details taken to book it. The tutor works a past question and a short mechanism task with your child and reports which component is losing marks: Paper 1A speed, Paper 1B uncertainty, Paper 2 command terms, or genuine content gaps in a named topic.

process.title: Mix the bands deliberately
process.description: Most families should be buying mid-market hours for Structure 1 arithmetic and bonding, and specialist hours only for organic mechanisms, Paper 2 technique and the investigation. Paying one rate for everything is how a Chemistry budget doubles without the mark moving.

process.title: Book the investigation block early
process.description: Around six sessions in Year 12, with a submission deadline attached, covering the research question, uncertainty handling and feedback on the student's own drafts. Twenty per cent of the grade is banked at a predictable one-off cost instead of competing with revision and mechanisms in the spring.

process.title: Review against marked scripts
process.description: Progress is judged on complete papers marked against the published criteria, not on how sessions felt. Each review names the component that improved and the one that did not, and where the evidence says a standing weekly hour is no longer earning its cost, that is what the review says.

whyPoints.title: The premium is explained, not assumed
whyPoints.description: This page names the three components that justify specialist rates in Chemistry and the ones that do not. Premium Dubai rates reach AED 650 an hour; a parent is entitled to know what the extra contains before agreeing to it, and most providers in this market never say.

whyPoints.title: Level stated before any rate
whyPoints.description: Every match says whether it covers Higher Level, Standard Level or both, and which of the six syllabus topics it teaches most often. That removes the mismatch that wastes a term, which is a tutor priced for Higher Level mechanisms who last taught Standard Level content.

whyPoints.title: Mechanisms taught by convention
whyPoints.description: Higher Level organic chemistry is assessed on arrow-pushing conventions, so it is taught that way rather than as reactions to memorise. This is the component where a specialist and a generalist produce visibly different results inside a single session.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1B treated as its own skill
whyPoints.description: Uncertainty, significant figures and gradient interpretation are taught thinly in most schools, appear in Paper 1B and are assessed again under criterion B of the investigation. Hours spent there count twice, which makes them the highest-yield purchase in the course.

whyPoints.title: A stated limit on investigation help
whyPoints.description: Tutors challenge research questions, teach uncertainty on other data and respond to drafts the student wrote. Nobody here produces a report or supplies a draft for submission. In a market where finished assessed work is advertised at fixed prices, that boundary protects the candidate.

whyPoints.title: Sources named, dates withheld where unverified
whyPoints.description: Rate bands come from published Dubai rate cards and Bestimate's 2026 cost table. Cambridge and Pearson dates come from the boards. No IB examination or results date appears on this page, because none has been confirmed from the IB's own site.

faqs.question: What does an IB Chemistry Higher Level specialist charge in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published 2026 rates put Diploma, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and upwards, with premium named tutors advertised at AED 500 to 650. Qualified subject tutors working online sit between about AED 150 and 300, and budget or university-student tutors between AED 45 and 150. Those are market observations from Dubai rate cards and Bestimate's 2026 cost table, not IB Gram prices. What matters more than the band is which component the hour is aimed at.

faqs.question: Is the premium for a Chemistry specialist worth it over a general science tutor?
faqs.answer: For three parts of the course, yes. Higher Level organic mechanisms are assessed on arrow-pushing conventions that are either exact or worthless. Paper 2 carries forty-four per cent and is marked against command terms, so a good answer of the wrong kind scores nothing. And the scientific investigation is twenty-four marks across four criteria, three of which are not really about chemistry. For the mole, bonding, energetics and Le Chatelier reasoning, the middle of the market teaches them perfectly adequately.

faqs.question: How much does IB Chemistry tutoring cost a Greens family per term?
faqs.answer: A term is about twelve weeks, so one weekly hour is twelve sessions. At the published Dubai middle band of AED 150 to 300 an hour that is roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600 for the term; at specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 it is AED 2,400 to 5,400. Higher Level at two hours a week in the second year doubles it. A sensible plan mixes bands rather than paying one rate for every hour, which is where most of the overspend in this subject comes from.

faqs.question: Which Chemistry topics do Greens families end up paying for twice?
faqs.answer: Organic chemistry, almost always. The first purchase is a generalist who teaches the reactions as transformations to memorise, which produces a student who can predict products but cannot draw mechanisms. The second is a specialist who has to undo the memorised version before teaching the conventional one. Buying the specialist first costs less in total. Higher Level equilibrium algebra runs a close second, for the same reason: it is taught as chemistry when the obstacle is the mathematics.

faqs.question: Can an IB Chemistry tutor help with the Chemistry IA without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the limit is specific rather than vague. A tutor may challenge a research question until the student narrows it to something measurable, teach uncertainty propagation using unrelated data, explain each of the four criteria by letter, read a draft the student wrote and say where it falls short, and press on limitations the student has missed. No tutor here will write the report, produce a draft for submission, or edit one until the words stop being the student's own. Submitting work a candidate did not produce is malpractice.

faqs.question: How many Chemistry sessions does an HL student need before Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Four to eight sessions spent entirely on extended responses is the highest-yield short block in the subject, because Paper 2 carries forty-four per cent of the grade and runs two and a half hours at Higher Level. The sessions have to involve real past questions written under time and marked against the published criteria, with scripts returned annotated. Discussion of answers without marking is a cheaper product that looks similar. Ask which it is before booking.

faqs.question: Is IB Chemistry HL much harder to tutor than SL, and does it cost more?
faqs.answer: It costs roughly double in hours rather than in rate. Papers lengthen, with Paper 1 going from ninety minutes to two hours and Paper 2 from ninety minutes to two and a half, and the practical scheme rises from forty hours to sixty. The additional depth is integrated into the same six topics rather than sitting in a separate block, so it is met continuously. Most Higher Level students need two weekly hours from September of the second year; Standard Level students usually need one.

faqs.question: What does the collaborative sciences project involve, and can a tutor help?
faqs.answer: It is an interdisciplinary project taking around ten hours of the practical scheme, which is forty hours at Standard Level and sixty at Higher Level, and it carries no separate grade. Families should know it exists mainly because it consumes time in a term that is already crowded, not because it needs tutoring. A tutor's useful contribution is scheduling advice: move the scientific investigation earlier so the two do not collide with the start of serious revision.

faqs.question: Does organic chemistry need more tutoring hours than the other themes?
faqs.answer: At Higher Level, yes, and for a structural reason. It arrives late in the course and is assessed as though it arrived early, and the Higher Level demand is mechanisms rather than reactions. The arrow-pushing conventions have to be exact, so a student who narrates products confidently may still score nothing on a mechanism. A quick home test: ask your child where the arrow starts when a hydroxide ion reacts with a halogenoalkane, and what happens to the leaving group.

faqs.question: Do we need a Chemistry tutor with a lab, or is online enough?
faqs.answer: The assessed practical skills are data handling and investigation design rather than manipulation, and both work well over video with screen sharing. Uncertainty propagation, graph work with error bars, gradient interpretation and research-design critique are all done on a screen in school too. The physical practical work belongs to the school's forty or sixty-hour scheme. What a tutor adds is the analysis and write-up skill that criterion B and Paper 1B assess, and that needs a shared screen rather than a bench.

faqs.question: Which schools near The Greens offer DP Chemistry at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Several Diploma campuses within fifteen to thirty minutes of The Greens run Chemistry at both levels, across the Emirates Living, Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Jumeirah Village clusters. The more useful question to ask each school is how large this year's Higher Level Chemistry group is. The International Baccalaureate accounted for about seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, which is why Higher Level science groups stay small even at large schools.

faqs.question: Do Dubai medical schools insist on Chemistry at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Chemistry is a common requirement for medicine and for chemical and biomedical engineering, but the requirement belongs to the individual programme and intake year rather than to a country. Check the published entry requirement for the specific course and year, because they change and differ between jurisdictions. Treat any tutoring page that states a universal rule as unreliable, and treat the claim that tutoring is required for admission as false urgency about a process the family controls.

faqs.question: Does an in-home Chemistry tutor in The Greens charge for travel time?
faqs.answer: Travel is inside the quoted price rather than itemised, which is why in-home rates in Dubai sit higher. The market quotes in-home one-to-one visits from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with monthly packages of four two-hour visits advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Against online rates at the same qualification level the difference buys transport. In this community it also costs evening minutes from a window that runs from about four o'clock to half past seven. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai.

faqs.question: What is the smallest sensible block of IB Chemistry tutoring to buy?
faqs.answer: Four sessions, aimed at one named component. The two blocks that reliably pay for themselves are Paper 1B data handling, which also feeds criterion B of the investigation, and Paper 2 extended-response technique, which addresses forty-four per cent of the grade. Both are short, both are measurable, and both end. Open-ended weekly arrangements started without a diagnosis are where Chemistry budgets grow without the mark moving, so start with the free diagnostic session.

faqs.question: How does the 2023 Chemistry syllabus change what we are paying to fix?
faqs.answer: The course is now built on two themes, Structure and Reactivity, with three topics each, and the Higher Level depth is integrated into those topics rather than kept in a separate section. That means a Higher Level student cannot schedule the harder material as a block, and a tutor who last taught the earlier guide will cover the right subject at the wrong depth. The assessment also shifted: Paper 1 at thirty-six per cent now splits into multiple choice and data-based sections, so recall drilling buys less than it used to.

intro.heading: The real obstacle is the calendar, not the chemistry
paragraphs: Ask a Lakes parent what stopped them arranging Chemistry support last term and the answer is almost never about the subject. It is about Tuesday. School finishes at three, football finishes at five, the younger one has to be collected from a different campus, dinner is at seven and homework is still outstanding. Somewhere in that sequence an hour of Chemistry has to fit, and if the hour also involves somebody driving across Emirates Living, it does not fit at all. The tuition conversation stalls on logistics long before anybody discusses Reactivity 3.

This page is written around that problem rather than around a sales argument. The Lakes sits in the middle of Emirates Living, with Emirates International School Meadows, Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Regent International School within a few minutes and the Al Barsha cluster fifteen to twenty minutes east depending on the hour. Those schools do not end at the same time, they do not run activities on the same days, and the two that offer the Diploma do not sequence Chemistry identically. A tuition plan that ignores all of that is a plan that gets cancelled in week three.

Delivery for every UAE family is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For the school-run problem this is the whole point rather than a compromise. A tutor who does not travel can start at 7:15pm because that is when your child is finally free, can take a session on a Friday morning when the school week has ended early, and can move a slot by forty minutes on the day of a late fixture without anybody losing an hour to Sheikh Zayed Road.

The chemistry itself is covered properly below. There are six syllabus units, three under Structure and three under Reactivity, and the page sets out what each contains and what Higher Level adds. It explains what the data booklet gives a student in the examination and what therefore has to be remembered, because that distinction decides what revision is worth doing. It publishes Dubai market rates in AED by monthly cost rather than by hourly rate, with the source of each figure, since monthly is how families actually budget. And it covers the parts of the Dubai year that move the timetable: activity season, mock season, Ramadan and the Cambridge entry deadlines that sit months before the exams.
If you are reading this at 10pm after a school run, start with the two timetable tables. They are the part that decides whether this works for your household.

subjects.description: 110 taught hours with identical weightings to Higher Level: Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44%, investigation at 20%. Standard Level students most often lose marks in Reactivity 2, where equilibrium and rate questions reward a precise answer rather than a broadly correct one.

sections.heading: A Lakes weekday, hour by hour, and where an hour of Chemistry can actually go
paragraphs: Start with the day as it is rather than as a timetable describes it. Most Emirates Living secondary schools finish the academic day between 2:30pm and 3:30pm. For a child at a school inside the community that means home by about 3:15pm. For a child at a school in Al Barsha it means a return drive in the slowest part of the afternoon and home closer to four. Activities, where they exist, run until about five, and many Lakes households are also collecting a younger sibling from a different campus at a different time.

The window between five and seven is therefore more contested than it looks. It holds the second school run, dinner, and whatever homework has been set, and it is also the window when a child is least able to absorb a new concept. The windows that actually work for Chemistry in this neighbourhood are later than parents expect: roughly 6:30pm to 8:30pm on a weekday, a shortened Friday morning, and weekend mornings before the day fills up. Those are not compromises. They are the times a fifteen-year-old can concentrate on equilibrium.

This is where delivery format stops being a marketing point and becomes arithmetic. A visiting tutor needs a start time that accommodates their drive, which in practice means either an early slot that collides with activities or a late one that collides with bedtime, plus the cost of the travel inside the hourly rate. sections.heading: Structure and Reactivity: the six units, and what Higher Level adds
paragraphs: The current Chemistry course is built on two organising ideas. Structure asks what matter is made of and how it is arranged: Structure 1 covers models of the particulate nature of matter, including the nuclear atom, electron configurations, the mole and ideal gases; Structure 2 covers models of bonding and structure across ionic, covalent and metallic models and the materials that follow from them; Structure 3 covers classification, meaning the periodic table and the functional groups of organic chemistry.

Reactivity asks what happens when matter changes. Reactivity 1 covers what drives reactions, through enthalpy, energy cycles and fuels, with entropy and spontaneity added at Higher Level. Reactivity 2 covers how much, how fast and how far, meaning amount of change, rate and extent, which is where equilibrium lives. Reactivity 3 covers mechanisms, organised by electron behaviour: proton transfer, electron transfer, electron sharing and electron-pair sharing. That organisation is deliberate and it is a gift to a student who learns it, because it tells them which tool a question is asking for before they read the chemistry.

Higher Level is not a seventh unit. The extra seventy taught hours sit inside the six, which is why a student moving up a level finds that Reactivity 1 has grown rather than been supplemented. In Dubai cohorts the predictable pressure points are Reactivity 2, where equilibrium questions punish approximate answers, and Reactivity 3 at Higher Level, where organic mechanisms require a student to draw and justify rather than recall. Structure 1 is the quiet risk: mole calculations feel like arithmetic, so students stop practising them, and then lose marks on them in Paper 2 two years later.

sections.heading: The data booklet: what the examination gives you and what has to be in your head
paragraphs: A chemistry data booklet is available in both written papers, and most students use it badly for the first year. It contains the periodic table, constants, common relationships and reference values, which means a student does not need to memorise them. What it does not contain is the judgement about which relationship applies, and under timed conditions the lookup itself costs seconds a student may not have.

The practical consequence is that revision should split into two piles rather than one. Anything in the booklet needs recognition speed: knowing that the value exists, knowing which page it is on, knowing the units it is quoted in. Anything not in the booklet needs genuine recall: definitions, mechanisms, the reasoning that connects structure to property, and the command-term structure of a good extended answer. Students who revise everything as though it must be memorised waste weeks, and students who assume the booklet will carry them arrive at Paper 2 unable to start. A useful diagnostic is to hand a student a past-paper question and time how long they spend hunting for a value they should have recognised in three seconds.

This is a skill that teaches well on a screen, because the booklet can be open on a shared document while a past-paper question is worked beside it. A tutor can watch the lookup happen, time it, and intervene at the point of hesitation. That is far more useful than being told afterwards that the answer was wrong, and it is the part of Chemistry support that Lakes parents most often report as unexpected value.

sections.heading: Two children, two sciences, one evening: the Lakes scheduling problem
paragraphs: The households that struggle most are not the ones with a weak student. They are the ones with two children at different schools, or one child carrying Chemistry and Physics at Higher Level. Both situations create a competition for the same two-hour window, and the usual response is to alternate weeks, which is the worst available option because it halves the contact frequency in both subjects at the point when frequency is what builds technique.

A better pattern is to separate by day rather than by week and to use the parts of the Dubai week that nothing else wants. Chemistry on Tuesday evening, Physics on Thursday evening, and investigation or revision work on a Friday morning when many schools finish early. Two children can take sequential slots on the same evening, since nobody is travelling between them, and a ninety-minute block can be split as sixty and thirty when one child needs maintenance rather than teaching. None of that is possible when a tutor has to be physically present for both.

The second half of the problem is the Dubai calendar. Activity season, mock weeks, internal investigation deadlines, Ramadan and the long summer all move the usable window, and a plan that assumes a constant Tuesday collapses three times a year. The sensible approach is to agree the standing slot and then agree in advance what happens to it during each of those periods, rather than renegotiating under pressure in the week it arrives.
