faqs.question: Should our son take IB chemistry or A Level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Both are widely accepted for medicine, pharmacy, biochemistry and chemical engineering, so decide on how he works rather than on which sounds harder. The structural difference is coursework: IB chemistry carries a scientific investigation worth 20% of the grade, written independently and submitted months before the papers, while A Level Chemistry assesses practical skills through an endorsement rather than as a weighted mark, leaving the grade to the examinations. A student who plans and writes well banks a fifth early; a student who peaks under timed conditions carries less risk on the A Level route.

faqs.question: Our son wants to study medicine. Which chemistry level does he need?
faqs.answer: Commonly, and often biology alongside it, but the specific combination, level and minimum grade differ by country and by institution and are revised. The practical point is timing: a Higher Level requirement can only be met if the student is registered at Higher Level, and once the second Diploma year begins a change of level usually means resetting the investigation as well as the accumulated content. Read the published admissions pages of the specific medical schools on the shortlist during the first Diploma year, not the second.

faqs.question: Why do energetics questions cost so many marks?
faqs.answer: Sign conventions. An enthalpy change entered with the wrong sign invalidates every subsequent step in a cycle, so a student who understands the method completely can score close to nothing on a multi-mark question. The fix is procedural rather than conceptual: write the sign convention at the top of the working before any numbers appear, every time, without exception. Students resist it as unnecessary until they see a marked paper where it cost five marks. It is the fastest available improvement in the subject.

faqs.question: My daughter says organic chemistry is her weakness. Is it?
faqs.answer: Often not. Students report organic chemistry as the hardest area because it feels unfamiliar, while marked papers frequently show most of the losses in energetics and moles arithmetic, which feel routine and therefore invisible. A term spent re-teaching organic chemistry to a student whose actual losses are procedural changes very little, and both parent and student then conclude that tutoring does not work. Look at a marked paper, classify each lost mark by cause, and address the causes by how many marks they account for.

faqs.question: How is the IB investigation different from an A Level practical endorsement?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and families moving between routes often assume otherwise. The IB investigation is an independently designed piece worth 20% of the final grade, marked against published criteria and submitted once to a school deadline. An A Level practical endorsement assesses competence across required activities without the same weighted contribution. The tutoring consequence is large: on the IB route, scoping the research question is the highest-value session in the subject, while on the A Level route the same money is better spent on examination technique.

faqs.question: What makes Higher Level chemistry harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Substantial extension in energetics with entropy and spontaneity, in acids, bases and equilibrium with buffer and logarithmic calculations, in redox, and most demandingly in organic mechanisms where unfamiliar substrates appear. The mathematical load rises with it. Students upgrading mid-year are usually surprised by the mechanism reasoning rather than the content volume, because memorisation works at Standard Level and fails at Higher Level. That shift is teachable within a few weeks once it is correctly identified as the problem.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor really teach organic mechanisms?
faqs.answer: Better than most parents expect. A shared whiteboard shows the mechanism being drawn step by step, the right way up and large enough to see, with the tutor able to stop at the exact arrow that is wrong. Compare that with a tutor drawing upside down across a kitchen table. The requirement is that every mechanism is tested on an unseen substrate rather than the textbook one, because a memorised diagram works on the familiar case and fails on the examined one. That works identically over video.

faqs.question: Our daughter takes chemistry and biology at Higher Level. Is that manageable?
faqs.answer: It is the common pre-medicine pairing and it is manageable with one specific piece of planning: two scientific investigations fall due in the same year, both to school deadlines in roughly the same term. That is a scheduling problem rather than an academic one, and it is solvable only if it is noticed in the first Diploma year. In a community with a long school run it matters more, because the available working hours are fewer than in a household living beside the school.

faqs.question: Where should the money go if we can afford only a few sessions?
faqs.answer: On the IB route, scoping the investigation, if it has not yet been fixed. Two sessions testing whether the research question produces enough usable data to analyse costs a fraction of a term and determines most of a component worth 20% of the grade. If the investigation is already submitted, spend the same money on calculation discipline, because moles and sign errors leak marks across every paper. On the A Level route, examination technique, since that is where the grade is decided.

faqs.question: There are eight weeks left. What can chemistry tutoring still change?
faqs.answer: Not too late to be useful, but the target must be honest. In the final term the realistic gains are technique: command-term discipline, sign conventions, pacing against marks and the data-based section of the paper, plus narrow content repair on recurring topics. What is not available is any influence over the investigation once submitted, or broad content coverage. A tutor implying a two-grade lift in that window is selling, and we would rather state the limit before a booking than defend it afterwards.

faqs.question: Will a chemistry tutor come to our villa in The Valley?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in this community. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard for mechanisms, calculations and diagrams. Home tutoring is a service we operate in India only. In a community with no school inside it and no local tutor network, the practical gain is that your child is matched to someone who teaches their level rather than to whoever will drive the Al Ain road at five.

faqs.question: How should chemistry sessions be timed around a long school run?
faqs.answer: Split by the type of work. Calculation drilling benefits from frequency rather than length, so a short weekday evening slot plus daily between-session sets suits moles and sign discipline. Mechanism reasoning and investigation writing need an uninterrupted block, because both involve holding several steps in mind at once, and in this community that time genuinely exists only at the weekend. One weekday slot and one weekend block is the pattern that lasts a full term here.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level chemistry support cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures put qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. For Higher Level work the specialist tier is usually right, because mechanism reasoning and investigation judgement are what is being bought. Bestimate's monthly estimate for one weekly hour runs AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market. Those figures were read in October 2026 and belong to the companies that published them.

faqs.question: Why do you ask for marked work from both halves of the course?
faqs.answer: Because Structure and Reactivity fail in different ways. Structure losses are explanatory — a trend stated without its reason, the wrong force named for a property. Reactivity losses are procedural and quantitative — sign errors, qualitative answers to quantitative command terms, curly arrows from the wrong species. A tutor who sees only one half will treat chemistry as one undifferentiated subject and spend the term on whichever part they prefer, which is how a family pays for work the student did not need.

faqs.question: Do you publish results or ratings for chemistry students?
faqs.answer: No, because a figure without a sample size, a date and a method is a marketing claim rather than evidence. Several providers in this market publish self-asserted ratings that contradict their own page text. What this page publishes instead is checkable: the syllabus themes, the investigation weighting, the AED bands with their publishers and the month read, and a plain statement of the approvals we do not hold. Progress in an individual case shows up in the session notes rather than in a percentage.

intro.heading: Cost the Diploma, not the hour
paragraphs: A parent in The Views comparing tutors usually collects hourly rates. It is the obvious thing to compare and it is close to useless, because the hourly rate is the smallest variable in what you will actually spend. Two families can pay the same AED figure per hour and one spends four thousand dirhams across a Diploma while the other spends twenty-two thousand, because one bought ten sessions aimed at a named component and the other bought a weekly hour for two years aimed at chemistry in general.

So this page prices the real thing. Higher Level chemistry runs over two years with three distinct cost moments: the quantitative wall in the first term of DP1, the scientific investigation in the middle, and the extended-response paper in DP2. Each one has a different sensible spend, and knowing which one you are in tells you whether you need forty sessions or eight. Everything below is set out that way, with the Dubai market bands attributed to the providers who published them in October 2026.

The delivery arrangement is relevant to the money, so it belongs in the first paragraphs rather than the last. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in The Views or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor each week. The market quotes in-home one-to-one visits in Dubai at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the gap is the car rather than the chemistry. In a tower community where visitor bays fill by 18:00, part of a booked in-home hour also disappears into access and an early departure.

There is a second reason online matters for this subject specifically, and it is about value rather than convenience. Chemistry tutoring is heavily diagrammatic: a reaction mechanism drawn one arrow at a time, an energy profile annotated, a titration dataset processed with its uncertainties propagating in front of the student. On a shared screen those are built, corrected and saved for the following week. The same work on a sheet of paper across a dining table is gone by Thursday, and a family paying AED 250 an hour for work that cannot be revisited is paying twice for the same explanation.

What follows is the honest version of a pricing page. It gives the market bands and what each one includes. It names four specific ways families in this community overspend, including the most common one, which is buying a weekly hour as insurance rather than as treatment. It prices the investigation block, shows which examination component returns the most per paid hour, puts tutoring spend next to the one school-fee fact KHDA has fixed for 2026-27, and ends with the section no tutoring page writes: the signals that an arrangement has done its job and should stop.

We publish no fixed price list of our own on these pages, because a ten-session organic mechanisms block and a two-year weekly arrangement are not the same product and pretending they are is how families overspend. dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-the-views.programmesIntro: Chemistry costs different amounts at different points in a Views student's path, because the thing going wrong changes. These are the four stages where money gets spent on this subject.

programmes.name: Chemistry, Higher Level

Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium carry most of the lost marks and therefore most of the tutoring spend.
programmes.countryNote: The level most Views students on chemistry are taking, because the subject travels with medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and engineering intentions. It is also the most expensive Diploma subject to support badly, since a weekly hour held for two years without a target is the commonest overspend we see from this community.

programmes.name: Chemistry, Standard Level
programmes.description: The same organisation at reduced depth, with the same assessment weightings and the same investigation out of twenty-four marks. The quantitative content is lighter, which changes the economics: Standard Level problems are more often content gaps than technique failures, and content gaps are cheaper to fix early than late.

sections.heading: A Higher Level chemistry year, priced by phase
paragraphs: The useful way to budget for Diploma chemistry is to split the two years into the phases where something specific goes wrong, and to attach a realistic quantity of support to each. Done that way, the total is both lower and more predictable than a weekly hour maintained from September of DP1 to May of DP2 out of caution.

The first phase is the quantitative wall, which arrives in the first term of DP1. Moles, concentration, limiting reagents and the arithmetic of titration calculations are where a student with a comfortable IGCSE grade discovers that applying a given formula and reasoning from a proportional relationship are different skills. This phase responds to a short, dense block: six to ten sessions, finished and stopped. Left untreated, it contaminates everything afterwards, which is why it is the one phase where spending early is unambiguously cheaper.

The second phase is organic chemistry and mechanisms, usually in the second and third terms of DP1, overlapping the scientific investigation. The investigation itself is the most budgetable item in the whole Diploma, because its scope is fixed: four criteria, twenty-four marks, a known deadline, four to eight sessions. The third phase is DP2, where the money should shift away from content entirely and towards extended-response writing and past papers under timing.

The table prices those phases against the published Dubai bands. Read it as a planning document rather than a quotation: it shows which phase you are in, what quantity of support that phase actually needs, and roughly what the market charges for that quantity. The total across two years in the specialist band comes out well below what a continuous weekly hour costs over the same period, and it buys more, because every session has a target.

sections.heading: The Dubai bands, and what each one actually includes
paragraphs: A rate on its own means nothing without knowing what sits inside it. Across the Dubai market the same hourly figure can include marked work between sessions, written notes and a tutor who reads your child's school materials, or it can include an hour of talking and nothing else. The bands below are other providers' published figures as read in October 2026, with what the band typically covers.

Online supervision from university-student tutors is advertised from roughly AED 33 to AED 52 an hour by Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 by EdFlik. Qualified online subject tutoring begins around AED 150, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IB specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table reaching AED 450 or more at the specialist end and premium examiner-led tutoring quoted at AED 650 by BartyED. In-home one-to-one visits run AED 180 to AED 500 including travel, with Bestimate's common band AED 180 to AED 350.

Three questions turn a rate into a price you can compare. Is the figure per hour or per session, because a fifty-minute session quoted hourly is a sixth of your money. Is marking between sessions included, because for chemistry extended-response work that is where much of the value sits. And does the tutor work from your child's school materials and deadlines, or from their own scheme, because a tutor teaching a different order from the school doubles the student's load rather than halving it.

The fourth question is the uncomfortable one: what happens to unused sessions in a monthly package. Advertised Dubai packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. A family that travels for half of March has paid for sessions it cannot take unless the terms say otherwise, and the terms are worth reading before the first payment rather than after the third.

sections.heading: Four ways Views families overspend on chemistry
paragraphs: These are not hypothetical. They are the four patterns that account for most of the wasted money we see in this community, and all four are easy to avoid once named.

The first and largest is the weekly hour bought as insurance. A parent sees a grade 4 at the end of DP1 term one, books a weekly session, and keeps it for eighteen months because stopping feels risky. Nothing is targeted, so nothing is finished, and at the specialist monthly band of AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 that is a five-figure commitment in dirhams for work that a phased set of blocks would have done for a fraction. The test is simple: if nobody can say what the current block is for, it is insurance rather than treatment.

The second is paying specialist rates for supervision. A student who is not doing the practice does not need a better explanation, and an AED 270 hour spent watching them complete a problem set is the most expensive form of babysitting available in Dubai. The market prices supervision at AED 33 to AED 65 online for a reason. Diagnose which one your child needs by looking at a marked assessment: marks lost on unattempted work is a supervision problem, the same error repeated three times is a teaching problem.

The third is funding content when the loss is in writing. Paper 2 carries 44% of the chemistry grade and awards marks to steps in an argument. A student who knows the chemistry and writes the conclusion without the reasoning loses most of those marks, and no amount of further content teaching recovers them. This is the single most common misdirected spend in DP2, and the fix is eight to twelve sessions of writing answers under timing and having them marked immediately.

The fourth is starting the investigation support too late. Once a research question has been approved and data collected, the room to improve the design criterion has gone, and a late block can only tidy the analysis and evaluation. The same money spent three weeks earlier, on pressure-testing the question before it was submitted, protects twice as many marks.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: why it consumes the most paid hours
paragraphs: Across the Diploma chemistry students we see from Emirates Living, organic chemistry takes more paid hours than any other part of the course, and a large share of those hours are spent badly. Understanding why changes how much it costs to fix.

The core problem is that organic chemistry is usually learned as a list and assessed as a reasoning task. A student memorises that a halogenoalkane with hydroxide gives an alcohol, and can reproduce it. The paper then asks why one pathway dominates over another, or what the mechanism implies about the structure of the product, and the list provides nothing. Each memorised reaction is a separate fact to a student working this way, which means the revision load grows linearly while the marks do not, and that is what turns organic chemistry into an apparently bottomless demand for sessions.

Taught as mechanisms rather than outcomes, the same content collapses into a handful of patterns about where electrons come from and where they go. That is a genuinely different teaching job, it takes eight to twelve sessions rather than an open-ended commitment, and it is the main reason a chemistry specialist is worth more per hour than a general science tutor. A tutor who draws the arrows one at a time on a shared whiteboard, has the student redraw them, and saves the file for revision is doing something a list cannot do.

It is also where the choice of band matters most. Supervision at AED 50 an hour cannot teach mechanisms, because the work requires somebody who can answer why rather than confirm whether. At the other end, a premium examiner-led rate buys nothing additional here: the content is well defined and the teaching requirement is skill rather than privileged knowledge. The named-specialist band at AED 200 to AED 300 is where this work sits, and twelve sessions in that band is a far smaller number than most families expect once they stop thinking in terms of a standing weekly hour.

sections.heading: Value per paid hour, component by component
paragraphs: If a family has a limited number of sessions to buy, the question is which component returns the most marks for each one. The answer is not evenly distributed, and it changes with how far through the Diploma a student is.

Extended response on Paper 2 is the highest-return target for most DP2 students. It carries 44% of the grade, the losses are structural rather than knowledge-based, and the remedy is mechanical: write answers under timing, mark them immediately against the real allocation, repeat. Eight to twelve sessions typically produces visible movement, because the same fault appears in every question and fixing it once fixes all of them.

The data-based section of Paper 1 is the second-best target and the most under-bought. It rewards graph work, uncertainty handling and saying what a gradient or an anomaly actually means, and schools cover those skills early and then assume them. A short block here is cheap and it pays twice, because the same skills carry marks in the investigation.

At the other end, multiple choice is a poor target for paid hours, because the fix is volume of timed practice rather than teaching, and a student can do that alone. And content revision across whole themes is the weakest use of money in DP2 specifically, because there is not enough time to rebuild a foundation and the marks available from technique are larger. In DP1 the ranking reverses: content and the quantitative foundation are the right targets, and Paper 2 technique is premature.

sections.heading: What investigation supervision should and should not cost
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is 20% of the chemistry grade, marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Because its scope is fixed, it is the only part of a Diploma where a family can genuinely know the cost in advance, and that makes it worth treating as a defined purchase rather than part of a rolling arrangement.

A realistic block is four to eight sessions. One or two before the research question is submitted, pressure-testing whether it yields a measurable relationship with equipment the school actually has. One or two on the method and on how the uncertainties will be handled, which is the difference between a data-analysis criterion that holds up and one that does not. Two or three on the student's own drafts, with feedback on which criterion is underserved. At the named-specialist band that is roughly AED 1,000 to AED 2,400 across the whole component, which is a knowable number.

What should not cost anything is the part some of this market sells. There are sites in this region selling completed internal assessments at published prices, and buying one is academic malpractice under the IB's own rules. The consequence falls on the student rather than the seller and it can be the loss of the Diploma. No part of what IB Gram arranges goes near that. A tutor teaches the published criteria, helps narrow a question, demonstrates a technique on entirely different data, and reads a draft the student wrote. A tutor does not write, rewrite, or supply data or conclusions.

The timing point is worth repeating because it is a money point as much as an academic one. Help bought before the research question is approved protects all four criteria. Help bought after data collection can only tidy two of them, and the same spend therefore buys half as much. If you are going to fund one block in DP1, fund this one and fund it early.

sections.heading: Tutoring spend in context, and the one number KHDA has fixed
paragraphs: Tutoring costs read very differently next to the other education numbers in a Dubai household budget, and one of those numbers has recently been fixed. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a Views family that is a known quantity in a budget where most lines are not.

The scale of the market around that decision is worth knowing too. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37% of enrolment, Indian 26%, US 14% and the International Baccalaureate 7%. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by 6%.

Against that, tutoring is a smaller and more controllable line than most families treat it as. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. The phased approach in the first table on this page lands well under the continuous version while targeting more. The honest framing is that chemistry tutoring is a discretionary purchase that should be bought in defined quantities, not a fixed cost of attending a Dubai school.

Two figures deliberately do not appear here. We publish no school fee band, because fees vary enormously by school and KHDA publishes them per school; look them up there rather than trusting a figure on a tutoring page. And we publish no examination entry fee, because entry as a private candidate is arranged and priced through a centre and we have no sourced figure to quote. Where we cannot source a number, it is left out rather than estimated.

sections.heading: Where to stop paying: the signals an arrangement has finished
paragraphs: No tutoring page writes this section, which is why it is the most useful one here. An arrangement that should have ended in February and runs until May is the single largest avoidable cost in a Diploma, and the signals that it is finished are recognisable if somebody tells you what to look for.

The first signal is in the session notes. If the note from week ten is describing the same weakness as the note from week three, the arrangement is not working and more of it will not help; the answer is a different tutor or a different target, not another term. If the notes have moved on and the current target is vague, the block has done its job and the honest move is to stop and see whether the gain holds. Chemistry grades lag teaching by a few weeks, so a pause is a legitimate test rather than a risk.

The second signal is the student. A child who arrives at a session with specific questions is getting value. A child who arrives with nothing and waits to be taught has either outgrown the arrangement or never needed it, and in both cases the money is buying attendance. This is a harder conversation than a scheduling one, and it is worth having at the six-week mark rather than the six-month mark.

The third is the arithmetic. If the target was organic mechanisms and the student can now reason from a mechanism to a product rather than recall a list, the thing you paid for has happened. Keeping the slot because exams are coming converts treatment back into insurance, at AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 a month in the specialist band. The better use of that money is to hold it until DP2 term one, when extended-response work becomes the highest-return target in the whole course, and to buy a defined block then.

sections.heading: Starting from The Views without overspending
paragraphs: Begin by deciding what you are buying, which is a question almost nobody is asked. Is the problem a quantitative foundation, a body of content, a piece of assessed work, or the way answers are written? Those are four different purchases at four different prices, and buying the wrong one for two terms costs more than any hourly rate difference in this market.

The fastest way to find out is a marked script. A recent assessment or mock with the marks on it shows whether the loss is in recall, in calculation, in the data-based section or in extended-response writing. Bring it to the free first lesson, which is one per family, about thirty minutes, with no charge and no card details taken. A tutor who reads the script and names the pattern has told you what to buy. A tutor who offers to work through the syllabus has not, and you have spent nothing establishing that.

Then buy a block rather than a subscription. Four to ten sessions with a named target, a review at the end, and a deliberate decision about whether to continue. That structure is harder to sell than a standing weekly hour and it is cheaper for the family and better for the student, because every session has to justify itself. If a weekly arrangement genuinely is the right answer, which happens where the foundation gap is real, it should be entered into knowingly rather than by default.

The limits, stated before anything is booked. Nobody travels to a UAE address; home visiting is an India-only service. We publish no fixed price list, no grade guarantee and no examination dates, because the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically and your school's coordinator is the only reliable source. We do not reproduce IB subject guides, past papers or mark schemes; we reference them. We do not write any part of an investigation. We claim no approval from the IB, KHDA or the Ministry of Education. And where no chemistry specialist is free in your slot, you get a realistic date instead of a general science tutor at the same price.

Online supervision from student tutors is advertised from roughly AED 33 to AED 65. Those are other providers' published October 2026 figures, not ours. We publish no fixed price list, because a ten-session block and a two-year arrangement are not the same product.

faqs.question: Should I budget by the hour or by the term?
faqs.answer: By the phase, which is neither. Higher Level chemistry has three cost moments: the quantitative wall in the first term of DP1, the investigation in the middle of DP1, and extended-response technique in DP2. Each needs a defined block of roughly six to twelve sessions. Planned that way the two-year total sits well below a continuous weekly hour, which at the specialist monthly band of AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 runs to a five-figure commitment in dirhams across the same period and targets nothing in particular.

faqs.question: Is a weekly session for two years ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, where there is a genuine foundation gap in quantitative chemistry that needs time rather than intensity. It is the right answer far less often than it is bought. The test is whether anybody can say what the current block is for: if the answer is general reassurance, you are buying insurance rather than treatment. Enter a long weekly arrangement knowingly, review it every six weeks against the session notes, and taper it once the gap it was bought to close has closed.

faqs.question: Why is organic chemistry so expensive to fix?
faqs.answer: Because it is usually learned as a list and assessed as reasoning. A student who memorises that a particular reagent gives a particular product can reproduce it, and then the paper asks why one pathway dominates, and the list gives nothing. Every reaction is a separate fact, so the revision load grows without the marks following. Taught as patterns of electron movement instead, the same content becomes eight to twelve sessions rather than an open-ended demand, and that is what the specialist band is actually buying.

faqs.question: Which chemistry component gives the most marks per paid hour?
faqs.answer: In DP2, extended response on Paper 2, which carries 44% of the grade and where losses are structural rather than knowledge-based. Eight to twelve sessions of writing answers under timing and having them marked immediately usually produces visible movement, because the same fault repeats in every question. The second-best and most under-bought is the data-based section of Paper 1, which also pays into the investigation. In DP1 the ranking reverses: the quantitative foundation comes first.

faqs.question: How much should investigation support cost?
faqs.answer: At the named-specialist band, roughly AED 1,000 to AED 2,400 across the whole component, because the scope is fixed: four criteria, twenty-four marks, four to eight sessions. One or two before the research question is submitted, one or two on method and uncertainties, two or three on the student's own drafts. Timing changes the value more than the rate does. Bought before the question is approved it protects all four criteria; bought after data collection it can only tidy two of them.

faqs.question: Is it ever acceptable to buy a ready-made internal assessment?
faqs.answer: No, and you should treat any offer to do so as a warning about the provider. Sites in this region sell completed internal assessments at published prices. Buying one is academic malpractice under the IB's own rules, the consequence falls on your child rather than on the seller, and it can mean the loss of the Diploma. A tutor teaches the published criteria, helps narrow a question, demonstrates a technique on different data and gives feedback on drafts your child wrote. Nothing more than that.

faqs.question: Is a group chemistry class in Barsha Heights cheaper in real terms?
faqs.answer: For shared Standard Level content, genuinely yes, provided the students are at the same level with similar gaps. For Higher Level organic mechanisms, no, because the problems are individual and the class has to teach to an average. Count the full cost as well: a fifteen-minute drive each way at 17:30 plus waiting turns a sixty-minute class into a two-hour commitment for a parent, and that hour belongs in any honest comparison against an online session at the kitchen desk.

faqs.question: Does an in-home chemistry tutor cost more for the same teaching?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the premium is travel rather than expertise. The market quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. In a tower community the booked hour also shrinks: visitor bays in Emirates Living fill from about 18:00, and a tutor with a second booking across Interchange 5 starts watching the clock at the fifty-minute mark. You pay more and receive fewer teaching minutes.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child needs teaching or just supervision?
faqs.answer: Look at a marked assessment. If the lost marks are on work that was never attempted, you have a supervision problem and the market prices that at AED 33 to AED 65 an hour online. If the lost marks are on work that was attempted and came out wrong in the same way three times, you have a teaching problem and the named-specialist band is appropriate. Paying AED 270 an hour to watch a child complete a problem set is the most expensive mistake available in this market.

faqs.question: What questions should I ask before paying for the first session?
faqs.answer: Four. Is the figure per hour or per session, since a fifty-minute session priced hourly costs you a sixth more than you think. Is marking between sessions included, because for extended-response chemistry that is where much of the value sits. Will the tutor work from my child's school materials and deadlines or their own scheme. And what happens to unused sessions in a monthly package, because advertised Dubai packages run AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and families travel.

faqs.question: Are tutoring costs going up along with school fees in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School fees are the clearer picture: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase for private schools in the emirate for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Tutoring is unregulated by comparison and the published bands have a very wide spread, from roughly AED 33 to AED 650 an hour. That spread is why checking a quote against the published market, as the bands on this page let you do, is worth fifteen minutes.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest point to start chemistry support?
faqs.answer: The summer before DP1, or the first term of DP1 at the latest. Six to eight sessions on moles, concentration and proportional reasoning at that point prevents the problem that otherwise contaminates every topic afterwards, and almost nobody buys it because nothing has visibly gone wrong yet. The most expensive point to start is the second term of DP2, when there is no time to rebuild a foundation and the only remaining gains are in technique and timing.

faqs.question: How do we know when to stop paying for chemistry sessions?
faqs.answer: The session notes tell you. If the note from week ten describes the same weakness as week three, change the tutor or the target rather than extending the arrangement. If the notes have moved on but the current target is vague, the block has finished its job and pausing is a legitimate test, because grades lag teaching by a few weeks. A student arriving at sessions with no questions of their own is a third signal: at that point the money is buying attendance.

faqs.question: What happens if no chemistry specialist is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a date, and you are not charged to wait. Higher Level chemistry in the 17:00 to 18:00 window is one of the tighter combinations in Dubai, because every Emirates Living family wants the same hour. The alternative to saying so is placing a general science tutor at the same rate, which costs a term before anyone admits the mismatch. Usually the fix is an adjacent evening or a weekend morning; occasionally it is a short wait, and that decision is yours.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-the-views.closingHeading: Buy a block with a target, not a slot with a hope
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-the-views.closingBody: The number that decides what Diploma chemistry costs your household is not the hourly rate. It is whether each session is aimed at something nameable. Send a marked script, tell us the level and which evenings are free, and we will say which of the four purchases you are actually looking at and roughly what it should cost at the published Dubai bands. The first lesson is free, one per family, about thirty minutes, with no card details taken. If the honest answer is that you need eight sessions rather than two years, that is what you will be told.

intro.heading: Chemistry fails in specific, nameable places
paragraphs: Chemistry is the Diploma science where a parent can be told exactly what is wrong. The subject is built from a small number of recurring operations — a mole calculation, a mechanism, an energy cycle, a titration curve, a structure deduced from spectra — and a student either executes each one reliably or does not. So a marked paper does not have to produce the vague verdict that chemistry is difficult. It can produce a sentence like: the mole calculations are secure, the organic mechanisms are memorised rather than reasoned, and every energetics question with a negative enthalpy lost its sign.

That sentence is what the first session should deliver, and it is the difference between a plan and a programme of general support. A student whose organic chemistry is memorised performs well on familiar molecules and collapses on unfamiliar ones, which is precisely what the Higher Level paper presents. A student whose mole work is shaky fails in titration, yield, gas volume and equilibrium questions, and the report will list four weak topics rather than one weak operation.

So this page works through the syllabus operations where marks actually go: the calculation types and the trap in each, the energetics sign conventions, the mechanism types and what a mark scheme wants drawn, the strength-and-concentration confusion that survives into Higher Level, and the systematic method for deducing a structure from mass spectrometry, infrared and nuclear magnetic resonance together. It is deliberately specific, because the pages currently ranking for this search between them name almost no syllabus content at all.

Tilal Al Ghaf contributes one practical advantage worth using. The community has a British-curriculum school inside its boundary and DAMAC Hills and Dubai Sports City next door have their own provision, so pupils are frequently home before four. Chemistry is precision work — a rounding decision at step one survives to the final answer — and a student at four-thirty makes arithmetic errors at a far lower rate than the same student at seven. That is a scheduling advantage with a mark consequence.

The scientific investigation carries 20% of the chemistry grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria. In chemistry the characteristic trap is a reaction whose measurable change is too small or too fast for school apparatus, which means the mark is largely decided before any solution is made up. It is the earliest real deadline in the subject and the point where a tutor can most legitimately help.

IB Gram delivers chemistry tuition to Tilal Al Ghaf as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Chemistry teaching is a shared screen with every line of a calculation visible, a marked mechanism and a conversation about an investigation design, none of which needs anyone in the room.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-tilal-al-gha.subjectsIntro: These are the chemistry operations Tilal Al Ghaf families ask about, each with the specific trap attached. Read this list against a marked paper and the diagnosis is usually obvious.

subjects.name: The mole concept
subjects.description: Amount of substance, molar mass, concentration and gas volumes. The load-bearing operation: titration, yield, limiting reagent and equilibrium questions all rest on it. The trap is units — moles per cubic decimetre against moles per cubic centimetre — which costs more across a paper than any conceptual gap.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and limiting reagents
subjects.description: Reacting masses, percentage yield and atom economy. The trap is identifying the limiting reagent before calculating anything else; students who work from the wrong reactant produce an internally consistent answer that is entirely wrong and lose the whole question.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Electron configuration, ionisation energy trends and periodic behaviour, with transition metal chemistry at Higher Level. Marks go to students who explain trends from shielding and effective nuclear charge rather than reciting them. Transition metals are self-contained and respond well to focused work.

subjects.name: Bonding, structure and shape
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces and molecular geometry, with hybridisation and formal charge at Higher Level. Shape and polarity questions are lost by students who know the theory and do not count lone pairs before deciding the geometry.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess cycles, bond enthalpies and, at Higher Level, entropy and Gibbs free energy. Sign convention decides the marks: a correct magnitude with the wrong sign scores nothing. Drawing the Hess cycle before calculating almost eliminates the error.

subjects.name: Kinetics
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Rate, collision theory, activation energy and, at Higher Level, rate laws, orders of reaction and the Arrhenius treatment. Determining order from data is a procedure teachable in one session and then permanent, which makes it good value late in the course.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Dynamic equilibrium, Le Chatelier reasoning and, at Higher Level, equilibrium constant calculations. Written answers lose marks by saying the equilibrium shifts without naming the change driving it; calculations lose marks to assumptions that are never stated.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and buffers
subjects.levels: HL and SL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Strength against concentration, pH scales and, at Higher Level, weak acid calculations, buffers and titration curves. The strength-and-concentration confusion is the most persistent conceptual error in the course and survives into Higher Level unless addressed directly.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half-equations, electrochemical cells and, at Higher Level, cell potentials and electrolysis calculations. Balancing half-equations in acidic or basic conditions is a procedure rather than an insight and is reliably learnable in a session or two.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.levels: HL and SL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Functional groups, reaction pathways and, at Higher Level, nucleophilic substitution and electrophilic addition mechanisms. The commonest Dubai request and the commonest failure: memorising products instead of reasoning from electron movement, which fails on any unfamiliar molecule.

subjects.name: Spectroscopy and structure determination
subjects.description: Mass spectrometry, infrared and nuclear magnetic resonance used together to deduce a structure. Systematic and therefore highly learnable, and reliably skipped in revision because students treat it as an add-on rather than as a method with a fixed order.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and data processing
subjects.levels: HL and SL, examined and internally assessed
subjects.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, and consistent significant figures. Examined in the data section of the written papers and central to the investigation, so time spent here is paid for twice and is almost always under-taught.

sections.heading: The calculation types, and the trap in each
paragraphs: Chemistry calculations are not a single skill. They are a handful of distinct operations, each with a characteristic failure, and a student is usually reliable in some and not others. A diagnosis that says 'struggles with calculations' is therefore almost useless; one that says 'secure on molar mass, loses limiting reagent questions, and drops units in titration work' is a three-session plan.

The unit problem deserves naming first because it is the largest single source of lost marks in the subject. Concentration appears as moles per cubic decimetre in most of the syllabus and volumes are routinely given in cubic centimetres, so every solution question contains a conversion. Students who hold the conversion in their heads lose marks they would keep if they wrote it down, and the fix is procedural rather than conceptual: write the conversion as a line of working, every time, until it is automatic.

The second is compounding. Mark schemes credit the steps, so a multi-step calculation with no visible working loses everything when an early rounding decision propagates, whereas the same error with full working loses one mark and keeps the rest. Students who calculate quickly in their heads are the most affected, and they are usually surprised to learn that a strength they have been praised for since primary school is costing them marks.

The third is the limiting reagent, which fails differently. A student who works from the wrong reactant produces a clean, internally consistent answer that is entirely wrong, and because the arithmetic is correct they often cannot see what happened. The fix is a habit: identify and state the limiting reagent as a separate step before any mass or volume is calculated. The table below sets out the operations with the trap attached to each.

sections.heading: Energetics: the sign conventions that decide the marks
paragraphs: Energetics is the topic where students most often produce correct chemistry and score nothing. The reason is narrow and fixable: the sign carries the meaning, and a correctly calculated magnitude with the wrong sign is a wrong answer rather than a partially right one. Exothermic changes are negative, endothermic positive, and every operation in the topic either preserves or reverses that.

The commonest error is sign reversal in a Hess cycle. When a step is used in the opposite direction to the way it was given, its enthalpy change reverses, and a student working algebraically without a diagram will reverse some and not others. Students who draw the cycle before doing any arithmetic almost never make the error, because the arrows make the direction visible. That is a procedural change achievable in one or two sessions and permanent afterwards.

The second is bond enthalpy calculations, where the convention runs the opposite way to intuition: breaking bonds is endothermic and forming them exothermic, so the arithmetic is bonds broken minus bonds formed. Students who memorise the formula without the reasoning invert it under pressure. The third is calorimetry, where the mass used is the mass of the solution being heated rather than the mass of the solute reacting, and the sign has to be applied to the enthalpy change rather than to the temperature change.

At Higher Level the same discipline extends to entropy and Gibbs free energy, where a spontaneity conclusion depends entirely on getting signs right across two quantities and a temperature. A student who is unreliable on signs at Standard Level will be unreliable on spontaneity at Higher Level, which is why this block is worth doing properly early rather than patching later. It is also why energetics questions are a good diagnostic: a student's sign discipline is visible in a single question.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: mechanisms, not product lists
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is the commonest chemistry request in Dubai and the one most often studied in the least useful way. Students learn what named reactions produce and perform well on familiar molecules, and then meet an unfamiliar one in the Higher Level paper and have nothing. The marks are in reasoning from electron movement, and that reasoning transfers to any structure.

The reasoning is a small number of questions asked in order. Where is the electron-rich site and where is the electron-poor one? Which bond is polarised, and in which direction? Which species is the nucleophile and which the electrophile? What intermediate forms, and is it charged? What leaves, and why is it a good leaving group? A student who asks those five questions can handle a molecule they have never seen, which is exactly what the paper requires.

The mechanisms themselves are also marked on how they are drawn, which students under-estimate. A curly arrow must start from a lone pair or a bond and end where the electrons go; an arrow drawn from the wrong place loses the mark even where the overall transformation is right. Charges must be shown on intermediates. Partial charges should be marked where polarisation is being used in the argument. These are conventions, and conventions are teachable in a way that chemical intuition is not.

At Higher Level the organic content extends substantially, and the structural distinctions matter: whether a substitution proceeds in one step or two, whether the carbon is primary or tertiary, whether a reagent attacks the most or least substituted position. Each of those is a reasoning step rather than a fact to be recalled. Rebuilding a memorising student into a reasoning one takes a term, and it is the commonest second-year request from capable students in this part of Dubai.

sections.heading: Acids and bases: strength is not concentration
paragraphs: This is the most persistent conceptual confusion in the whole course and it survives into Higher Level in students who have been taught it several times. Strength describes how completely an acid dissociates; concentration describes how much of it is present. A concentrated weak acid and a dilute strong acid are different things, and almost every acids question in the Diploma depends on the distinction somewhere.

The confusion shows up in predictable places. A student asked to compare the pH of two solutions reasons from concentration alone and ignores dissociation. A student asked why a weak acid's titration curve has a different shape describes the curve rather than attributing the shape to partial dissociation and the buffer region. A student asked to explain why a weak acid reacts with the same stoichiometry but a different rate conflates the two ideas entirely.

The diagnostic for this is a single question and worth asking early: which has the lower pH, a dilute solution of a strong acid or a concentrated solution of a weak one, and what information would you need to decide? A student who answers immediately from one variable has the confusion; a student who asks for the dissociation constant and the concentrations does not. Resolving it takes one or two sessions and immediately improves every subsequent acids question.

At Higher Level the topic extends into weak acid calculations, buffers and titration curves, all of which assume the distinction is secure. Buffer questions in particular require holding both ideas at once: a buffer resists pH change because a weak acid and its conjugate base are both present in appreciable concentration. A student who has not separated strength from concentration cannot reason about that, and no amount of practice on buffer arithmetic fixes the underlying confusion.

sections.heading: Spectroscopy: a method with a fixed order
paragraphs: Structure determination from spectra is the most systematic part of the chemistry syllabus and therefore the most teachable, and it is reliably the least revised because students treat it as an add-on rather than as a method. There is a fixed order to work in, and following it turns an intimidating question into a sequence of small deductions.

Start with the mass spectrum for the molecular mass, which constrains the possible formulae immediately. Then use the infrared spectrum to identify functional groups from the characteristic absorption regions, which narrows the possibilities further — the presence or absence of a carbonyl, a hydroxyl or a carbon-nitrogen bond eliminates whole families of structures. Then use the nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum for the carbon or hydrogen environments: how many distinct environments, in what ratio, and with what splitting pattern.

Each technique on its own is ambiguous and the three together are usually decisive, which is the examiner's point in giving all three. Students lose marks by working from one spectrum and guessing, or by identifying the functional group correctly and then proposing a structure with the wrong number of environments. Writing down what each spectrum has told you before proposing anything is the discipline that earns the marks.

Because the method is fixed, this is one of the best-value blocks in the subject: two or three sessions on the order of operations and the characteristic regions, and a student can approach any structure determination question systematically for the rest of the course. It is also near-perfect for online delivery, since the work is reading spectra on a shared screen and annotating them together, which is easier than passing a printed spectrum back and forth across a table.

sections.heading: A past-paper routine for chemistry
paragraphs: Chemistry past-paper work is usually done in the least productive order: questions attempted, answers checked against a worked solution, mistakes noted as careless. That routine teaches almost nothing, because it does not distinguish between the operations and it treats every error as the same kind of error.

What works has four elements. First, work by operation rather than by paper at the start: a set of mole questions, then a set of energetics questions, then a set of mechanisms. This exposes which operations are reliable and which are not, which a mixed paper obscures. Second, enforce visible working on every multi-step calculation, because the mark scheme credits the steps and a student who writes nothing cannot see where the error entered either.

Third, mark against the published scheme rather than against a worked answer, and categorise each loss: unit error, sign error, limiting reagent, mechanism convention, command term, or genuine content gap. Those six categories cover the large majority of chemistry losses and each points to a different and specific repair. A tally across three or four papers produces a diagnosis no single paper gives.

Fourth, once the operations are reliable, switch to full papers under timing. Chemistry papers are long and the error rate rises towards the end, which only becomes visible under real conditions. This is where Tilal Al Ghaf's early slot earns its keep: a full paper at four-thirty is a fair test, and the same paper at seven in the evening measures tiredness. A misleadingly poor result late in the day knocks confidence for no useful reason.

sections.heading: The investigation, and the chemistry-specific trap
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each — research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation — and carries 20% of the grade at both levels. Confirm the current criteria with your child's teacher, since the IB revises its guides. What distinguishes chemistry is where the design fails.

In chemistry the trap is measurability against school apparatus. A student picks a reaction that is genuinely interesting and then discovers the colour change is too subtle to quantify, the reaction too fast to time by hand, the temperature change inside the resolution of a school thermometer, or the yield too small to weigh reliably. The data then shows noise rather than a relationship, and no amount of careful writing afterwards recovers it. The most valuable hour a chemistry tutor spends is asking, before any apparatus is booked, whether the proposed change can actually be measured with the equipment available.

The second chemistry-specific issue is significant figures and uncertainty carried consistently through a multi-step calculation. Data analysis rewards correct processing and genuine uncertainty treatment, and a chemistry investigation usually involves several steps between the raw measurement and the reported result, so inconsistency compounds. This is the same skill examined in the data section of the written papers, which means the teaching is paid for twice.

Conclusion and evaluation together carry twelve of the twenty-four marks and are the cheapest to improve, because they reward thinking rather than apparatus. A conclusion must answer the stated research question, justified by the data and compared with accepted chemistry where relevant. An evaluation must identify specific methodological weaknesses — a reagent that degrades, a reaction sensitive to temperature, a measurement with poor resolution — and propose realistic improvements rather than mentioning human error.

Chemistry is unusually well suited to being bought as blocks rather than as open-ended weekly support, because the operations are discrete and most repair in one to three sessions. A units-and-working block is two sessions. An energetics sign block is one or two. A spectroscopy method block is two or three. A kinetics order-determination block is one. Each has a calculable price at any band and a target you can check on the next paper.

The expensive exceptions are worth naming honestly. Rebuilding organic chemistry from memorised to reasoned takes a term, because it is a change in how the student thinks rather than a procedure to learn. Rebuilding quantitative fluency where the mole concept was never secure takes a holiday block at four or five sessions a week, because fluency comes from volume. sections.heading: Practical work, honesty and the permit position
paragraphs: Practical chemistry happens at school. Your child's school has the reagents, the balances, the fume cupboard and the supervision, and it runs the laboratory sessions in which investigation data is collected. No tutor in any delivery format runs experiments for a student, and an in-home tutor arriving at a Tilal Al Ghaf villa with a burette is not what in-home tutoring looks like either. What a tutor contributes is design, uncertainty and data treatment, and feedback on the student's own writing, all of which work on a shared screen.

On assessed work the boundary is firm. There are providers in this region selling completed internal assessments at published prices; submitting one is academic misconduct and the consequence falls on the student. A tutor may teach any chemistry the investigation requires, test whether a design is measurable, explain each criterion and its descriptors, teach uncertainty propagation, and read the student's own draft and say what is not working. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply data, choose the research question outright, or edit a draft into something the student did not produce.

On materials: syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. A tutor works from legitimately obtained material and teaches the student to read the assessment criteria themselves. We also do not describe tutors as IB examiners where current status cannot be evidenced, and examiner experience gives no access to marking, boundaries or unseen paper content.

On regulation: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Those operating without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published — Khaleej Times reported the ministry did not specify the amounts — so distrust any page printing a figure. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from the IB, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education.

faqs.question: What specifically goes wrong in IB chemistry calculations?
faqs.answer: Three things, and they fail differently. Unit handling, where concentration in moles per cubic decimetre meets volumes in cubic centimetres and the conversion is held in the head rather than written down. Compounding, where a multi-step calculation with no visible working loses the whole question because the mark scheme credits the steps. And the limiting reagent, where a student works from the wrong reactant and produces a clean, internally consistent answer that is entirely wrong. Each is a one or two session repair once named.

faqs.question: Why does my child's organic chemistry collapse on unfamiliar molecules?
faqs.answer: Because they learned what named reactions produce rather than reasoning from electron movement. The reasoning is five questions asked in order: where are the electron-rich and electron-poor sites, which bond is polarised and in which direction, which species is the nucleophile, what intermediate forms and is it charged, and what leaves and why. A student who asks those can handle a structure they have never seen, which is exactly what the Higher Level paper presents.

faqs.question: How do curly arrow conventions affect marks?
faqs.answer: Directly, and students under-estimate it. A curly arrow must start from a lone pair or from a bond and end where the electrons actually go; an arrow drawn from an atom rather than from its lone pair loses the mark even where the overall transformation is correct. Charges on intermediates must be shown, and partial charges should be marked where polarisation is part of the argument. These are conventions rather than chemistry, which makes them quickly teachable and quickly fixable.

faqs.question: Why do correct enthalpy answers score zero?
faqs.answer: Because the sign carries the meaning, so a correct magnitude with the wrong sign is a wrong answer rather than a partially right one. The commonest version is Hess cycle sign reversal: when a step is used in the opposite direction to the way it was given its enthalpy change reverses, and a student working algebraically reverses some and not others. Drawing the cycle before any arithmetic makes the directions visible and almost eliminates the error, in one or two sessions.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated one?
faqs.answer: Strength describes how completely an acid dissociates; concentration describes how much is present. A concentrated weak acid and a dilute strong acid are different things, and almost every acids question depends on the distinction somewhere. The diagnostic is one question: which has the lower pH, a dilute strong acid or a concentrated weak one, and what would you need to know to decide? A student who answers immediately from one variable has the confusion, and resolving it takes one or two sessions.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram visit homes in Tilal Al Ghaf for chemistry?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Practical chemistry happens in your child's school laboratory in any case, so no tutor in any format substitutes for it. What a screen does well is calculation with every line visible, annotated spectra shared by both parties, and marked mechanisms, which is most of what a chemistry session consists of.

faqs.question: How should structure determination questions be approached?
faqs.answer: In a fixed order, which is why this is the most teachable part of the syllabus. Mass spectrometry first for the molecular mass and likely fragments. Then infrared for functional groups present and, importantly, absent. Then nuclear magnetic resonance for the number of distinct environments, the integration ratio and the splitting pattern. Each technique alone is ambiguous and the three together are usually decisive. State what each spectrum has told you before proposing any structure.

faqs.question: Which chemistry blocks repair fastest?
faqs.answer: Most of them. A units-and-visible-working block is two sessions. An energetics sign block is one or two. A limiting reagent habit is one. A spectroscopy method block is two or three. Kinetics order determination from data is one. The two genuine exceptions are rebuilding organic chemistry from memorised to reasoned, which takes a term because it changes how the student thinks, and rebuilding quantitative fluency where the mole concept was never secure, which needs a holiday block.

faqs.question: How should my child use chemistry past papers?

faqs.question: Why does the session time matter for chemistry?
faqs.answer: Because chemistry is precision work and tiredness produces arithmetic errors rather than conceptual ones. A rounding decision at step one survives to the final answer, so a session spent on multi-step calculation gets a materially better return from an alert student. Tilal Al Ghaf has a school inside the community and neighbouring communities have their own provision, so pupils are often home before four and a four-thirty start is genuinely available here.

faqs.question: Where does the chemistry investigation usually fail?
faqs.answer: At the design stage, on measurability. A student picks an interesting reaction and finds the colour change too subtle to quantify, the reaction too fast to time by hand, the temperature change inside the resolution of a school thermometer, or the yield too small to weigh reliably. The data then shows noise rather than a relationship and later writing cannot recover it. One conversation about measurability before any apparatus is booked is the most valuable hour on a component worth a fifth of the grade.

faqs.question: Can anything still be improved once the investigation data is collected?
faqs.answer: Yes, and specifically twelve of the twenty-four marks. Research design and data analysis are largely fixed once the data exists, but conclusion and evaluation each carry six marks and reward thinking rather than apparatus. A conclusion must answer the stated research question, justified by the data and compared with accepted chemistry. An evaluation must name specific methodological weaknesses — a reagent that degrades, a temperature-sensitive reaction, a poor-resolution measurement — and propose realistic improvements rather than human error.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level chemistry much more work than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Roughly half again in tutoring hours, and the reason is structural. Higher Level deepens the treatment of most topics rather than appending separate ones, and adds transition metals, buffers, cell potentials and extended organic mechanisms. That means it cannot be prepared by learning the Standard Level course and bolting content on at the end. Whether it is worth it depends on the degree route: medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering commonly expect it, and the requirement is published on each university's course pages.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics give the cheapest marks late in the course?
faqs.answer: The procedural ones, because each is a session or two and then permanent. Determining order of reaction from kinetics data. Balancing half-equations in acidic or basic conditions. The spectroscopy method. Qualitative-analysis recall where the syllabus includes it. Alongside those, the leakage habits: units written as a line of working, the limiting reagent stated as a separate step, and signs attached to every enthalpy value. Together those usually outweigh another month of general content revision.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-town-square.tutorsIntro: Chemistry tutors matched to Town Square students teach the IB course at the level sat, and start by finding out which of the three layers is actually missing rather than re-covering the topic the student named.

intro.heading: Chemistry is three subjects, and only one of them is usually broken
paragraphs: Is there anybody near Town Square who actually knows this syllabus? That is the question behind the search, and the more useful version is sharper: does the tutor know which part of chemistry your child is missing? Because IB chemistry is not one skill. It is three layers stacked on each other, and a student can be entirely secure in one and absent in another while the school report says nothing more specific than that more effort is needed.

The bottom layer is quantitative. Moles, stoichiometry, concentration, limiting reagent, percentage yield, gas volumes. Every topic in the course uses it, which is why a weakness here presents as a weakness in everything and gets misdiagnosed as a general problem with chemistry. A student who can balance an equation but cannot carry a multi-step conversion through unit changes under time pressure will look weak in energetics, in equilibrium and in acids and bases simultaneously.

The middle layer is explanation. Chemistry punishes imprecision harder than any other Diploma science, and the marks go to answers that name the specific factor and finish the reasoning. Asked why one compound boils higher than another, an answer gesturing at intermolecular forces scores partial credit at best; an answer naming the force, comparing its strength and connecting that to the energy needed to separate molecules gets the marks. The difference is a habit, not knowledge.

The top layer is mechanism, and it is where most students announce that chemistry has become impossible. Organic chemistry taught as a catalogue of reagents and products survives until a question presents an unfamiliar molecule, at which point a perfect catalogue provides nothing. What the marks reward is reasoning about where a molecule is electron-poor and why a nucleophile goes there.

The practical realities out here shape delivery. Town Square is a Nshama community off Al Qudra Road, and Diploma chemistry students travel out — Motor City, Dubai Sports City, or further into Al Barsha and Silicon Oasis — so a half three finish becomes a 4:45pm arrival home. IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only.

And supply is genuinely thin. The IB is roughly 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools, spread citywide, with only the final two years sitting the Diploma. Chemistry at Higher Level is a narrow specialism inside that, and the probability that a qualified HL chemistry teacher lives near Town Square with a free weekday evening is low. Online matching is how that constraint disappears.

One practical note on sequence. Where two layers are weak at once, the bottom one gets fixed first regardless of which the student finds more alarming, because mechanism questions frequently carry a quantitative part and an explanation answer frequently rests on a calculated value. Working top down feels responsive and produces a term in which nothing quite consolidates. Working bottom up feels slower for a fortnight and then everything above it becomes cheaper to teach.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences, the chemistry strand

Fixing it in Years 9 and 10 is the cheapest preparation for Diploma chemistry available, and it predicts how a student will handle the investigation two years later.

The pairing is sensible, but the two reward different habits — biology rewards recall structured by command term, chemistry rewards finished explanation — and students sometimes import the biology habit into a chemistry paper.

programmes.description: Additional depth plus an extra written paper, with the investigation still at 20%. HL organic chemistry extends into reaction pathways and stereochemistry, and HL energetics into entropy and spontaneity. The level rewards building an argument across several steps and penalises formula lookup.

Families here frequently need precisely the specialist the neighbourhood cannot supply, which is the whole case for matching online rather than by distance.

programmes.name: IGCSE or MYP into Diploma chemistry

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-town-square.subjectsIntro: The chemistry topics and components Town Square students need work on, grouped by which of the three layers each one actually tests.

subjects.name: Moles, stoichiometry and concentration
subjects.description: The bottom layer, and the first thing a diagnostic should test whatever the student names. Multi-step conversions between mass, moles, volume and concentration, limiting reagent, percentage yield and gas calculations under time pressure rather than at leisure.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.description: The explanation layer at its most testable. Students state a trend in ionisation energy and lose every explanation mark because the answer labels the trend rather than naming shielding, nuclear charge and atomic radius as the reason behind it.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.description: Intermolecular forces, molecular geometry and the link between structure and physical property. Explaining a boiling point difference properly means naming the specific force, comparing its strength and completing the reasoning; partial answers lose most of the credit.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermodynamics
subjects.description: Enthalpy cycles, bond enthalpies and at HL entropy and Gibbs free energy. The chemistry is usually understood and the sign conventions are not, which produces answers that are internally consistent and wrong. A bookkeeping fix rather than a content one.

subjects.name: Equilibrium and kinetics
subjects.description: Le Chatelier reasoning, equilibrium constants, rate equations and at HL determining orders from data. Students state what shifts rather than explaining why, and the HL rate-determination questions expose data-handling confidence directly.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and redox
subjects.description: pH and pKa calculations, buffers, titration curves and electrochemical cells. Titration-curve interpretation and buffer reasoning are reliably examined and reliably weak, and both improve quickly with worked practice against the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry: mechanisms
subjects.description: The top layer. Nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and at HL longer pathways and stereochemistry. Marks are in explaining why a species attacks where it does using electron density and partial charge, not in reciting reagent-product pairs.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry at Higher Level: pathways
subjects.description: Planning a route to a target molecule and justifying each step. Students who treat every reaction as a separate fact cannot plan a route, and the fix is working backwards from the product, which is a technique almost nobody is taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainty in chemistry
subjects.description: Percentage uncertainty in titrations and mass measurements, significant figures justified by the apparatus, and whether a result supports a conclusion. Examined in the papers and decisive in the investigation's processing and evaluation marks.

subjects.name: The Chemistry investigation
subjects.levels: HL and SL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: An individual investigation against published criteria, lost most often at design: no measurable variable, insufficient repeats, a range too narrow to show a trend, or apparatus whose uncertainty swamps the effect being measured.

subjects.name: Chemical language and command terms
