sections.heading: Which of the three layers is actually missing?
paragraphs: This is the diagnostic question, and getting it right determines whether a term of tutoring changes anything. The three layers fail in distinguishable ways, and the symptoms a parent notices do not map neatly onto them.

A quantitative failure looks like inconsistency. The student is fine in a homework task with time to think and falls apart in a test. They lose marks across unrelated topics, which makes it look like a general problem with chemistry rather than a specific one with conversions under pressure. The giveaway is that the chemistry in their answers is usually correct and the arithmetic or the unit handling is not.

An explanation failure looks like unfairness. The student knows the material, says so, and is right — and still scores in the middle. Their answers are true and incomplete: the force is mentioned but not compared, the trend is stated but not caused, the conclusion is reached but not supported by the step that earns the mark. Parents often describe this as the examiner being harsh, and it is the most straightforwardly fixable of the three.

A mechanism failure looks like a wall. Everything was fine until the organic topic, and then it stopped. The student can recite reagents and products and cannot say anything about an unfamiliar molecule, because they were taught a catalogue rather than a way of reasoning. The table below sets out how each layer presents, what it is, and what the work actually is.

sections.heading: Why organic chemistry stops working, and how it is fixed
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is the most predictable topic in IB chemistry and it has a reputation for being the least. The reputation comes from how it is usually revised rather than from what it is.

Taught as a catalogue, it is a memory task of growing size: this reagent plus that substrate gives this product, under these conditions, learn the list. That approach works for a while because early questions ask for exactly what was memorised. It collapses the moment a paper presents an unfamiliar molecule or asks for the mechanism, because a catalogue has no generative power. The student has nothing to say, concludes that organic chemistry is impossible, and is reasonable to do so given what they were given.

Taught as reasoning, the same content becomes a small number of principles applied repeatedly. Where is this molecule electron-poor, and why. What is attracted to that position. What happens to the intermediate that forms. Why does one pathway dominate over another. A student who can run that sequence can attack a molecule they have never seen, which is exactly what the harder questions require and exactly what the catalogue approach cannot deliver.

The retraining is faster than parents expect, usually a matter of weeks rather than terms, because the content is already known. What changes is the order of operations: trace the mechanism out loud before writing anything, name the electron-poor site, justify the attack, then follow the intermediate. Done on unfamiliar molecules every week, the habit transfers. At Higher Level the same reasoning extends into planning a route backwards from a target product, which is a technique almost nobody is taught explicitly and which turns pathway questions from guesswork into procedure.
bullets: A reagent catalogue has no generative power on an unfamiliar molecule
Electron density and partial charge are the reasoning the marks reward

sections.heading: The investigation is decided before the data exists
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the chemistry grade comes from an individual investigation, and by the time most students ask for help the marks that mattered have been settled — in the fortnight when the research question was chosen and the method planned, rather than in the write-up.

The design faults recur. A research question whose independent variable cannot be varied systematically with school apparatus. A range so narrow that any trend sits inside the uncertainty. Too few repeats to say anything honest about reliability. A controlled variable that was named but not controlled, discovered at the evaluation stage when the only remaining option is to admit it. And the specifically chemical one: a titration-based investigation whose apparatus uncertainty is larger than the effect being measured.

None of those can be rescued by a better conclusion, which is why a tutor who reads the criteria with the student in week one is worth several who read a draft in week ten. The permitted work is substantial and genuinely useful: explaining what each criterion rewards and its mark allocation, testing whether a proposed question is feasible with available equipment, checking the planned range and repeats will generate analysable data, pointing out that a chosen method's uncertainty will swamp the result, and giving criterion-level feedback on a draft the student has written.

The line on the other side of that list is absolute, and it is worth putting in chemistry terms. A tutor does not write a section, does not supply the titration data or run the processing calculations, does not hand over a model investigation to be adapted, and does not edit a draft into a finished state. Two signatures sit beneath the submitted work - the student's authorship declaration and the supervisor's alongside it - and where that declaration proves false the IB withdraws awards for malpractice. The reason this belongs on a Town Square page rather than in a policy document is that the same search which found us also returns operators selling completed Internal Assessments, one of them advertising at AED 3,750. Hold that figure against what it buys: AED 3,750 is a substantial block of legitimate investigation coaching, spent instead on risking the entire Diploma rather than one component.

sections.heading: What online chemistry tuition can and cannot do
paragraphs: The reasonable objection to online chemistry is the bench, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. Nobody on a screen can stand beside a burette and correct a student's eye level at the meniscus.

What is true is that bench technique is a small share of the assessed marks and the assessed part of it happens at school. Titration precision, dilution, gravimetric handling — taught and practised in the laboratory, and no tutor substitutes for that, in person or online. A provider claiming otherwise is overselling, and a parent should treat the claim as a signal.

What one-to-one work adds is the reasoning around the bench, where most of the available marks actually sit. Predicting what an experiment should produce before it runs. Deciding what to do with an anomalous result rather than quietly discarding it. Calculating percentage uncertainty from the apparatus and judging whether the effect exceeds it. Writing up so that the processing and evaluation criteria are addressed rather than merely satisfied in spirit. All of that is paper-and-screen work.

The same applies to the written papers, where experimental questions ask a student to evaluate a method rather than perform one: identify the flaw, name the controlled variable that was missed, say whether the data supports the stated conclusion. That is examinable reasoning and it is what we teach. Ask your child's school which practical components are assessed and how, and we will match a tutor who has prepared students for those specific components.

sections.heading: Fitting chemistry into a Town Square week
paragraphs: Chemistry needs a particular kind of hour, and the layer being worked on decides which. Mechanism work especially requires holding several things in mind at once — structure, charge, what moved where — and a tired student cannot do it. Quantitative drilling tolerates a later slot. Explanation practice sits somewhere between.

The timetable out here is tight. A half three finish in Motor City or Dubai Sports City means a 4:45pm arrival home once the Al Qudra approach traffic is counted; from an inner-city school it is nearer five. Because nobody is driving to you, a session can begin at 4:45pm, which for a Year 12 student working on mechanism or new content is usually the best hour available. For Year 13 the better choice is often 8pm for ninety minutes, when a full past-paper section plus marking fits without rushing the marking.

Weekend mornings are the underused option and for chemistry they are particularly effective during an investigation term: two uninterrupted hours on method design or data processing is worth more than three scattered weekday half-hours, and it competes with nothing else in the week.

Ramadan gets planned rather than discovered. School days shorten and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so Town Square families typically move to a late-morning, early-afternoon or post-Iftar slot, or pause part of the month and resume with a heavier block. Prayer times are built into the slot from the start. What we work to avoid is the drift of cancel, reschedule, cancel — in chemistry that breaks the thread quickly, because mechanism work builds directly on the previous session.

sections.heading: Chemistry Higher Level and the degree routes that require it
paragraphs: A large share of the chemistry enquiries we take from this corridor are really about medicine, dentistry or pharmacy, and the framing matters because in those cases the subject is a hard requirement rather than a preference.

What can be said plainly: many medical, dental and pharmacy programmes specify chemistry, frequently at Higher Level and often alongside a second science. What we will not do is publish a points threshold or an entry requirement for any named university, because those are set by the institution, change between cycles, and differ across UAE, UK, European and North American systems. Check the published requirement of the actual programmes under consideration, for the year of entry rather than the current one.

Nor will we suggest that tutoring is required for an admissions outcome. That would be a false-urgency claim about a competitive process whose variables — interview performance, admissions testing, personal statement, school reference, the strength of a particular year's applicant pool — sit well outside a chemistry tutor's reach. What chemistry support can do is narrower and real: make sure the Higher Level chemistry grade is not the thing that removes the option.

The planning consequence is about timing. A student aiming at a chemistry-requiring degree needs the HL grade secure by the end of Year 12, not improving through Year 13, because applications and predicted grades are made before the final result exists. That pushes the sensible start date for support to early Year 12 — which is also when it is cheapest and when the quantitative layer is still straightforward to fix.

sections.heading: What chemistry tutoring costs in this market
paragraphs: Sort the published Dubai figures by what each tier can actually teach and the market stops reading as one long list. At the bottom, budget online advertises from AED 33-65 an hour - Tutopiya at AED 33-52, EdFlik at AED 45-65 - which buys the quantitative layer and not much beyond it. A qualified online subject tutor sits at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Named IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists form the band above at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate putting the same band at AED 200-450 plus, while BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Cutting across all of it, in-home visits are AED 180-500 including travel, which prices the drive out to Town Square rather than the chemistry taught once somebody arrives. Every figure here was read from the provider's own page in October 2026.

The three-layer view explains where the budget band fails. A capable graduate can drill the quantitative layer perfectly well — moles practice is moles practice, and a competent generalist can set and mark it. What they generally cannot do is teach mechanism as reasoning rather than as a catalogue, or tell a student what the investigation's processing criterion actually rewards. So the cheap option is not uniformly useless; it is useless for two of the three layers, which is worth knowing before you choose.

Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for one weekly hour at the budget band, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home two-hour visits.

Each figure belongs to the provider named beside it. None is an IB Gram price — we publish no rate card on these pages, because the honest number depends on level, which layer is missing and the weeks remaining. Take the free trial lesson and get a quote after the diagnostic.

sections.heading: What we will not claim about a chemistry result
paragraphs: No grade guarantee. Not a specific number, not a points improvement, not a particular paper score, and specifically not an admissions outcome. The variables — prior quantitative fluency, weeks remaining, whether the investigation was designed well, whether the student has ever been taught to finish an explanation — are not all under a tutor's control.

No statistics without a sample size, a date and a method, which means none at all. No average chemistry score achieved by students we have taught, no percentage improved, no satisfaction figure, no self-generated star rating. Competitors publish such numbers routinely, sometimes in two conflicting versions on the same page, and almost never say how any of them was produced. Self-asserted review markup also breaches Google's structured-data policy.

No regulator or awarding-body claim, and no examiner descriptions. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, has no office or centre anywhere in the UAE, and does not describe tutors as IB examiners because current examiner status is not something we can evidence. Examiner status confers no access to marking, boundaries or paper content whatever is implied. We host no IB past papers, mark schemes or subject guides as downloads either; they belong to the IB and we link the official source.

What we will give you is a layer diagnosis. After watching your child work real paper questions, a chemistry specialist will say whether the gap is quantitative, explanation or mechanism, roughly how long each takes to move, and whether the available time is enough. Occasionally the answer is that it is not, and that fixing one layer properly beats touching all three.

faqs.question: How do I know which part of chemistry my child is actually missing?
faqs.answer: By how it presents. A quantitative gap looks like inconsistency: fine in homework with time to think, falling apart in tests, weak across unrelated topics because every topic uses conversions. An explanation gap looks like unfairness: the student knows the material and scores in the middle, because answers are true and unfinished. A mechanism gap looks like a wall: everything was fine until organic chemistry and then it stopped. Those need three different kinds of work, which is why the diagnostic tests all three rather than the named topic.

faqs.question: Why does organic chemistry feel impossible to Town Square students?
faqs.answer: Because it is usually learned as a catalogue: this reagent plus that substrate gives this product, memorise the list. That works until a paper presents an unfamiliar molecule or asks for the mechanism, at which point a perfect catalogue provides nothing at all and the student reasonably concludes the topic is impossible. Taught as reasoning — where is this molecule electron-poor, why is a nucleophile attracted there, what happens to the intermediate — the same content becomes a small set of principles applied repeatedly, and retraining takes weeks.

faqs.question: Should the quantitative layer be checked before the organic topic?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and it is why our diagnostic starts there regardless. Stoichiometry, concentration, limiting reagent and percentage yield sit underneath every topic in the course, so a weakness in multi-step conversion presents as a weakness in everything else. Students arrive from IGCSE able to balance an equation and unable to carry a calculation through unit changes against a clock. Fixing the bottom layer first also makes the top layer cheaper to teach, because mechanism questions frequently carry a quantitative part.

faqs.question: My child knows the content but scores in the middle. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always the explanation layer. Chemistry punishes imprecision harder than any other Diploma science: the marks go to answers that name the specific factor and finish the reasoning. Asked why one compound boils higher, an answer gesturing at intermolecular forces gets partial credit; one naming the force, comparing its strength and connecting that to the energy needed to separate molecules gets the marks. Command terms compound it — explain wants a cause, deduce wants a conclusion from given data. It is the most straightforwardly fixable of the three layers.

faqs.question: What is the quickest chemistry improvement before mocks?
faqs.answer: Three things in order. Sign conventions in energetics written down as a fixed rule and drilled, because the chemistry is usually understood and the bookkeeping is what fails. A rule that every step of a calculation goes on paper, since method marks are forfeited by mental arithmetic. And command-term discipline, because a knowledgeable student answering the wrong command term scores nothing. All three are weeks rather than months, and none of them requires covering new content.

faqs.question: When should investigation coaching begin for a chemistry student?
faqs.answer: In the fortnight the research question and method are chosen, which is months before most families ask. The recurring faults are an independent variable that cannot be varied with school apparatus, a range too narrow for a trend to exceed the uncertainty, two readings per point so nothing honest can be said about reliability, and a titration whose apparatus uncertainty swamps the effect. None is rescuable by a better conclusion, which is why week-one criterion reading is worth several week-ten draft readings.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do with my child's chemistry investigation?
faqs.answer: A good deal, and nothing that produces it. Permitted: explaining what each criterion rewards and its mark allocation, testing whether a proposed question is feasible with available equipment, checking the planned range and repeats will produce analysable data, pointing out that an apparatus uncertainty will dominate the result, and giving criterion-level feedback on a draft the student has written. Not permitted: writing any section, supplying data or calculations, providing a model to adapt, or editing to a finish. The student signs an authorship declaration.

faqs.question: How are chemistry practicals handled with online tuition?
faqs.answer: Bench technique — titration precision, dilution, gravimetric handling — is taught and assessed at school, and no tutor substitutes for it, in person or online; a provider claiming otherwise is overselling. What one-to-one work adds is the reasoning around the bench, where most of the marks live: predicting what an experiment should produce, deciding what to do with an anomaly, calculating percentage uncertainty from the apparatus, and writing up so the processing and evaluation criteria are addressed. Written experimental questions test evaluating a method, not performing one.

faqs.question: Is there an HL chemistry specialist living near Town Square?
faqs.answer: Usually not. The IB is roughly 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils spread across the whole emirate, only the final two years sit the Diploma, and Chemistry at Higher Level is a narrow specialism inside that. The pool who have taught it to final grade is small citywide, and most are serving school staff whose permit code of conduct bars tutoring students enrolled at their own school. Town Square is also newly settled, so residential growth outran tutoring supply. Online matching removes the constraint that never mattered to the grade.

faqs.question: Can a budget tutor help with any part of IB chemistry?
faqs.answer: With one layer, yes, which is more honest than a blanket no. At AED 33-65 an hour a capable graduate can set and mark moles practice perfectly well — the quantitative layer is drillable by a competent generalist. What they generally cannot do is teach mechanism as reasoning rather than as a catalogue, or tell a student what the investigation's processing criterion rewards. So the cheap option is not uniformly useless; it is useless for two of the three layers, and knowing which layer is missing tells you whether it will help.

faqs.question: What time should a chemistry session be in a Town Square week?
faqs.answer: It depends on the layer. Mechanism work needs an alert hour, because holding structure, charge and movement in mind at once does not survive fatigue — so 4:45pm straight off the Motor City or Sports City run for Year 12. Quantitative drilling tolerates a later slot. For Year 13, 8pm for ninety minutes suits full past-paper sections with marking. Weekend mornings are best for investigation work, where two uninterrupted hours beat three scattered weekday half-hours.

faqs.question: Is Chemistry HL needed for medicine, and can tutoring secure a place?
faqs.answer: Many medical, dental and pharmacy programmes specify chemistry, frequently at Higher Level and often with a second science, but the requirement belongs to the institution and the entry year rather than to a general rule — check the published requirement of the programmes actually under consideration. On the second question, no. Admissions depend on interview, testing, references and that year's applicant pool, none of which a chemistry tutor reaches. What support can do is make sure the chemistry grade is not what removes the option.

faqs.question: What do Town Square families pay for IB chemistry support?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures read in October 2026: qualified online subject tutors AED 150-300 an hour with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, IB specialists AED 200-450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate giving AED 200-450 plus, budget online from AED 33-65 with Tutopiya and EdFlik, in-home visits AED 180-500 including travel, and BartyED at AED 650 premium. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid and AED 1,000-2,000 plus for specialist exam-year work. Those belong to the providers named.

faqs.question: Should chemistry and biology share a tutor at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and this is one pairing where we would rather match two specialists. The content depth pulls apart at HL, and the two subjects reward different habits: biology rewards recall structured by command term, chemistry rewards explanation built from mechanism. A tutor strong in one often imports the wrong habit into the other, which is a subtle but real cost over a term. Chemistry and physics share the quantitative layer and pair more naturally where one tutor genuinely teaches both courses.

faqs.question: Will a chemistry tutor come to our home in Town Square?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram delivers chemistry tuition to Town Square one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only, at any price. Other Dubai providers do visit, at published rates of AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and from Al Qudra Road a real share of that is driving. For Diploma chemistry the binding question is whether the tutor can teach mechanism reasoning and investigation design, which proximity does not predict.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Diploma Chemistry at Standard and Higher Level to students across Umm Al Sheif and the Jumeirah schools. Each works from the current subject guide, teaches with the data booklet in view, and marks written answers against the published scheme rather than by impression.

intro.heading: Chemistry is a syllabus problem before it is a confidence problem
paragraphs: The 2023 Chemistry course is organised into two themes rather than a list of topics. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far they go, and the mechanisms by which they proceed. Higher Level extension content sits inside those six headings rather than in a separate options block, which means a student cannot treat a sub-topic as skippable.

That reorganisation matters to anyone choosing a tutor for a student in Umm Al Sheif. A tutor who last taught the previous course will set practice built around options and around a topic list that no longer matches the paper. The content overlaps heavily, so the error is invisible for weeks, and then a mock arrives with a question framed in a way the student has never seen. Asking a prospective tutor which themes Reactivity 3 covers is a fair and quick test.

The second thing a parent needs to know is that Chemistry marks are lost in identifiable, nameable places. Organic mechanisms are the headline: students learn the products and never learn to draw the arrows, so a mechanism question scores one mark out of four. Sign conventions in enthalpy and in electrochemistry are the second. Equilibrium questions that ask for a direction of shift and get a calculation instead are the third. State symbols omitted from equations are the cheapest marks in the subject to lose.

Umm Al Sheif itself has no Diploma school within its boundary. Students here commute to the Jumeirah, Al Safa, Al Sufouh and Al Barsha schools, so the teacher, the internal coursework deadline and the mock timetable all belong to a school somewhere else. A tutor's value comes from knowing the subject guide and the student's own school calendar, neither of which depends on how close the tutor lives. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Teaching for Umm Al Sheif is delivered one-to-one over live video.

What follows is the subject detail: the assessment structure with weightings, the mechanism work that fixes organic chemistry, a table of mark-scheme traps, a six-week past-paper sequence, the Dubai rate bands with their sources, the Ministry of Education equivalency rules, and the honesty boundary on the Scientific Investigation. Figures carry their source. Examination series are named by month rather than by year, because a month stays true and a year does not.

One more thing before the detail, because it shapes everything below. Chemistry rewards precision of expression more than any other science at this level. Two students can hold the same understanding and be separated by three grades purely on how they write an answer: whether the sign is stated, whether the state symbols are present, whether the explanation names a cause or merely narrates an outcome. That is good news for a family starting late, because expression is faster to repair than understanding. It is also why a tutor who marks against the published scheme, rather than nodding at a broadly correct answer, is worth more than one who simply knows more chemistry.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.programmesIntro: Chemistry sits at the top of a long run-up. Most of the Chemistry problems that surface in Year 12 were laid down earlier, in MYP Sciences or in the mathematics the subject assumes without teaching. These are the programmes an Umm Al Sheif family is likely to be working through.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Chemistry runs 150 teaching hours at Standard Level and 240 at Higher. Both levels sit Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the Scientific Investigation at 20%. Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section sat together. A data booklet is supplied, which changes what revision should concentrate on: not recall of constants, but knowing which page to turn to and what the symbol means.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Al Sheif students reach Diploma Chemistry through the coastal and inland Dubai schools, among them Jumeirah Baccalaureate School in Al Safa and Emirates International School on the Jumeirah side of Sheikh Zayed Road. Each sets its own internal investigation deadline, and in this cluster those tend to fall in the second term, alongside the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay dates. Sequencing around them is a planning job before it is a teaching one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is marked against four criteria out of 8 each, using descriptors rather than percentages. The investigation habits transfer well into Diploma Chemistry. What does not transfer is quantitative fluency: moles, concentration, and the rearrangement of a formula with three variables are the areas where MYP students arrive under-practised, and Chemistry starts using all three in the first fortnight.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Umm Al Sheif student changes school between MYP and the Diploma, the handover is rarely clean, and the gap that shows up most often is the mole concept treated as a formula to memorise rather than a counting unit. That is a two-session repair in Year 11. Left until Year 12 it reappears in every Reactivity 2 calculation for two years.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examination, no subject marks. Learning runs through transdisciplinary units of inquiry, reported against conceptual understanding and the learner profile. The part that bears on Chemistry much later is measurement confidence: reading a scale, recording a value to a sensible precision, and noticing when a number is implausible.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Umm Al Sheif often have a child in PYP and another in the Diploma simultaneously, and we keep them on separate tutors. Primary inquiry teaching and Higher Level Chemistry are different crafts, and a tutor strong at one has no particular reason to be strong at the other.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: A Chemistry Extended Essay needs a research question with a measurable variable and apparatus a school laboratory can supply, which rules out most of the questions students first propose. Theory of Knowledge has three assessment points competing for the same weeks as the Chemistry investigation. Core deadlines are the usual reason a capable Chemistry student's term falls apart.
programmes.countryNote: For an Umm Al Sheif household the practical answer is to ask the school for its core deadline schedule in the first week of the year and plan Chemistry revision into the gaps. A tutor who never asks for those dates will book content sessions into a fortnight the student has already committed elsewhere.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is almost never taken alone, and the combination changes the teaching plan. A Higher Level Chemistry student taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation needs different support from one taking Analysis and Approaches, because the logarithm work for pH arrives at different points.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two themes, two papers, one investigation, one data booklet. Marks go missing in organic mechanisms, in sign conventions for enthalpy and electrode potentials, and in equilibrium questions where a shift is asked for and a calculation is supplied. Higher Level extension content is embedded in the six sub-headings, so no section is safely skippable.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Taken with Chemistry by nearly every medicine applicant. The shared investigation criteria mean one set of research-design skills serves both subjects. The command terms behave differently though: an explain in Biology wants a mechanism in words, in Chemistry it wants a particulate-level cause, and students who answer in the wrong register lose marks in both.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The third science for engineering applicants. Thermodynamics overlaps conceptually with Chemistry energetics, and the uncertainty and graphing skills are identical, which makes joint revision efficient. Students taking both should prepare data-handling once and apply it twice rather than treating them as separate skills.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Supplies the logarithms that pH and pKa calculations need and the algebraic fluency that equilibrium expressions assume. A student behind here is behind in Chemistry too, and the symptom is a student who understands the chemistry of a buffer perfectly and cannot produce the number.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology-weighted and statistically focused. It leaves the algebraic rearrangement gap that Chemistry then exposes in Reactivity 2. Students on this route benefit from a short block on manipulating expressions with three or more variables before equilibrium work begins.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Sometimes taken alongside Chemistry, sometimes instead of a second science. The quantitative content is lighter but the data-interpretation demand is similar, and Chemistry students find the systems diagrams unfamiliar at first. Short targeted work usually closes that quickly.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: The biochemistry section reuses Chemistry content on macronutrients and energy systems, so students taking both can revise once. Where a student has dropped Chemistry and met it again here, a small block on energetics is normally all that is required.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Relevant because Paper 2 extended-response marks reward structured written argument. A student who writes well in English and badly in Chemistry is usually answering a different question from the one set, which is a command-term problem rather than a writing problem.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A frequent sixth subject. The transferable skill is diagram discipline: labelled axes, stated units, an explained change. Chemistry graph and titration-curve questions want the same habits and students lose marks for the same omissions.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paired with Chemistry by students interested in modelling and spectroscopy data. The internal assessment is a developed solution, not an experiment, so a student doing both has two unrelated coursework projects running at once and needs the deadlines mapped before either starts.

sections.heading: Structure and Reactivity: what the current course actually contains
paragraphs: Chemistry is built on two organising themes. Structure asks what matter is made of and how it holds together: models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity asks what happens when matter changes: what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far they proceed, and the mechanisms by which they proceed.

That framing is not decoration. It tells a student where a question sits and therefore what kind of answer is wanted. A question about why a reaction is spontaneous belongs to Reactivity 1 and wants an energetics and entropy answer. A question about why the reaction is slow belongs to Reactivity 2 and wants a kinetics answer. Students who have learned Chemistry as an undifferentiated pile of facts answer the first with the second and score nothing.

Higher Level extension content is embedded inside the six sub-headings rather than separated into options. The practical effect is that a Higher Level student who leaves out a sub-topic loses the Standard Level marks on it as well as the extension marks. There is no safe partial coverage. This is the single most important structural fact for planning a Higher Level revision sequence, and it is why theme-by-theme completeness has to precede any technique work.

A data booklet is provided in the examination. That changes what revision is for. Nobody needs to memorise the gas constant or an electrode potential. What a student does need is fluency in locating a value, reading the conditions attached to it, and knowing which of two similar-looking tables applies. Practising with the booklet closed is a common and expensive mistake.

sections.heading: Chemistry assessment, paper by paper
paragraphs: Both levels sit two written papers and submit one internal investigation. Paper 1 carries 36% and is sat in two parts: 1A is multiple choice, 1B is data-based and experimental-technique questions. Paper 2 carries 44% and runs from short response into extended response. The Scientific Investigation carries 20%.

The split inside Paper 1 is where most families are under-informed. Paper 1A rewards breadth and speed; Paper 1B rewards a narrow set of handling skills done properly. Reading a titration curve, propagating an uncertainty, spotting a systematic error and quoting a result to a defensible precision are all directly assessed in 1B, and all four are trainable within a small number of sessions.

Paper 2 is where the subject is won or lost at the top end. Extended-response questions want a chain of reasoning at the particulate level, and students who know the chemistry still lose marks by describing an outcome instead of explaining a cause. The fix is to plan the answer before writing it: name the principle, state the consequence, then apply it to the specific case in the question.

Teaching hours give the scale of the Higher Level step: 240 against 150. That is the clearest planning number a parent has. It does not mean a Higher Level student needs sixty per cent more tutoring, but it does mean the depth expected in the same two years is substantially greater, and a student who was comfortable at Standard Level content may still need support with extension material.

sections.heading: The organic chemistry wall, and how students get over it
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is where the largest single block of Chemistry marks is routinely forfeited, and the reason is consistent. Students learn reactions as input-to-output pairs: this reagent with that condition gives that product. The examination asks for mechanism, and a mechanism is a sequence of electron movements drawn with curly arrows. A student who has memorised products can name the product and score one mark from four.

The repair is mechanical and it works. Start from the electron source and the electron sink. Identify which species has a lone pair or a pi bond and which has a partial positive charge or a leaving group. Draw the arrow from the source to the sink, every time, in that order. Students who internalise the source-and-sink habit can construct a mechanism they have never been taught, which is precisely what the harder questions require.

The second organic failure is naming and structural ambiguity. Students draw a structure that is chemically correct and ambiguous as drawn, or name a compound with the substituent on the wrong carbon. These are marks lost to care rather than to understanding, and they respond to deliberate practice: draw it, then read it back as though you were the examiner and had no idea what was intended.

At Higher Level, spectroscopy joins the picture. Infrared tells you which functional groups are present, mass spectrometry tells you the molecular mass and the fragments, and nuclear magnetic resonance tells you the hydrogen environments. Students treat these as three separate puzzles. They are one puzzle with three clues, and the efficient method is to take the molecular formula first, then the functional group, then the skeleton.

sections.heading: Mark-scheme traps worth knowing before the next test
paragraphs: Mark schemes are not mysterious; they are specific, and they reward specific wording. A student who knows the chemistry and does not know what the scheme wants loses marks that content revision will never recover. The table below lists the traps that appear most often in the work of Diploma Chemistry students in this part of Dubai.

Sign conventions are the most expensive. Enthalpy change is negative for exothermic, and students write the magnitude without the sign or attach the sign by guesswork. Electrode potentials carry a sign that depends on the direction the half-equation is written, and reversing the equation without reversing the sign is a single-step error that loses the whole calculation.

State symbols are the cheapest marks in the subject to give away. An equation without them is incomplete, and the scheme says so. Significant figures are the second cheapest: a correct calculation quoted to seven figures or to one both lose the precision mark. The rule is to carry full precision through the working and round only at the end, to the precision of the least precise measurement.

The last trap is linguistic. Chemistry command terms have defined expectations. State wants an answer with no justification. Deduce wants a conclusion drawn from information given in the question. Determine wants a calculation shown. Explain wants a cause. Students who answer describe when the question says explain write correct chemistry and earn nothing for it, and this is the fastest-paying thing to fix in the weeks before a paper.

sections.heading: A six-week past-paper sequence that is worth the hours
paragraphs: Past papers are the most over-prescribed and under-planned revision activity in this subject. Working through papers in chronological order and marking them yourself produces a score, a vague sense of progress, and very little change. The useful version is organised by skill, with analysis attached to every attempt.

Week one and two should be theme-specific question sets rather than whole papers, because a whole paper at this stage tells you only that the student is not ready. Pull every Reactivity 2 question from the last several series, do them untimed, and mark them against the scheme line by line. The output is not a percentage; it is a list of three or four recurring error types.

Weeks three and four move to timed sections. Paper 1A under full time pressure, then Paper 1B separately with the data booklet, then a single Paper 2 extended-response question planned on paper before being written. Timing is the variable being trained here, and the mark is secondary. Students who have never written a Paper 2 answer to time overrun the first question and lose the last.

Weeks five and six are full papers, two of them, with a gap between. The gap is the point: a paper sat and analysed is worth more than three papers sat in a row. Analysis means going back to the scheme, identifying which of the error types from week one are still present, and spending a session on each. The final week should be light, revisiting the mechanism work and the data booklet rather than introducing anything new.

sections.heading: What Chemistry tuition costs in Dubai, cheapest band first
paragraphs: Taking the bands from the bottom up is more useful than the usual premium-first presentation, because it shows where the money starts to buy something a Diploma Chemistry student can use. Budget online tuition in Dubai is published at AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. At that level you are generally buying homework supervision, and a tutor who can draw a curly-arrow mechanism correctly is not guaranteed to be in the pool.

The next band up, a qualified subject tutor online, runs AED 150 to AED 300. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is where a tutor who knows the current subject guide becomes likely rather than lucky. Above that, specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors are published between AED 200 and AED 450 and upwards, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate quoting AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500 to AED 650, with BartyED at AED 650.

In-home one-to-one sits separately at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors reaching AED 500. Note where that lands: an in-home visit at AED 350 costs more than an online specialist at AED 270. The premium is paid for presence, not for subject depth, and for a Higher Level Chemistry student subject depth is the binding constraint.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and upwards for specialist examination-year support. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Every figure here belongs to the provider named beside it. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson has established what the actual gap is, which is the only sensible basis for a number.

sections.heading: Why Chemistry students in this area end up learning online
paragraphs: In-home tutoring has real advantages and it is worth saying so. A younger child concentrates better with an adult in the room. A reluctant teenager finds it harder to disengage. Nothing has to be set up. For a primary student who needs supervision as much as teaching, in-home is frequently the better product and the premium is defensible.

Diploma Chemistry is a different problem. The binding constraint is specificity: you need someone who can draw a nucleophilic substitution mechanism, explain why a buffer resists pH change at the particulate level, and read a titration curve for the equivalence point. Insisting that person also lives within a short drive of Umm Al Sheif and is free at 4.30pm on a Tuesday reduces the candidate pool to a handful of people, and the chance that one of them has that specificity is low.

The format differences are smaller than expected and some run in favour of video. Working is written on a shared digital whiteboard that is saved and can be re-read, which a page in an exercise book cannot be. Mechanisms are drawn live and the student's own arrows are corrected one at a time. The data booklet is on screen for both parties. Past-paper scripts are annotated where the student can see each mark being awarded or withheld.

To be unambiguous, since this market is not: IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. Every Chemistry lesson for an Umm Al Sheif family is one-to-one over live video, and the trial lesson exists so the format can be tested on your own child before any commitment is made.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency and what the grades have to show
paragraphs: A Chemistry grade is not only a university entry number in the UAE; it also feeds into Ministry of Education equivalency, which no competitor page in this market explains. Equivalency is the process by which a foreign school certificate is recognised in the UAE, and the requirements differ by curriculum track.

For the British track the published rule is specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. Those are the published figures for that track.

For the IB there is a point worth being honest about. No IB points threshold for equivalency has been read on a Ministry of Education source, so none is published here. Several sites quote one. Treat any such figure as unverified until you have seen it on the ministry's own page or been told it by the emirate's attestation authority. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs or can influence, and nobody should tell you that tutoring is required in order to obtain it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on the Chemistry investigation
paragraphs: The Scientific Investigation is 20% of the Chemistry grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria of 6 marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Research design is where most marks disappear, because a question the school laboratory cannot answer cannot be rescued by good graphs later. Evaluation is where strong students under-score, by listing limitations instead of ranking them by their effect on the conclusion.

What a tutor may do is bounded, and the boundary deserves to be printed rather than assumed. A tutor may teach experimental design, explain uncertainty propagation, ask whether a conclusion actually follows from the data, and give feedback against the published descriptors. A tutor may not produce the report, rewrite it into final form, or supply data the student did not collect themselves.

This matters because one page competing for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments outright. Under IB academic-honesty rules that is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, who can lose the diploma. No grade is worth that exposure, and no provider who offers it should be trusted with anything else either.

Two further limits apply. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we cite them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter. And IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and does not operate a UAE office or centre.

process.title: Say which sub-heading is failing

Higher Level, Year 12, Reactivity 3 organic mechanisms, investigation due in six weeks, school in Al Safa is enough to act on. A request for Chemistry help in general is a request for a guess.

process.title: A free trial lesson used as a diagnostic
process.description: The trial is a working session. The tutor sets a short problem sequence and watches where the reasoning breaks, then sends a written note naming the gap. If the real problem is the mole concept rather than organic chemistry, you find that out before paying for a term of the wrong lessons.

process.title: Map the school's dates first
process.description: We ask for the internal investigation deadline, the mock window and the core deadlines, then build the lesson sequence backwards from them. In this cluster the core dates cluster in the second term, so content work has to be front-loaded or it collides with weeks the student has already committed.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a written record
process.description: Each lesson ends with a short note: what was taught, what went wrong and why, what to practise. The shared whiteboard file is saved, including every mechanism drawn. Parents can read the note without sitting in on the lesson, which is usually what is actually wanted.

process.title: Change the tutor if the fit is wrong
process.description: Subject competence and teaching fit are separate things. If the match is not working after two or three sessions, tell us and we move the student. There is no argument for persisting with a poor fit; it costs weeks the examination calendar will not give back.

whyPoints.title: The current subject guide, not the previous one
whyPoints.description: Chemistry was restructured around Structure and Reactivity with extension content embedded in the themes. A tutor working from the older options-based course sets practice that no longer matches the paper, and the mismatch stays invisible until a mock exposes it. Our tutors work from the current guide.

whyPoints.title: Mechanisms taught as electron movement
whyPoints.description: Organic chemistry is the largest single block of recoverable marks in the subject, and it is recoverable because the method generalises. Source, sink, arrow, in that order, lets a student build a mechanism they were never taught, which is what the harder questions require.

whyPoints.title: The data booklet used in every lesson
whyPoints.description: The booklet is supplied in the examination, so revising without it trains the wrong skill. We keep it on the shared screen so that locating a value and reading its conditions becomes automatic rather than a search under time pressure.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on the investigation
whyPoints.description: We teach technique and give feedback against the four criteria. The student writes the report. We say this to the student at the first session, in a market where at least one provider openly sells completed Internal Assessments, because the student is the one who carries the consequence.

whyPoints.title: Figures that name their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page says who published it and every regulatory statement names the authority. We publish no satisfaction percentage, no self-awarded rating and no tutor headcount, because an unsourced number tells a parent nothing useful about anything.

faqs.question: What does the current IB Chemistry course actually cover at HL and SL?
faqs.answer: Two organising themes. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far they go, and reaction mechanisms. Standard Level runs 150 teaching hours and Higher Level 240, and the Higher Level extension content sits inside those same six sub-headings rather than in a separate options block. That last point has a practical consequence: skipping a sub-topic at Higher Level forfeits the Standard Level marks on it as well as the extension marks, so partial coverage costs more than students expect.

faqs.question: My child finds organic chemistry very hard. Where does that usually go wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always in the same place. Students learn reactions as input-to-output pairs and the examination asks for mechanism, which is a sequence of electron movements drawn with curly arrows. A student who has memorised products can name the product and take one mark from four. The repair is procedural: identify the electron source, which has a lone pair or a pi bond, identify the sink, which carries a partial positive charge or a leaving group, then draw the arrow from source to sink. Done consistently, that lets a student construct a mechanism nobody taught them, which is what the harder questions demand.

faqs.question: Is IB Chemistry at Higher Level significantly harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: The teaching-hour ratio is the clearest measure: 240 hours against 150. Both levels sit Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the investigation at 20%, and both cover the same two themes. What differs is depth, and because the extension content is embedded in the sub-headings rather than separated out, a Higher Level student cannot treat any section as optional. Spectroscopy is the content area students most often name as the step up, since infrared, mass spectrometry and nuclear magnetic resonance arrive together. Treating those three as one problem with three clues, rather than three puzzles, is what makes it manageable.

faqs.question: How is Chemistry Paper 1 split, and does that change revision?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 is 36% of the grade and is sat in two parts. Paper 1A is multiple choice across both themes. Paper 1B is data-based and experimental-technique questions. They reward different things, so revising them as one block hides which is costing the marks. Paper 1A punishes slow working and elimination by feel. Paper 1B punishes weak uncertainty handling, misread titration curves and sloppy precision. We practise them separately and under time, and we look at the pattern of errors rather than the score, because the 1B skills can be trained in a handful of sessions and pay on every sitting.

faqs.question: Can your tutors coach the Chemistry Internal Assessment properly?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary we state to the student in the first session. A tutor may teach experimental design, explain how to propagate an uncertainty, challenge whether a conclusion follows from the data, and give feedback against the four published criteria. A tutor may not write the report, rewrite it into final form, or supply data the student did not collect. The component is 20% of the grade and is marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. Most marks are lost in research design, because a question the school laboratory cannot answer cannot be rescued later.

faqs.question: Which mark-scheme mistakes cost Chemistry students the most?
faqs.answer: Six recur. Enthalpy signs written as a magnitude with no sign. Electrode potentials kept at their tabulated sign after the half-equation has been reversed. State symbols missing from equations, which is the cheapest loss in the subject. Significant figures rounded mid-calculation or quoted to the full calculator display. Organic products drawn correctly with no curly arrows attached. And command terms answered loosely, with a description supplied where the question said explain. All six are fixable without learning any new chemistry, which is why they are the first thing we look at in the weeks before a paper.

faqs.question: How should my child use past papers so the hours are not wasted?
faqs.answer: By skill, not in chronological order. Weeks one and two should be theme-specific question sets, untimed, marked against the scheme line by line, with the output a list of three or four recurring error types rather than a percentage. Weeks three and four move to timed sections: Paper 1A under full time, Paper 1B separately with the data booklet, and single Paper 2 extended responses planned before being written. Weeks five and six are two full papers with a gap between them, because a paper sat and analysed is worth more than three sat in a row. The analysis is the part students skip and the part that works.

faqs.question: Does the data booklet change how we should revise?
faqs.answer: Considerably, and most students revise as though it did not exist. The booklet is supplied in the examination, so memorising the gas constant or an electrode potential is wasted effort. What needs practice is fluency: locating a value quickly, reading the conditions attached to it, and knowing which of two similar tables applies. Students who revise with the booklet closed train the wrong skill and then lose time in the paper hunting for a figure. We keep it open on the shared screen in every lesson so that finding a value becomes automatic rather than a search under pressure.

faqs.question: How much does an online IB Chemistry tutor cost for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: Taking the market from the bottom: budget online tuition is published at AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB and IGCSE specialists are published at AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 600 to AED 1,200 for weekly mid-tier sessions. Those are the providers' own published figures; we quote after a free trial establishes the gap.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home Chemistry tutor more expensive than an online specialist?
faqs.answer: Because travel is priced in and the pool is smaller. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate at AED 180 to AED 350. Compare that with a published online specialist rate of AED 270 and the premium is clear. What it buys is physical presence. What it does not buy is subject depth, because requiring a tutor to reach your area at a fixed weekday hour limits the choice to whoever lives nearby and is free. For Higher Level Chemistry, depth is the binding constraint, which is why this page argues for the online format.

faqs.question: Can Chemistry really be taught well over video when it is a laboratory subject?
faqs.answer: The assessed parts can, and some are easier. Mechanisms are drawn live and the student's own arrows are corrected one at a time. The data booklet sits on the shared screen for both people. Past-paper scripts are annotated where the student watches each mark being awarded or withheld. The whiteboard file is saved and re-readable, which an exercise book is not. What video cannot replace is the school laboratory, and it is not meant to: apparatus work belongs at school under the teacher's supervision, and the investigation requires the student to collect their own data in any case.

faqs.question: What does UAE Ministry of Education equivalency require from a British-curriculum student?
faqs.answer: The published rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. At least one ranking site states six subjects, which does not match the sourced figure. Equivalency is handled by the ministry and the emirate attestation authority, not by any tutoring provider, and nobody should tell you tutoring is required to obtain it.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry publish a Diploma points score that Chemistry grades feed into?
faqs.answer: Not one we have been able to read on a Ministry of Education source, so this page publishes none. Several third-party sites quote a number. Until you have seen it on the ministry's own page or been told it by the emirate's attestation authority, treat any such figure as unverified, because an equivalency decision is one a family plans around. The British-track numbers in the table on this page are sourced and can be relied on as published; the IB line deliberately says to verify. A provider willing to invent that figure is a provider willing to invent others.

faqs.question: When do UAE students sit the examinations my child is preparing for?
faqs.answer: For the IB Diploma, UAE schools sit the May session as the main series with November as the alternative. This page does not state IB session or results dates, because the authoritative source is the IB and your child's IB coordinator, and a restated date can be wrong in a way a family acts on. For the IGCSE qualifications feeding in, Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge assigns every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 12 and scoring a 4 in Chemistry. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With a diagnosis rather than a revision plan. A student at 4 is rarely weak across both themes; the usual pattern is adequate understanding with one structural gap and two or three recurring technique errors. The most common structural gap in this cohort is the mole concept learned as a formula rather than as a counting unit, which then undermines every Reactivity 2 calculation. The technique errors are usually sign conventions, state symbols and command-term misreading. All of those are repairable in weeks. The trial lesson exists to find out which applies before anyone commits to a schedule.

The tutor will work your child through a short problem sequence, watch where the reasoning breaks, and send a written note naming the gap. If the real issue turns out to be the mole concept rather than organic chemistry, you will know that before committing to a term of lessons aimed at the wrong thing.

intro.heading: Why chemistry costs what it costs in this market, and what the money reaches
paragraphs: Chemistry is priced by scarcity in Dubai. The city has a large supply of science teachers and a much smaller supply of people who can prepare a Higher Level Diploma chemistry candidate for the current guide, read a marked Paper 2 and say which four marks are recoverable. That scarcity sits at particular hours, which is the part families discover late: the tutor exists, and the tutor is already teaching at six on a Tuesday.

The published Dubai bands are worth putting down plainly, because most pages in this market publish none. Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45-150, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, as read on their own pages in October 2026. A qualified subject tutor online sits broadly AED 150-300, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit including travel is quoted at AED 180-500, Bestimate's own band being AED 180-350. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Those are market figures from those organisations, not our price list.

The useful question is not which band is cheapest but which band can move which component. Chemistry is assessed in three pieces: a paper of multiple choice and data-based questions, a paper of short and extended response, and a single scientific investigation marked internally and moderated externally. The investigation is a fifth of the grade. A budget tutor can rehearse content and will usually have nothing useful to say about the investigation criteria. A specialist can read a draft against four named criteria and tell you where six marks sit. Those are different purchases with different prices and different returns.

The second thing scarcity does is distort the in-home decision. The published in-home band runs to AED 500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor working online, and for a family in Umm Suqeim the premium is substantially the cost of someone crossing Dubai in evening traffic. In a subject with as few genuine Higher Level specialists as this one, insisting on a person in the room does not just add the premium: it narrows the choice to whoever is both qualified and within a twenty-minute drive, which in practice often means accepting a general science teacher at a specialist price.

IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The in-home figures above are included because the gap between them and the online band is the clearest number on this page, and because an Umm Suqeim family deciding how to spend two years of chemistry money deserves to see the premium before paying it.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.programmesIntro: Chemistry appears in three different shapes before a Diploma grade is awarded, and each carries a different cost profile. The Diploma is externally examined with internal coursework. Middle Years science is criterion-marked with no examination. IGCSE science is the route many Umm Suqeim students arrive from.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Diploma chemistry runs at Standard or Higher Level, organised into three Structure themes and three Reactivity themes with a set of experimental, technological and mathematical tools threaded through them. Assessment is two written papers plus one scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade and marked against four criteria. A data booklet is provided in the examination, which changes what is worth memorising and what is worth practising.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Higher Level chemistry cohort at any one school is small, often a single class, which means a student who falls behind has nowhere inside the school to go for a different explanation. That is the structural reason tutoring demand concentrates here and the reason evening slots for Higher Level chemistry fill first across the city. Families in Umm Suqeim who wait until the first Diploma report to look are usually looking at the hours nobody else wanted.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years sciences are reported against four criteria on eight-point bands, with no terminal examination and therefore no past paper to practise. Chemistry content appears inside integrated science units rather than as a separate subject in most years, which is why students can arrive at the Diploma with strong scientific reasoning and no experience of sustained quantitative chemistry.
programmes.countryNote: Schools in the Jumeirah and Al Sufouh corridor that run the Middle Years Programme to Year 11 send students into Diploma chemistry without an IGCSE-style quantitative grounding. The predictable consequence is the first-term collapse on moles and concentration work. Hours bought in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 are the cheapest chemistry hours a family will ever buy, because they prevent a problem rather than repairing one.

programmes.name: International GCSE sciences
programmes.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson Edexcel 4CH1 chemistry, or the combined and co-ordinated science routes, are where most British-curriculum students in this neighbourhood meet chemistry formally. The Extended or Higher tier is the realistic prerequisite for Diploma chemistry at Higher Level, and a combined-science background is a genuine, closable gap rather than a disqualification.
programmes.countryNote: An Umm Suqeim student arriving at Diploma chemistry from Co-ordinated Sciences rather than separate chemistry has met less organic chemistry, less quantitative work and fewer practical techniques. Schools here will usually accept them onto Standard Level and be cautious about Higher Level. The honest tutoring answer is a bridging block in the summer, priced as a finite number of hours, rather than two years of weekly catch-up.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.subjectsIntro: Below are the chemistry courses and the subjects whose grades move with the same skills. Families paying for chemistry and physics separately are sometimes paying twice for one problem, because the shared difficulty is proportional reasoning rather than either subject's content.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The full Structure and Reactivity content plus the additional higher level material, with longer papers and more extended response. The reliable pressure points are organic reaction pathways, equilibrium and acid-base calculations, and the electron-transfer content, where students who learned reactions as lists cannot answer a question framed as a mechanism.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The same six themes at reduced depth with shorter papers, and the same scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. Students arriving from Co-ordinated Sciences find the quantitative work the unfamiliar part rather than the descriptive chemistry, and that is where the first term's marks go.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Shares the investigation model and the four marking criteria with chemistry, so a student doing both can prepare the coursework skills once. The biochemistry content also rewards chemical understanding, and students frequently lose biology marks on enzyme and respiration questions for chemical rather than biological reasons.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The other science with a data booklet and the same investigation structure. Where a student is losing marks in both chemistry and physics on calculation questions, the shared cause is usually rearrangement, logarithms and unit algebra, and one maths-focused hour serves both subjects more cheaply than two subject hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Logarithms, exponentials and proportional reasoning underpin pH, equilibrium constants and kinetics. A chemistry student who cannot manipulate a logarithmic expression under time will concede the same marks in every series, and the repair belongs in a maths hour rather than a chemistry one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The route many Diploma chemistry students take, strong on statistics and modelling and lighter on algebraic manipulation. Useful for the investigation's data analysis criterion, and a known weak point for the algebra that equilibrium and acid-base work demands.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Taken by some students alongside or instead of a second science, with overlapping content on acidity, pollution and energy. Its assessment model differs from chemistry's, so a tutor should not assume the coursework skills transfer directly even though the subject matter sometimes does.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0620 and Edexcel 4CH1, Core and Extended
subjects.description: The preparation route most Umm Suqeim students take. Moles, concentrations, yields and titration arithmetic are where able students concede marks, and these are exactly the skills the first Diploma term assumes are already secure.

subjects.name: IGCSE Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: A single or double award covering all three sciences, with less chemistry depth than separate chemistry. The gap into Diploma chemistry is real and closable with a defined bridging block, and pretending it does not exist is the usual reason a student drops from Higher to Standard Level in the first term.

subjects.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion-marked on eight-point bands with no public examination. Worth preparing on criterion B and C, inquiring and designing and processing data, because those are the skills the Diploma investigation then marks under different names.

sections.heading: What you are actually paying for when you hire an IB chemistry tutor in Umm Suqeim
paragraphs: You are paying for scarcity at a particular hour. That sentence explains almost every pricing oddity a family meets in this subject. Dubai has plenty of chemistry graduates and plenty of experienced science teachers. It has far fewer people who have taught the current Diploma chemistry guide through a full two-year cycle, marked investigations against the four criteria, and read enough Paper 2 scripts to know where a Higher Level candidate's marks go.

Higher Level chemistry at a Dubai school is usually one class. There is no second teacher to ask for a different explanation, no parallel set to move into, and no cohort big enough for the school to run targeted intervention. When a student loses the thread in the equilibrium sequence, the school's options are limited and the family's first instinct is to buy an hour. That is a reasonable instinct, and it is why every specialist's weekday evening between five and seven is contested across the whole city by November.

The practical consequence is that the thing in short supply is not money but the combination of the right person and the right hour. A family that books in September pays the same rate as a family that books in February and gets a materially better match. A family that insists on a tutor within driving distance of Umm Suqeim pays a travel premium and reduces the pool to whoever is both qualified and local, which in a thin subject is frequently a general science teacher being paid at specialist rates.

So the spending advice on this page runs against the usual instinct. Do not shop for the cheapest hour and do not shop for the most expensive one. Shop early, specify Higher or Standard Level in the first message, and treat the specialist's availability as the scarce resource it is. The sections below price the subject component by component so you can see which hours are worth buying and which are being sold to you.

sections.heading: The published Dubai rate bands, and what each can reach in chemistry
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible pages in this market publish no price, and the two that do quote in dollars. The table below sets out what Dubai providers have actually published in dirhams, with each organisation named and the month the page was read, and then says what that band can realistically do for a Diploma chemistry student.

The key column is the last one. A budget tutor can rehearse content, keep a student company through homework and reteach a topic the class moved past. That is a real service and for some students it is the right one. What it cannot usually do is read a marked Paper 2 and name the four recoverable marks, or look at an investigation draft and say that the research design criterion is where six marks are sitting unclaimed. Those require familiarity with the current guide and the marking criteria.

The premium band deserves particular scepticism in chemistry, because examiner status is the claim most often used to justify it. Examiner status should be evidenced before it is paid for, and it should never be presented as access to marking, boundaries or paper content, because it is not. A tutor who implies otherwise is telling you something about their judgement.

The in-home row is the one to look at hardest. Published in-home rates run AED 180-500 including travel against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor working online. For a Diploma chemistry student the premium buys presence in the room. It does not buy familiarity with the Structure and Reactivity organisation, and in this subject that is the variable that moves the grade.
