sections.heading: Priced by component: where the chemistry grade actually sits
paragraphs: Parents are given weightings and almost never told which weighting responds to paid hours. Diploma chemistry is assessed in three pieces, and they are not equally movable. Spending the same money across them in equal shares is the most common inefficiency in this subject, and it usually means over-investing in content rehearsal and under-investing in the investigation.

Paper 1 combines multiple choice with data-based questions and rewards breadth, speed and confident use of the data booklet. It is the component where a student's gaps are most exposed and the one that responds most slowly to tutoring, because the fix is coverage across six themes rather than technique on one. Paper 2 carries short and extended response and rewards structured written chemistry: defining terms precisely, showing calculation steps, and answering the command term that was actually used. That is technique, and technique responds quickly to marking practice.

The scientific investigation is worth a fifth of the grade, is marked by the school against four criteria and moderated externally, and is the component most Dubai competitor pages never mention. Twenty-four marks sit there, divided evenly across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A student working on it months ahead with criterion-specific feedback can bank marks that no amount of revision replaces; a student treating it as a last-fortnight task gives those marks away.

The practical conclusion is a spending order. Protect the investigation first because it is the cheapest marks per hour. Buy Paper 2 technique second because it responds fast. Treat Paper 1 coverage as the long-run job that a weekly hour across two years does and a crash block does not. Anybody selling a six-week programme that promises to move all three equally is describing a hope.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, and the price difference in hours
paragraphs: The level decision has a direct cost. Higher Level chemistry carries additional content, longer papers and more extended response, and the extra teaching time in the school timetable is not matched by extra weeks in the year. For a tutoring budget that means a Higher Level student realistically needs either more hours or a longer run-up, and families who buy the same arrangement at both levels and expect the same result are mispricing the subject.

The honest test for the level is not a predicted grade but a marked script. A student who earns method marks on a Higher Level question they could not finish is at the right level; a student who cannot start the question is not, and discovering that in the first term is cheap while discovering it in the second year is not. Moving down from Higher to Standard Level is a decision for the school and its deadlines, and the evidence that supports the conversation is a marked paper rather than a view.

Most of the Higher Level pressure concentrates in three places. The equilibrium and acid-base content, where logarithmic manipulation defeats students who were never fluent in it. The energetics sequence, where Born-Haber style reasoning asks for a chain of steps held in order. And organic chemistry, where the additional reaction pathways turn a memorised list into something that must be reasoned through. Each of those is teachable and each takes weeks rather than days.

For university purposes, Higher Level chemistry is a common requirement for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and several engineering routes, and requirements vary by institution and are revised. Read the current published requirement on each university's own admissions page for the year your child applies. A tutor's job is to help you read it accurately, not to tell you what it says, and no tutor should imply that tutoring is required for an admissions outcome.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry, energetics, and the three places chemistry money gets wasted
paragraphs: Waste in this subject has a recognisable shape. The first and largest form is paying for content rehearsal when the problem is written technique. A student who understands equilibrium and still loses Paper 2 marks is losing them to vague definitions, unshown steps and command terms they did not answer. Reteaching equilibrium a third time cannot fix that, and it is what most paid hours quietly go on.

The second is organic chemistry taught as a list. Students arrive having memorised reagents and conditions, which works for recall questions and fails the moment a question asks for a pathway or a mechanism. The fix is sequencing: learning which functional group converts to which, and why, so the student can construct a route they have not been shown. It takes several weeks and it is the single highest-yield block of teaching in Higher Level chemistry.

The third is the investigation left until the last fortnight. Twenty-four marks across four criteria, worth a fifth of the grade, and the common pattern is a student designing an experiment too large to control, collecting data they cannot analyse properly, and writing an evaluation that lists what went wrong without evaluating anything. Every part of that is preventable with three sessions at the right time, and none of it is repairable with three sessions at the wrong one.

A fourth, smaller leak worth naming: the data booklet. It is provided in the examination, which changes what is worth memorising. Students who spend revision time learning values they will be given are spending time they could have spent practising retrieval from the booklet under pressure. A tutor who does not know what the booklet contains is planning revision from the wrong premise.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks, four criteria, and what a tutor may do
paragraphs: This is the cheapest fifth of a chemistry grade to protect and the part of the course Dubai competitor pages almost never explain. The investigation is a single piece of work, marked by the school against four criteria and moderated externally, carrying twenty-four marks split evenly between research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Naming those four and their marks turns a vague anxiety into a checklist.

Each criterion fails in a predictable way. Research design loses marks where the question is too broad, the variables are not properly identified or the methodology would not actually produce usable data. Data analysis loses marks on uncertainty and processing rather than on arithmetic. Conclusion loses marks where a result is stated but not interpreted against the scientific context. Evaluation loses marks where the student lists limitations instead of weighing their effect and proposing a specific improvement.

The boundary on tutoring is firm and worth stating plainly, because two operators in this market cross it and one of them openly sells completed coursework. A tutor may teach the chemistry and the experimental technique the investigation needs. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards and what examiners mean by the terms used in it. A tutor may read a draft the student has written and give feedback on it. A tutor may not design the investigation for the student, may not write any part of the report, and may not edit it to completion.

Work submitted to the IB must be the student's own, and a breach is a malpractice matter for the candidate rather than an inconvenience for the tutor. That is why the investigation block here is short, early and spread: three or four sessions across the term before the school's internal deadline, with the student writing between them. Anybody offering to produce the document is offering to put your child's diploma at risk.

sections.heading: A two-year chemistry plan priced against the May session
paragraphs: Dubai schools sit the May Diploma session, and the useful way to budget is to count backwards from it rather than forwards from today. Because the IB blocks automated access to its own site, no specific examination or results date is quoted here, and any date a tutor gives you should be confirmed against the IB's own published assessment information or your school's IB coordinator before you plan around it.

What can be planned confidently is the shape. The first Diploma year is for teaching, and it is where a weekly hour earns the most because content can be met properly rather than patched. The investigation sits in the second half of the first year or the start of the second, driven by the school's internal deadline rather than by the examination. The final stretch is paper technique: timed papers, marked properly, with the plan following the script rather than the student's sense of which topics feel hard.

Priced out, a weekly hour across both Diploma years at the published qualified-online band of AED 150-300 is roughly seventy-two hours and a five-figure dirham commitment, which is why it deserves a term-by-term review rather than a standing order. An investigation block of four hours at the specialist band is a small fraction of that and protects a fifth of the grade. A final technique block of ten to twelve hours after a marked mock is the other high-return purchase. Those are derived figures on published bands, not a quote.

Context for the household budget: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A year of flat fees is a better moment to commit to two years of chemistry support than the week after a disappointing report, and the planning is calmer.

sections.heading: Starting from Umm Suqeim, with the scarcity stated first
paragraphs: Say Higher or Standard Level in the first message, name the school, and name the hour your child is genuinely home and settled rather than the hour you hope for. Those three facts determine whether a specialist match exists, and sending them first saves a week. If you do not know which level, send the school and year and we will establish it before matching anyone.

The trial lesson is free and exists to produce a verdict rather than a relationship. A useful one ends with the tutor naming what is secure across the six themes, which component is currently costing the most, and whether the investigation has been started. If the feedback is encouragement without specifics, you have learned something about the term ahead at no cost.

On availability, the limit is stated rather than implied. Higher Level chemistry between five and seven on a weekday is the thinnest slot in the UAE schedule, and there are weeks when every specialist in it is teaching. We will tell you so and set out the options: a different hour with the specialist you want, the hour you want with a strong but less specialised tutor and the trade made explicit, or a place in the queue. Nobody is put in front of a Higher Level candidate on the grounds of being free.

After the trial the shape is a fixed weekly hour with a written note each time, an investigation block timed to the school's deadline, a timed paper under conditions once a term, and a review each term about whether the arrangement still earns its cost. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the travel premium described above is not something you will ever be quoted here.

faqs.question: What does an IB chemistry tutor cost per hour in Dubai in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures read in October 2026 put budget online tutoring from about AED 45-150, a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150-300 with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 including travel, and IB specialists at AED 200-450 or more with TutorChase publishing AED 270. One premium provider publishes AED 650. Those are market rates from those organisations rather than our price list. For chemistry specifically, the band that matters is the specialist one, because the investigation criteria and Paper 2 technique sit there.

faqs.question: Why are Higher Level chemistry tutors harder to book than other Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Because the cohort is small and the demand is concentrated. Higher Level chemistry at a Dubai school is typically a single class, so when a student loses the thread there is no second teacher or parallel set inside the school, and the family buys an hour. Multiply that across the city and every specialist's weekday slot between five and seven is contested by November. The practical answer is to book in September, when the rate is identical and the choice of tutor is much wider.

faqs.question: Which part of the chemistry grade should we spend tutoring money on first?
faqs.answer: The scientific investigation. It carries a fifth of the grade, twenty-four marks split evenly across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and it can be worked on months in advance with criterion-specific feedback. Paper 2 technique comes second because it responds quickly to marking practice. Paper 1 coverage is the long-run job a weekly hour across two years does well and a crash block does badly. Spending equally across all three is the most common inefficiency in this subject.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level chemistry worth the extra tutoring cost for a medicine application?
faqs.answer: Higher Level chemistry is a common requirement for medicine, dentistry and pharmacy, but requirements differ by university and are revised, so read the current published requirement on each institution's own admissions page for the year your child applies. What a tutor can honestly say is that the Higher Level content needs more weeks rather than more intensity, which argues for starting earlier rather than buying more hours later. No tutor should imply that tutoring is required for an admissions outcome.

faqs.question: My child memorised all the organic reactions and still lost marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the questions ask for pathways, not for recall. A student who has learned reagents and conditions as a list can answer a question that names the reaction and cannot answer one that asks how to get from a named starting material to a named product. The repair is sequencing: learning which functional group converts to which, under what conditions, and why, so a route can be constructed rather than remembered. It takes several weeks and it is the highest-yield block in Higher Level chemistry.

faqs.question: How many chemistry sessions a week does a Diploma student in Umm Suqeim need?
faqs.answer: One protected weekly hour across both Diploma years, with a short investigation block timed to the school's internal deadline and a technique block after the mock. Doubling the weekly hours rarely returns what families expect, because the limiting factor is usually practice between lessons rather than teaching time inside them. The exception is a student bridging a genuine content gap from Co-ordinated Sciences, where a finite block of eight to twelve hours early on is better value than a longer weekly arrangement.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help design my child's chemistry investigation?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the line. A tutor may teach the chemistry and the experimental technique the investigation needs, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not design the investigation, write any part of the report, or edit it to completion. Work submitted to the IB must be the student's own, and a breach is a malpractice matter for the candidate. Anyone offering to produce the document is offering to risk your child's diploma.

faqs.question: Does the chemistry data booklet change what my child should revise?
faqs.answer: Substantially. The booklet is provided in the examination, so revision time spent memorising values it supplies is time taken from practising retrieval under pressure. The skill worth building is knowing what the booklet contains, where each table sits, and how quickly a value can be found mid-question. Students who have never practised with it lose minutes they cannot afford on a timed paper. A tutor who does not know the booklet's contents is planning revision from the wrong premise.

faqs.question: My child came from Co-ordinated Sciences. Is Diploma chemistry realistic?
faqs.answer: Usually yes at Standard Level, and possible at Higher Level with a defined bridging block. The gap is real: less organic chemistry, less quantitative work, fewer practical techniques. It is also finite, which is the important part. Eight to twelve hours in the summer or first term, with a written list of the content being bridged and a short diagnostic at the end, closes it. An open-ended weekly catch-up arrangement costs more and never declares itself finished, which is why the block is the better purchase.

faqs.question: Is a group chemistry class in Al Barsha cheaper than one-to-one online?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour and generally weaker per mark. A group is taught at the pace of the middle of the room, so a student who needs the equilibrium sequence rebuilt sits through content they have, and a student who is ahead pays to revisit. Groups work for a timed-paper clinic where the content is genuinely shared. For rebuilding a specific gap in a specific student's chemistry, the one-to-one hour is what does the work, and in a scarce subject it is also what secures the specialist.

faqs.question: Will an examiner-trained chemistry tutor get my child a better grade?
faqs.answer: Treat the claim carefully. Examiner status should be evidenced before it is paid for, and it should never be presented as access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because it is not. What genuinely helps is somebody who has marked work against the published criteria and read enough scripts to see where marks go, which is a skill rather than a title. Ask what they would look for first in a marked Paper 2, and judge the answer rather than the label.

faqs.question: Does a chemistry tutor in Dubai need a permit, and can we check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The official route is listed on mohre.gov.ae as private tutor licensing, and you can ask any tutor directly.

faqs.question: Can we buy chemistry help only for the final term before the May papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is good value if the plan is built from a marked mock rather than from a feeling. A final block does paper technique well: precise definitions, shown calculation steps, answering the command term that was used, and managing time across the paper. What it cannot do is rebuild two years of the six themes, and anybody promising that is selling a hope. Start with a timed paper marked against the published scheme and let the script choose the content.

faqs.question: Do the KHDA mandatory UAE subjects affect a Diploma science timetable?
faqs.answer: They take timetable space, which is worth planning around. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum they are licensed for, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. The effect is a fuller week than the six Diploma subjects suggest, which argues for one well-placed chemistry hour rather than two squeezed ones.

faqs.question: Can chemistry lessons shift during Ramadan without extra cost?
faqs.answer: Yes. School days shorten, the evening reorganises around Iftar, and a slot that worked in February stops working. Because teaching is delivered over live video, moving to a later evening start is an administrative change rather than a logistical one, and there is no travel window to rebuild and no premium attached to the change. It is worth agreeing the Ramadan pattern a fortnight ahead and using the quieter afternoons for investigation drafting rather than for new quantitative content.

intro.heading: In chemistry, where you spend matters more than what you spend
paragraphs: Villanova is a townhouse community off Al Qudra Road in the Dubailand belt, and the families there asking about IB chemistry are usually asking two questions at once: can this be fixed, and what will it cost. Chemistry is unusual among Diploma subjects in that the answer depends almost entirely on which part of the course is failing. Some chemistry problems are cheap to solve. Others are not, and no rate makes them cheaper.

The cheap ones are specific and identifiable. Organic mechanisms, where students understand the reaction and draw the curly arrow from the wrong electron pair, lose the same mark in every question and recover it in three or four sessions. Moles calculations under time pressure are a fluency problem, not a comprehension problem, and fluency responds fast. Command-term discipline and significant-figure habits are single-session fixes that pay across both papers.

The expensive ones are structural. A student who never secured bonding and intermolecular forces in DP1 is carrying a deficit that touches every later topic, and that is a content programme rather than a block of sessions. So is a Higher Level student who has been avoiding energetics since the first term. Those cases need twenty to thirty hours, and a family should know that before they start rather than discover it in April.

Published Dubai rates put IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more per hour, with TutorChase at AED 270, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table showing AED 200 to 450+. Those are market figures, not ours; we quote after the free trial lesson, once somebody has read a marked paper and can say how many hours the job needs.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. Villanova students are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That removes the in-home travel premium, which in this belt sits at the top of the AED 50 to 150 per hour range because the drive out is long, and it means the tutor is selected for chemistry at your child's level rather than for living in Dubailand.

One standing caution that applies to every page on this site: we publish no IB exam or results date, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and a date a family plans around has to be checkable. UAE schools sit the May session. Get the window and your school's internal investigation deadline from your child's IB coordinator. The useful planning fact, which does not depend on a date, is that the chemistry investigation in most Dubai schools is due in the same few weeks as two or three others, so the money spent late is spent in competition with every other subject at once.

That raises the stakes on spending decisions: a family whose child needs Higher Level chemistry for a medical route is buying a grade with a hard requirement attached, which justifies the specialist band in a way general support does not.
programmes.countryNote: Requirements vary by university and programme, so read the specific programme pages rather than relying on a general rule, and never treat tutoring as a requirement for admission. For Ministry of Education equivalency the British-track rules are published while no IB points threshold has been read on moe.gov.ae, so verify any IB equivalency question with the Ministry.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-villanova.subjectsIntro: This page is about chemistry, so these are the syllabus areas and components, each with the cost logic attached: how many sessions it typically takes and what it returns.

subjects.name: Structure 1: particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Atomic structure, the mole concept, electron configuration and ionisation. The mole work is the foundation of every calculation in the course, and fluency rather than understanding is usually what is missing. Three to five sessions of timed calculation practice typically secures it for good.

subjects.name: Structure 2: models of bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces and structure-property reasoning. The most expensive gap in the course to leave unfilled, because every later topic assumes it. A student shaky here needs a content programme rather than a short block.

subjects.name: Structure 3: classification of matter
subjects.description: Periodicity, trends and the behaviour of groups, plus the organic and spectroscopic classification strands at Higher Level. Trend questions reward explanation in terms of shielding and nuclear charge, and students who answer with the trend rather than its cause lose marks consistently.

subjects.name: Reactivity 1: what drives reactions
subjects.description: Energetics and thermodynamics, including enthalpy cycles and, at Higher Level, entropy and Gibbs free energy. The topic most commonly avoided from DP1 onwards, which is why it appears as a large deficit in DP2. Avoidance is expensive: it compounds.

subjects.name: Reactivity 2: how much, how fast, how far
subjects.description: Rates of reaction and equilibrium, with rate laws and the equilibrium constant extended at Higher Level. Equilibrium questions punish students who recite Le Chatelier without reasoning about the system. Responds well to question-led teaching and poorly to re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Reactivity 3: mechanisms of change
subjects.description: Acid-base behaviour, redox and organic mechanisms. Organic is the highest-return block in the whole subject: narrow, rule-governed, and the place where a single correctable habit — where the curly arrow starts — is costing marks in every question it appears in.

subjects.name: Organic mechanisms and curly arrows
subjects.description: The most diagnosable error in chemistry. A student who draws the arrow from the wrong electron pair loses the mark every time, and nobody has told them because the answer otherwise looks right. Three or four sessions, marked strictly, usually ends it permanently.

subjects.name: Paper 1A: multiple choice
subjects.description: No partial credit, so timing and elimination technique carry real marks. Students lose here by fully working questions that could be settled by a units check or an order-of-magnitude estimate, then running short on the data-analysis section that follows.

subjects.name: Paper 1B: data analysis
subjects.description: Unseen data: processing, graphing, uncertainty and a supported conclusion. Deliberately practised by almost nobody, which makes it the best value target for a mid-grade student. Three sessions here routinely outperform three sessions of content revision.

subjects.name: Paper 2: extended response
subjects.description: The largest component and the one where the grade mostly sits. Marks go to structured reasoning, correct state symbols and equations, and answers that match the command term. Marks are lost to abandoning a part-answered calculation instead of stating the method intended.

subjects.name: The Scientific Investigation
subjects.description: An individual investigation of up to 3,000 words, worth 20 per cent, marked on four criteria of six marks each. Research design sets the ceiling. Testing a research question for a measurable, controllable relationship costs twenty minutes of a tutor's time and protects a fifth of the grade.

subjects.name: Calculation technique and significant figures
subjects.description: Rearranging before substituting, carrying units, not rounding mid-calculation, and quoting answers to a defensible precision. Silent marks, lost in volume across both papers, and recovered in one or two sessions of strict marking — the cheapest purchase in the subject.

sections.heading: What decides the chemistry bill, case by case
paragraphs: The question every Villanova parent wants answered before committing is how many sessions this will take. It is answerable, and the answer depends on the diagnosis rather than on the student. The table below gives honest estimates by case, priced at the specialist band that Higher Level chemistry genuinely needs.

The spread is the point. A mechanisms habit costs four to eight sessions. An unsecured bonding foundation costs twenty to thirty. Both present to a parent as 'struggling with chemistry', and the difference between them is roughly AED 8,000. Nobody can tell which case they are in without reading marked work, which is why the first session should look at papers rather than discuss impressions.

The second pattern is about timing. Every case in the table gets more expensive the later it is addressed, but not evenly: habit problems stay cheap almost to the end, while content deficits become effectively unfixable in the final term and the money then buys damage limitation. A family with limited funds and a DP1 student should spend them on content. The same family with a DP2 student in March should spend them on technique and the investigation.

Our own practice follows the table. The free trial lesson exists to place a student in one of these rows and to say so plainly, including when the row is 'four sessions and then stop' — which happens often enough that we would rather be known for it than for selling a year.

sections.heading: The syllabus in two halves, and what each half costs to fix
paragraphs: Diploma chemistry is organised into Structure and Reactivity, studied at both levels with Higher Level extending each. Knowing which half is failing is the difference between a cheap intervention and an expensive one, and it is visible in two marked papers.

Structure is the foundational half: atomic structure and the mole concept, bonding and intermolecular forces, and the classification of matter through periodicity. Gaps here are expensive because everything later assumes them. A student who cannot reason from structure to property will keep meeting the same wall in new topics, and no amount of topic-specific teaching fixes it.

Reactivity is the applied half: energetics, rates and equilibrium, and the mechanisms of change including acid-base, redox and organic chemistry. Gaps here are more local and therefore cheaper, with one exception. Energetics is the topic students avoid, and avoidance compounds across two years into something that behaves like a structural deficit even though it started as a preference.

The practical implication for spending is to diagnose by half before buying hours. If the problem is in Structure, the honest conversation is about a content programme with a term-length horizon. If it is in Reactivity, a targeted block is usually enough, and organic in particular is the cheapest grade movement available in the subject. The diagnosis itself is quick: a Structure problem shows up as the same kind of reasoning failing in unrelated topics, while a Reactivity problem shows up as whole questions on one topic going wrong and the rest of the paper holding up.

sections.heading: Where chemistry money buys marks fastest
paragraphs: If a Villanova family has a limited budget and a DP2 student, there is an efficient order in which to spend it. This is that order, and it is not the order most tutoring arrangements follow.

First, organic mechanisms. The subject's single most diagnosable error is a curly arrow drawn from the wrong electron pair, and it costs the same mark in every question where a mechanism appears. The student usually has the chemistry right, which is why nobody has caught it: the answer looks plausible to everyone except a marker. Three or four strictly marked sessions typically end it permanently.

Second, calculation technique and significant figures. Carrying units, rearranging before substituting, not rounding mid-calculation and quoting a defensible precision. These are silent losses spread across both papers, and they are usually untaught rather than careless — few students have been shown what a defensible precision actually is. One or two sessions.

Third, Paper 1B data analysis, which is practised deliberately by almost nobody because revision defaults to content. Processing unseen data, plotting something interpretable, handling uncertainty and writing a conclusion the data supports. Fourth, whichever of equilibrium or energetics is failing, identified from the papers rather than from the student's own sense of which topic feels worst. And last, if the budget stretches, a general weekly arrangement — which is where most families start and which should usually come last. The order gets inverted in practice because a weekly slot is the easiest thing to buy and to sell, while a four-session block requires somebody to have read the marked work and to be willing to recommend less than a parent came expecting to purchase.
bullets: 1. Organic mechanisms: 3-4 sessions, marks in every mechanism question
2. Calculation technique and significant figures: 1-2 sessions, silent marks across both papers
3. Paper 1B data analysis: 3-5 sessions on a component nobody practises
4. Equilibrium or energetics, whichever the marked papers show
5. A general weekly arrangement — last, not first

sections.heading: Paper components, weightings and where the grade sits
paragraphs: Chemistry is assessed by two written papers plus the Scientific Investigation, and the split inside Paper 1 is the part families most often do not know about. Paper 1 carries a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section — two different skills in one sitting — and together with Paper 2 accounts for the great majority of the grade.

Approximate weightings are 36 per cent for Paper 1, 44 per cent for Paper 2, and 20 per cent for the investigation, with Higher Level sitting longer papers covering the additional content. Specification versions are revised, so confirm exact durations and weightings for your child's cohort with the school rather than treating any page as final, including this one.

For spending decisions the implication is direct: Paper 2 holds the largest share and is the component students practise least, because extended-response work is slow and feels less productive than answering thirty multiple-choice questions. One Paper 2 question properly marked and reviewed is worth more than a page of multiple choice, and families paying by the hour should ask what the session actually worked on.

The investigation is the other place where the arithmetic favours the parent. Twenty per cent of the grade, protected by three to six sessions of coaching that cost a fraction of a year of weekly tuition. The condition is timing: it has to happen before the research question is locked in and the data collected, because afterwards the ceiling is already set.

sections.heading: The investigation, and the cheapest twenty minutes in the course
paragraphs: The Scientific Investigation is 20 per cent of the chemistry grade, runs to a maximum of 3,000 words, and is marked against four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. That is twenty-four marks, publicly described, and most students choose their research question without having read the descriptors.

Research design sets the ceiling, which is why the highest-value conversation in the entire course takes about twenty minutes. A viable chemistry question needs a variable the student can change, a quantity they can measure with the school's equipment, and the other relevant variables controllable in that laboratory. Questions failing that test cannot score well on the later criteria, because there is nothing to process and nothing to conclude.

Data analysis and conclusion carry most of the recoverable marks: correct processing with uncertainties, a graph that supports an argument, and a conclusion justified by the measurements rather than by what the textbook predicts. Evaluation is the criterion most often written the night before, and it asks for specific prioritised weaknesses with realistic improvements, not generic remarks about human error.

The boundary needs stating plainly, because at least one operator ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments outright. A tutor may explain criteria, test a research question's viability, question reasoning, and give honest feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not design the investigation, produce or process the data, write or rewrite text, or supply a previous student's report. Those are passing off another person's work as the student's own — misconduct under IB rules, and a risk to the Diploma rather than to one grade.
bullets: Four criteria, six marks each, 24 total, 20% of the grade, 3,000 words maximum
Research design sets the ceiling — test the question before collecting data
Evaluation needs specific prioritised weaknesses, not remarks about human error
No tutor may design it, produce data, or write any part of it

sections.heading: In-home or online for chemistry, priced honestly
paragraphs: Because chemistry sits in the specialist band, the in-home travel premium lands on an already high rate, and in Villanova it lands at the top of the range. That makes this the subject where the format decision has the largest absolute cost.

The arithmetic: market in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, per Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. A specialist willing to drive to Al Qudra Road will quote at the upper end of that, because forty to sixty minutes each way has to be paid for. The same specialist online is in the AED 200 to 450 band. Over a twenty-session block the difference is commonly AED 1,000 to 3,000 for driving.

What the premium buys is presence, which is worth paying for in specific cases — a student who cannot concentrate on a screen, or who has a particular need that makes video work harder. It does not buy better chemistry teaching. The subject's working surface is a page of equations, mechanisms and graphs, all of which transfer well to a shared screen, with the advantage that mechanism diagrams drawn and annotated in a session are saved rather than lost in a notebook.

To be explicit: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, in Villanova or elsewhere, because that is a service we run only in India. If presence in the room is the requirement, the independent in-home market in this belt exists and the premium is its honest price. For most Diploma chemistry students it is a cost without a corresponding gain.
bullets: In-home: AED 180-500/hr including travel; Villanova sits at the top of that range
Online specialist: AED 200-450+; over 20 sessions the gap is often AED 1,000-3,000
The premium buys presence, not better teaching of mechanisms or calculations

sections.heading: Where chemistry tutoring money gets wasted in this belt
paragraphs: Five patterns, each seen often enough from Dubailand households to be worth naming, and each avoidable with a question asked before the first payment.

Buying a weekly year for a habit problem. A curly-arrow error or a significant-figures habit is four sessions of work; thirty sessions of general chemistry costs eight times as much and spends most of its time on topics the student already has. Second, paying the specialist band for supervision. If what your child needs is somebody to make them do the questions, that is a budget-band service at AED 33 to 65, and paying AED 300 for it wastes most of the hour.

Third, buying group science classes for a diagnosed gap. A group delivers one pace to everyone, which suits consolidation and cannot address an individual mechanisms or energetics problem. Monthly packages in this market are advertised from around AED 799 for eight sessions, which looks cheap until the drive and the mismatch are counted.

Fourth, leaving the investigation until the deadline, then paying for emergency sessions that cannot change the research design. Twenty per cent of the grade is decided at the question-choosing stage, and money spent after that is spent on presentation. Fifth, starting in March of DP2 with a structural content gap, when the realistic purchase is damage limitation rather than the grade the family is paying for. Being told that honestly is worth more than the sessions. The common thread in all five is that money is committed before evidence is read, and the evidence in every case is a marked paper the school has already produced for free.
bullets: A weekly year bought for what was a four-session habit problem
Specialist rates paid for homework supervision
Group classes bought to fix an individual diagnosed gap
Investigation help bought after the research question was locked in
A content deficit addressed in March, when only technique is still movable

sections.heading: Practicals, honesty, and what no price can buy
paragraphs: Two things need stating plainly in a subject where both are routinely fudged. The first is how laboratory work is handled when teaching happens online. The second is what is on sale in this market that should not be.

On practicals: the apparatus work stays at school, where the equipment, the technician and the safety framework are, and for the Scientific Investigation that is a requirement rather than a preference. Your child weighs, titrates, heats and records in the school laboratory under their teacher's supervision. No online session substitutes for that, and anyone claiming otherwise is overselling. What online teaching covers is the design, the processing, the uncertainty treatment, the graphing and the argument — which is where most of the assessed marks are.

On what cannot be bought: a promise about the final grade is not a product, and any page offering one either has unpublished refund terms or is making a claim it cannot honour. Completed coursework is not a shortcut but misconduct that risks the qualification. Board material — syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables — is published by the IB and should be cited and linked, never resold as a resource pack. And a star rating nobody can trace is not a reason to accept a higher quote.

One further caution specific to this market. We do not describe tutors as IB examiners unless current status can be evidenced, and examiner status in any case gives no access to marking, boundaries or paper content. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation or partnership, has no UAE office or centre, and names no school as a client. Those are the claims to check in any quote, including ours.
bullets: Apparatus work stays at school; the investigation requires it
Online teaching covers design, processing, uncertainty, graphing and argument
No promises about final grades, no completed coursework, no resold board material
No regulator or board approval is held or implied, and there is no UAE office

process.title: Send the level and two marked papers
process.description: Higher or Standard Level, the school and year group, and photographs of two marked papers. Those papers place a student in one of the diagnosis rows above within minutes, which is the only honest basis for an hours estimate. A description of what the student finds hard is a much weaker signal than their own marked work.

process.title: Hours estimated before a rate is quoted
process.description: We say how many sessions the job looks like, then quote. That order matters because chemistry cases range from four sessions to thirty, and a single headline rate quoted in advance tells a family nothing about what they will actually spend.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: A real lesson with the person who would continue, no card required. It tests the diagnosis and the fit at the same time: whether the losses are habit, technique or content, and whether the two of them work well together. If the style does not suit your child, say so and we match again.

process.title: A plan in spending order
process.description: The plan names what to attack first, and for a budget-limited family that order is deliberate: mechanisms and technique before general content, investigation coaching before the research question is locked. Each item carries a session count and a finish date rather than running indefinitely.

process.title: Marked strictly, reviewed each term
process.description: Work is marked the way an examiner marks it: state symbols, units, significant figures, command terms and mechanism conventions treated seriously rather than ticked as broadly right. Each term the plan is reviewed against marked evidence, and when a block is done we say so instead of extending it.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before a price
whyPoints.description: Chemistry cases range from four sessions to thirty, and the difference is roughly AED 8,000. We read marked papers and give an hours estimate before quoting, because a rate quoted in advance of any evidence is set for the seller's convenience rather than the student's need.

whyPoints.title: The cheap fixes first
whyPoints.description: Organic mechanisms, calculation technique and significant figures are the fastest grade movement in the subject and cost a handful of sessions. Most arrangements start with general weekly content instead, which is comfortable, expensive and slower.

whyPoints.title: Investigation coaching while it still matters
whyPoints.description: Twenty per cent of the grade is decided when the research question is chosen. Three to six sessions before that point protect it; the same sessions afterwards only improve presentation. Timing is the whole of the value here.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium on an already specialist rate
whyPoints.description: Nobody drives to Al Qudra Road, which in this belt removes the top of the AED 50 to 150 hourly travel premium from a rate that is already in the specialist band. Over a twenty-session block that is commonly AED 1,000 to 3,000 not spent on driving.

whyPoints.title: Claims you can check
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here names who published it. No promises about final grades, no completed coursework, no resold board material, no self-awarded ratings, no examiner claims we cannot evidence, no regulator approval, and no IB exam date — because ibo.org blocks automated verification.

faqs.question: What does an IB chemistry tutor cost for a Villanova family?
faqs.answer: Chemistry sits in the specialist band, which published Dubai figures put at AED 200 to 450 or more an hour: TutorChase at AED 270, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, and Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 200 to 450+. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, and Villanova sits at the top of that because the drive is long. The total matters more than the rate: a four-session mechanisms block is AED 800 to 1,800, while a year of weekly sessions is AED 6,000 to 13,500.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Villanova chemistry case usually take?
faqs.answer: It depends on the diagnosis, not the student. A curly-arrow habit in organic mechanisms is four to eight sessions. Moles fluency is three to six. Command terms and significant figures are one to three. Equilibrium or rates reasoning is six to ten. An unsecured bonding foundation from DP1 is twenty to thirty, because every later topic assumes it. All of those present to a parent as 'struggling with chemistry', and only marked papers distinguish between them — which is why a first session should read work rather than discuss impressions.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topic gives the fastest improvement for the money?
faqs.answer: Organic mechanisms, almost always. The subject's most diagnosable error is a curly arrow drawn from the wrong electron pair, which loses the same mark in every mechanism question and is invisible to the student because the rest of the answer looks right. Three or four strictly marked sessions usually end it for good. Second fastest is calculation technique and significant figures — carrying units, not rounding mid-calculation, quoting a defensible precision — which is one or two sessions and recovers marks spread across both papers.

faqs.question: Which chemistry problems are expensive to fix?
faqs.answer: The structural ones. A student who never securely learned bonding and intermolecular forces in DP1 is carrying a deficit that touches every later topic, and that is a content programme of twenty to thirty sessions rather than a block. The same is true of energetics avoided since the first term: avoidance compounds, and by DP2 it behaves like a foundational gap. Both get worse with delay in a way that habit problems do not, so a DP1 family with limited funds should spend them here rather than on technique.

faqs.question: Where does the chemistry grade actually sit across the components?
faqs.answer: Mostly in Paper 2. Approximate weightings are 36 per cent for Paper 1, which combines multiple choice with a data-analysis section, 44 per cent for Paper 2 extended response, and 20 per cent for the Scientific Investigation. Higher Level sits longer papers with additional content; confirm exact durations with your child's school, since specification versions get revised. The spending implication is that extended-response practice carries the most weight and is practised least, because thirty multiple-choice questions feel more productive than one question properly reviewed.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for help with the chemistry investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the timing is right, because three to six sessions protect 20 per cent of the grade at a fraction of the cost of a year of weekly tuition. The condition is that it happens before the research question is locked and the data collected. Research design sets the ceiling: a viable question needs a variable the student can change, a quantity measurable with the school's equipment, and the other variables controllable. Spent after that point, the same money only improves presentation.

faqs.question: What may a chemistry tutor do with my child's investigation?
faqs.answer: Explain each criterion, test whether a research question has a measurable and controllable relationship in it, question the reasoning, and give honest feedback on a draft your child wrote. What a tutor may not do is design the investigation, produce or process the data, write or rewrite text, or supply a previous student's report as a model. Those are passing off another person's work as the student's own, which is misconduct under IB rules and risks the Diploma rather than one grade. At least one operator in this market sells completed reports; avoid them.

faqs.question: How are chemistry practicals handled if the tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: The apparatus work stays at school, where the equipment, technician and safety framework are, and for the Scientific Investigation that is required rather than preferred. Your child weighs, titrates, heats and records in the school laboratory under their teacher's supervision. What online teaching covers is everything around it: investigation design, processing with correct uncertainties, graphing, and writing conclusions and evaluations — which is where most of the assessed marks are. A tutor claiming a screen can replace the laboratory is overselling.

faqs.question: Will a chemistry tutor travel to our home in Villanova?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we offer only in India, so no tutor will arrive at a Dubailand address. Independent in-home chemistry tutors work in this belt at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, at the top of that range for Villanova because the drive is long. Over a twenty-session block the travel component commonly adds AED 1,000 to 3,000, and it buys presence rather than better teaching of mechanisms.

faqs.question: Is a group science class cheaper than one-to-one chemistry?
faqs.answer: Per hour, clearly; monthly packages in this market are advertised from around AED 799 for eight sessions. Per outcome it depends on the diagnosis. A group delivers one pace to everyone, which suits a student who is broadly on track and wants more practice, and cannot address an individual mechanisms or energetics gap. Add the drive from Villanova to Motor City — twenty-five to forty minutes each way plus waiting — and a short one-to-one block is often cheaper to the finish line.

faqs.question: My child needs Higher Level chemistry for medicine. Does that change the budget?
faqs.answer: It changes the justification rather than the arithmetic. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and most life-science routes commonly expect chemistry at Higher Level, so the grade has a hard requirement attached and the specialist band becomes easier to justify than it would be for general support. What does not change is the order of spending: mechanisms and technique first, investigation coaching before the question is locked, content programmes only where marked papers show a structural gap. And no tutoring is a requirement for admission anywhere.

faqs.question: Can we stop paying once the grade moves?
faqs.answer: That is how we would prefer it to work. Plans name a session count and a finish date, and each term the arrangement is reviewed against marked papers to ask whether it still earns its place. Most chemistry problems are finite — a habit, a technique, one topic — and the ones that are not should be identified at the start rather than discovered after twenty sessions. If a block is done, we will say so rather than extend it quietly into the next term.

faqs.question: Does the price include VAT and any materials?
faqs.answer: Ask, and require the answer in writing before the first paid session. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general fact, because that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an opinion. On materials: nobody should be charging you for IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are published by the IB and should be cited and linked. A provider bundling them as a paid resource pack is selling you something they do not own.

faqs.question: Do chemistry tutors working with Dubai students need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years according to u.ae. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service. Since the permit is free, no tutor should pass on a licensing cost, and because no fine schedule is published, treat any penalty figure quoted at you as unverified.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-villanova.closingHeading: Find out which chemistry problem you have before you buy hours
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-villanova.closingBody: The difference between a cheap chemistry fix and an expensive one is roughly AED 8,000, and only marked work tells you which you are facing. Dig out two marked papers, note the level, and send both. You will get an honest placement — habit, technique or structural gap — a session count, and a rate quoted after the free trial lesson rather than before anyone has seen the evidence. Teaching is live, one-to-one and online on Gulf Standard Time; the laboratory stays at school, and nobody drives to Dubailand.

dubai/ib-classes.tutorsIntro: The specialists below teach single Diploma subjects rather than a general science or maths brief. Each works from your child's own marked papers and your school's assessment calendar, and each writes the session note you receive afterwards. Pick a subject and level and ask for a trial.

intro.heading: The evidence a class leaves behind, week by week
paragraphs: Most Dubai families book IB classes on a feeling. A report card came back lower than expected, or a mock paper landed two grades below target, and something has to change. Six weeks later the same family is trying to decide whether the classes are working, and the only thing available to judge by is their child's mood on a Thursday evening. That is not a decision anybody can make well. An IB class should leave a paper trail — a marked script, a list of the syllabus statements covered, a mark against a named criterion, a note of what was set for the week ahead — and that trail is the only honest basis for continuing, changing tutor, or stopping.

Dubai is the densest private-school market in the country. The Dubai Media Office reported 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment against 37% on UK curricula. KHDA inspects those schools annually and publishes a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak. That report is genuinely useful context, and it is also the wrong instrument for the question a parent is asking. It describes a school. It says nothing about which four marks your child dropped in the last structured question on energetics.

A session record closes that gap. Ours lists the syllabus sub-topics touched, the questions attempted, the marks earned per question against the published mark scheme, and the specific error category behind each loss — method not shown, units omitted, command term misread, concept absent. After four sessions the pattern is visible on a page rather than remembered differently by three people. After six weeks there is a second marked script on the same topic to set beside the first, which is what movement actually looks like.

The record protects the student as well as the family. Diploma coordinators in Dubai schools routinely ask whether outside help was used on an Internal Assessment, and they are right to ask. A dated trail of the student's own drafts, with the tutor's feedback held separately from the writing, answers that question in the student's favour. A tutor who edits paragraphs into a draft leaves no such defence, and under IB academic-honesty rules the consequence lands on the candidate, not on the tutor.

One point of plain fact about delivery. These classes are taught one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time so a session can sit after a school run and before homework collapses. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. That is a limit worth stating early, because it also buys something: a Higher Level Chemistry specialist is matched to the subject rather than to whoever happens to live twenty minutes from your building.

Marked past paper questions with the per-question mark breakdown attached
A topic checklist reviewed every fourth session, not rewritten from memory
Dated coursework drafts kept separate from the tutor's written feedback
A six-week review that compares two marked scripts on the same component

dubai/ib-classes.programmesIntro: Dubai schools run the IB continuum in different combinations: some offer the Primary Years Programme through to the Diploma, others pick up the IB only at 16 after IGCSE. What each programme produces as evidence differs sharply, and that changes what a weekly class should be generating.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations and no published grades. Assessment is continuous and teacher-held, which means a parent rarely sees a mark at all. Support at this stage works on readable artefacts instead: a reading record, a written number-sense check, a piece of writing before and after a fortnight of work on structure. The useful evidence is a comparison, not a score.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP schools must also deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies under KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab pupils. For a non-Arab child starting Arabic as an additional language in Year 3, the only honest early evidence is a vocabulary and script-formation check repeated every few weeks.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Marked against criteria A to D in most subjects, each on a 0-8 band, then converted to a 1-7 grade by a published boundary table the school holds. This is where a parent can start reading real evidence, because every task comes back with criterion letters attached. Most families never ask to see the band descriptors, which is the single cheapest piece of homework available to them.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools that run MYP then DP tend to set the eProject or personal project in Year 11, in the same term as IGCSE-equivalent mock weeks at sibling schools. Session records matter here because the criterion language carries straight into the Diploma: a student who learns what a Criterion C 7-8 band looks like at 15 reads an Internal Assessment rubric faster at 17.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries internally assessed work worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade, marked by the teacher against published criteria and then moderated externally. The evidence trail here is dense and almost never organised: marked papers, draft feedback, internal deadlines and a predicted grade that arrives before any of it is final.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts sit the May session, with results used for UK, North American and increasingly UAE university entry. The pressure point is DP1 term two, when Internal Assessment work in three or four subjects lands at once beside the Extended Essay question deadline. A dated draft trail is what keeps that fortnight from turning into an academic-honesty conversation.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Smaller in the UAE than the full Diploma, and the assessment evidence is a mix of IB-marked components and provider-marked units, which is why families often cannot tell which mark counts for what.
programmes.countryNote: Only a handful of Dubai schools license the Career-related Programme, so a family moving into it usually has no peers to compare notes with. Weekly classes here work best on the Diploma courses taken alongside it, where the mark scheme is public and the reflective project criteria can be read directly from the IB subject guide the school holds.

dubai/ib-classes.subjectsIntro: What follows is read from marked scripts rather than from subject descriptions. For each Diploma subject below, the note says what a marked paper usually reveals first — the error that shows up before anything else, and the one a session note should be recording week by week.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marked scripts almost always show method marks earned and accuracy marks lost: a correct differentiation followed by an arithmetic slip, or a right answer with no working line to award M1 against. The session note should separate those two categories, because they need entirely different work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics questions come back with the test chosen correctly and the conclusion written in the wrong register — a p-value quoted with no reference to the hypothesis. Graphic display calculator questions lose marks for undocumented screens. Both are visible on the script and fixable inside two sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and equilibrium produce the heaviest losses, and the mark scheme usually shows why: a sign convention dropped, or an explanation that describes the shift without naming the driver. Higher Level organic mechanisms lose marks on curly-arrow placement rather than on the chemistry itself.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Scripts show the pattern plainly: strong numerical work, thin written explanation. Marks go on questions asking for a reason rather than a value, and on units and significant figures in the final line. Error-carried-forward credit is routinely lost because students stop after a wrong intermediate result.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Marked papers show recall intact and application missing. A student who can define osmosis loses four marks on a data-based question about a specific tissue. The error log almost always fills with command-term misreads: described where the question asked for an explanation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams appear unlabelled, or labelled and then never referenced in the prose. Evaluation paragraphs list two sides and stop short of a judgement, which is where the top band sits. Higher Level calculation questions lose accuracy marks rather than method marks.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study answers return with tool names used as decoration — a SWOT drawn, then ignored. The marked script shows application marks missing because the answer never touches the stimulus material. Quantitative questions lose marks on formula recall, not on interpretation.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 scripts show close reading replaced by summary. Marks are earned for analysis of a specific technique in a specific line, and lost when a paragraph describes what the text is about. Individual Oral feedback usually names the global issue as the weak half.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study detail is the dividing line. Scripts with named places, dates and figures score; scripts with general processes do not. Marked papers show the missing specifics clearly, and a session note can track how many named examples a student can now deploy unaided.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode answers lose marks on initialisation and loop boundaries rather than on logic. Higher Level questions on resource management return with the concept understood and the terminology imprecise. Both show up as a repeated annotation on consecutive scripts.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay comes back with knowledge questions treated as topics. Marks sit in the discussion of how a claim is justified, not in the subject content used as an example. Feedback on a draft should name the assessment instrument's wording rather than rewrite the argument.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils and Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for first-language cohorts. Progress evidence is script formation, reading fluency and vocabulary retention, checked on a repeated task rather than a single test.

dubai/ib-classes.regionsIntro: Dubai is a city of distinct school catchments rather than one market. The notes below record what each area actually contains and what it changes about scheduling an evening session, because a 5pm start means different things in Mirdif and in Dubai Marina.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha South
regions.note: The densest concentration of IB World Schools in the emirate, which is why families here compare notes constantly. Pupils often reach home by 3.30pm, making a 4.30pm session realistic without eating into the evening.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Apartment living, so the practical constraint is a quiet surface and a door that closes rather than travel. Most secondary pupils here commute out of the area to school, returning between 4pm and 5pm depending on the Sheikh Zayed Road run.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Villa communities feeding both British and IB schools along the beach road. Sessions here commonly sit at 6pm, after sport, with the family wanting the written note the same evening rather than the next morning.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Served by a full IB continuum school and several large CBSE schools, so households frequently run two curricula at once. A single written record per child matters more here than anywhere, because the two systems report progress in incompatible language.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Long school runs in both directions, with secondary pupils regularly home after 4.30pm. Evening slots at 6.30pm or 7pm are normal, and the session note is often read by a parent who was not in the house when the lesson happened.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Newer villa stock around two established IB continuum schools. Families here often start Diploma support in DP1 rather than DP2, which makes a six-week evidence log genuinely comparable over two years.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: High-rise households with students travelling to schools across the city. Scheduling is driven by the return commute, not the distance, and a recorded topic checklist survives a month of travel better than a verbal plan.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf and Dubai Creek Harbour
regions.note: A growing catchment around one IB continuum school, with many families new to the Diploma and no local precedent to draw on. The first diagnostic script matters most here because there is nothing to benchmark it against.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Barsha South and Al Sufouh
schoolClusters.note: Students we support in this cluster most often ask for Higher Level Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, and the Internal Assessment drafts arrive in DP1 term two rather than DP2. Inspection bands for these schools are published annually on KHDA's own site and should be read there rather than taken from a tutoring website.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Nad Al Sheba and Al Jaddaf
schoolClusters.note: A continuum cluster, so students arrive in the Diploma having been marked against MYP criteria for five years. That is an advantage a session note should use: the criterion vocabulary is already familiar, and the first evidence log can start from a real baseline rather than a guess.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Hills, Arabian Ranches and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: Mixed British and IB provision, with several schools running A Level and the Diploma side by side. Students we support here often need help choosing between the two routes in Year 11, and the useful evidence for that decision is a marked IGCSE paper rather than a preference.

dubai/ib-classes.modesIntro: Three ways a Dubai family uses these classes. Each produces a different kind of record, and the choice should follow what you need to be able to read at the end of a month rather than what sounds most thorough.

modes.title: Weekly diagnostic cycle
modes.description: One 60-minute session a week on a single subject, structured as diagnose, rebuild, re-test. The first session of each cycle is a timed question marked against the published scheme; the second rebuilds the topic it exposed; the third re-tests on a different question. The record is two comparable marked scripts per topic.

sections.heading: What an IB class should leave behind when it ends
paragraphs: A 60-minute class is worth whatever survives it. If nothing is written down, the lesson exists only in two memories that will diverge within a fortnight — the student's, which tends to record how difficult it felt, and the tutor's, which tends to record what was intended. Neither is evidence. The table below lists what each session in a Dubai family's plan actually produces, when it is produced, and who ends up holding the copy.

The point of naming the holder is practical. A session note that lives only in a tutor's own files is useless to a parent deciding in week seven whether to carry on. A marked script that lives only on the student's desk gets lost before the next mock. Each artefact has one owner and one purpose, and a family should be able to produce all five from a single folder by the end of a term.

Nothing in the list is expensive to generate. The marked script takes the time it takes to mark; the session note takes a few minutes; the topic checklist is a single page updated with a pen. The reason competitors do not publish anything like it is not cost but exposure: a written record makes a stalled plan visible at week six, which is precisely when a provider would rather the conversation did not happen. That is the right time for it to happen.

Ask for the shape of the record before the first paid session rather than after the first disappointing month. A provider that writes session notes already has a template and can show you one. A provider that does not will tell you the lessons are going well, which is reassurance rather than information. The question costs nothing and sorts this market quickly.

sections.heading: Reading a marked paper: the annotations that carry the diagnosis
paragraphs: Most parents in Dubai have seen a marked IB or IGCSE script and read only the total. The useful information is in the margin, written in a shorthand nobody explains at parents' evening. Learning five of those abbreviations changes what a report card means, because it tells you whether your child lost marks for not knowing something or for not writing it down in the order the scheme wanted.

The distinction matters because the remedies have nothing in common. A student losing accuracy marks on correct methods needs drilling on units, significant figures and exact forms — a fortnight of work, no new content. A student losing method marks has a content gap that will reappear in every paper until it is rebuilt from the syllabus statement upwards. Treating the second as the first is the most common wasted month in private tuition anywhere.

Ask your child's teacher for the published mark scheme alongside a returned script, or ask a tutor to mark a past paper question against it in front of the student. The schemes are the boards' copyright and we neither host nor distribute them; they are available through the school, which holds a licence. What a class adds is the reading: which annotation repeats, how often, and on which component.

One practical warning about buying marking. A tutor who marks a script inside the paid hour is charging you to read, and twenty minutes of a sixty-minute lesson disappears before any teaching starts. Marking belongs between sessions. Ask where it happens before agreeing a rate, because the answer changes the useful cost of an hour more than the rate itself does.

sections.heading: Command terms are the gap between a 4 and a 6
paragraphs: Every IB question opens with an instruction, and the instruction is worth more than the topic. A student who knows the content of a syllabus statement and answers an evaluate question by describing the situation will score in the bottom half of the band every time, in every subject, for two years. It is the most reliably recoverable loss on any Diploma script, and almost nobody treats it as a topic in its own right.

The command terms are published in the front matter of each IB subject guide, which your child's school holds. Reading them takes twenty minutes. Using them is harder, because the habit being replaced is the one that worked at 14: write everything you know and hope the marks are in there somewhere. In the Diploma that habit costs time on a paper with no spare minutes and earns nothing above the lowest band.

A class fixes this with marked evidence rather than advice. Take a returned script, highlight every command term, and compare what the student did with what the term demanded. Do it twice and the pattern is undeniable; the student usually names it themselves. The figures in the final column below are indicative of what is typically at stake per question — check the real allocation against the subject guide and the paper your child is sitting.

The subjects where this costs most are the written ones. In Biology, Geography, Economics and History a misread command term can cost most of the marks on a long question, while in Mathematics it usually costs one. A student carrying three essay-based Higher Level subjects should treat command terms as a topic in their own right, with sessions allocated to them.

sections.heading: Six weeks of evidence: what movement actually looks like
paragraphs: Progress in a Diploma subject is not a smooth line and does not show up weekly. It shows up as a second marked script on the same topic scoring differently from the first. Six weeks is roughly the shortest honest window for that, because it takes one session to diagnose, two or three to rebuild a topic properly, and one more to re-test on an unseen question.

The log below is the shape of a real first block for a single Higher Level subject. The detail that surprises families is week one: the diagnostic routinely narrows four assumed weaknesses to two actual ones. A student who believes they are bad at a whole subject is usually losing marks in two identifiable places, and the relief of seeing that written down does more for the next five weeks than any amount of encouragement.

Week six is the decision point, not week two. If the comparison script shows no movement on the component worked on, the honest conclusions are a different tutor, a different diagnosis, or a different number of sessions — and the family has a page to argue from rather than an impression. We would rather have that conversation at six weeks than take a payment at twelve.

Keep the baseline script. Families routinely throw the first diagnostic away because the result was poor, which destroys the only thing a week-six comparison can be measured against. Scan it, date it, put it in the folder. By the end of a first term it is the most useful single page in the file, precisely because it was the worst result.
