dubai/ib-computer-science-tutor.programmesIntro: Computer Science formally exists only in the Diploma Programme, but the computational thinking it assesses is built earlier, and Dubai families often ask about it before the DP choice is made.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Computer Science sits in Group 4, the sciences, at Standard or Higher Level. Core content covers system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and computational thinking, with Higher Level adding abstract data structures, resource management and control. All candidates study one option topic chosen by the school, and all submit a computational solution developed for an identified client. Higher Level candidates additionally sit a paper on an annually released case study.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Computer Science cohorts are small, and Higher Level groups in a single school are often fewer than ten students. That has two consequences. Teaching is frequently excellent because the teacher is a specialist who chose the subject, and there is almost no peer benchmarking, so a student has no idea whether their solution documentation is strong or weak until it is moderated.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Design is where the habits that carry the computational solution are formed: identifying a client, specifying success criteria, developing a design, testing against the criteria and evaluating honestly. There is no MYP Computer Science, but a student who has taken the MYP design cycle seriously arrives in DP1 understanding why documentation matters, which is more than half the battle.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai IB continuum schools run MYP Design into DP Computer Science in the same building, and the handover is one of the better ones in the programme. What does not transfer is scale: an MYP design project forgives a vague client, and a DP computational solution does not, because the client is the source of the success criteria everything else is tested against.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Where the career-related study is technology, Computer Science is a natural DP pairing on the CP route, and students sit the same papers and submit the same computational solution as DP candidates. The lighter overall load often means more time for the solution, which is an advantage in a component where development time is the real constraint.
programmes.countryNote: CP technology pathways are growing in the UAE alongside the wider economy, and a CP student taking Computer Science in Dubai is frequently the only one in their cohort. For a subject assessed partly through documentation standards, that isolation matters: there is nobody to compare a draft against, which is exactly the gap an external reader fills.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No Computer Science content. PYP units build inquiry habits and some schools introduce block-based programming, but presenting any of that as preparation for the Diploma Programme course would be dishonest. The genuinely useful early foundation is mathematics fluency and clear written explanation, both of which the DP course leans on heavily.
programmes.countryNote: For Dubai parents planning a long IB route, the practical note is that Computer Science is chosen in Year 11 and that the mathematics course taken alongside it matters. Students arriving at Higher Level Computer Science with weak algebraic fluency find the abstract data structures content considerably harder than their programming ability predicts.

dubai/ib-computer-science-tutor.subjectsIntro: Computer Science is almost always requested alongside something else, usually mathematics or physics, and the combinations are worth understanding because the overlap is real.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Core system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and computational thinking, plus one option topic and a computational solution. Higher Level adds abstract data structures, resource management, control and a case study paper. Marks go missing on written papers, not in code.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The standard partner for students aiming at computer science degrees. Algebraic fluency and proof habits transfer directly to complexity reasoning and to the abstract data structures content at Higher Level, which is where weaker mathematicians stall.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Works for students heading towards data or information systems rather than theoretical computer science. Statistics and modelling content supports the data-handling parts of a computational solution, though some overseas computer science degrees prefer Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Shares Group 4 and a quantitative mindset. Circuit and logic content sits close to the computer organisation topic, and students taking both find the hardware half of the core less abstract than those meeting it for the first time.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: The nearest relative outside Group 4 thinking. Both courses assess a client-driven design process with testing against stated criteria, so a student taking both practises the same documentation discipline twice and usually writes a stronger solution.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: Covers the social and ethical dimension the Computer Science course touches more briefly. Students taking both write better evaluations, because they can discuss consequences of a system design rather than only its performance.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frequently paired by Dubai students planning technology entrepreneurship. The overlap that matters is client identification: both subjects penalise a vague stakeholder and reward a specific one with stated needs.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Underrated for this subject. The computational solution is assessed through written documentation, and students whose technical writing is loose lose marks their code does not deserve to lose. Clear English is worth real marks here.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Supplies the vocabulary for evaluating a system honestly rather than defending it. Students who engage with TOK tend to write evaluations that acknowledge limitations, which is exactly what the solution criteria reward.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Common in Group 4 pairings for students keeping medicine and engineering open alongside computing. No content overlap with Computer Science, but both courses demand precise recording of method, which transfers to documentation quality.

dubai/ib-computer-science-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities Computer Science requests come from
dubai/ib-computer-science-tutor.regionsIntro: Because the subject is a minority option, requests cluster tightly around the schools that offer it, and the pattern across the emirate is less about geography than about which school a community feeds.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Technology-sector households and several universities nearby, so parents often have professional programming experience and are surprised to find it does not translate into helping with written papers. Requests here are usually precise and component-named.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Lakes
regions.note: Feeds long-established Diploma Programme provision where Computer Science has been offered for years with a settled option topic. Requests tend to arrive early in DP1 and concern the computational solution rather than content.

regions.name: Al Barsha South and Dubai Production City
regions.note: Mixed housing with schools running both the IB and British routes, so siblings sometimes study Computer Science under different specifications. Families here frequently ask how the DP course differs from IGCSE Computer Science.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Beach Residence
regions.note: High mid-year arrival rates, and Computer Science is particularly unforgiving of a mid-programme school move because the new school may have chosen a different option topic and a different programming language.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Nahda
regions.note: Established eastern communities a long drive from much of the emirate's Diploma Programme provision. For a minority subject, the chance of a specialist living within a reasonable travel radius is small, which is where video delivery stops being a preference.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Al Barari
regions.note: Newer villa communities with a growing secondary population and families often planning Group 4 choices a year ahead. The common question is whether Computer Science or Physics is the better keep-options-open pick.

regions.note: Apartment living with short commutes, which makes weekday sessions straightforward. Computational solution work is easier to schedule here than in communities where sport and the school run take the early evening.

schoolClusters.note: Schools that have run the Diploma Programme course long enough to have a settled option topic and a teacher who specialises in it. Students we support from these schools usually need documentation standards and case study technique rather than content.

schoolClusters.note: Schools that added the Diploma Programme more recently or emphasise technology in their wider offer, where Computer Science may run at Standard Level only depending on numbers. Enquiries often begin with whether Higher Level will actually be available.

schoolClusters.note: Schools running IGCSE and A Level Computer Science whose students sometimes move into the Diploma Programme, or whose families are comparing the routes. The conversation here is usually about how a DP computational solution differs from an A Level project.

modes.title: Written paper content and technique
modes.description: Weekly or fortnightly sessions on the core and option content that the written papers examine: system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks, computational thinking and the Higher Level extensions. This is the half of the course students neglect, because it feels less interesting than programming and carries more marks than programming does.

The tutor explains what each documented section has to demonstrate, questions whether the success criteria are testable, and points out where a design decision has been made without being recorded. sections.heading: The five checks, and what a good answer sounds like
paragraphs: Verification in this subject is unusually easy once a parent knows what to ask, because every question has a factual answer that a genuine Diploma Programme tutor gives instantly and a generic programmer cannot. The table below sets out the five, what a confident answer looks like, and what an evasive one looks like.

The language question is first for a reason. Dubai schools teach the course in different programming languages, and a tutor who has taught it in one and not the other will spend the student's paid hours learning the syntax. That is not a crime, but it should be disclosed and it should affect the rate. Ask the school which language is used before you ask any tutor anything.

The documentation question separates professionals from practitioners faster than any other. A software engineer describes how they would build the solution. A Diploma Programme tutor describes what the documentation has to demonstrate, section by section, and explains that a working program with thin documentation scores worse than a modest program documented properly. That distinction is the whole component.

The permit question is the one parents skip and should not. Any individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time. A tutor who holds one will say so immediately; a tutor who has never heard of it is telling you something.

sections.heading: What a scarce subject does to AED rates in Dubai
paragraphs: Computer Science prices differently from mathematics in this emirate, and not for the reason families assume. The published bands are the same, because providers price by level and format rather than by subject. What differs is availability: with the International Baccalaureate at around 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment and Computer Science a minority option within that, the number of people in or near Dubai who have taught Higher Level Computer Science is small.

The practical effect is that the binding constraint in the exam term is a calendar, not a price list. A family that waits until February to look for a Higher Level specialist for the case study paper may find that the right person has no slots, at any rate. Booking earlier costs the same per hour and secures something that money cannot reliably buy later, which is an unusual situation in a tutoring market.

The second effect concerns in-home tutoring specifically. Market in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, and for a common subject that premium buys convenience. For Computer Science it often buys a compromise, because the set of people who have taught this course and are willing to drive to a particular community on a particular evening may be empty. The honest answer in that situation is to widen the pool, not to accept a generalist.

None of the figures below is our price. IB Gram's model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and a specific number for a specific student comes from that conversation. What the table does is let a Dubai family judge any quote they receive against what the market has actually published.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually are: written papers, not working code
paragraphs: The most expensive misunderstanding in this subject is that Computer Science is assessed through programming. It is not. The majority of the grade comes from written examination papers testing core content, and the internally assessed component is judged on documentation. A student who writes elegant software and cannot explain a two-dimensional array in prose will be disappointed in August.

The core content is broad and specific: system fundamentals including the planning and installation of systems, computer organisation including architecture and binary representation, networks, and computational thinking covering problem specification, algorithm design and the construction of flowcharts and pseudocode. Higher Level adds abstract data structures, resource management and control systems. All of it is examined in written prose, often against command terms that students handle loosely.

The characteristic loss is the answer that demonstrates understanding without answering the question asked. A question that says outline wants a brief account of the relevant points; one that says explain wants reasons; one that says evaluate wants a weighed judgement. Students with strong technical knowledge frequently write everything they know, which earns the marks for one command term and none for the others.

The second characteristic loss is pseudocode. Students who code fluently in a real language write pseudocode in that language's syntax and lose marks for conventions. It is a small, mechanical fix, and it is worth finding before the examination rather than in it. Tracing a given algorithm by hand, with a trace table, is the other skill worth drilling: it appears regularly and it is pure technique.
bullets: Most of the grade is written prose about systems, not code
Command terms handled loosely cost marks that knowledge has already earned
Pseudocode written in a real language's syntax loses convention marks
Trace tables are pure technique and appear regularly
Binary and hexadecimal conversion marks are free and routinely rushed
Higher Level abstract data structures need written explanation, not just implementation

sections.heading: The computational solution: a client, testable criteria and honest testing
paragraphs: The internally assessed solution asks a student to develop a product for an identified client, with success criteria agreed with that client, and to document the planning, design, development, functionality and evaluation. Every weak solution fails in the same place: the client is fictional, so the criteria are whatever the student felt like building, so the evaluation has nothing real to be measured against.

A good client is a person who will answer questions and who wants something. A school librarian, a sports coach who records results on paper, a small business that tracks bookings in a notebook. Dubai is full of such clients, which is an advantage, and the student has to approach one honestly and early. The criteria then come from the client's actual need, which makes the evaluation section write itself.

The documentation is where the marks live, and it rewards decisions that were recorded as they were made. A student who develops for six weeks and documents afterwards is reconstructing a story, and it reads like one. A student who records each design decision, with the alternative they rejected and why, produces development documentation an examiner can follow. That habit costs ten minutes a session and is the single highest-return discipline in the component.

The boundary is firm. A tutor may explain what each documented section must demonstrate, ask whether a success criterion is actually testable, question a data structure choice, read the student's own documentation and respond with questions and criteria references. A tutor may not write code for the solution, debug it by supplying corrected lines, or draft documentation text. Supplying any part of assessed work is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate.

sections.heading: The Higher Level case study, and why it should be started early
paragraphs: Higher Level candidates sit an additional paper based on a case study released by the IB ahead of the examination. It describes a scenario and names specific technologies, and the paper asks candidates to apply core content and researched understanding to that scenario. It is the most front-loadable assessment in the subject and the one most often left until the last month.

The reason it is left late is that it looks like reading. Students read the case study, feel they understand it, and move on. The paper does not reward having read it; it rewards knowing what each named technology actually is, how it works, what its limitations are, and how the core content applies to the scenario. Building that knowledge takes weeks of small research tasks, which is exactly the kind of work that fits into DP2 before the pressure arrives.

The productive method is a glossary. Every technology, protocol and acronym in the case study goes into a list, each one gets researched to the depth of a paragraph the student could write from memory, and then extended answers are practised that connect those terms to syllabus content. A tutor is genuinely useful here as a quality check on depth: students consistently stop researching at the point where they could recognise a term rather than explain it.

A practical caution about dates. The case study changes between examination sessions, so any material found online referring to a previous one is useless, and some of the tutoring market sells exactly that. Confirm with the school's teacher which case study is live for the session the student is sitting, and work only from that.

sections.heading: Why screen sharing is the right room for this subject
paragraphs: Most arguments about online tutoring concern whether video is an acceptable substitute for presence. For Computer Science the argument runs the other way: the work happens on a screen, and a session where both people can see and control the same screen is better than two people leaning over one laptop.

Three specifics. Debugging is observational work, and a tutor watching a student's editor in real time sees the moment the student guesses rather than reasons, which is the habit worth fixing. Tracing an algorithm benefits from a shared document both parties can annotate line by line. And documentation work is reading and commenting on a live file, which is native to a shared screen and clumsy on paper.

There is a fourth, less obvious advantage in a small-cohort subject. Over video, a Dubai student can be matched with somebody who has taught their specific option topic in their specific language, which is unlikely to be true of anybody within a twenty-minute drive. For a subject with single-figure Higher Level cohorts, that is the difference between a specialist and a willing generalist.

The honest case for a tutor in the room still exists for younger students who need supervision as much as teaching, and for households where connectivity is unreliable. IB Gram does not offer that service in the UAE regardless; home visits are part of our India offering only, and no sentence here should suggest otherwise. For a Diploma Programme Computer Science candidate, we think the trade is clearly the right way round.

sections.heading: Option topics, school choices and the mid-year move problem
paragraphs: Every Computer Science candidate studies one option topic, and the school chooses it. The content is examinable, it differs substantially between options, and a student cannot sensibly revise an option their school did not teach. Families should know which one their school selected, and it is worth asking the teacher directly rather than assuming.

This becomes a live problem in Dubai because the school population is mobile. A student who moves school mid-programme may arrive at a school teaching a different option topic, in a different programming language, having built a computational solution to a different timetable. That is three separate catch-up jobs, and the one families notice last is the option topic, because it does not surface until revision begins.

The sensible response is an audit rather than a panic. List what the previous school covered, list what the new school's option requires, and identify the gap precisely. Usually a term of fortnightly work closes it, and the earlier it is identified the less it costs. Where the programming language has changed, the solution may need to be restarted, which is a scheduling problem more than an academic one.

A practical note on advice from outside the UAE. Much of the Computer Science tutoring material online is written for a different option topic or a previous version of the guide. Dubai families should confirm the live specification and the chosen option with their school's Diploma Programme coordinator, and treat any tutor who does not ask which option the school teaches with appropriate caution.

sections.heading: Availability, fallback and what we will not pretend
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages end with an invitation. This one ends with a disclosure, because for a minority subject the honest constraint is supply. Higher Level Computer Science with case study support in the exam term is one of the narrowest specialisms we match, and there are weeks when nobody suitable has a slot.

When that happens, the options are a start date in the future, a tutor who covers the core content but not the specific option topic for interim work, or a recommendation to wait until after the mock window when demand eases. We say which one we are offering. No competitor page found in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all, and several conceal non-local delivery behind a phone number; a family can reasonably treat silence on availability as a warning.

The practical advice that follows is to plan this subject earlier than any other. A Dubai family that identifies a Computer Science need in October of DP2 has a wide choice. The same family in February has whatever is left. Because the published rate bands do not rise in the exam term, waiting does not save money; it only reduces the set of people available.

One final verification point. Any individual tutoring privately in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is free for two years, applications run through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time, and MoHRE warns that tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask. It is a reasonable question and it takes ten seconds.

process.title: Ask the school three things first
process.description: Which programming language is taught, which option topic was chosen, and what the internal deadline for the computational solution is. Those three facts shape every sensible tutoring decision that follows, and no tutor can supply them for you.

process.title: Send a written answer, not just code
process.description: A marked written paper answer tells us more than a repository does, because written papers carry most of the marks. A solution draft is useful too, particularly the documentation sections rather than the program itself.

process.title: Run the five checks on the matched tutor
process.description: Language, documentation sections, option topic, case study mechanics, MoHRE permit. The trial session is free and is the right place to ask all five. A tutor who answers all of them precisely is worth booking.

process.title: Book early for a thin-cohort subject
process.description: Rates do not rise in the exam term, but availability collapses. A family looking in October of DP2 has a choice of specialists; the same family in February has whatever remains. This is the subject where planning ahead buys the most.

process.title: Review against written answers and documentation
process.description: Progress shows up in specific places: command terms answered properly, trace tables completed correctly, design decisions recorded as they are made. Those are what we check, rather than whether the program got longer.

whyPoints.title: Verification before price
whyPoints.description: Five questions with checkable answers, published so a Dubai parent can run them on any provider including this one. No other page found in this cluster gives a parent a way to test a Computer Science tutor's claims.

whyPoints.title: The marks are named honestly
whyPoints.description: Most of the grade is written prose about systems, and the internal component is assessed on documentation rather than working software. Saying so loses us the parent who wanted to hear that programming ability is enough.

whyPoints.title: Option topic treated as school-specific
whyPoints.description: A tutor who does not ask which option the school chose is guessing at examinable content. We ask first, because option content differs substantially and a student cannot revise what their school did not teach.

whyPoints.title: Screen sharing suits this subject
whyPoints.description: Debugging is observational, tracing wants a shared annotated document, and documentation feedback happens in a live file. Two-way screen sharing is better for this work than two people over one laptop, not a substitute for it.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on the solution
whyPoints.description: No code written, no lines supplied, no documentation drafted. The tutor explains what each section must demonstrate and asks questions. Supplying assessed work is malpractice under IB rules and the penalty falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed in advance
whyPoints.description: Higher Level case study support is the narrowest specialism here, and we say so with a fallback rather than taking the booking and hoping. No page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a Computer Science tutor really knows the IB course?
faqs.answer: Ask five things. Which programming language have you taught this course in, what must the computational solution documentation contain section by section, which option topic does my child's school teach, how does the Higher Level case study paper work, and do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit. A genuine Diploma Programme tutor answers all five quickly. A professional programmer with no course experience will answer the first well and the rest vaguely, usually by describing how they would build the program rather than what the documentation has to demonstrate.

faqs.question: Is IB Computer Science mostly a programming course?
faqs.answer: No, and assuming otherwise is the most expensive mistake families make in this subject. Most of the grade comes from written examination papers on system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and computational thinking, with Higher Level adding abstract data structures, resource management and control. The internally assessed computational solution is judged on documentation rather than on working software. A student who programs fluently and writes poorly about systems will underperform, which is why written answers matter more in tutoring than code review does.

faqs.question: What does the computational solution documentation have to contain?
faqs.answer: It records the planning, design, development, functionality and evaluation of a product built for an identified client, with success criteria agreed with that client. The marks reward decisions documented as they were made, including alternatives rejected and why. Students who develop for weeks and document afterwards are reconstructing a narrative, and it reads as one. Confirm the exact current requirements with the school's teacher, because the subject guide is revised periodically and older material online describes a previous version.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the computational solution without writing code?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the only legitimate form of help. A tutor can explain what each documented section must demonstrate, ask whether a success criterion is genuinely testable, question a data structure choice, read the student's own documentation and respond with questions and criteria references. A tutor cannot write code, supply corrected lines while debugging, or draft documentation text. Supplying any part of assessed work is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than on whoever provided it.

faqs.question: Does anyone come to our home in Dubai for Computer Science lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Computer Science support for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time with two-way screen sharing. For this subject the format is an advantage rather than a compromise: debugging is observational work best watched live on the student's own editor, and documentation feedback happens in a shared file rather than on a printed draft.

faqs.question: Why does my child's school teach a different option topic from their friend's?
faqs.answer: Because the school chooses it. Every candidate studies one option topic, the content is examinable, and the options differ substantially from each other. Two Dubai schools a few kilometres apart may teach different options, which matters when students compare revision notes or when a family moves school mid-programme. Ask the teacher directly which option is being taught, and treat any tutor who does not ask you the same question with caution, because they are guessing at examinable content.

faqs.question: How early should we start preparing the Higher Level case study?
faqs.answer: Months before the examination. The case study is released ahead of the session and rewards knowing what each named technology actually is, how it works and what its limitations are, which takes weeks of small research tasks. Students consistently stop researching at the point where they can recognise a term rather than explain it. Build a glossary of every technology and acronym, research each to the depth of a paragraph written from memory, then practise extended answers connecting those terms to syllabus content.

faqs.question: My child moved Dubai schools mid-Diploma. What does that break in Computer Science?
faqs.answer: Potentially three things at once: the programming language taught, the option topic chosen, and the timetable for the computational solution. The language and the solution surface quickly; the option topic usually goes unnoticed until revision, which is the worst time to discover it. Audit the gap early by listing what the previous school covered against what the new school's option requires. A term of fortnightly work normally closes it, and identifying it in DP1 costs far less than finding it in DP2.

faqs.question: Why is it hard to find a Computer Science tutor in Dubai specifically?
faqs.answer: Supply, not price. The International Baccalaureate accounted for roughly 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, Computer Science is a minority option inside the Diploma Programme, and Higher Level cohorts in a single school are often fewer than ten students. The pool of people in or near Dubai who have taught the Higher Level course is correspondingly small. Published rate bands do not rise in the exam term, so waiting does not save money; it only shrinks the set of specialists still available.

faqs.question: What do written Computer Science papers penalise most often?
faqs.answer: Command terms handled loosely. A question that says outline wants a brief account, explain wants reasons and evaluate wants a weighed judgement, and technically strong students often write everything they know, collecting the marks for one command term and none for the others. The second recurring loss is pseudocode written in the syntax of a real programming language, which forfeits convention marks. Trace tables are the third: pure technique, examined regularly, and improved quickly by practice rather than by more content.

faqs.question: Which mathematics course should a Computer Science student take in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the usual choice for students aiming at computer science degrees, because algebraic fluency and proof habits transfer to complexity reasoning and to the Higher Level abstract data structures content. Applications and Interpretation suits students heading towards data or information systems, with statistics and modelling supporting the data-handling side of a solution. Some overseas computer science degrees state a preference, so check the entry requirements of likely destinations in Year 11 rather than after the choice is locked.

faqs.question: Can my child find a real client in Dubai for the solution?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a real client makes the component far easier. A good client is someone who will answer questions and actually wants something: a librarian, a coach recording results on paper, a small business tracking bookings in a notebook. Dubai has no shortage of these. The student approaches them honestly, explains what the work is for, promises nothing, and derives the success criteria from the client's real need, which is what makes the evaluation section possible to write.

faqs.question: Does a Computer Science tutor in the UAE need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, applies to any individual providing private tuition in the UAE. It is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system, and warns that tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties.

faqs.question: Is online material about IB Computer Science reliable?
faqs.answer: Treat it carefully. Much of what circulates was written for a previous version of the subject guide or for a different option topic, and case study material refers to a session that has already passed. Some of the tutoring market sells exactly that, repackaged. Confirm the live specification and the chosen option with your school's Diploma Programme coordinator, and work only from material that matches both. A tutor who does not ask which option and which language your school uses cannot be working from the right material either.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level Computer Science specialist is free?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and name the alternative. The options are a start date in the future, a tutor who covers the core content but not the specific option topic for interim work, or a recommendation to wait until after the mock window when demand eases. Case study support in the exam term is the narrowest specialism we match. No competitor page found in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all, so silence about availability from any provider is worth treating as a warning rather than as reassurance.

dubai/ib-computer-science-tutor.closingHeading: Run the five checks, then book early
dubai/ib-computer-science-tutor.closingBody: Find out from the school which language and which option topic your child is studying, send a marked written answer rather than a code repository, and use the free trial session to run the five checks on whoever is matched. For a subject with single-figure Higher Level cohorts in Dubai, booking in October costs the same per hour as booking in February and gives you a far wider choice of specialist. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time with two-way screen sharing; home visits are not part of our UAE service. intro.heading: Four moving parts, assessed four different ways
paragraphs: The Career-related Programme is the least documented of the three IB programmes a Dubai sixth-former can be in, and the gap in public information is wider than the gap in difficulty. Search for help with it and what comes back is Diploma Programme marketing with the letters CP substituted into the headline. That is not a small editorial failure. A CP student is assessed in at least four structurally different ways at once, by at least two different organisations, and a tutor who treats the whole thing as a Diploma with fewer subjects will spend the year teaching the wrong component.

Here is the shape. A CP student takes at least two Diploma Programme courses, graded on the familiar one-to-seven scale by the IB. They take a career-related study, which is provided and certificated by an external body rather than by the IB, so its rules, deadlines and grading are not the IB's. And they take the CP core, which has four parts: a taught course in Personal and Professional Skills, Service Learning, the Reflective Project, and Language Development. The Reflective Project is graded on a letter scale rather than a number scale. Nothing about that arrangement is intuitive, and almost nothing about it is explained to parents.

The practical consequence is that CP candidates lose ground in places a Diploma candidate never visits. The Reflective Project is the clearest example. It asks a student to identify an ethical dilemma arising from their own career-related study and examine it in depth, which means the quality of the dilemma decides the quality of the project before a word of it is produced. A student who picks a topic rather than a dilemma has already capped the mark, and no amount of later polishing recovers it. Nobody can see that from outside, which is why it is worth saying out loud on a page like this.

Personal and Professional Skills is the second place. It is a taught course with its own assessment, it sits in the timetable like a subject, and students routinely treat it as an administrative obligation until the point at which it is not. Service Learning is the third: it requires sustained engagement and documented reflection, both of which are difficult to reconstruct in April if nothing was recorded in October. Language Development runs quietly across the whole programme as a portfolio, and portfolios built retrospectively look exactly like portfolios built retrospectively.

What a CP tutor in Dubai should therefore do is unglamorous. Establish which two or three DP courses the student is sitting and at what level, and teach those properly to the published assessment shape. Separate the career-related study's deadlines from the IB's, because they are set by different bodies and collide at predictable moments. Work the Reflective Project at the dilemma stage rather than the drafting stage. Audit the Service Learning and Language Development records early enough to fix them. And be honest that structural details in this programme change between guides, so every claim on this page should be confirmed against the current CP documentation with your school's coordinator.

One more thing belongs at the top. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai, and we do not run in-person lessons anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. Everything described below is delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For the CP specifically that format has an unusually strong case, because the cohort is small, the component knowledge is scarce, and a family's chance of finding a tutor who has actually supervised a Reflective Project within driving distance of their villa is poor.

dubai/ib-cp-tutor.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes run at secondary level and a Dubai student may meet two of them. The CP and the DP share courses but not structure, and the difference in structure is where the tutoring work actually sits.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma Programme courses, a career-related study delivered and certificated by an external provider, and a four-part core: Personal and Professional Skills, Service Learning, the Reflective Project and Language Development. The outcome is a CP certificate together with DP course results and the external provider's own qualification, rather than an IB Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in Dubai is thin relative to the Diploma. The emirate licenses seventeen curricula across 227 private schools, and the IB accounts for a smaller share of private-school enrolment than the British, Indian or American curricula. Ask a school directly which IB programmes it is authorised to offer rather than assuming that an IB World School offering the Diploma also runs the CP.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. Externally examined with internally marked components moderated by the IB. The courses a CP student takes are these courses, with the same published assessment structure and the same one-to-seven grading.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six openings in 2025-26 and a 6 per cent rise in enrolment. More Diploma capacity in the emirate does not automatically mean more CP capacity, because authorisation is programme by programme.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against published criteria marked out of eight and reported as levels from one to seven. Students arriving in the CP from the MYP already understand criterion marking, which is a real advantage for the Reflective Project; students arriving from IGCSE usually do not.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run the MYP and then offer only the Diploma at sixth form, so a student who would suit the CP sometimes has to change school at sixteen to find it. That transfer, and the question of whether it is worth making, is one of the more common CP conversations a Dubai family has.

dubai/ib-cp-tutor.subjectsIntro: A CP student carries Diploma Programme courses, usually at Standard Level and usually chosen to sit alongside the career-related field rather than against it. These are the ones that appear most often in Dubai CP timetables, with what each one is actually assessed on.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Written papers plus an internally assessed research component. Marks are lost on tool application rather than knowledge: a student who describes a framework without applying it to the stimulus organisation scores in the lower bands. Pairs naturally with business, hospitality and management career studies.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Assessed on command-term precision more than recall. The difference between describe, explain and evaluate decides whole mark bands, and students routinely answer a lower command term well. Study evaluation, not study description, is where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: Inquiry-led, with an internally assessed component built on real-world examples. Candidates who choose familiar examples rather than well-evidenced ones lose claim-support marks. Suits career studies in technology, media and digital operations.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and data-handling rather than proof. Technology is assumed in part of the assessment, and the common loss is unjustified rounding and context-free answers. This is the mathematics route most CP students take and the one most career fields actually use.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis across literary and non-literary material, with an oral component. Weak scripts summarise the text; strong scripts analyse how meaning is constructed. The analytical habit here transfers directly to the Reflective Project.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Physiology and research methods with an internally assessed investigation. Data handling and evaluation of method carry more marks than content recall. A frequent pairing with sports management and fitness career studies in this market.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy plus evaluation. Candidates who draw correctly and evaluate thinly plateau in the middle bands. Real-world application is explicitly rewarded, which suits a CP student who already has a career-related context to draw on.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Portfolio-based assessment with comparative and curatorial components. The recurring failure is documentation: strong work with thin process evidence scores below weaker work that is properly recorded. Pairs with design and creative-industry career studies.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Design cycle work with an internally assessed project, plus written papers. Candidates lose marks on justification rather than making: a decision that is not evidenced is treated as a decision that was not made. A natural fit with engineering and product career fields.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Interdisciplinary, with a strong emphasis on evaluating environmental value systems. Useful to CP students because its ethical-reasoning demands overlap with what the Reflective Project is marked on, which makes the two reinforce each other rather than compete.

sections.heading: What the Career-related Programme actually is, and who takes it in Dubai
paragraphs: The Career-related Programme is an IB qualification for students aged roughly sixteen to nineteen that combines three things: at least two Diploma Programme courses, a career-related study delivered by an external provider, and a four-part CP core. A student who completes it receives a CP certificate alongside their DP course results and whatever qualification the external provider awards. They do not receive an IB Diploma, and the distinction matters more in a university admissions office than it does in a school corridor.

That structure exists to solve a real problem. The full Diploma asks for six subjects with three at Higher Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. It is a heavy, broad, deliberately academic load. A sixteen-year-old with a clear vocational direction and strong practical ability can be badly served by it, and the alternative in most markets is to drop the IB framework altogether for A Levels or a BTEC. The CP lets a student keep IB courses and IB-style reflective assessment while carrying a genuine career-related qualification.

In Dubai the practical question is availability rather than suitability. The emirate licenses seventeen curricula across 227 private schools, and IB enrolment is a smaller share of the private-school total than the British, Indian or American curricula. IB authorisation is granted programme by programme, so a school running the Diploma is not thereby running the CP. Families regularly discover this late, after a year of assuming their school's IB status covered everything. The only reliable answer comes from asking the school which IB programmes it is specifically authorised for.

Who ends up in the CP, in this market, falls into three groups. There are students with a settled vocational direction who chose it deliberately. There are students who began the Diploma, found three Higher Levels unsustainable, and moved across rather than out. And there are students who arrived in Dubai mid-sixth-form from a system that did not map onto the Diploma and were placed into the CP as the nearest fit. Those three groups need different tutoring, and the first thing a tutor should establish is which one is in front of them.

sections.heading: The four parts of the CP core
paragraphs: The core is where the CP stops resembling a lighter Diploma. It has four components and they are assessed in four different ways by at least two different bodies. Personal and Professional Skills is a taught course with its own assessment. Service Learning requires sustained engagement with documented reflection. The Reflective Project is an extended piece of work examining an ethical dilemma, graded on a letter scale. Language Development runs across the whole programme as a portfolio of evidence.

Each of these fails in a characteristic way, and the failures are mostly administrative rather than intellectual. Personal and Professional Skills fails because students treat a timetabled course as an obligation rather than a subject. Service Learning fails because the engagement happens and the reflection does not get recorded, which is indistinguishable at the deadline from the engagement not happening. The Reflective Project fails at the choice of dilemma, months before anyone looks at a draft. Language Development fails because a portfolio assembled in one weekend reads exactly like a portfolio assembled in one weekend.

What that means for tutoring is that the highest-value intervention in the CP core is an audit, and the best time to buy it is early in the first year rather than late in the second. A session that establishes what is currently documented, what the school's internal deadlines are, which deadlines belong to the career-related provider instead, and what reflection routine the student can actually sustain through a term is worth more than five sessions of rescue work in April.

Treat the detail in the table as a map rather than as a specification. Component requirements, recommended hours and criterion structures are set in the IB's current CP documentation and they change between editions. Every CP school has a coordinator whose job includes exactly this, and the correct instruction to any family is to confirm the specifics with that person before planning around them. A tutor who states hour requirements as settled fact without that caveat is guessing.

sections.heading: The Diploma Programme courses inside a CP, and how they are graded
paragraphs: The courses a CP student takes are ordinary Diploma Programme courses. Same guides, same published assessment structure, same examinations, same one-to-seven grades. The only difference is how many of them there are and, usually, at what level: CP students commonly take two or three courses, frequently at Standard Level, chosen to sit alongside the career field rather than to assemble a broad academic spread. A tutor working on these courses is doing exactly what a Diploma tutor does, which is the one part of CP support that is not specialised.

What changes is prioritisation. A Diploma candidate with six subjects and three Higher Levels is managing breadth. A CP candidate with two Standard Level courses is carrying a smaller academic load but a larger administrative one, because the career-related study and the core are both live at the same time. The marks available in those two courses matter proportionally more to the overall record, and a single weak internally assessed component has nowhere to hide. That argues for front-loading the internal component rather than leaving it where most students leave it.

Course choice itself deserves a conversation. The strongest CP combinations are the ones where the DP course and the career field genuinely reinforce each other: Business Management with a business or hospitality study, Sports Exercise and Health Science with a sports study, Digital Society with a technology study, Design Technology with an engineering one. Environmental Systems and Societies is an underrated choice for a CP student because its demands on evaluating value systems overlap directly with what the Reflective Project is marked on, so the two components teach each other.

sections.heading: The Reflective Project: an ethical dilemma, and the criteria that mark it
paragraphs: The Reflective Project is the component that most distinguishes the CP, and it is the one most commonly handled badly. It asks the student to identify an ethical dilemma arising from an issue in their own career-related study and examine it in depth over an extended period, producing a substantial piece of work assessed against published criteria and reported on a letter scale rather than as a number out of seven.

Almost everything that decides the final letter happens in the first fortnight. An ethical dilemma is not a topic and it is not a problem; it is a situation in which two defensible positions conflict and something has to give. A student who writes about the environmental impact of the construction industry has a topic. A student who writes about whether a site manager should report a safety breach that will halt a project and cost colleagues their income has a dilemma. The second project can reach the top bands and the first cannot, however well it is written, because the criteria reward the examination of competing positions.

A supervisor's job at that stage is to test, not to supply. Useful tests are blunt. Can you state the two positions in one sentence each? Can you name a person who would hold each one, and what they would lose? Is there evidence available for both sides, or only for the one you already agree with? Would someone reasonable disagree with your conclusion? A student who cannot answer those questions does not have a dilemma yet, and the honest thing a tutor can do is say so in week two rather than in month four.

After that the work is the student's and must remain so. A tutor reads what the student has produced, maps it against each criterion, and names what is missing. A tutor does not supply sentences, restructure paragraphs into their own prose, or research the counter-position on the student's behalf. This is the same academic-honesty principle that governs assessed work throughout the IB, and the record of sessions should make it obvious which words are the student's and which are feedback. Criterion names, mark allocations and length requirements are set in the current CP documentation and should be confirmed with the school.

sections.heading: Personal and Professional Skills, and the Language Development portfolio
paragraphs: Personal and Professional Skills is a taught course and the single most underestimated part of the CP. It sits in the timetable like a subject, it has its own content and its own assessment, and it covers professional conduct, ethical reasoning, intercultural understanding, communication and applied skills. Students treat it as an administrative requirement because it does not look like Business Management, and then meet an assessment that expects them to use its vocabulary accurately. Schools commonly timetable a substantial number of hours for it; confirm the current requirement with your coordinator rather than assuming.

The tutoring work here is mostly translation. The course's concepts have precise meanings and students use them loosely, which is exactly the failure mode that costs marks in any criterion-assessed component. A session spent making a student define intercultural understanding in their own words and then apply it to a real situation from their own placement does more than a session spent reviewing notes. The overlap with the Reflective Project is substantial: the ethical reasoning taught here is the reasoning the project is marked on, and students who connect the two get two components for the price of one.

Language Development is quieter and easier to neglect. It asks for ongoing development in a language other than the student's best language, evidenced in a portfolio. In Dubai this is often genuinely useful rather than nominal, because a large share of students are already operating across Arabic, English and a home language, and because the emirate's schools teach Arabic as a mandatory subject in any case. The difficulty is evidence over time. A portfolio is a record of development, and a record assembled in a single weekend shows it.

The practical fix for both components is the same and it is dull: a short, repeatable routine set up early. Ten minutes of dated reflection a week, in whatever form the student will actually maintain, produces at the deadline something no amount of concentrated effort can reconstruct. A tutor can set that routine up, check it monthly, and name the gap while it is still a gap. This is unglamorous work and it is the highest-return hour a CP family buys.

sections.heading: Service Learning: the component left until it is too late
paragraphs: Service Learning asks for planned, sustained engagement with an identified community need, with reflection recorded through the process rather than summarised afterwards. It is not volunteering hours and it is not a charity drive, although both can form part of it. The emphasis is on identifying a need with the community rather than for it, acting over time, and showing what the student learned and how their thinking changed.

The failure is almost always documentation rather than activity. Dubai students are generally busy and generally engaged; schools here run substantial service programmes and many students are involved in more than the CP requires. What does not happen is the recording. A student who spent eight months supporting a literacy programme and wrote nothing down has, at the deadline, the same evidence as a student who did nothing, and no supervisor can honestly sign off what cannot be shown. This is the single most recoverable loss in the CP and the one most often left unrecovered.

The geography of Dubai matters here in a way it does not for tutoring. A placement or service partner has to be physically reachable on a school night, and the emirate's commercial clusters are not evenly distributed. Students in Business Bay, Dubai Silicon Oasis or Media City have options within a short radius. Students in Dubai Investments Park or Jebel Ali lose more of the evening to travel than anyone else, and their plans need to account for it rather than assume it away.

What a tutor contributes is structure and honesty. Structure means a reflection prompt the student will actually answer, a monthly check, and a format that matches what the school will accept. Honesty means saying when a plan is too thin to produce a defensible record, and saying it early. It also means staying out of the activity itself: the service is the student's, the reflection is the student's, and a supervisor who helps compose the reflection has removed the only thing being assessed.

sections.heading: CP, the full Diploma, A Levels and BTEC compared for a Dubai sixth form
paragraphs: Most Dubai families arrive at the CP question from the other direction: they are deciding between sixth-form routes and want to know what the CP gives up and what it buys. The honest comparison is structural rather than evaluative, because the right answer depends entirely on the student. A broad academic load suits some sixteen-year-olds and damages others, and a vocational route that is a sensible match for one university plan is a dead end for another.

The full Diploma offers breadth, three Higher Levels, and the widest recognition. It is also the heaviest load and the least forgiving if a student's strengths are uneven. A Levels offer depth in three or four subjects with no required core, which suits a student who already knows what they want and is comfortable dropping everything else. A BTEC or similar vocational qualification offers applied assessment, often coursework-weighted, with a direct line into related employment and into some degree routes but not all.

The CP sits between them in a specific way: IB courses and IB-style reflective assessment, plus a genuine vocational certification, plus a core that is explicitly about professional conduct and ethical reasoning. What it gives up is the IB Diploma itself and the breadth that comes with six subjects. What it adds, and this is the part most comparisons miss, is a documented record of reflective and ethical reasoning tied to real work, which some admissions processes and most employers read more readily than a grade profile.

The thing to check before choosing is the destination, not the programme. University recognition for the CP is not uniform across institutions or countries, and the UAE's own equivalency route treats curricula differently. Write down the three or four destinations the student is actually considering, then ask each one in writing what it does with a CP certificate plus DP course grades plus the external qualification. That takes a fortnight and settles the question better than any comparison table, including this one.

sections.heading: UAE equivalency and university admission for a CP graduate
paragraphs: A UAE secondary qualification normally has to be recognised through the Ministry of Education's equivalency process before it can be used for university admission or for certain employment purposes here. The rules are published by curriculum track, and they are specific. For the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

For the American track the published requirements include an English proficiency threshold, met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and a mathematics requirement of at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. These figures are sourced and quotable. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a requirement of six IGCSE subjects for UAE candidates, which does not match the published rule; being correct on a detail like that is worth more than any amount of reassurance.

For the IB, and specifically for the Career-related Programme, no equivalency figure is published that this page can stand behind. The sourced material on equivalency does not state an IB points threshold at all, and nothing available states how a CP certificate plus DP course grades plus an external vocational qualification is treated. Anyone telling you confidently what the CP converts to in the UAE should be asked for the moe.gov.ae page it comes from. The correct route is to check with the Ministry of Education or the emirate's attestation channel directly, and with each target university's own admissions office.

Two cautions follow from this. Equivalency is a regulatory process carried out by the authority, not something a tutoring service performs, guarantees or accelerates; our role is to describe it and point you at the official channel. And nobody should imply that tutoring is required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. It is not, and framing a regulatory process as something that needs purchasing is the kind of false urgency this market has too much of already.

sections.heading: A thin cohort, and what that means for finding a CP tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: The CP is a small programme. That is the plain reason this page exists and the plain reason it has to be honest about coverage. A family looking for someone who has actually supervised a Reflective Project, or who knows what Personal and Professional Skills assesses, is looking for a narrow specialism inside an already narrow programme. Searching for that person within a twenty-minute drive of a Dubai villa is a poor use of a short list, which is the practical argument for the format we use rather than a marketing one.

What we will say plainly is what we have and what we do not. DP course teaching at Standard Level in the subjects CP students commonly take is well covered, because those are ordinary Diploma courses. Reflective Project supervision, extended reflective writing and ethical reasoning are covered by tutors who do that work in the Diploma core as well. The career-related study itself is not ours to teach: it belongs to an external provider with its own syllabus, its own assessors and its own calendar, and a tutor who claims to cover it should be asked which provider and which qualification.

When a specialist is not free, we say so rather than matching whoever is available. That costs us enquiries and it is the right position; the alternative is a family paying specialist rates for general support, which is the most common quiet failure in this market. Where a component genuinely needs the school rather than a tutor, the honest answer is the school: a CP coordinator can confirm requirements, deadlines and acceptable evidence formats in one conversation, and no external party can do that for them.

Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the career-related study and the placement rather than against them. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai and holds no centre, office or branch anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. We state that here rather than after an enquiry, because two providers found in this market route UAE families to numbers outside the UAE without disclosing it, and disclosure is the cheapest trust signal available.
