sections.heading: Coverage, matching and what we will not promise
paragraphs: Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled around a Dubai school week in Gulf Standard Time, with a short written note afterwards. Matching for common subjects at common levels usually takes a few days. Scarce Higher Level components take one to two weeks, longer between February and May when every Diploma cohort in the emirate is looking for the same specialists in the same eight weeks.

Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match comes from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones, at a Dubai-friendly hour, with no change to the format or the subject depth. We tell you that before you commit rather than after, because a disclosed limit costs a family nothing and a concealed one costs them a fortnight at the worst possible moment of the year.

What we will not do: send anyone to a UAE address, because that is not a service we offer here; produce any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge piece, because everything submitted must be the student's own work and the risk falls on the candidate; or promise a result, because external outcomes depend on papers nobody has seen and boundaries set after marking.

What we will do is tell you when the problem is not a tutoring problem. A Diploma student whose work collapsed across all six subjects in one term is usually telling you about sleep, health or circumstances. A student with three Higher Levels that do not fit needs a timetable conversation with the school's coordinator while a change is still possible. Saying that costs us bookings and is the advice we would want for our own children.

process.title: Tell us the week before the subject
process.description: School, commute, activities, the slots that are genuinely free and which subject prompted the call. A plan built on the family's real evening survives; one built on the slot that looked convenient on a calendar gets cancelled by week three.

process.title: Free first lesson in the slot you actually want
process.description: One full lesson at no cost, scheduled at the real time rather than a demonstration hour, so you can see whether that slot works for your child. It also tests the connection and the set-up before any commitment.

process.title: Agree the schedule around the school calendar
process.description: Internal deadlines, mock windows, breaks and Ramadan. We ask for your school's assessment calendar and plan the hours into the fortnights where they change what is submitted, rather than spreading them evenly.

process.title: Set the Ramadan and travel rules in advance
process.description: Post-Iftar timing, shortened sessions over busy periods, and rescheduling rather than cancelling during trips. Agreeing this in week one is what keeps a schedule alive through a year that contains several disruptions.

process.title: Use the notes as your oversight
process.description: A short written note follows every session naming the target. For a household where nobody is in the room at 19:30, that note is the product you are checking, and it is the record the session-four review is built from.

process.title: Review and adjust at session four
process.description: We look at whether the slot is working as well as whether the teaching is. Sometimes the fix is a different time, a shorter session or a weekend block for the heavy work, rather than more hours or a different tutor.

whyPoints.title: Sessions start on time
whyPoints.description: No journey means no traffic risk, so a 20:00 slot begins at 20:00. Over a term that is a measurable amount of teaching that a visiting arrangement in Dubai evening traffic quietly loses.

whyPoints.title: Session length follows the student
whyPoints.description: Because nobody is driving, there is no minimum booking designed to justify a trip. A Diploma student who works well for seventy minutes books seventy minutes instead of paying for a two-hour block.

whyPoints.title: The specialist, not the nearest tutor
whyPoints.description: Diploma provision sits in a minority of Dubai schools, so geographic matching would hand you the nearest science teacher. Online matching gives you the person who has taught your child's exact Higher Level component.

whyPoints.title: A record you can actually check
whyPoints.description: Annotated material, a short written note, and a recording on request. For working parents this is the only realistic oversight, and it is also what makes progress visible before a school report catches up.

whyPoints.title: The schedule survives the year
whyPoints.description: Post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, daytime blocks during breaks, and rescheduling by time zone when a family travels. Each of those is routine online and difficult or impossible with a visiting arrangement.

whyPoints.title: We say what we do not do
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. No production of assessed work. No promised results. Stating the limits is what makes the rest of the offer worth anything.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our address in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Diploma lessons for Dubai families are delivered one-to-one over live video on a shared screen, scheduled around the school week in Gulf Standard Time. We are explicit about this because the search term is the phrase parents use and it would be easy to let the wording imply otherwise. The practical trade is that you give up physical presence and gain a tutor chosen for your child's exact Higher Level component rather than for living nearby.

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma session realistically start on a school night?
faqs.answer: For most Dubai Diploma students, between 16:30 and 20:30, with 18:30 to 20:30 the most reliable window for a DP2 candidate who needs the earlier evening to clear immediate deadlines. The 15:30 to 16:30 slot looks sensible on a calendar and is the one most often cancelled, because the student has just finished a commute, has not eaten properly and has not yet sorted what is urgent. After 20:30, keep the work to recall and light practice; anything needing sustained judgement produces poor work and a discouraged student.

faqs.question: How much of a visiting tutor's session is lost to Dubai traffic?
faqs.answer: The teaching time is not lost, but the reliability is. A tutor crossing the emirate at 17:00 faces a twenty to forty minute journey each way, and evening traffic here is variable rather than merely slow. A twenty-minute delay costs a third of a sixty-minute lesson, and over a term that attrition is real. The arithmetic also explains the rest of the in-home market: a sixty-minute lesson occupies two and a half hours of the tutor's evening, which is why minimum session lengths of ninety or a hundred and twenty minutes exist and why slot choice is narrow.

faqs.question: How do we handle Diploma sessions during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Move them rather than cancelling them, and shorten them rather than fighting the energy curve. School days are shorter during Ramadan and late-afternoon concentration drops noticeably, so most families switch to a post-Iftar slot. Continuity matters more than duration here: a focused forty minutes keeps the target and the habit alive, while a month of cancellations resets both and lands the student back at the start in the weeks before final papers. Because no tutor has to drive anywhere at an awkward hour, the change is a rescheduling question rather than a negotiation.

faqs.question: What do we need at home for an online Diploma lesson to work properly?
faqs.answer: Five things, all mundane. A quiet space, or at least one without a television and a sibling, because a student who will not speak cannot be diagnosed. A laptop or tablet rather than a phone, since annotating a past paper on a phone screen is unusable. A working microphone. The relevant marked script and assessment brief open before the start, which saves the ten minutes otherwise spent hunting for them. And an adult within earshot for younger students, with the session in a shared room rather than a bedroom. Test all of it in the free first lesson.

faqs.question: Can the tutoring schedule follow us when we travel out of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and agreeing how in advance is what stops a travel month costing a term's momentum. For short trips, move the session and shorten it if the itinerary is tight. For longer trips, switch the content to work that travels well: coursework scoping, reading and planning rather than timed paper practice needing a quiet desk. Gulf Standard Time sits between South Asia and Europe, so a family travelling a few hours either way usually keeps roughly the same slot. North American travel needs a different arrangement, set up before departure rather than discovered mid-trip.

faqs.question: How do I know what happened in a lesson if I was not in the room?
faqs.answer: By looking at what the session left behind. Ours leaves a short written note naming what was covered, what the student managed unaided, the target before the next session and anything you should act on, written to be read in half a minute. The annotated material is already a document, and a recording is available on request. Over a term those notes accumulate into the record the session-four review is built from. If notes stop arriving, raise it immediately rather than at the end of term, because they are the only oversight a working parent realistically has.

faqs.question: Should Diploma sessions continue through the winter and spring breaks?
faqs.answer: Change their purpose rather than their existence. A break is the only period in the Dubai year with uninterrupted daytime hours, which makes it the right time for the work a tired student cannot do on a school night: investigation design, Extended Essay scoping, Theory of Knowledge title choice, internal assessment planning. Trying to maintain a normal weekly practice timetable through a break usually fails, because the household rhythm has gone. Switch to a small number of longer daytime blocks aimed at coursework, then resume the weekly subject slot when term restarts.

faqs.question: Can two Diploma siblings be taught one after the other?
faqs.answer: Yes, and consecutive sessions are almost always better than a shared one. Where two students are at genuinely different levels, a shared session becomes two half-lessons and each child works above or below where they need to be. Back-to-back slots keep the attention undivided, allow a different specialist for each level, and still solve the household problem of disrupting one evening rather than two. We also keep the notes separate, so feedback on one child's Higher Level chemistry does not arrive blended with the other's Standard Level maths.

faqs.question: Is a weekend session better than a weekday one for a DP2 student?
faqs.answer: For different work, yes. Weekday evening slots suit practice, content teaching and timed paper work, which a reasonably tired student can still do well. Weekend sessions suit the work that needs decisions rather than energy: investigation design, Extended Essay scoping, internal assessment planning and prescribed-title choice for Theory of Knowledge. The efficient pattern for most Dubai Diploma families is one weekday evening slot plus an occasional longer weekend block, rather than two identical weekday sessions competing with six subjects' worth of homework.

faqs.question: What happens if my child misses a session at short notice?
faqs.answer: Ask any provider this before you book, because school events, fixtures, illness and travel are routine in a Dubai term rather than exceptional. A reasonable policy names a notice period you can actually meet and says what happens to a session the tutor cancels as well as one the family cancels. We would rather move a session than lose it, and where a week is genuinely impossible we would rather shorten the next one than pretend the target survived untouched. A vague policy is worse than a strict one, because it gets interpreted after the disagreement.

faqs.question: How long should a Diploma session be on a school night?
faqs.answer: Sixty to ninety minutes for most students. The limiting factor is not willingness but the amount of genuinely demanding work a sixteen-year-old can produce after a full school day, which for most is around seventy minutes before the session turns into revision of ground already covered. Two-hour weekday bookings generally exist because a tutor needed the journey to be worthwhile, which is not a constraint online. If more time is genuinely needed, a weekend block is a better use of it than extending a school-night session past the point of usefulness.

faqs.question: Does my child need a room to themselves for an online lesson?
faqs.answer: Not a room to themselves, but a space where they will speak freely and will not be interrupted every few minutes. Speaking is how a tutor diagnoses, so a student who will not talk in front of a sibling loses much of the session's value. For younger students the opposite consideration applies and a shared space with an adult in earshot is the right arrangement rather than a bedroom. In a crowded apartment the practical fix is usually a time rather than a place: a slot when the main living space is quiet.

faqs.question: How do we keep Extended Essay work moving over the long summer?
faqs.answer: Schedule three or four short sessions deliberately across the break, at whatever hour the family's location allows, and give them a specific job: a scoped research question, a source list the student can actually reach, and a method they can defend. This is the single most reliable point of failure in a Dubai Diploma, because no deadline is visible and families travel. Students who return to the second year with no usable draft spend the weeks they needed for revision writing an essay instead. The work remains entirely the student's; a tutor questions and gives criterion feedback.

faqs.question: Does it matter if the tutor is in a different time zone from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not for the lesson, and it often helps the schedule. Gulf Standard Time sits between South Asia and Europe, so a Dubai evening slot falls within normal working hours for a wide pool of IB subject teachers, which is precisely why a specialist for a scarce Higher Level component is findable at all. What matters is that the slot is fixed in your time zone rather than theirs, and that it holds through term. If no UAE-based specialist is free for your component, we say so when quoting and tell you where the match would come from.

dubai/ib-diploma-home-tutor.closingHeading: Plan the evening, then plan the teaching
dubai/ib-diploma-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB Diploma home tutor in Dubai, start with the week rather than the subject: when your child is actually home, fed and able to think, and what happens to that slot during Ramadan, a break or a travel month. Then choose the format that survives it. IB Gram delivers one-to-one Diploma lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, starting on time because nobody is driving, at a length matched to your child rather than to a journey, with a written note after each session. We do not offer home visits in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

dubai/ib-diploma-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma subjects over live video to Dubai students. Each profile names the subjects, levels and components taught, and because the match is not constrained by geography, the specialist for a narrow Higher Level component is usually reachable.

intro.heading: What a Dubai family is actually buying when the tutor is on a screen
paragraphs: An online Diploma session is not a video call about chemistry. It is a shared document with two people working on it, one of whom knows where the marks are. That distinction is the whole thing, and it explains both why the format works and why some online tutoring is worthless: a tutor who talks at a camera for an hour has delivered a lecture, while a tutor who puts a past-paper question on a shared screen and makes the student work on it has delivered a lesson. The medium does not determine which one you get; the tutor does.

What the medium does determine is what survives. Work done on a shared screen is already a file. An annotated question, a method built up on a whiteboard, a marked answer with the criteria beside it: all of it can be saved and looked at again on Thursday. A session at a kitchen table leaves a page of handwriting and a student's memory of it. For a Diploma student revising across six subjects over two years, that accumulation is worth a surprising amount.

The second thing the medium determines is who is available. Diploma provision in Dubai sits in a minority of the emirate's 227 private schools, so the pool of teachers who have taught a specific Higher Level component to examination here is small. Online matching lifts the geographic constraint, which matters little for Maths Analysis at Standard Level and matters entirely for Chemistry at Higher Level, Paper 3 investigation work, or a specific internal assessment criterion. Gulf Standard Time sits at UTC+4, between South Asia and Europe, so a Dubai evening slot falls inside working hours across a wide area.

The third thing is cost, which is the angle this page takes most seriously. Published in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is included, while online qualified subject tutors are advertised from AED 150 and exam-level specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above. The overlap is the useful part: a specialist online hour and a generalist visiting hour often cost the same, and one of them contains forty minutes of driving. Remove the journey and two things follow, a different price for the same teaching and a session length chosen by the student rather than by the road.

This page also states the limits, because a page that only sells the format is not worth reading. Laboratory practical work belongs to the school and always will. A student who genuinely will not engage with a screen is better served by a different intervention. And a household with unreliable connectivity will have a worse experience online than with a visiting tutor, which is one of the things the free first lesson exists to test. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

dubai/ib-diploma-online-tutor.programmesIntro: The online format suits the IB programmes differently, and it is worth knowing which parts of your child's programme it serves well before fixing a plan around it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The programme the format suits best. Six subjects with externally marked papers, internally assessed components and a core, all of which are document-based work that benefits from annotation, saved files and a specialist who may not live nearby. Sixty to ninety minutes is the usual session, with the shared screen carrying the past paper and the criteria side by side.
programmes.countryNote: A Dubai Diploma candidate's scarcest resource is a teacher who has taught their exact Higher Level component. Because provision is concentrated in relatively few schools here, geographic matching narrows that pool sharply, while an online match at a Dubai evening hour does not. That is the practical reason most of our Diploma work is delivered this way.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Works well with shorter sessions of forty-five to sixty minutes, particularly for criterion literacy: putting a task sheet and the criteria on screen together and working out which criterion is holding a grade down. Younger MYP students need a shared family space and an adult in earshot rather than a closed door.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP families often have two children at different stages, and consecutive online sessions solve that more cleanly than a shared session does. It also removes the need to find one visiting tutor who can teach two levels well, which is a much narrower search than it sounds.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The programme where the format needs most care. Thirty to forty-five minutes is the ceiling, an adult should be nearby, and the session should run in a shared room. Reading fluency and number work transfer well; anything requiring physical manipulation of materials transfers poorly and we say so.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai primary timetables end early enough for an afternoon slot, which suits short frequent sessions. Arabic as an additional language is the emirate's most requested primary subject, and short repeated practice works better for it than a long weekly block.

programmes.name: Extended Essay, TOK and internal assessment
programmes.description: The components where the saved-document advantage is clearest. Feedback is given as comments and questions against criteria on material the student has already written, and version history shows who made each change, which is a protection as well as a record. Nothing is drafted or supplied by the tutor at any stage.
programmes.countryNote: Internal deadlines differ by several weeks between Dubai IB World Schools, so blocks are planned from your own school's calendar. The long summer break between the Diploma years is when Extended Essay work stalls, and an online schedule can follow a travelling family through it.

dubai/ib-diploma-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below, each subject carries a note on what the online format specifically adds or cannot provide. The honest entries are the useful ones.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Gains most from the format. Working is built on a shared whiteboard, saved and revisited, and method communication, the commonest source of lost marks, is easier to coach when both people can see the same line of working at once.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics work involves calculator output and spreadsheets, all of which are screen-native. A tutor can watch regression work being produced rather than hearing about it afterwards, which is where interpretation marks are won.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Content, mechanisms and calculation work transfer fully. The scientific investigation can be designed, critiqued and written about online, but the practical work itself happens in the school laboratory, and no online provider should suggest otherwise.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Problem-solving and uncertainty treatment work well on a shared screen, where a graph with error bars can be annotated jointly. Apparatus handling and measurement technique remain the school's domain.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Extended-response practice and data analysis transfer completely, and marked answers sit beside the criteria on one screen. Microscopy and dissection skills do not transfer and are not claimed.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram work is better online than on paper, because a diagram can be built step by step, corrected and saved. Higher Level quantitative papers and the internal assessment commentaries both work entirely within the format.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis suits a shared screen, with the text annotated jointly in real time. The individual oral can be rehearsed on camera, which is closer to the assessed conditions than a rehearsal across a kitchen table.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source analysis is screen-native and essay planning benefits from a saved outline the student can return to. Archive-based investigation work depends on what the student can access, which is a library question rather than a format one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study work transfers fully, with the stimulus and the answer visible together so the application marks can be pointed at precisely. Group presentation practice is the one element that works better in a classroom.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Spoken practice is effective one-to-one over video, which gives a student more speaking time than a class of twenty does. Script writing works with a tablet and stylus or a document camera; agree which before the first session.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Entirely suited to the format, since the work is argument rather than material. Prescribed-title choice and knowledge-question framing happen in conversation with a shared document, and the student keeps the notes.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The subject with the strongest case for online delivery: code, documentation and theory all live on a screen already. It is also the thinnest specialist market in Dubai, which is why UAE-based coverage most often runs out here.

sections.heading: An online IB Diploma session in Dubai, minute by minute
paragraphs: A session that works has a predictable shape, and knowing it lets you judge whether you are getting one. The first five minutes are the previous target: what was set last week, what the student did with it, and whether it held. Not a general enquiry about how the week went, but a specific check on a specific thing, usually by asking the student to do it again.

The next forty to sixty minutes are the student working. A question appears on the shared screen and the student attempts it while the tutor watches the working appear. This is the part that distinguishes a lesson from a lecture, and it is also where the online format has a quiet advantage: the tutor can see the working being produced line by line, which is harder across a table where a student instinctively covers what they are writing. Interventions are short and specific, and a good tutor says less than a parent expects.

The last ten minutes are the record. The tutor marks or part-marks what was produced, states where the marks were and were not available, saves the annotated file, and sets the next target. Then a short note goes to the parent: what was covered, what the student managed unaided, the target, and anything to act on. That note is the product a parent can actually inspect, and it should be readable in half a minute.

What should not be happening: a tutor explaining for forty minutes, a student watching a screen share passively, or a session that ends without anything written down. If any of those is the pattern after three sessions, the format is not the problem and the match should change. We review at session four partly to catch exactly that, and changing tutor at that point costs nothing.

sections.heading: Science and the laboratory: the limit we will not talk around
paragraphs: Every Diploma science subject includes a substantial internally assessed investigation, and a large part of that work is practical. An online tutor cannot run a laboratory, cannot supervise apparatus, and cannot substitute for the hours a student spends measuring something that behaves unexpectedly. Any provider implying otherwise is selling something they do not have, and the student is the one who discovers it.

What an online tutor genuinely can do with the investigation is considerable, and it sits either side of the practical work. Before: critique the research question for scope and controllability, ask what is uncontrolled, test whether the data can actually be gathered with school apparatus in the time available, and talk through the method until the student can defend each step. Those conversations are where most investigation marks are won or lost, and they are entirely document-based.

After: work on uncertainty treatment, graph construction with error bars, the distinction between a limitation and an improvement, and the evaluation writing that most students underprepare. All of that is screen-native and benefits from the shared annotation, since a graph can be marked up jointly in a way a photographed page cannot.

The same honesty applies elsewhere. Group presentation practice works better in a classroom. Microscopy and dissection skills do not transfer. A student who needs an adult physically present to start working at all may need something other than an online tutor, and a household with genuinely unreliable connectivity will have a worse experience in this format than with a visiting arrangement. We would rather name those cases than argue with them.

sections.heading: Oral components over video, which is closer than it sounds
paragraphs: Several Diploma components are spoken: the individual oral in language and literature subjects, the oral assessments in language acquisition, and the Theory of Knowledge exhibition commentary where schools ask for a presented version. Parents reasonably assume these need a person in the room. In practice video rehearsal is closer to the assessed conditions than a kitchen-table rehearsal is, because the student is speaking to a device, to time, with notes they are not allowed to read from.

The work itself is structural rather than conversational. An individual oral fails for predictable reasons: a global issue chosen too broadly, extracts that do not actually support the argument, time mismanaged so the second text gets three minutes, and a reliance on notes that the conditions do not allow. Each of those is diagnosable from one rehearsal and fixable in two or three. None of it requires physical presence.

For language acquisition, the gain is speaking time. A student in a class of twenty speaks for a small fraction of a lesson; a student in a one-to-one video session speaks for most of it. That is the single biggest determinant of oral fluency improvement, and it is a quantity argument rather than a pedagogical one. Recording a rehearsal and watching it back is also unusually effective here, and students who resist it the first time generally ask for it the second.

The limits: a tutor cannot conduct the actual assessment, cannot see the stimulus material the school will use, and should not be rehearsing a script. The school runs the assessment under its own conditions. What a tutor rehearses is a shape that survives an unseen extract, which is exactly what the criteria reward.

sections.heading: What disappears from the price when the journey disappears
paragraphs: Here is the cost argument, stated as plainly as the numbers allow. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Published online rates for qualified subject tutors run roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and exam-level specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Those are other providers' figures, named, read in October 2026, and not IB Gram's prices.

Three cost components come out of the hour when nobody drives. The first is the travel time itself, twenty to forty minutes each way across the emirate at the hours families want. The second is the minimum session length, usually ninety or a hundred and twenty minutes, which exists to make a journey worthwhile and which obliges a family to buy time their child cannot use. The third is less visible: the geographic filter on who can teach, which pushes a family towards the nearest available tutor rather than the right one, and a mismatched tutor is the most expensive purchase in this market because the hours achieve nothing.

What does not change is the teaching itself. The subject guide is the same, the criteria are the same, the marked script is the same script. Anyone claiming online teaching is inherently superior is overselling, exactly as anyone claiming it is inherently inferior is. The honest claim is narrower: for document-based assessed work, which is most of the Diploma, the format is equivalent, and it removes three costs that have nothing to do with teaching.

There is one cost the format adds, and it is small but real. A household needs a usable device, a workable space and a stable connection. Most Dubai homes have all three. Where one is missing, the free first lesson will show it, which is part of why that lesson exists rather than a fifteen-minute introductory call.

sections.heading: Buying by session length instead of by package
paragraphs: Once travel is out of the equation, session length becomes a genuine choice rather than a constraint, and that is where a Dubai family can take real money out of a tutoring budget without taking anything out of the teaching. Most Diploma students sustain roughly seventy minutes of genuinely demanding work after a school day. Past that, a session becomes revision of what has already been covered, which is useful at a quarter of the intensity and not worth a specialist rate.

So the efficient purchase for a weekday evening is sixty to ninety minutes, and for a primary or lower-MYP student thirty to forty-five. A two-hour weekday booking is almost always a legacy of a travel constraint rather than a teaching judgement. Where more time is genuinely needed, a weekend block with a fresher student does more than extending a school-night session past the useful point.

Packages deserve the same scrutiny. Advertised monthly figures in this market include about AED 799 for eight online sessions, which implies roughly AED 100 a session and tells you which band of tutor is teaching, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which implies roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Convert any package to a cost per hour before comparing it with anything.

Our approach is to quote per match after a free trial rather than publish a rate card, and to pay per session until the match has proven itself. The risk in a prepaid package is not the price, it is the expiry and the notice period: unused hours lapsing at month end during a travel week turns a discount into a loss. Ask four questions of any package before buying one, and reasonable answers to all four make it a genuine saving.

sections.heading: A Dubai evening slot and the tutor pool it reaches
paragraphs: Gulf Standard Time sits at UTC+4, which is an unusually convenient position for this purpose. A Dubai session at 18:00 falls in the late afternoon for a tutor in Europe, mid-evening for one in South Asia, and the middle of the working day for one further east. That means an evening slot that suits a Diploma student after school also suits a wide pool of IB subject teachers at a reasonable hour of their own day, which is the structural reason a narrow Higher Level component is findable at all.

That matters because of how concentrated Diploma provision is locally. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools with 17 curricula in 2024-25, and the UK curriculum is by far the largest share by enrolment while the International Baccalaureate is a much smaller one. The emirate is adding three new International Baccalaureate schools among seven new private schools for 2026-27, creating 16,846 new places, so the pool is growing. It is still the case that a specific Higher Level component may have very few resident teachers who have taught it to examination.

The practical upshot for a family: ask where the tutor is based, because it affects the slot's stability rather than the teaching. A tutor whose own evening is your evening will hold a slot through term more reliably than one for whom your slot is the middle of their night. We set slots in your time zone and tell you where the tutor is, so that a schedule is agreed on real information.

The format also makes the slot portable, which matters in a city where families travel. A session can be repositioned to the time zone a family is actually in, which is a rescheduling question rather than a cancellation. That is particularly useful across the long summer break between the Diploma years, where Extended Essay progress stalls with great reliability.

sections.heading: Safeguarding, recordings and data when the student is a minor
paragraphs: Online lessons with a child involve personal data and a live video connection, and both deserve clear rules rather than a privacy page nobody reads. The UAE has a federal data protection framework in Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection, and the sensible posture for any tutoring provider is to collect the minimum needed, say what it is for, and delete it on request.

What we need is narrow: a name, a contact for the parent, the school, the subjects and levels, and whatever work the family chooses to share. What we do not need and do not ask for is a photograph of the child, a full academic history or any medical information, unless a parent volunteers something relevant to how a session should run. If a form ever asks your child's school, grades and photograph without saying why, that is a reasonable moment to stop filling it in, wherever you are buying from.

On recordings, the rule is that they happen on request rather than by default, they are shared with the family that asked for them, and they are deleted on request. Students use them more than parents do, usually to rewatch one difficult explanation. A recording is not a substitute for being told what happened, which is what the written note is for.

On safeguarding, four practical things. Sessions run on the platform link rather than a tutor's personal channel. A new match begins with the tutor confirming their name, subject and level on camera with the parent present. Younger students work in a shared family space with an adult in earshot rather than behind a closed door. And a parent is welcome to sit in on any session, at any time, without arranging it in advance; a provider who discourages that is telling you something.

sections.heading: Coverage, honest limits and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Matching for common Diploma subjects at common levels usually takes a few days. Scarce Higher Level components take one to two weeks, and longer between February and May, when Diploma cohorts across the emirate converge on the same specialists in the same eight weeks. Computer Science at Higher Level is the request most likely to exhaust UAE-based coverage at any time of year.

Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match comes from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones, at a Dubai-friendly hour, with no change to format or subject depth. We tell you at the quoting stage rather than later. Where we cannot cover a request at all, we say so instead of substituting a generalist and leaving you to find out in week three.

What we will not claim. That online teaching is inherently better than a tutor in the room; it is equivalent for document-based assessed work and worse for some things, and we have named which. That we can run laboratory practical work; we cannot, and that stays with the school. That we can produce any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge piece; everything submitted must be the student's own work and the risk of crossing that line falls on the candidate. And that we can promise a result, which nobody can.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We quote per match after a free trial lesson with no card details taken, tell you which band the request sits in and why, and recommend paying per session until the match has proven itself at the session-four review.

faqs.question: What actually happens during an online IB Diploma lesson?
faqs.answer: A good session has a shape. Five minutes checking the previous target by asking the student to redo it unaided. Then forty to sixty minutes of the student working on a question on the shared screen while the tutor watches the working appear and intervenes briefly at the point of error. Then ten minutes marking what was produced, saving the annotated file and setting the next target, followed by a four-line note to the parent. What should not be happening is a tutor explaining for forty minutes to a passive student. If that is the pattern after three sessions, change the match rather than the format.

faqs.question: Is an online tutor as effective as one sitting beside my child?
faqs.answer: For document-based assessed work, which is most of the Diploma, the two are equivalent, and the online format has one specific advantage: the tutor sees the working appear line by line on a shared screen, where across a table a student instinctively covers what they are writing. Where online is genuinely worse is laboratory practical work, group presentation practice, and any student who will not start working at all without an adult physically present. We name those cases rather than arguing with them, and the free first lesson exists partly to test which situation you are in.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with the Diploma scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: With most of it, but not the laboratory part, and no honest provider should suggest otherwise. What transfers fully is the work either side of the practical: critiquing the research question for scope and controllability, checking whether data can realistically be gathered with school apparatus, talking through the method until the student can defend each step, then uncertainty treatment, graphing with error bars, limitations and evaluation writing. Those are where investigation marks actually move. The practical execution happens in your school's laboratory under the subject teacher, who also authenticates the work.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor prepare my child for the individual oral?
faqs.answer: Yes, and video rehearsal is closer to the assessed conditions than a rehearsal across a kitchen table, because the student is speaking to a device, to time, without reading from notes. Individual orals fail for predictable reasons: a global issue chosen too broadly, extracts that do not support the argument, time mismanaged so the second text gets three minutes. Each is diagnosable from one rehearsal. What a tutor cannot do is conduct the assessment, see the school's stimulus material, or rehearse a script, since the criteria reward a shape that survives an unseen extract.

faqs.question: What does my child keep after an online session?
faqs.answer: Four things. The annotated material worked on, since anything done on a shared screen is already a file. The marked answer with the criteria beside it, showing where marks were and were not available. A named target for the week, which gives the days between sessions a job. And a recording of a difficult explanation if the student asked for one. For a Diploma student revising across six subjects over two years, that accumulation becomes genuine revision material, which a page of handwriting from a session at the table does not.

faqs.question: Is online Diploma tutoring cheaper than a tutor who travels in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures say yes at the qualified level and overlapping at the specialist level. In-home one-to-one is advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is included; online qualified subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200; and online exam-level specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. The interesting part is the overlap: a specialist online hour and a generalist visiting hour often cost the same, and one of them contains forty minutes of driving. Those are other providers' published rates, read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Can we book a 45-minute online session rather than a full hour?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for younger students it is usually the right length. Minimum bookings of ninety or a hundred and twenty minutes exist because a visiting tutor needs the journey to be worthwhile, which is not a constraint here. Most Diploma students sustain about seventy minutes of genuinely demanding work after a school day, so sixty to ninety is the usual range for them, while a primary or lower-MYP student is better served by thirty to forty-five. Matching length to what a child can actually use is the simplest way to reduce a tutoring budget without reducing the teaching.

faqs.question: Where are your tutors based, and does the location matter?
faqs.answer: It matters for the stability of your slot rather than for the teaching. Gulf Standard Time sits at UTC+4, so a Dubai session at 18:00 is late afternoon in Europe, mid-evening in South Asia and inside the working day further east, which is why a wide pool of IB subject teachers can hold a Dubai evening slot at a reasonable hour of their own day. A tutor for whom your slot falls in the middle of their night will hold it less reliably through term. We set slots in your time zone and tell you where the tutor is, so the schedule is agreed on real information.

faqs.question: What personal data do you collect about my child?
faqs.answer: The minimum needed to match and teach: a name, a contact for the parent, the school, the subjects and levels, and whatever work the family chooses to share. We do not ask for a photograph of the child, a full academic history or medical information unless a parent volunteers something relevant to how sessions should run. The UAE has a federal data protection framework in Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, and the sensible posture is to collect little, say what it is for and delete on request. If any provider's form asks for a child's photograph and grades without explaining why, that is worth questioning.

faqs.question: Are lessons recorded, and who can see a recording?
faqs.answer: Recordings are made on request rather than by default, shared with the family that asked, and deleted on request at any time. In practice students use them more than parents do, usually to rewatch a single difficult explanation rather than a whole hour. A recording is not a substitute for being told what happened in the session, which is what the short written note is for: what was covered, what the student managed unaided, the target and anything to act on. You are also welcome to sit in on any session without arranging it beforehand.

faqs.question: What kind of internet connection does an online Diploma lesson need?
faqs.answer: Less than most families expect, but it has to be stable rather than fast. A shared screen with annotation and a video window runs comfortably on an ordinary household broadband connection; the thing that breaks a session is intermittency rather than bandwidth. The practical requirements are a laptop or tablet rather than a phone, since annotating a past paper on a phone screen is unusable, and a working microphone, since speaking is how a tutor diagnoses. Test all of it during the free first lesson, which is part of why that lesson is a full one rather than a short call.

faqs.question: Can the tutor see my child's working as they write it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the format's real advantages. On a shared document or whiteboard, the working appears line by line to the tutor as the student produces it, which means a missing method line can be caught at the moment it is omitted rather than after the mark is lost. Across a table, students instinctively shield what they are writing until it is finished. For mathematics and the quantitative sciences, where most recoverable marks sit in unwritten method rather than wrong answers, that visibility is worth more than it sounds.

faqs.question: How do we handle a textbook or calculator during an online session?
faqs.answer: Agree it before the first lesson rather than losing ten minutes to it. A graphical calculator's screen can be shared directly or shown to the camera, and spreadsheet output can be screen-shared, which is usually better than a photograph. For a textbook or a school worksheet, a photograph sent before the session works, or the student can hold it to the camera for a quick reference. The one habit worth building is having the marked script, the assessment brief and anything the tutor asked for open before the session starts, which protects the first ten minutes.

faqs.question: What if my child will not engage with a screen at all?
faqs.answer: Then say so early and we will tell you honestly whether we think this is the right service. Some students need an adult physically present to start working, and no amount of good teaching over video substitutes for that. More often, though, the resistance is about the shape of the session rather than the medium: a student who was lectured at for three sessions will disengage from any format. Our first check is whether the student is being asked to work within the first five minutes. If they are and the resistance persists, a different intervention is the honest recommendation.

faqs.question: How soon can an online Diploma tutor start in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Common subjects at common levels are usually matched within a few days, with the free first lesson scheduled in the slot you actually want. Scarce Higher Level components take one to two weeks, and longer between February and May when Diploma cohorts across the emirate converge on the same specialists. Computer Science at Higher Level is the request most likely to exhaust UAE-based coverage at any point in the year. Where nobody local is free, we say so when quoting and match from our wider pool at a Dubai-friendly hour, with the format and subject depth unchanged.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a timetable problem before it is a subject problem
paragraphs: Most families arrive at Diploma tutoring thinking they have a chemistry problem or a maths problem. Often they have a loading problem. A Diploma candidate carries six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, plus an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge course with two assessed pieces, a CAS programme, and in Dubai the mandatory subjects every private school must teach whatever curriculum it is licensed for. The grade that slipped is frequently the symptom of a week that does not fit, and the useful tutor is the one who notices that before selling thirty hours of chemistry.

That makes a Diploma tutor's first job diagnostic in a broader sense than usual. Which of the six subjects is actually at risk, as opposed to merely uncomfortable? Is the Extended Essay running quietly behind and about to consume a term? Are three Higher Levels producing more written work per week than this particular student can produce at all? Those questions have different answers for different students, and the answers determine whether tutoring, a timetable conversation with the school, or simply a better plan for the holidays is the right next move.

Dubai adds its own structure to this. The emirate's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with UK curricula at well over a third of enrolment and the International Baccalaureate a much smaller share. Diploma provision therefore sits in a minority of schools, specialist teachers are correspondingly thinner on the ground, and a DP candidate's peer group for comparison is small. For 2026-27 the emirate adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, so that balance is shifting rather than fixed.

The other Dubai-specific feature is the mandatory subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Diploma candidate that is additional timetabled time that does not appear in any IB document, and it is one of the reasons a Dubai DP week feels fuller than the programme structure suggests.

IB Gram matches Diploma students to subject specialists for one-to-one lessons delivered over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time around a Dubai school week. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The practical gain for a Diploma family is that the tutor is chosen for the group, level and component the evidence points at, rather than for living within driving distance of your community, and every session leaves a written note you can read in half a minute.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects chosen across six groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, assessed through externally marked papers plus internally assessed components the school marks and the IB moderates. The core adds the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Award conditions, including how the core contributes, are set by the IB and confirmed by your school's coordinator.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma competes with a well-established A Level route, so many candidates arrive having considered both and some switch after DP1 term one. A tutor working here should know what the student would have been doing on the other route, because the comparison shapes how the family reads every result for the next two years.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each out of eight, judged against descriptors rather than percentages. Students arriving in the Diploma from MYP have met criterion marking and inquiry-led work, which helps with internal assessment and leaves them underprepared for the volume of timed written papers.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running MYP often offer a choice at 16 between the Diploma and a British sixth form, so the final MYP year points at two destinations. Where a student is heading for the Diploma, the most useful preparation is timed extended writing, which MYP assessment does not demand in the same quantity.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry units ending in the Year 6 Exhibition, with no external assessment. Relevant to Diploma families mainly as context: a student who came through PYP and MYP in the same school has a decade of criterion-based feedback behind them and reads a rubric fluently.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's primary cohorts turn over quickly with arrivals from British, Indian and American systems, so a single Year 6 class may contain children with four different assessment vocabularies. That is also why Arabic as an additional language is the most requested primary subject in the emirate.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two DP courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and language development. The DP courses inside it are examined exactly as they are for Diploma candidates, so tutoring requests for CP students are usually about those specific subject papers.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of UAE schools offer the Career-related Programme, so UAE-based tutor coverage is thin and most matches come from our wider pool. The online format and the subject depth are unchanged; the tutor's location is what differs.

subjects.description: Group 1. Language and Literature or Literature, assessed through unseen textual analysis, a comparative paper, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an additional essay on a studied work. The scarce skill is analysis rather than content knowledge, which catches out students arriving from content-heavy systems.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition: Arabic B and ab initio
subjects.description: Group 2. Arabic is the most commonly taken acquisition language in Dubai, partly because the emirate requires Arabic teaching in all private schools. Streams differ sharply, so a tutor must know whether your child sits ab initio, B at Standard or B at Higher before planning anything.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies: Economics
subjects.description: Group 3. Diagram accuracy and real-world application decide the grade, with Higher Level adding a quantitative paper that exposes students who revised theory only. The internal assessment commentaries are marked against published criteria and are where early feedback pays most.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies: History
subjects.description: Group 3. Source analysis plus essay writing on prescribed topics, with a historical investigation as internal assessment. Match a tutor to the specific prescribed subject your school teaches, because strength in one region of study does not transfer to another.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies: Business Management
subjects.description: Group 3. Case-study application separates the grades: a correctly drawn framework that never refers to the stimulus forfeits the application and evaluation marks. Popular in Dubai, with reasonable supply at Standard Level and thinner coverage at Higher.

subjects.name: Sciences: Chemistry
subjects.description: Group 4. Structure and reactivity content with a single scientific investigation as internal assessment. The tightest Higher Level market in Dubai between February and May, which makes it the subject where booking early changes what is available to you.

subjects.name: Sciences: Physics
subjects.description: Group 4. Method and reasoning marks reward stated steps, so answers given without working score below their potential. Uncertainty treatment in the investigation is the component Dubai students most often underprepare for.

subjects.name: Sciences: Biology
subjects.description: Group 4. Extended responses are marked against lists of creditable points, so making five accurate plain statements beats writing elegantly about one. Command-term discipline is the dominant diagnosable error across Dubai cohorts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Group 5. The route most often expected for mathematics-heavy degrees, with Higher Level adding a third paper that rewards structured investigation of an unfamiliar problem. Check your target universities' stated requirements rather than assuming.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Group 5. Statistics, modelling and technology use, with marks available for interpretation in context as well as calculation. Growing in Dubai faster than the number of teachers who have genuinely taught both maths courses.

subjects.name: The Arts and group substitutions
subjects.description: Group 6, which a candidate may replace with a second subject from groups 1 to 5. Dubai students aiming at science or engineering frequently take that substitution, which produces the two-science or two-maths patterns that make a week heavy.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Assessed against published criteria with stated limits, including 4,000 words for the Extended Essay. The school supervises both. A tutor may question, critique method and give criterion-based feedback on what the student has already written, and nothing beyond that.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools where the Diploma sits alongside other routes
schoolClusters.note: Students at these schools often choose between the Diploma and a British sixth form, and a minority switch after the first Diploma term. That decision, rather than any single subject, is the most consequential thing a tutor can help a family think through clearly.

sections.heading: What the IB Diploma asks a Dubai student to carry
paragraphs: The Diploma's shape is six subjects taken across six groups, with one subject from each group and a permitted substitution of a sixth-group subject for a second from groups one to five. Normally three are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Alongside those sit three core elements: the Extended Essay, an independent research piece with a 4,000-word upper limit; Theory of Knowledge, which produces an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title; and CAS, a programme of creativity, activity and service that is not graded but is a requirement for the award.

Assessment is split. Most of each subject grade comes from externally marked papers sat at the end of the course. A further portion, commonly around a fifth, comes from an internally assessed component which the school marks against published criteria and the IB then moderates. Award conditions, including how the core contributes and what constitutes a pass, are set by the IB; your school's coordinator is the right person to confirm the current rules for your child's cohort rather than any tutoring page.

The honest description of why this is hard is not that any one subject is harder than its A Level equivalent. It is that six subjects, two of which the student may not have chosen enthusiastically, run simultaneously with three pieces of independent extended work, over two years, with the heaviest coursework deadlines landing in the same months. Students who struggle in the Diploma are usually competent in every individual element and overwhelmed by the aggregate.

That is why the first useful conversation is about load rather than content. Count the written work due per week across six subjects. Find out where the Extended Essay actually stands rather than where it is supposed to stand. Ask whether the Higher Level combination produces three sets of long written assignments in the same fortnight. A tutor who starts there will often recommend fewer paid hours than one who starts with the chemistry grade.

sections.heading: The core, and what a tutor may legitimately do with it
paragraphs: The core is where Diploma plans most often come apart, and it is also where the boundary around tutoring is tightest. All three elements belong to the student and the school. The Extended Essay has a school supervisor who holds formal responsibility and runs the reflective sessions. Theory of Knowledge is taught as a course with an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. CAS is a programme of experiences with its own reflective requirements, overseen by a coordinator.

What a tutor may do is teach skills, ask questions about material the student has already produced, and give feedback against the published criteria. What a tutor may not do is supply content, restructure a draft or provide text. Everything submitted must be the student's own, and the consequences of that boundary being crossed fall on the candidate. In this market at least one site openly sells completed internal assessments; buying one puts an entire Diploma at risk for a handful of marks.

Given that boundary, the highest-value intervention is early and cheap. A few hours spent testing whether an Extended Essay research question can actually be answered within 4,000 words, with sources the student can reach, prevents the crisis that otherwise arrives in the final year. The same is true of Theory of Knowledge: the prescribed title chosen effectively sets the ceiling, and a poor choice cannot be recovered by polishing later.

The practical failure pattern in Dubai is seasonal. Extended Essay progress stalls over the long summer break between the two Diploma years, when families travel and nobody is chasing a deadline. Students who return in the second year with no usable draft lose the weeks they needed for subject revision. Putting a small amount of structured support into the term before that break is worth more than a large amount of support after it.

sections.heading: Two years, counted from the end rather than the beginning
paragraphs: Diploma plans fail when they are built forwards from September rather than backwards from the final papers. Counted backwards, the structure is clear: final papers are preceded by a mock window, which is preceded by the last internal assessment deadlines, which are preceded by the Extended Essay submission, which is preceded by the long summer break where everything stalls. Each of those is a hard date set by a school or a board, and each one has work that must be finished before it.

Specific dates differ by school and by board, and some of them cannot be published responsibly. Cambridge and Pearson publish their series and key dates openly: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and the Checkpoint tests that sit outside those windows are Primary and Lower Secondary assessments rather than IGCSE papers, so they are no guide to when a Year 11 candidate sits anything. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November, and the November 2026 timetable is the cleanest published illustration of the shape: papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students the following January, as the November 2025 results did on 22 January 2026. Entries for either board close well before the papers, and the school registrar rather than the student is the person who files them. IB session dates, by contrast, are not confirmable from automated sources, so this page does not publish one: confirm every IB date with your school's coordinator or on ibo.org.

The useful discipline is to take your own school's assessment calendar, mark the internal deadlines and mock windows, and then count backwards from each. A plan built that way reveals the two or three fortnights in the whole programme where support actually changes what is submitted. Hours spent in those fortnights are worth several times the same hours spent in a quiet month.

Dubai adds two calendar features worth planning around. The school year runs from late August or early September to late June or early July, with winter and spring breaks. And Ramadan moves earlier each year, shortening school days and reshaping evening availability, which is why many families shift sessions to a post-Iftar slot. A revision plan built on a normal evening pattern can quietly lose its best fortnight.

sections.heading: The IGCSE jump, subject by subject
paragraphs: A large share of Dubai's Diploma candidates arrive from an IGCSE background, either by transferring at 16 or by choosing the Diploma inside a school that offers both. The gap is real and it is specific rather than general. Students arrive with strong content recall and weak extended-response structure, because IGCSE rewards accurate short answers and the Diploma rewards sustained argument. They also arrive unused to independent extended work, because nothing in IGCSE resembles a 4,000-word essay with a supervisor.

Subject by subject the gap differs. In mathematics the jump is in abstraction and in the expectation that method is communicated, not just performed. In the sciences it is in quantitative treatment and in the single extended investigation replacing a series of short practicals. In English the jump is from comprehension and directed writing to unseen analysis and comparative argument. In the humanities it is from recall with some explanation to evaluation with weighted evidence.

The useful response is a short mapped block in DP1 term one, not a term of general support. Six to ten hours spent on timed extended writing, on command-term structure and on scoping the Extended Essay will close more of the gap than thirty hours of content coverage, because content is not where the gap is. That is also the cheapest tutoring a Diploma family will ever buy, since DP1 rates and availability are both better than DP2's.

One caution about the transition decision itself. Where a student is genuinely unsuited to three Higher Levels, no amount of tutoring substitutes for a timetable change, and only the school can make one. A tutor's job in that case is to say so clearly and early, while a change is still possible, rather than to sell a plan that manages the symptoms for eighteen months.

sections.heading: Higher Level choices and what universities actually ask for
paragraphs: The Higher Level decision shapes two years and it is usually made in a fortnight with incomplete information. Two patterns cause most of the later trouble in Dubai: three Higher Levels that each demand long written assignments in the same weeks, and a mathematics route chosen by preference rather than by what the student's intended degrees expect.

On mathematics, the practical rule is to check rather than assume. Analysis and Approaches is the route most often expected for mathematics-heavy degrees including engineering, physics, mathematics itself and many economics courses; Applications and Interpretation suits data-oriented and social-science destinations. Requirements differ by university and by course, they change, and universities in the UAE, the United Kingdom, North America and Europe do not state them identically. The only reliable method is to read the stated entry requirements for the specific courses on the specific universities' own admissions pages, in the year your child applies.

On subject combinations, count the written load rather than the difficulty. Two Higher Level sciences plus a Higher Level humanity produces three internal assessments and three sets of extended written work, often bunched. That is manageable for a well-organised student and brutal for a disorganised one, and the difference is a timetable judgement rather than an ability judgement. The school's coordinator can usually show which combinations their own cohorts find heavy.

Nothing on this page implies that tutoring is required for university admission or for equivalency. It is not, and any claim that it is would be a false-urgency claim about a regulatory and admissions process. What tutoring can legitimately do is help a student meet a requirement they have chosen, and help a family read that requirement accurately before two years of work are organised around a guess.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency for Diploma graduates in the UAE
paragraphs: Families planning on a UAE university, or on using a school certificate inside the country, meet the equivalency process. It is run by the Ministry of Education rather than by a school or a tutoring provider, and it has published requirements that differ by curriculum. Describing it accurately matters, because at least one ranking competitor in this market publishes the wrong subject count for the British track.

On the British track the published requirements are specific: students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for that count. On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For the International Baccalaureate specifically, no points threshold is published on this page, and nobody should quote you one from a tutoring site. The source that sets out the British and American tracks states no IB figure, so any IB equivalency number would be unsourced. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly, or ask your school's coordinator who deals with these submissions every year.

Two boundaries worth stating. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation for anyone; we describe the process and point to the authority. And equivalency is a documentation process rather than an academic one, so it is not something tutoring prepares a student for. Where it interacts with tutoring at all, it is in making sure a student's subject choices do not accidentally leave a gap the process will notice two years later.

sections.heading: What evidence of Diploma progress looks like across two years
paragraphs: Across a two-year programme a parent needs indicators that move faster than school reports do. Reports average work produced over months, so a real improvement in October can stay invisible until January, by which point a decision may already have been taken. The alternative is a short list of artefacts that exist or do not exist at a given point.

In DP1 the artefacts are a tested Higher Level load, a scoped Extended Essay research question, and evidence that the student can write a timed extended response in each subject. If those three exist by the end of DP1, the programme is on track regardless of what any individual grade says. If the Extended Essay question is still vague at the end of DP1, that is a more serious signal than a disappointing chemistry mark, and it is the one families most often miss.

In DP2 the artefacts are internal assessment drafts at a stage where feedback can still change them, marked timed papers in each subject, and a short list of near-miss questions from the mock. The progress indicator inside sessions is narrower: can the student now do unaided what they could not do three weeks ago, and do they catch their own errors before the tutor does? Both are visible long before a grade moves.

None of this predicts a result and no honest provider will offer one. External outcomes depend on papers nobody has seen, on boundaries set after marking, and on what the student does on the day. What can be held to a standard is whether these artefacts exist, whether the indicators are moving, and whether the provider shows you the evidence when asked. At session four we review exactly that, and sometimes the right recommendation is fewer hours or none.
