sections.heading: Delivery, scheduling and honest coverage for Diploma families
paragraphs: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on a shared screen, scheduled around a Dubai school week in Gulf Standard Time. Most Diploma sessions land between 16:30 and 20:30 after the school run and activities, and sixty to ninety minutes is the usual length, since that is what a Diploma student can sustain at the level of demand these subjects require. A short written note follows each session.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a Diploma family the relevant consequence is choice of tutor. Diploma provision sits in a minority of Dubai schools, so the specialists for a given Higher Level component are few, and geographic matching would hand you the nearest available science teacher rather than the person who has taught that component to examination.

Coverage is uneven and we publish the position rather than discovering it with you. Common subjects at common levels are matched within a few days. Scarce components, Chemistry at Higher Level between February and May or Computer Science HL at any time, take one to two weeks or longer. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match comes from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones at a Dubai-friendly hour, with no change to format or subject depth.

Two things we will decline. Anything that involves producing assessed work, because everything submitted must be the student's own and the risk of crossing that line falls on the candidate. And a large plan where a timetable conversation with the school is the actual remedy. Saying so costs us bookings and is the reason the programme planning session exists as a separate, smaller thing you can buy instead.

process.title: Start with the whole timetable
process.description: Tell us the six subjects, the three Higher Levels, where the Extended Essay stands and which component prompted the call. A Diploma request framed at programme level gets diagnosed properly; one framed as a single bad grade often produces a plan aimed at the wrong thing.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson on real material
process.description: One full lesson at no cost, built around a marked script, an internal assessment draft or a research question. It ends with a written statement of what is actually at risk across the programme and roughly how many hours that needs.

process.title: We name what belongs to the school
process.description: Timetable changes, supervisor deadlines, moderation outcomes and equivalency submissions belong with your school's IB coordinator. We say which parts of your problem are theirs, including when that means you need less tutoring than you expected.

process.title: Match on group, level and component
process.description: Not the subject alone. A Higher Level Paper 3, a scientific investigation criterion and an unseen-text paper need different teachers, and we say which specialist we are proposing and what they have taught.

process.title: Build the plan from your school's calendar
process.description: Internal deadlines and mock windows differ by several weeks between Dubai IB schools. We ask for your calendar and count backwards from it, so the hours land in the fortnights where they change what is submitted.

process.title: Review at session four, then decide
process.description: We look at the artefacts: a redone question, a changed draft, a marked paper. If the indicators have not moved we revisit the diagnosis rather than adding hours, and if the match is wrong we change the tutor at no extra cost.

whyPoints.title: We work to the programme, not one subject
whyPoints.description: A Diploma problem is often a loading problem. We look at the six-subject week, the Higher Level combination and where the core stands before proposing subject hours, which regularly produces a smaller plan than a family arrived expecting.

whyPoints.title: Matched on component, not proximity
whyPoints.description: Lessons are delivered online, so the tutor is chosen for the group, level and component the evidence points at. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

whyPoints.title: A published boundary on core work
whyPoints.description: The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and every internal assessment must be the student's own work. We question, critique method and give criterion-based feedback, and we state that in writing before a block starts.

whyPoints.title: Dates handled honestly
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson key dates are quoted from their published pages. IB session dates are not confirmable from automated sources, so we do not publish one and we point you to your coordinator or ibo.org instead.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency described, never promised
whyPoints.description: We set out the ministry's published requirements with the source named, state plainly that no IB points figure is published there, and point you to the authority. We neither perform nor guarantee any part of the process.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits before you commit
whyPoints.description: Scarce Higher Level components take one to two weeks to match and longer between February and May. If no UAE-based specialist is free we say so and explain where the match would come from instead.

faqs.question: How many subjects does an IB Diploma student in Dubai take?
faqs.answer: Six, chosen across six groups, with one subject from each group and a permitted substitution of a sixth-group arts subject for a second subject from groups one to five. Normally three are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Alongside those six sit the three core elements: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. In Dubai there is additional timetabled content that does not appear in IB documentation, because private schools in the emirate must also teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies whatever international curriculum they are licensed for.

faqs.question: How should my child choose which three subjects to take at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: By counting written load as well as interest and requirements. Two Higher Level sciences plus a Higher Level humanity produces three internal assessments and three sets of extended written assignments, frequently bunched into the same weeks. That is manageable for a well-organised student and punishing for a disorganised one, which is a timetable judgement rather than an ability judgement. Check your intended degrees' stated entry requirements on the universities' own admissions pages before choosing, and ask the school's coordinator which combinations their own cohorts find heavy. Changing later is possible but much harder.

faqs.question: How long does the Extended Essay have to be and who supervises it?
faqs.answer: It has an upper limit of 4,000 words, and it is supervised by a member of staff at your child's school who holds formal responsibility for the process, including the recorded reflective sessions. A tutor may critique the scope of a research question, question method, and give feedback against the published criteria on material the student has already written. A tutor may not supply content, restructure a draft or provide text, because everything submitted must be the student's own work. The highest-value hours are spent early, testing whether the question can actually be answered within the limit.

faqs.question: What does Theory of Knowledge require a Diploma student to produce?
faqs.answer: Two assessed pieces: an exhibition, in which the student links objects to a prompt and explains why each one answers it, and an essay written on a prescribed title with a published word limit. Both are judged against criteria on a best-fit basis, which means polish does not move a band but the named qualities in the descriptors do. The choice of prescribed title effectively sets the ceiling, and a weak choice cannot be recovered by later work. That makes title selection the cheapest high-value thing a tutor can help a student think through properly.

faqs.question: Does CAS affect my child's Diploma result?
faqs.answer: CAS is not graded, but it is a requirement for the award, and a student who has not completed it to the school's satisfaction has a problem no subject grade compensates for. It runs across both Diploma years as a programme of creativity, activity and service with its own reflective requirements, overseen by a coordinator at the school. It is also the element a tutor has no business touching: the experiences and the reflections belong to the student. Where CAS is behind, the conversation is with the coordinator, not with a tutoring provider.

faqs.question: Which schools in Dubai run the full IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Diploma provision sits in a minority of the emirate's private schools, which served 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25 with UK curricula the largest share by enrolment. Established Diploma cohorts include schools in Emirates Hills, Al Barsha, Al Garhoud, Dubai Festival City and Al Jaddaf, and the emirate is adding three new International Baccalaureate schools among seven new private schools for 2026-27, creating 16,846 new places overall. For an authoritative current list, check the regulator's own school listing rather than any tutoring directory.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from IGCSE to the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Specific rather than general. Students arrive with strong content recall and weak extended-response structure, because IGCSE rewards accurate short answers while the Diploma rewards sustained argument with weighted evidence. They also arrive with nothing in their experience resembling a 4,000-word independent essay. In mathematics the jump is in abstraction and in communicating method; in the sciences it is in quantitative treatment and a single extended investigation; in English it is from comprehension to unseen analysis. Six to ten hours in DP1 term one on timed extended writing closes more of that gap than thirty hours of content coverage.

faqs.question: Will a UAE university accept an IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Universities set their own entry requirements and the Ministry of Education runs a separate equivalency process for school certificates, so there are two things to check rather than one. For the British track the published equivalency rules are specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. For the International Baccalaureate no points threshold appears in that source, so nobody should quote you one. Check moe.gov.ae, the emirate's attestation authority, or your school's coordinator.

faqs.question: Does my child need Maths Analysis or Maths Applications for engineering?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the route most often expected for mathematics-heavy degrees including engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics courses, while Applications and Interpretation suits data-oriented and social-science destinations. That is a general pattern rather than a rule, because requirements differ by university and by course, they change between admission cycles, and institutions in the UAE, the UK, North America and Europe do not state them identically. Read the stated requirements for the specific courses on the specific universities' own admissions pages, in the cycle your child will apply in.

faqs.question: Is taking two Higher Level sciences too much for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on written output rather than on intelligence. Two Higher Level sciences means two extended investigations plus two sets of long written assignments, and in most schools those land in overlapping weeks. A student who plans ahead and drafts early handles it; a student who works to deadlines does not, and no amount of subject tutoring fixes the scheduling. If the combination is genuinely wrong, only the school can change the timetable, and the window for doing that comfortably is DP1 term one. That is why we offer a programme planning session separately from subject hours.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma student start the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most do, and specifically before the long summer break between the two Diploma years. The pattern we see in Dubai is that progress stalls over that break while families travel and no deadline is in sight, and students return to the second year with no usable draft, then lose the weeks they needed for subject revision. The target worth setting is a scoped research question by the end of DP1 term two and a usable draft before the break ends. Scoping work takes only a few hours and is the cheapest high-value support in the whole programme.

faqs.question: Can my child change a Higher Level subject after starting the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it gets harder every week. The decision belongs to the school, which has to consider timetable capacity, how much of the course has been covered and whether the student can realistically catch up. In practice DP1 term one is when a change is straightforward, DP1 term two is when it becomes difficult, and after that it is usually not possible. If the evidence points at a wrong combination rather than a weak student, the right move is a conversation with the coordinator immediately, not a tutoring plan that manages the symptoms for eighteen months.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the Diploma?
faqs.answer: They are separate requirements rather than part of the Diploma's six subjects, unless your child takes Arabic as their group 2 language acquisition subject. Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For equivalency purposes, Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five-subject GCSE or IGCSE count.

faqs.question: How does a Dubai school report translate into a Diploma grade?
faqs.answer: Loosely, and with a lag that catches families out. School reports average work produced over months, and internal predictions are the school's own judgement rather than a result. Internal assessment marks shown on a report are also provisional, because the school's marking is moderated by the IB against its own standard and a whole cohort can be adjusted. Treat a report as a direction of travel and look instead at artefacts: a timed extended response in each subject, internal assessment drafts at a changeable stage, and a mapped list of where marks were lost in the most recent paper.

faqs.question: How early should we arrange a Diploma tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: DP1 is both cheaper and better supplied than DP2, so the practical answer is earlier than most families act. Specialist availability in Dubai tightens from January to April because every Diploma cohort in the emirate converges on the same weeks, and the tutor who was bookable in November may not be in March at any rate. If you are not sure support is needed, run a free diagnostic session rather than committing: it costs nothing, produces a written statement of what is actually at risk, and frequently results in fewer hours than a family expected to buy.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-a-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Arabic A at Diploma level: Literature and Language and Literature, SL and HL, including the school-supported self-taught route. Each one marks to the published criteria rather than to a personal standard, so a parent can see which criterion moved and which did not.

intro.heading: Start with the script, not the syllabus
paragraphs: An IB DP Arabic A home tutor in Dubai is almost never hired at the start of DP1. The call comes after a report, a mock, or a returned Paper 2 with a mark the family did not expect. By then the useful question is narrow: on this script, under which criterion did the marks go, and is that a reading problem, a structure problem or a language problem? Those three failures look identical on a report card and need completely different lessons. A tutor who opens with a tour of the course has already wasted the first hour.

So the first session is a diagnostic on paper your child has already written. We ask for the most recent marked Paper 1 or Paper 2, the learner portfolio if the school keeps one, and the draft of whatever is next due. The tutor re-marks the script against the criteria, writes down a mark for each one, and compares that with the school's mark. Where the two disagree, that gap is the lesson: it is usually the difference between what the student thought the question asked and what the criterion rewards.

Arabic A carries a complication no other Group 1 subject in Dubai has. Your child probably speaks a dialect at home, reads fusha in class, and is assessed entirely in fusha. A student can be fluent, confident, the one the family relies on for translation, and still lose marks under criterion D because the register slipped. Marking that as a language weakness is accurate and useless. Naming it as dialect interference in a specific sentence, on a specific line of their own last essay, is something a student can correct inside a fortnight and then check for themselves on everything they write afterwards.

The second complication is Dubai itself. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language. That means a DP student taking Arabic A is also carrying the school's mandatory Arabic provision, and the two do not always align. Families arrive assuming one subject is being taught; often two are, with different expectations and different teachers.

What we do about all of this is unglamorous and visible. Each fortnight your child produces one piece of timed work. It is marked criterion by criterion, the marks are written into a running record, and the next session starts from the lowest one. A parent does not have to take anyone's word about progress. The record either shows criterion B moving from 3 to 5 across four attempts, or it shows it flat, in which case the plan was wrong and we change it.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-a-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Arabic A sits inside a longer arc. A Dubai student usually meets fusha in PYP or a national-curriculum primary, formalises it through MYP Language and Literature, and then chooses between Arabic A and Arabic B at 16. The programme notes below describe what each stage leaves unfinished.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subjects, and the core of Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Arabic A occupies the Group 1 slot as either Literature or Language and Literature, at SL or HL. Assessment is three external components plus an internally assessed oral, and at HL a written essay produced across several months.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP cohorts are unusually mixed in Arabic background: Emirati nationals, Arab expatriates from a dozen dialect regions, and heritage speakers born here who read fusha slowly. One class can hold all three. A tutor working one-to-one can set the register and reading-speed targets a shared classroom cannot.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Arabic appears as Language and Literature for first-language students and Language Acquisition for others. MYP marking uses four criteria out of eight each, with grades on a 1-7 scale derived from criterion totals, which is why MYP 6 and DP 6 mean very different things in Arabic.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Arabic A step catches Dubai families out more than any other transition we see. MYP rewards personal response and creative text production; Arabic A Paper 1 rewards close reading of an unseen passage against a guiding question. A student can hold a steady MYP 6 and open DP1 with a Paper 1 mark in the low teens out of 20.

programmes.name: School-supported self-taught Arabic A
programmes.description: Where a school does not teach a student's first language, the IB allows Literature SL to be taken self-taught with school support. The student reads the nine works independently, the school supervises the Individual Oral, and the external papers are identical to the taught course. It is available at SL only, never HL.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this route is used less for Arabic than it should be. Several British-curriculum schools here run no Arabic A class at all, so an Arab first-language student is pushed into Arabic B and assessed on a course beneath their reading level. The self-taught Literature SL route keeps the Group 1 slot and the bilingual diploma in reach.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller UAE presence than the Diploma, pairing DP courses with a career-related study and a personal and professional skills course. Students take fewer DP subjects, so a language choice carries more weight in the overall profile.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai CP student takes Arabic A as one of their DP courses, the tutoring plan narrows to the components that actually count rather than the whole course. That usually means Paper 1 technique and the Individual Oral, because those are the two that can be rehearsed to a timetable.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-a-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Arabic A is one subject with several faces, and a tutoring plan has to name which one. The entries below are the components and skill areas we actually teach against, with the mark allocation attached to each.

subjects.name: Paper 1 guided literary analysis
subjects.levels: SL 1 h 15 min - HL 2 h 15 min
subjects.description: An unseen passage with a guiding question, marked out of 20 on criteria A to D. SL sits one analysis, HL sits two. The skill is reading a passage cold and building an argument that answers the guiding question from the first paragraph, not the last.

subjects.name: Paper 2 comparative essay
subjects.description: One question answered through two studied works, marked out of 30. The marks live in the comparison itself. Candidates who write a strong paragraph on each work and then a linking sentence at the end score under criterion B however good the two halves are.

subjects.name: Arabic A HL essay
subjects.description: A formal essay on one work or body of work studied, worth 20% of the HL grade and marked out of 20. The usual failure is a question too large to sustain. Narrowing it from a theme to an argument is a single session that changes the whole mark.

subjects.name: Arabic A Individual Oral
subjects.description: Fifteen minutes, marked out of 40: a ten-minute statement on how a global issue is presented in two extracts, then five minutes of questions. Extract choice decides the mark before the student speaks, which is why we rehearse selection before delivery.

subjects.name: Fusha register and dialect interference
subjects.description: The commonest criterion D problem in Dubai. Colloquial verb forms, dialect vocabulary and spoken sentence rhythm reach the page unnoticed because they sound right. We work from the student's own marked scripts, listing their specific slips rather than teaching grammar in general.

subjects.name: Classical and modern Arabic literary text handling
subjects.description: Pre-modern poetry, the modern novel and contemporary drama need different reading strategies. A qasida and a Mahfouz chapter cannot be annotated the same way. Students who have one method apply it everywhere and lose criterion A marks on whichever text it does not fit.

subjects.name: Works in translation
subjects.description: Arabic A: Literature requires works read in translation alongside works originally in Arabic. Students often treat a translated novel as if style were authorial. Separating what can be argued about a translation from what cannot is a criterion B skill examiners reward.

subjects.name: Learner portfolio discipline
subjects.description: Not assessed directly, but the portfolio is where the evidence for the Individual Oral and the HL essay accumulates. A student with a thin portfolio in DP2 term one has no material to choose from and ends up writing on whichever work is freshest.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Language and Literature non-literary bodies of work
subjects.description: The Language and Literature course sets literary works against non-literary material such as advertising, journalism and political speech. The analytical vocabulary differs from Literature, and students moving between schools mid-DP often arrive with the wrong one.

subjects.name: Timed writing under exam conditions
subjects.description: Arabic handwriting at speed degrades, and criterion D notices. A student who scores well on coursework and poorly in mocks usually has a stamina problem rather than a knowledge problem. The fix is timed practice at the real paper length, fortnightly.

sections.heading: What a search for an Arabic A home tutor in Dubai is really asking
paragraphs: The phrase people type is home tutor. The need underneath it is a specialist who can mark Arabic A to the published criteria and explain the result. Those are different things, and in Dubai they pull in opposite directions. The pool of tutors who will drive to your villa is limited to whoever lives within a reasonable radius. The pool who can take apart a Paper 2 comparative essay in fusha is small across the whole emirate, and the odds that the two sets overlap in your community are poor.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Arabic A tuition here is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. That is not a compromise dressed up as a feature. It is the reason a family in Arabian Ranches can work with an Arabic A Literature specialist rather than with the nearest available Arabic teacher, and the reason a 19:30 session is possible at all on a weeknight.

There is a second, duller advantage. A screen-shared script can be annotated live and saved. A paper script annotated at your dining table leaves the house with the tutor. Over two years, the saved record of marked work is the single most useful artefact the tuition produces, because it is what tells you whether criterion B is moving. Parents who have had both arrangements tend to notice this before they notice anything else about the format.

sections.heading: Which Arabic A course is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: Three or four different courses answer to the name Arabic A, and families regularly do not know which one is on the timetable. Literature and Language and Literature share a paper structure and a criteria set but study different material. SL and HL differ in the number of works, the length of Paper 1 and the presence of the HL essay. The self-taught Literature SL route differs again in who supervises the oral. A tutoring plan built on the wrong one of these wastes a term.

The practical test is to look at what the student is reading and how many works there are. Nine works and no non-literary material means Literature SL. Thirteen works means Literature HL. Four literary works alongside advertising, journalism or speeches means Language and Literature SL. If nobody at home can answer the question, the school's subject report or the learner portfolio will, and it is worth five minutes to establish before booking anything.

The weightings matter more than they look: at HL, Paper 2 drops to 25% while the HL essay takes 20%, so a student who ignores the essay until DP2 term two has left a fifth of the grade until the busiest point of the two years. At SL there is no essay, and the Individual Oral carries 30% instead, which changes where the revision effort should go entirely.

sections.heading: Reading the criteria off a marked script
paragraphs: A grade tells a parent that something is wrong. A criterion breakdown tells them what. Every Arabic A component is marked on four criteria, and the pattern of which ones are low is diagnostic. Low A with healthy B means the student is analysing confidently but has misread the passage or the question. Low B with healthy A means they understood it and then only described what they saw. Low C is structure. Low D is language, and in Dubai low D is dialect interference more often than it is weak grammar.

This is why the first thing we ask for is paper rather than a conversation. A parent's account of the problem is honest and second-hand; the script is first-hand. The tutor marks it blind, records four numbers, and only then compares with the school's marks. Two independent markings of the same piece, with the gaps named, is more information than most students get in a term, and it costs one session.

The table sets out where the marks sit and what we see go wrong most often in Dubai cohorts specifically. None of these failures is exotic. All of them are visible on a script, and each has a different fix: a reading drill, a structural template practised and then discarded, a personal error list for register. What they do not have is a shared solution, which is why a general Arabic tutor and an Arabic A tutor produce different results on the same student.

sections.heading: Fusha, dialect and the thing no competitor page mentions
paragraphs: Arabic is the only Group 1 language in a Dubai DP cohort where the version spoken at home and the version assessed are reliably different. A student may speak Emirati, Levantine, Egyptian or Maghrebi Arabic at home, hear a mixture of all four in the corridor, and be examined entirely in Modern Standard Arabic. Fluency is not the issue. Register is. The student who sounds most confident in the room is often the one whose written criterion D marks are lowest, because confidence carries spoken habits onto the page.

The correction is specific rather than general. We do not teach Arabic grammar from the start to a fluent speaker; that is insulting and it does not work. We build an error list from the student's own marked scripts: their particular colloquial verb substitutions, their dialect vocabulary, the structures they reach for under time pressure. Twelve to twenty items, usually. The student checks their own work against their own list before submission, and the list shortens over a term. Criterion D marks follow it.

There is a Dubai layer on top. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires that Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies are taught in separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. A DP student taking Arabic A is therefore often carrying mandatory Arabic provision as well. Knowing which teacher is assessing what stops a family chasing the wrong report.

sections.heading: The HL essay: a draft history, not a rewrite
paragraphs: The Arabic A HL essay is 1,200 to 1,500 words, worth 20% of the HL grade, marked out of 20, and produced over months rather than in a hall. That makes it the component where outside help is most tempting and most dangerous. The IB treats work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not on whoever helped. So the boundary has to be stated rather than implied, and it has to hold when a deadline is three days away.

A tutor working on an HL essay may do four things. Help narrow a theme into an arguable question. Discuss whether the chosen evidence supports the argument. Read a draft and respond to it against the criteria. Teach the conventions of academic writing in Arabic. A tutor may not supply content, write or rewrite passages, edit the prose to a finish, or decide the argument. IB Gram does not write, redraft or complete any assessed component, and a tutor who offers to is a risk to your child's diploma rather than a shortcut.

In practice the honest version is also the one that scores. Most weak HL essays fail under criterion A or C, and both failures are decided at the question stage, before any writing happens. A question such as how one novelist presents exile is a theme, not an argument; it invites summary, and summary caps criterion B. Reworking it into a claim that can be contested takes one session and lifts the ceiling of everything written afterwards. We keep every draft, dated, so the school can see a progression that belongs to the student.

sections.heading: What Arabic A tuition costs in Dubai, and what the rate hides
paragraphs: Three of the six ranking pages we examined for this cluster publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. So here are the Dubai market bands in the currency families actually pay in, with the source and date attached to each. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list: our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and the figure we quote depends on level, component and session length rather than on a published tier.

The number that moves most is not the hourly rate but what the rate includes. An in-home visit prices travel inside the billed hour, and in Dubai that can be twenty minutes of a sixty-minute session in each direction on a weekday evening. A coursework supervision block is priced differently from weekly subject support almost everywhere, because it involves reading drafts between sessions. And a rate quoted for Arabic frequently assumes Arabic B; Arabic A Literature at HL is a different specialism and a thinner market.

Set against Dubai school fees, the arithmetic is less dramatic than it feels. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Against a fee bill that is already fixed, a weekly one-to-one session across the two DP years is a small marginal line, and families tend to decide it on whether the marks move rather than on the hourly figure.

sections.heading: Is your Arabic tutor permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is a question Dubai families ask late and should ask first. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and it is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system under the service named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

Eligibility is wider than most parents assume. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students may all apply. That breadth is why a verification question is worth asking: a tutor being eligible and a tutor holding the permit are not the same thing, and the only person who can show you the permit is the tutor.

One boundary matters in Abu Dhabi and is worth knowing in Dubai too. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct along the same lines. So the arrangement some families ask for first - your child's own Arabic teacher, privately, for an hour on Saturday - is the one arrangement we will not broker. Verify any claim against MoHRE and the relevant authority directly; IB Gram holds no regulator licence and claims none.

sections.heading: Counting back from the May session
paragraphs: Arabic A is not a subject that can be rescued in six weeks, because two of its components close long before the written papers. The Individual Oral is recorded inside a school window in DP2, and the HL essay is submitted earlier still. By the time a family starts worrying about May, 40% of an HL grade and 30% of an SL grade may already be fixed. Working backwards from the session is therefore the only planning method that survives contact with a real DP timetable.

The deadlines that bind are mostly set by the school, not by the IB, and they differ between Dubai schools by several weeks. Ask the DP coordinator for the subject's internal deadline calendar in DP1, not DP2. Two local factors shift it further. Ramadan moves earlier each year and compresses the revision weeks before the session, with families often preferring post-Iftar session times. And the long summer between DP1 and DP2 is where portfolio work either consolidates or evaporates.

We publish no specific IB exam or results dates on these pages. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date we quoted would be second-hand, and a wrong date on a page like this is worse than no date. Confirm every session, upload and results date with your child's DP coordinator or on ibo.org. What is safe to plan against is the shape below, which is the same in every Dubai school even when the calendar dates are not.

sections.heading: What the evidence looks like after eight weeks
paragraphs: A parent paying for weekly tuition is entitled to something better than an impression. So the record is deliberately boring. Every marked piece gets four numbers, one per criterion, dated, in a running table the family can see. After eight weeks there are four marked pieces and sixteen numbers, and the pattern in them is the answer to whether this is working. Criterion C climbing from 3 to 5 while A stays at 3 is a clear message: the structure teaching landed and the reading work has not started yet.

That record also changes the conversation with the school. A subject teacher with twenty-four students and a mandatory-subject timetable cannot produce a criterion history for each one. A parent who arrives at a consultation with four dated markings is asking a different question from a parent who arrives with a worry, and in our experience gets a more specific answer. The school remains the authority on the student's predicted grade; the record simply makes the discussion concrete.

Where the numbers do not move, we say so. Eight weeks of flat criterion B usually means one of three things: the diagnosis was wrong, the student is not writing between sessions, or the match is not right. All three are fixable and only the third requires changing tutor. What none of them justifies is another term of the same plan, which is what happens by default when nobody is counting the criterion marks from one piece to the next.

process.title: Send the last marked script
process.description: Before anything is booked, send the most recent marked Arabic A paper, the school's criterion marks if they were given, and the next deadline. If the family does not know whether the course is Literature or Language and Literature, the script usually answers it.

process.title: Free trial lesson, used as a diagnostic
process.description: The trial is spent re-marking that script against criteria A to D and comparing the result with the school's. The output is four numbers and a named starting point, which the family keeps whether or not they continue. The free trial carries no card requirement.

process.title: Agree the component order
process.description: HL essay first, oral first, or Paper 1 technique first - the order depends on which deadline is nearest and which criterion is lowest, not on the syllabus sequence. We write the order down with the dates attached so it can be checked later.

process.title: Weekly session, fortnightly marked piece
process.description: Sessions run live online in Gulf Standard Time, usually after 18:00 on a Dubai weekday. Every second week the student produces one timed piece, which is marked criterion by criterion and becomes the material for the next two sessions.

process.title: Review the record at week eight
process.description: Four marked pieces in, the family and the tutor look at the criterion history together. If a criterion has not moved, the plan changes. If the match is wrong, we rematch rather than persist, and the record transfers to the new tutor.

whyPoints.title: Arabic A, not Arabic generally
whyPoints.description: Most Arabic tutoring available in Dubai is pitched at Arabic B or at school Arabic. Arabic A Literature at HL needs someone who can mark a comparative essay in fusha against criteria A to D and justify each number. That is the specialism we match for.

whyPoints.title: Dialect interference treated as a named list
whyPoints.description: A fluent speaker losing criterion D marks does not need beginner grammar. They need their own twelve to twenty recurring slips written down and checked before submission. The list comes from their scripts, so it is specific to them and it shortens.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line stated in advance
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reads drafts and responds to them against criteria. A tutor does not write, redraft or finish an HL essay, Extended Essay, TOK essay or any assessed component. Saying so before the first session is how we keep it from becoming a negotiation at a deadline.

whyPoints.title: Delivery that is honest about itself
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one and online, over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a UAE address, and no UAE office is claimed. What that buys is access to a specialist rather than to the nearest available teacher.

whyPoints.title: A record that survives the tutor
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts are screen-shared and kept, drafts are dated, criterion marks go into a running table. If the tutor changes, the history does not reset, and a parent can see two years of movement rather than remembering a sequence of impressions.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP Arabic A home tutor in Dubai actually cost?
faqs.answer: Dubai market rates for qualified online subject tutors run roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and premium named tutors above AED 500, according to published rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. In-home visits sit at AED 180-500 because travel is priced inside the hour. Those are market figures, not ours. IB Gram starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and quotes against level, component and session length rather than from a tier list, because Arabic A HL essay supervision and weekly Paper 1 practice are different pieces of work.

faqs.question: Is Arabic A Literature or Arabic A Language and Literature better for my child?
faqs.answer: Neither is stronger; they suit different readers. Literature studies nine works at SL and thirteen at HL, all literary, and rewards sustained close reading. Language and Literature studies four literary works at SL or six at HL alongside non-literary material such as journalism, advertising and political speech, and rewards analysis of how language works in context. A student who reads fiction willingly usually does better in Literature. A student who argues well about media and rhetoric often does better in Language and Literature. In Dubai the practical constraint is usually which one the school timetables, not which one suits.

faqs.question: Can my child take Arabic A if their school does not teach it?
faqs.answer: Often yes. The IB allows Literature SL to be taken school-supported self-taught, where the student reads the nine works independently and the school supervises the Individual Oral. The external papers are identical to the taught course. It is available at Standard Level only, never HL. In Dubai this route matters because several British-curriculum schools run no Arabic A class, which otherwise pushes an Arab first-language student into Arabic B and a course below their reading level. Raise it with the DP coordinator in DP1; it needs school agreement and it needs planning time.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Arabic A Individual Oral worth and how is it structured?
faqs.answer: Fifteen minutes, marked out of 40 across four criteria of 10 marks each. The student speaks for ten minutes on how a global issue is presented in two extracts - one from a work originally written in Arabic, one from a work studied in translation - then answers five minutes of questions. It carries 30% of the Standard Level grade and 20% at Higher Level. Extract selection decides a great deal of the mark before the student opens their mouth, which is why rehearsal starts with choosing extracts that genuinely let the issue be argued rather than ones that are easy to talk about.

faqs.question: My child speaks Arabic fluently but loses marks on written work. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always register rather than ability. Dubai students speak a dialect at home, hear several others at school, and are assessed entirely in Modern Standard Arabic. Spoken verb forms, dialect vocabulary and conversational sentence rhythm reach the page unnoticed because they sound correct to the writer. That lands under criterion D, and a report describing it as weak language is accurate and unhelpful. The fix is a personal error list built from the student's own marked scripts - usually twelve to twenty recurring items - checked before every submission. It is a fortnight of work, not a year.

faqs.question: What is the word limit on the Arabic A HL essay and how much does it count?
faqs.answer: Between 1,200 and 1,500 words, marked out of 20 across four criteria, and worth 20% of the Higher Level grade. It exists only at HL. Because it is written over months rather than in an exam hall, it is the component students postpone, and postponing it means a fifth of the grade lands in the busiest term of DP2. The single most useful session is the first one, where a theme is narrowed into an arguable question. Broad questions invite summary, and summary caps the analysis criterion whatever the quality of the writing that follows.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write my child's Arabic A HL essay?
faqs.answer: No, and any tutor who offers to is a risk to your child's diploma rather than a shortcut. The IB treats work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate. What a tutor may legitimately do: help narrow the question, discuss whether the evidence supports the argument, read drafts and respond to them against the published criteria, and teach the conventions of academic writing in Arabic. What a tutor may not do: supply content, write or rewrite passages, edit the prose to completion, or decide the argument. We keep every dated draft so the progression is visibly the student's.

faqs.question: How does the mandatory Arabic requirement in Dubai schools affect Arabic A?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies because expectations and language of instruction differ. A DP student taking Arabic A is therefore frequently carrying mandatory provision as well, sometimes with a different teacher and a different report. Knowing which teacher assesses which thing prevents families chasing the wrong feedback. The requirement is a school obligation, not something tutoring satisfies or replaces.

faqs.question: Does taking Arabic A get my child the IB bilingual diploma?
faqs.answer: It can. One route to the bilingual diploma is completing two language A courses and scoring grade 3 or higher in both, which for most Dubai students means Arabic A alongside English A. Other routes exist through studying a sciences or individuals-and-societies subject in a second language, or through an Extended Essay submitted in a second language. The award is made by the IB on the results, not applied for, and your DP coordinator can confirm which route your child's subject choices put them on. It is worth checking in DP1 while the timetable can still change.

faqs.question: Why is an online Arabic A tutor better than one who comes to our villa?
faqs.answer: Because of who is available rather than where the lesson happens. A tutor who travels to your community is drawn from whoever lives within a reasonable drive; Arabic A Literature specialists are thin across the whole emirate, so the overlap in any one area is small. Online delivery removes the radius. It also removes travel from the billed hour, which in Dubai on a weekday evening is a real portion of the session. And a screen-shared script can be annotated and saved, so the marked record accumulates instead of leaving the house with the tutor.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send Arabic tutors to homes in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Arabic A tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, which for most Dubai households means a slot after 18:00 on a weekday or a morning at the weekend. We also hold no UAE office, centre or branch, and claim no permit or accreditation from KHDA, the Ministry of Education or the IB. Any tutor you work with must hold their own MoHRE private tuition work permit.

faqs.question: When should we start Arabic A tutoring if exams are in May?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do, because two components close before the papers. The Individual Oral is recorded in a school window during DP2 and the HL essay is submitted before that, so by the spring of DP2 up to 40% of an HL grade is already fixed. The most useful entry point is DP1 term two, when the portfolio is forming and the oral works can still be chosen deliberately. Starting six weeks before the session is not pointless - Paper 1 technique responds quickly - but it limits the work to the components still open.

faqs.question: How will I know the tutoring is working rather than just happening?
faqs.answer: By four numbers per piece of work. Every marked piece gets a mark for each of the four criteria, dated, in a running table you can see. After eight weeks that is four pieces and sixteen numbers, and the pattern answers the question. Criterion C rising while A stays flat means the structure teaching landed and the reading work has not begun. Flat marks across eight weeks mean the diagnosis was wrong, the student is not writing between sessions, or the match is poor - and the first two are fixable without changing tutor. We say which one we think it is.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or around school exam weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they usually need to. Ramadan shifts earlier each year and compresses the revision weeks before the session; many Dubai families prefer post-Iftar session times, which online delivery accommodates without a travel calculation. School mock weeks and internal deadline clusters are the other reason to move a slot. The pattern we suggest is to protect the fortnightly marked piece even when the live session moves, because the marked work is what the record is built from. A paused month with no written work leaves a visible gap in the criterion history.

faqs.question: What should we send before the first Arabic A session?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them take long to gather. The most recent marked Arabic A script, with the school's criterion marks if they were written on it. The learner portfolio or a list of works studied so far, which also settles whether the course is Literature or Language and Literature. And the next deadline on the subject's calendar, whether that is an oral window, an essay draft or a mock. With those, the trial session can be spent re-marking real work rather than establishing basic facts about the course.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-a-home-tutor.closingBody: The useful first hour of Arabic A tutoring is not an introduction. It is a marked script, re-marked against criteria A to D, with the four numbers written down and compared against the school's. Send the most recent paper, the list of works studied and the next deadline, and the trial lesson produces a named starting point you keep whether or not you continue. Sessions run one-to-one online in Gulf Standard Time. We will tell you if Arabic A is not where your child's marks are actually being lost, because the alternative is billing you for the wrong subject.

intro.heading: Three different students search for the same thing
paragraphs: Arabic A is not one situation. The first student is in a Dubai school that teaches Arabic A properly, in a class of twenty, and is losing marks on written analysis despite speaking Arabic at home every day. The second is in a school that offers no Arabic A at all and wants to sit it as a school-supported self-taught candidate, which is possible but only in one specific configuration. The third is deciding whether to carry Arabic A alongside English A in order to receive a bilingual diploma. Those three need different first sessions, and most pages on this subject answer only the first.

The self-taught route is the one families know least about and the one where a wrong assumption costs the most. Language A: Literature may be taken as school-supported self-taught, at Standard Level only. That means no Higher Level, and it means Literature rather than Language and Literature. The school registers the candidate, provides a supervisor and administrative support, and is not obliged to teach the course. Everything else - reading the works, building the analysis, preparing the individual oral - sits with the student. Which is precisely why these candidates are the ones who most need a subject specialist.

The bilingual diploma question is the other one worth getting right early. Completing two Group 1 languages at grade 3 or above earns it, which is the route most Dubai families have in mind when they ask about Arabic A alongside English A. There is also a second route, which almost nobody mentions: taking a Group 3 or Group 4 subject in a language other than the nominated Language A, with a grade 3 or above in both. That second route changes the arithmetic for some students and is worth checking with the coordinator before a subject choice is locked.

Running underneath all of this in Dubai is a separate requirement that families routinely confuse with Arabic A. Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum a school is licensed by KHDA to teach, and KHDA requires that Arab and non-Arab students be taught separately in those subjects, with combined classes prohibited. Those lessons are not Arabic A. They have their own content, their own language of instruction rules and their own teachers, and a student can be doing well in one and badly in the other.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no accreditation from the IB, KHDA, the Ministry of Education or any other authority, we have no UAE office, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we offer only in India. Dubai families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time by a named Arabic A specialist, with a free trial lesson before any payment.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-a-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Arabic A sits in Group 1 of the Diploma, the studies in language and literature group, and it behaves exactly as any other Language A does. What differs in Dubai is the surrounding arrangement: who teaches it, whether the school offers it at all, and how it sits beside the mandatory Arabic lessons every private school must run.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Arabic A is offered as Literature or as Language and Literature, each at Standard and Higher Level, with the same assessment architecture as the equivalent English A courses: an unseen Paper 1, a comparative Paper 2 written without the texts, an individual oral on a global issue across two works, and at Higher Level a 1,200 to 1,500 word essay. All of it is assessed in Modern Standard Arabic.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the practical variable is provision rather than syllabus. Some schools run Arabic A at both levels with full teaching; some run Standard Level only; some offer nothing and register self-taught candidates. Ask the IB coordinator which course and which levels are actually taught before assuming a choice exists, because it frequently does not and the self-taught route has its own limits.

programmes.name: School-supported self-taught
programmes.description: A route for a student whose Language A is not taught by the school. It applies to Literature at Standard Level and not to Higher Level or to Language and Literature. The school registers the candidate and provides a supervisor and administrative support; the teaching of the course is not part of the arrangement, which is why these candidates need an external specialist more than any other group.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has an unusually high number of students in this position, because many schools serve highly international intakes and cannot staff every Language A. A self-taught Arabic A candidate here is often the only one in their year group, with no class to discuss works with and no scheduled lesson. The plan that works is a fixed weekly session, a written reading timetable and an early decision about which works go to which component.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language and Literature in Arabic builds the analytical criteria the Diploma extends, and a student who studied Arabic at first-language level through MYP arrives with the register and the reading speed already in place. Students who took Arabic as language acquisition in MYP and then move to Arabic A face a genuine jump in both.
programmes.countryNote: The split matters more in Dubai than almost anywhere, because KHDA requires separate provision for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language and a student's placement there is a strong predictor of whether Arabic A is realistic. Checking the MYP phase and stream a student was in is the fastest way to judge whether Arabic A at Higher Level is a sensible target.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-a-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: The list below is what Arabic A actually assesses, together with the Arabic and Islamic provision a Dubai student carries alongside it. The distinction between the two sets matters, because families often buy tutoring for one while the problem sits in the other.

subjects.name: Paper 1: guided analysis
subjects.description: Previously unseen material with a guiding question - literary passages on the Literature course, non-literary texts on Language and Literature. Standard Level answers on one, Higher Level on two, and the component carries 35% at both levels. Nothing about the text can be prepared, so the preparation is a procedure applied in Arabic.

subjects.name: Paper 2: comparative essay
subjects.description: Four general questions, one chosen, two studied works compared, with no copy of either text in the room. Worth 35% at Standard Level and 25% at Higher. For Arabic A the limiting factor is almost always precise recall of quotation in Modern Standard Arabic rather than analytical ability.

subjects.name: Individual oral
subjects.description: Ten minutes of prepared analysis on a global issue across two works, followed by five minutes of questions, conducted in Arabic. Worth 30% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher. Both works are then unavailable for any other component, which makes the choice strategic.

subjects.name: HL essay
subjects.description: A 1,200 to 1,500 word essay in Arabic on one work studied, developed from the learner portfolio and worth 20% of the Higher Level grade. Not available to self-taught candidates, since the self-taught route is Standard Level only.

subjects.name: Modern Standard Arabic register
subjects.description: The assessment is written and spoken in fusha. A student fluent in Gulf, Levantine or Egyptian dialect may be entirely confident in conversation and still lose marks on written register, verb forms and vocabulary that belong to speech rather than to formal writing.

subjects.name: Works in translation
subjects.description: A Language A course requires works originally written in other languages, read in Arabic translation. Students analyse these differently from works written in Arabic: structure, imagery and context survive translation, while fine lexical choice and sound patterning belong to the translator.

subjects.name: The learner portfolio
subjects.description: Compulsory and not directly assessed. It is the source for the individual oral's global issue and, at Higher Level, the HL essay's line of inquiry. For a self-taught candidate with no class discussion, the portfolio is often the only written record of their own thinking.

subjects.name: KHDA mandatory Arabic as a first language
subjects.levels: School requirement, not an IB course
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed by KHDA to teach, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Arabs. It is a different subject from Arabic A with different content.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.levels: School requirement, not an IB course
subjects.description: Also mandatory in Dubai private schools, with separate classes by group and language-of-instruction rules set by KHDA. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic are required to hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects, which is a credential a parent can reasonably ask about.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Arabic
subjects.description: Permitted in a Group 1 language within the category rules the school will explain, and written in Arabic. A tutor may discuss a research question, suggest reading and give written feedback on the student's own drafts; the essay remains the student's work and the school supervisor stays the examining relationship.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-a-online-tutor.regionsIntro: What varies between Dubai communities for this subject is not distance but provision: which schools nearby teach Arabic A at all, how large the Arab first-language cohort is, and whether a student will have classmates to discuss works with. The notes below are about that rather than about travel.

regions.name: Al Twar, Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: Large Arab first-language cohorts and schools with established Arabic departments, so a student here is more likely to be in a taught Arabic A class than a self-taught one. Early-evening private Arabic lessons are common, which fills the week quickly.

regions.note: Full-continuum IB provision alongside strong Arabic departments. Students here often have both Arabic A and the mandatory Arabic lessons with different teachers, which is where the confusion between the two subjects most often starts.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim, Al Manara and Al Safa
regions.note: Schools with highly international intakes, so Arab first-language students are sometimes a small minority and Arabic A classes are small. Self-taught candidates appear more frequently in this strip than anywhere else in the emirate.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba, Meydan and Nad Al Hamar
regions.note: Newer communities with Diploma and A Level schools nearby. Arabic A cohorts are small and a student may be one of three, so an external reader for set works matters more here than in a large class.

regions.note: Older, densely built areas with the best access to Arabic-language bookshops in the city, which matters more than it sounds when a set work has to be obtained in a specific edition for page references.

regions.note: Villa communities with longer drives to schools in Al Barsha and Emirates Hills. Students here frequently combine Arabic A with a demanding science or mathematics load, so the reading has to be timetabled rather than left to whenever there is a free evening.

regions.note: Cross-creek journeys and a mix of IB and British schools. These households are the most likely to be weighing Arabic A against Arabic B, and the honest test is written register in fusha rather than conversational fluency.

A taught candidate needs a second reader and marked written work; a self-taught candidate needs a course delivered. The three shapes below reflect that difference honestly.

modes.title: Self-taught Standard Level programme

sections.heading: What an IB DP Arabic A online tutor in Dubai is actually being asked for
paragraphs: The useful first question is not about Arabic. It is about the arrangement the student is in, because the same subject produces three entirely different pieces of work. A student in a taught class needs a second reader and marked essays. A self-taught Standard Level candidate needs the course delivered. A student weighing Arabic A against Arabic B needs a placement judgement made from written evidence rather than from how they sound at the dinner table.

Getting this wrong is expensive. Families sometimes buy a term of general Arabic conversation for a student who is already fluent and whose problem is written register in Modern Standard Arabic. Others buy literary discussion for a self-taught candidate who has not yet obtained two of the nine works and has no reading timetable. In both cases the tutoring is competent and aimed at the wrong thing, and nobody discovers it until a mock.

So the first session asks for documents. Which Arabic A course and level is the student registered for, or intending to register for. Whether the school teaches it or is supporting a self-taught candidate. The list of works. The most recent marked written piece in Arabic. And, separately, how the student is doing in the school's mandatory Arabic lessons, because those two subjects are frequently confused and the answer tells us a great deal about register.

The table-free answer to all this is short: the route determines the plan, and the route is a matter of fact rather than of preference. The sections below set out what each route actually involves, starting with the one families are given least information about.

sections.heading: The three routes into Arabic A in a Dubai school
paragraphs: Provision varies sharply across the emirate. Some Dubai schools teach Arabic A at both levels and both courses with full staffing. Some teach Standard Level Literature only. Some offer no Arabic A and will register a school-supported self-taught candidate instead. A family's realistic options are set by which of those their school is, and the answer comes from the IB coordinator rather than from the prospectus.

The self-taught route carries two hard limits that are worth repeating because they are frequently misunderstood. It applies to Language A: Literature, not to Language and Literature. And it is available at Standard Level only. A student who wants Arabic A at Higher Level needs a school that teaches it. A family planning on self-taught Higher Level is planning on something that does not exist, and discovering that after subject registration closes is a serious problem.

What the school does provide for a self-taught candidate is registration, a supervisor and the administrative handling of submissions. What it does not provide is teaching. The supervisor is not a subject teacher in this arrangement and should not be expected to mark essays weekly or teach nine works. Being clear about that boundary early keeps the relationship with the school good, which matters because every deadline and submission still goes through them.

The table below sets the three routes side by side, with what each one leaves to the family. Confirm the detail with your child's coordinator, since registration rules and school provision both change, and we publish no IB examination or results dates on this page because the IB's own site does not serve its calendar to automated checks.

sections.heading: The bilingual diploma arithmetic, including the route nobody mentions
paragraphs: A large share of Dubai families considering Arabic A are really asking about the bilingual diploma. The main route is straightforward: complete two languages from Group 1 and achieve grade 3 or above in both, and the diploma is awarded as bilingual. For an Arabic-speaking student in an English-medium Dubai school, that usually means English A plus Arabic A, which is a heavy Group 1 load but an entirely normal one.

The second route is much less discussed and sometimes more practical. A candidate who completes a subject from Group 3 or Group 4 in a language other than their nominated Language A, with grade 3 or above in both that subject and the Language A, also receives a bilingual diploma. For a student whose school teaches a humanities or science subject in Arabic, that can deliver the same outcome without carrying two full Group 1 courses.

Both routes depend on grades rather than on registration alone, which is worth saying plainly. A student who registers for Arabic A and finishes with a 2 does not get a bilingual diploma and has spent two years on a seventh commitment. The honest question in Year 11 is therefore not whether the student would like a bilingual diploma but whether a 3 or better in Arabic A is a realistic target given their written fusha, and a marked piece of writing answers that better than a conversation.

Nothing about this requires tutoring, and no honest page should imply it does. What tutoring can do is give you the evidence for the decision before subject choices close, and then support whichever route the family picks.

sections.heading: Fusha, dialect and the register problem in a Dubai household
paragraphs: Arabic A is assessed in Modern Standard Arabic. Most students in Dubai speak a dialect at home - Gulf, Levantine, Egyptian, Iraqi, Sudanese, Maghrebi - and move between dialect and fusha without thinking about it. That bilingual facility is an asset in conversation and a liability in an examination script, because the dialect forms are invisible to the student. They do not feel like errors; they feel like Arabic.

The errors are predictable enough to drill. Verb conjugation patterns that have levelled in speech, case endings dropped in the spoken form, vocabulary that is ordinary in dialect and wrong in formal writing, and sentence structures that work aloud and read as speech on paper. A student who logs their own corrected errors for a month usually finds the same six or seven patterns repeating, and once they are named they stop appearing within a term.

This is also why fluency is a bad placement signal. A student who converses confidently in Arabic may write at a level that will not sustain Arabic A, and a quieter student who reads Arabic literature comfortably may be a strong candidate. The test that answers the question is a piece of timed written analysis in fusha, marked honestly. It takes one session and it prevents a two-year mistake.

A note on the mandatory Arabic lessons here, because the two subjects interact. KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Arabic as a first language, which means a student in that stream is already working in fusha for part of the week. A student in the non-Arab stream is not, and that difference shows up quickly in Arabic A written work. Knowing which stream a student has been in is one of the more useful pieces of background a tutor can have.

sections.heading: Choosing and obtaining works in Arabic
paragraphs: For a taught course the school chooses the works. For a self-taught Standard Level candidate the choice is made with the supervisor, and it is where a good decision saves a year of difficulty. Nine works at Standard Level, drawn with the required balance of works originally written in Arabic, works in translation, and a limited allowance of freely chosen titles, covering several literary forms, periods and regions.

Two practical filters are worth applying before any literary judgement. The first is obtainability in Dubai, in the edition the student will cite from: page references matter for close reading, and a student working from a different printing than their supervisor creates a steady low-level problem for two years. The older bookshops in Bur Dubai and Al Karama remain the best physical source for Arabic titles in the city. The second filter is length. A poetry collection and a long modern novel both count as one work and demand completely different amounts of evening reading.

Then the allocation rule applies, exactly as it does in every Language A: a work used for one assessment component cannot be used for another. The individual oral needs two works, one of which must be a work in translation and the other originally written in Arabic. Paper 2 needs two more. For a self-taught Standard Level candidate that is four of nine committed, and the decision should be taken in the autumn of Year 12 rather than discovered in the spring of Year 13.

On works in translation specifically, Arabic A students make the same mistake English A students make in reverse: they analyse the Arabic of a translated novel as though the author had chosen those words. Structure, narrative method, imagery and context all survive translation and are fully available for analysis. The translator's diction is not. Two short written exercises settle this permanently.

sections.heading: Arabic A and the KHDA mandatory subjects are two different things
paragraphs: This is the single most common confusion in Dubai, and it is worth separating completely. Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under requirements KHDA has set out and which schools were required to implement by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Arabic A is an IB Diploma subject the student chose. They share a language and nothing else.

The KHDA requirements are specific in ways that affect a student's week. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and for Social Studies for Arab students, while non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Instructional time is counted in 40-minute lesson units. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which is a real constraint on what any tutoring material for those lessons can look like - and a reason to be sceptical of anyone selling a bespoke curriculum for them.

One further credential point a parent can reasonably check: schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. That applies to the school's staff. It is not something IB Gram holds or could hold, and any tutoring service implying otherwise about itself is misrepresenting a specific regulatory permission.

sections.heading: Where Arabic sits in Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: Families frequently assume that strong Arabic helps with the Ministry of Education equivalency a UAE university application depends on. For the British track the published position is the opposite of that assumption. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

For the American track the published requirements are about English and mathematics rather than Arabic: English proficiency evidenced by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in SAT Mathematics before applying. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five, and getting that detail right matters more than anything else on this subject.

For the International Baccalaureate we will not publish a points threshold. We have not read one on the Ministry's own site, and an unsourced figure on a page like this would be repeated by families as fact. Ask the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation authority directly for the IB position, and treat any site that quotes a specific IB equivalency score without citing the Ministry with caution.

Two further points. Equivalency and attestation are processes the authorities run, not services IB Gram performs or guarantees, and nothing about tutoring is required for either. The sensible use of this information is planning: a student choosing subjects in Year 11 should know which of them will count towards equivalency, because Arabic A may be the right choice for a bilingual diploma while counting for nothing in that particular arithmetic.
