sections.heading: The Diploma language year counted backwards
paragraphs: Language subjects fail quietly because nothing is due until suddenly everything is. The external papers sit at the end of Year 13 in the May session that UAE schools use, and the internal oral sits months earlier in a window the school chooses. Working backwards from those two fixed points, rather than forwards from September, produces a plan that survives the term when three internal assessments arrive together. Get the school's own dates from the Diploma coordinator in the first fortnight of Year 12 and treat them as the calendar, because they are the ones that bind.

In Year 12 the work is accumulation. Themes are covered in the school's order, writing is produced in volume at task length, and the error log is built. Higher Level students should have started both literary works by the end of the year, which is the single most commonly missed milestone on this course: the oral depends on them, and a work read in the final term is not a work the student can discuss. Listening is the other Year 12 priority, because it improves slowly and cannot be crammed.

Year 13 reverses the emphasis. The oral window dominates the first half, and the weeks before it are worth protecting from everything else. Once the recording is done, attention moves to Paper 2, which carries half the grade and is the component most students have practised least, and to Paper 1 under timed conditions across the full range of text types. Mock results arrive mid-year and are the last useful diagnostic. The exam-session dates themselves are set by the IB and published by the school, so confirm them with the coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taking any figure from a tutoring website, including this one.
bullets: Get the school's oral recording window in the first fortnight of Year 12
Both Higher Level literary works started before the end of Year 12

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with Diploma work
paragraphs: IB academic honesty rules apply to every piece of assessed work a Diploma student submits, and the boundary matters most in the components a tutor is most likely to be asked to help with. The rule in practice is that the student's submitted work must be their own, and a tutor teaches, questions, models and gives feedback on what the student has produced. Feedback on a draft the student wrote is support. Supplying sentences that end up in the submission is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the tutor.

For the individual oral this means practice stimuli, recorded rehearsals and feedback on fluency and structure are all legitimate, while a script to memorise is not, and would in any case score badly against the interactive criterion. For an Extended Essay written in Arabic, a tutor can teach research method, discuss sources, question an argument and comment on a draft the student has written. For Paper 1 practice there is no honesty question at all, because the work is not submitted, which is why timed practice tasks are the safest and most productive thing to set.

This boundary is worth stating plainly because this market does not always observe it. One provider found in the Dubai search results sells finished Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach that triggers IB malpractice procedures against the student who submits it. A tutor who declines to supply text is not being unhelpful; they are the only kind of tutor worth paying for on an assessed component. Ask any prospective tutor what they will do with a draft, and listen for whether the answer involves giving feedback or handing something over.

process.title: Tell us the level, the school and the next deadline
process.description: Standard or Higher Level, the Dubai school, and the date of the next thing that matters: an oral window, a mock, a school report. Those three facts decide which tutor fits and how a term is planned. If the level is still under discussion with the school, say so, because the placement conversation is a different and more urgent one.

process.title: A free 45-minute trial with an unseen writing task
process.description: The trial lesson is free, lasts 45 minutes, and takes no card details. Most of it is diagnostic: an unseen Paper 1 task written under time, read back with the student, and mapped onto Criteria A, B and C. You get a written summary of what the marks are actually being lost on, whether or not you continue.

process.title: A term plan built backwards from the school's dates
process.description: We ask for the school's oral recording window and internal deadlines, then plan the term from those backwards. For Higher Level students that includes when each literary work has to be finished. The plan names text types and themes rather than hours, so progress is visible against something other than attendance.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marked work returned first
process.description: Tasks are set between lessons and marked against the criteria before the session that discusses them, with the criterion named on every comment. The error log travels with the student across the course, so the same orthography mistake is not diagnosed fresh in March that was diagnosed in October.

process.title: Change the tutor if the fit is wrong
process.description: A language tutor who does not suit a student is worse than none, because the hour becomes something to survive. Say so early and we rematch without argument or a fee. If no Arabic B specialist is free at the time you need, we say that rather than offering a general Arabic tutor and hoping.

whyPoints.title: The tutor is chosen for the subject guide, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Diploma Arabic B is a narrow specialism, and the number of people in any one Dubai community who can mark a Higher Level task against Criterion C is small. Online delivery means the match is made on who knows the course, which for a subject this specific is the difference between a useful hour and a conversation class.

whyPoints.title: Written work is marked before it is discussed
whyPoints.description: A task read for the first time during the lesson wastes the hour. Work is set between sessions and marked against the published criteria first, so the lesson starts from a diagnosis. Each comment names the criterion it relates to, which teaches the student to read the mark scheme rather than the mark.

whyPoints.title: Dialect treated as an asset, not an error
whyPoints.description: A student who speaks Emirati or Levantine Arabic at home has something valuable for the oral's interactive criterion. The job is to build the standard variety alongside it for the papers, not to treat the home language as a mistake. Students who understand the diglossia stop concluding they are bad at Arabic.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the components fluency does not help
whyPoints.description: Home fluency helps least with Paper 2 listening in Modern Standard Arabic and with formal written register. Saying so early sets a realistic timeline: listening improves slowly and cannot be crammed, which is why it starts in Year 12 rather than in the spring of Year 13.

whyPoints.title: Clear boundaries on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Teaching, questioning, modelling and feedback on the student's own drafts, with no text supplied for submission. The rule protects the student, since IB malpractice procedures fall on them. It is also the clearest way to separate a tutor from the providers in this market selling finished coursework.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that survives a Dubai term
whyPoints.description: Sessions are timed to Gulf Standard Time around school finish times, co-curricular fixtures and Ramadan hours, and can shift to post-Iftar slots when the calendar requires it. No travel sits between a 4pm and a 5pm booking, so siblings in different year groups can be taught back to back.

faqs.question: My child speaks Arabic at home but scores a 4 in Arabic B. How is that possible?
faqs.answer: Arabic is diglossic: the Arabic families speak is a dialect, and the Diploma assesses Modern Standard Arabic in formal writing. Fluency at home does not supply the written register, the orthography or the text-type conventions the papers reward. A student can understand everything in a Paper 2 recording and still lose Criterion A marks on hamza placement and dialect constructions in Paper 1. The gap is structural rather than a sign of weak Arabic, and it responds quickly to an error log plus explicit text-type teaching, because the underlying language is already there.

faqs.question: What exactly does Paper 1 ask an Arabic B student to produce?
faqs.answer: One piece of writing, chosen from three tasks that each tie to one of the five prescribed themes and each specify a text type. Standard Level candidates write 250 to 400 words and Higher Level candidates 450 to 600. It carries a quarter of the final grade and is marked on three criteria: Criterion A for language, Criterion B for message, and Criterion C for conceptual understanding. Criterion C is where most marks go missing, because students produce a competent essay when the task named a blog post, a formal letter or a set of guidelines.

faqs.question: How much of the Arabic B grade sits in the individual oral?
faqs.answer: A quarter. The oral is assessed internally by the school and externally moderated. At Standard Level it starts from a visual stimulus linked to one of the five themes; at Higher Level it starts from an extract from one of the two literary works studied on the course. Four criteria apply, covering language, the message in response to the stimulus, the message in the conversation, and interactive skills. Language and interactive skills together carry twice the weight of the two message criteria, so a candidate giving accurate one-sentence answers scores below one who talks fluently with some error.

faqs.question: Does my child really have to read two literary works for Arabic B Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Yes, at Higher Level only. Two works are studied in Arabic across the course, and the Higher Level individual oral is built on an extract from one of them. Standard Level has no literature requirement, which is the most practical difference between the two levels. The common failure is leaving the reading until the final term: an extract from a work the student skimmed three weeks earlier produces a thin presentation and a thinner discussion. Both works should be finished before the end of Year 12 for a student sitting the oral in Year 13.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with Paper 2 listening if the lessons are over video?
faqs.answer: Listening is one of the components online delivery suits best. Audio is shared directly rather than played across a room, so the sound quality is better than a classroom speaker, and the recording can be played twice as the paper requires and then replayed afterwards for analysis, which is the part that teaches. Note-taking technique is taught explicitly before the second hearing, and an error log by question type shows whether marks are being lost on detail, inference or speed. Weekly practice from early in Year 12 matters more than intensity later, because listening improves slowly.

faqs.question: Should a strong home speaker in Dubai be taking Arabic A instead of Arabic B?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it is worth asking the Diploma coordinator rather than the Arabic department, because the decision involves eligibility and timetabling as well as language. Arabic A is a Group 1 language and literature course that assesses literary and non-literary analysis in Arabic at academic register. A confident conversational speaker who reads Arabic slowly can struggle badly in it. A student who reads Arabic comfortably and finds Arabic B unchallenging is usually in the wrong course. Most Dubai schools set a deadline early in Year 12, after which a change means restarting a two-year course.

faqs.question: Is my child eligible for Arabic ab initio if their Arabic B marks are low?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Ab initio is restricted to genuine beginners with little or no previous exposure to the language, and a student who has carried KHDA's mandatory school Arabic through a Dubai education generally does not meet that description, however disappointing their marks look. Schools apply the restriction because the course is designed for a different starting point and its tasks are much shorter. Low Arabic B marks are normally a register and text-type problem rather than a placement problem, and they respond to the diagnosis described on this page faster than a course change would.

faqs.question: How does Dubai's mandatory school Arabic differ from Diploma Arabic B?
faqs.answer: They are separate requirements with separate content and separate reporting. KHDA requires Arabic in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and the content is set by the Ministry of Education. Diploma Arabic B is an IB course assessed against the IB subject guide. A tutor supporting school Arabic works on the skills the Ministry-set content demands, since using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited. A tutor supporting Arabic B works from the IB guide. Confusing the two wastes half an hour every week.

faqs.question: What does Arabic B tutoring cost in Dubai at market rates?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist, with premium examiner-led providers publishing up to AED 650. Those figures come from providers' own pages and from Bestimate's Dubai 2026 table, not from us. Format drives the number more than subject does, because travel time is working time somebody pays for.

faqs.question: Do you send an Arabic tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a language subject the trade is a favourable one: writing is annotated live on a shared screen, exam audio is played under proper conditions, and oral rehearsals are recorded and reviewed, which is difficult across a kitchen table. The real gain is the tutor pool, which is selected on knowledge of the subject guide rather than on driving distance.

faqs.question: How many Arabic B sessions a week does a Diploma student usually need?
faqs.answer: One hour a week across Year 12 is the common pattern, rising to two in the term containing the individual oral and again in the weeks before the papers. More than two hours weekly rarely helps on a language subject, because the limiting factor is independent reading and listening volume rather than contact time. What changes outcomes is consistency: a task written and marked every fortnight for a year beats an intensive block in the spring, since orthography and register respond to repeated correction rather than to concentrated instruction.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools do your Arabic B students come from?
faqs.answer: Mostly the emirate's IB Diploma schools, including Dubai International Academy at Emirates Hills and Al Barsha, GEMS World Academy Dubai, Dubai American Academy, Deira International School, Uptown International School, Raffles World Academy and Emirates International School Jumeirah. Students also come from British-curriculum schools that transfer into a Diploma school for Years 12 and 13. Schools are named as market context only, with no affiliation or endorsement implied. What a tutor needs from a school is its internal calendar: the oral recording window and the mock dates drive the whole plan.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on an Extended Essay written in Arabic?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the boundaries IB academic honesty sets. A tutor can teach research method, discuss sources, question an argument, explain what the assessment criteria reward, and give feedback on drafts the student has produced. What a tutor must not do is supply text that ends up in the submission, because malpractice procedures fall on the student. A Group 2 Extended Essay in Arabic is a demanding choice and a genuinely distinctive one on a university application, and it works best when the research question is narrowed early with help and written entirely by the student.

faqs.question: Can Arabic B sessions move during Ramadan or exam leave?
faqs.answer: Yes. Session times shift to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan when families prefer that, and reduced school hours during the month usually free earlier afternoon slots as well. Exam leave, study leave and school trips are planned around rather than paid for, and a term plan is agreed against the school's own calendar rather than a fixed weekly grid. The one period we ask families to protect is the fortnight before the school's internal oral recording window, because that is the component with a fixed date and the least room to recover.

faqs.question: What happens if no Arabic B specialist is free at the time we want?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than offering a general Arabic tutor and hoping it works out. Diploma Arabic B at Higher Level in particular is a narrow specialism, and the honest options are a different time slot, a short wait for a specialist to free up, or a fortnightly rhythm with written work marked between sessions. What we will not do is put a conversational Arabic tutor in front of a Higher Level student with a literary extract oral in six weeks, because that hour helps nobody and the family finds out too late.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-online-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step on Arabic B is not a schedule, it is finding out which of the three common problems you have. Send the level, the Dubai school and the date of the next thing that matters, and the free 45-minute trial will put an unseen Paper 1 task in front of your child, mark it against Criteria A, B and C, and tell you in writing what the marks are being lost on. No card details are taken for the trial. If the answer is that your child is in the wrong Arabic course, we will say that too, because it is more useful than a term of lessons.

intro.heading: The question Dubai parents actually ask first, answered in AED
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring pages for this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars - a currency no UAE family transacts in. One of them asks the price question in its own list of frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it. That is the state of the market, and it is why this page leads with numbers rather than with an argument about quality.

On published figures, Arabic B tuition in Dubai runs from about AED 45 an hour at the bottom of the online market to AED 650 at the examiner-tier top. The band that matters for a Diploma candidate is narrower: roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IB specialist. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is published at AED 180 to AED 500, and the difference is travel, not teaching. Those are market rates gathered from providers' own pages and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, not IB Gram's price list.

What a parent needs beyond the band is which variables move a quote, because that is where the money is actually decided. Level moves it: Arabic B HL carries two literary works that have to be prepared outside the session. Component moves it: individual oral rehearsal with playback takes more tutor time per hour of lesson than marking a written task. Lead time moves it most of all: the same eight sessions booked in September cost less per hour than booked in March, because in March the only available specialists are the ones already carrying a full Year 13 load.

There is a second reason cost sits at the front of an Arabic B page specifically. Arabic B is one of the cheapest Diploma subjects to fix, because the three things that usually hold a Dubai student back - dialect interference in written Modern Standard Arabic, untrained listening, and no practice with the prescribed text types - all respond to a small number of well-targeted sessions. Families routinely spend more than they need to, over a longer period, because nobody diagnosed which of the three was the problem before the invoicing started.

IB Gram delivers Arabic B as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around a Dubai school day. We do not offer home visits in the UAE - sending a tutor to an address is a service we run only in India - and that is also a pricing fact: you are not paying for a car crossing Sheikh Zayed Road at 17:00 in either direction. Our own figure is quoted after the free trial lesson, when the level, the component and the session length are known, rather than advertised as a band that moves at checkout.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-tutor.programmesIntro: Arabic B appears in more than one IB programme, and the cost of support differs sharply between them because the assessment load does. These are the programmes Dubai schools run and what each one typically costs a family in tutoring hours rather than in fees.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Arabic B sits in Group 2 as a language-acquisition course, taken at SL or HL. Three assessed components: a written task, listening and reading comprehension, and an individual oral. HL adds two literary works in Arabic. For costing purposes the Diploma is the expensive end, because the components are externally assessed and the oral is moderated, so preparation is not optional.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma families typically buy Arabic B support in one of two shapes: a weekly session across Year 13, which at published specialist rates is a substantial two-term commitment, or a block of six to eight sessions aimed at one component. The second shape is cheaper and, where the problem has been diagnosed properly, often just as effective.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Arabic acquisition in the Middle Years Programme is assessed in phases against four criteria, internally, with no external paper. That changes the economics: there is no exam to prepare for, so support is about building the register and the reading habit that the Diploma will later assess. Rates for MYP work sit lower than Diploma rates across the market because the specialism required is narrower.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest Arabic B intervention available to a Dubai family is also the earliest one. An hour a week in Year 10, building Modern Standard Arabic reading and writing, costs less per hour than Year 13 crisis support and removes the need for most of it. Very few families buy it, because nothing has gone wrong yet.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Where Arabic B is taken as one of the Diploma courses inside the Career-related Programme, the student sits the same components and is marked on the same scale, so the preparation cost is the same. The surrounding load differs, with a reflective project in place of some written coursework, which usually leaves more weekday time available for language work.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of Dubai schools are authorised to run the Career-related Programme, so a CP student is often the only one in their year taking Arabic B on that route. School revision groups are timetabled for the Diploma cohort, which pushes these students towards paid one-to-one support earlier than their classmates.

paragraphs: The band is AED 45 to AED 650 an hour across the whole Dubai market, and quoting that range is almost useless, so here is the narrower version. An IB or IGCSE specialist is published at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. A named or examiner-tier tutor reaches AED 500 to AED 650. Monthly packages are also published in this market: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. sections.heading: The six variables that move an Arabic B quote in Dubai
paragraphs: An hourly band is a starting point, not a quote. Six things decide where inside the band a particular family lands, and five of the six are under the family's control. Knowing which ones matter turns a negotiation about price into a conversation about scope, which is the only version of that conversation worth having.

Level is the first. Arabic B HL carries two literary works that the tutor must also have read and prepared, which is unpaid time that gets priced into the hourly rate. Component is the second: marking a written task takes a tutor twenty minutes outside the session, while oral rehearsal with playback and examiner-style questioning takes closer to an hour. Lead time is the third and the largest. The same block of eight sessions booked in September and booked in March are different products, because in March the available specialists are the ones with a full Year 13 timetable already.

The remaining three are session length, delivery format and frequency. Ninety-minute sessions usually carry a lower effective hourly rate than sixty-minute ones because the preparation overhead is spread further. Format decides whether travel is in the price at all. And frequency cuts both ways: weekly work gives the tutor continuity and justifies a tighter rate, while sporadic one-off sessions cost more per hour because each one needs re-diagnosing.

The variable nobody lists is who is doing the quoting. A marketplace adds a platform margin to the tutor's own figure, an agency adds account management, and a freelancer quotes net but may not hold the permit the law requires. The same teacher can appear at three different prices in the same week depending on which route you reach them through, and none of those three prices tells you anything about their Arabic B experience. Ask for the component history first and the number second. The table below sets out the direction and the rough size of each effect so a quote can be interrogated rather than accepted.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or a tuition centre: the Dubai comparison
paragraphs: Parents searching for Arabic B help in Dubai are choosing between four delivery models, and the published price differences between them are mostly about logistics rather than teaching. An in-home visit prices two journeys. A tuition centre prices premises and prices a group. An independent freelancer prices whatever the local market will bear and may or may not hold the permit the law requires. Online one-to-one prices teaching time and preparation and nothing else.

The quality question runs on a separate axis from the price question, which is why a straight comparison of hourly figures misleads. A group class at AED 90 per student per hour is cheap and will not fix a conceptual-understanding problem, because the tutor cannot mark six students' written tasks against criteria inside one lesson. A premium in-home rate on Palm Jumeirah is not buying more expertise than the same tutor would bring to a video call; it is buying the drive. The useful comparison is cost per unit of marked, criterion-referenced work produced.

IB Gram offers one model: one-to-one lessons over live video. We make no home visits in the UAE and we hold no UAE premises, so the comparison below is between what the Dubai market charges for each model rather than between products we sell. Where a family genuinely needs a tutor physically present - a young child, a specific access need - an online platform is the wrong choice and we will say so rather than take the booking.

sections.heading: Why Arabic B is cheaper to fix than most Diploma subjects
paragraphs: Arabic B grades in Dubai are usually held down by three specific, diagnosable things, and all three respond to a small number of sessions. That is unusual. A Physics HL problem can be spread across eight topics and a year of missing foundations; an Arabic B problem is almost always one of three, which means the correct intervention is a block of six to eight sessions rather than a standing weekly commitment running to the end of Year 13.

The first is dialect interference in written Modern Standard Arabic. A Dubai student who speaks Gulf, Egyptian or Levantine dialect at home will carry dialect vocabulary and syntax into written responses under time pressure, and lose marks on the language criterion for things that are mechanical rather than conceptual. Timed writing, marked for register and returned with the pattern named, closes this in six to eight weeks. The second is listening. It is a trained skill, it is worth a substantial share of the grade, and almost no Dubai school timetables practice for it because there is no neat homework to set. Twice-weekly recorded practice over two months moves it.

The third is the prescribed text types. The written task names a text type - a blog, a formal letter, a speech, a set of guidelines - and its conventions carry marks under the conceptual-understanding criterion. Students who have never written a formal letter in Arabic lose those marks every time. This is the cheapest fix of the three: a session per text type, drilled in pairs on identical content, and the problem is gone. Families who buy a year of general Arabic conversation instead typically spend several times as much for less movement.

sections.heading: What the components cost in preparation hours
paragraphs: Arabic B has three assessed components: a written task from a choice of prompts, listening and reading comprehension, and an individual oral that is recorded and moderated. HL adds two literary works in Arabic which supply the material for the HL oral. Converting those components into hours is the piece of arithmetic no competitor page does, and it is the only way to turn an hourly rate into a budget.

The numbers below are typical preparation requirements for a Dubai student starting from a mid-band position, not a promise about any individual. A student further behind needs more; a student with a single narrow gap needs far less. What they show is the shape of the spend: the oral is the most expensive component per mark available, listening is the most expensive in elapsed weeks, and the written task is the cheapest to improve. A family with limited budget and a broad problem should spend it on text types and listening, in that order.

Confirm every weighting with your child's Diploma coordinator before planning around it, because the IB revises course structures on a cycle and schools set internal deadlines months ahead of external ones. The budgeting logic holds regardless: price the component, not the subject, and ask any tutor to tell you how many hours they think a component needs before you agree a rate.

One arithmetic point is worth doing out loud, because families rarely do it. Twelve hours of listening work at the mid band is a four-figure sum in AED, and it buys a component worth a substantial share of the final grade. Four hours of text-type drill at the same rate is a far smaller sum and often buys more movement, because the conceptual-understanding marks were being dropped wholesale rather than partially. Ordering the spend by marks-per-dirham rather than by what feels most urgent is the difference between a budget that works and one that runs out in April with the oral still unrehearsed.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: Dubai fees and the 2026-27 freeze
paragraphs: A tutoring invoice looks different next to a Dubai school fee bill. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are flat this year. Tutoring rates are not covered by that decision and have not behaved as though they were.

Scale matters too. Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with IB programmes accounting for roughly a fourteenth of enrolment. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by six per cent. More IB places means more Arabic B candidates competing for the same small pool of specialists, which is a supply pressure on rates rather than a quality one.

The practical conclusion for a Dubai family is that tutoring is the variable line in an education budget and the school fee is the fixed one. A single weekly specialist hour across two Diploma terms is a meaningful sum. Six targeted sessions after a proper diagnosis is a fraction of it.

There is one more item families forget to budget for, and it is not tutoring. A student sitting any component as a private candidate, or re-sitting in a later session, pays entry fees to the school or centre administering the examination, and those are set by the centre rather than by the board. Ask your school's examinations officer for the figure early, because it lands in the same term as the heaviest tutoring months and it is the expense that most often arrives unannounced. sections.heading: Packages, cancellations and the extras that catch Dubai parents
paragraphs: Most of the money lost in this market is not lost on the hourly rate. It is lost on terms. A monthly package of eight sessions is good value if eight sessions are used and poor value if four are, and Dubai families lose sessions constantly to school trips, travel, sport fixtures and exam weeks. Before agreeing a package, ask what happens to an unused session, how much notice a cancellation needs, and whether credit expires.

The second extra is marking. Some providers price the lesson and treat written marking as additional, which matters enormously in a language subject where the marked task is the product. Ask directly whether criterion-referenced marking of written work is inside the hourly rate or outside it, and get the answer before the first invoice. The third is level changes: a student moving from SL to HL mid-course changes the tutor's preparation load, and some providers reprice at that point.

A fourth is tax treatment, and the only honest position is a narrow one. We will not state how UAE value added tax applies to tuition fees in general, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation we do not have. What any provider can and should tell you is whether the AED figure they quoted you is inclusive or exclusive of VAT, and whether they hold a tax registration number. Ask that question of every quote you receive, including ours.

A fifth extra is the data you hand over to get a quote. A tutoring enquiry form that asks for a child's school, year group, recent grades and sometimes a photograph is collecting personal data about a minor, and under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection you are entitled to know what is collected, why, and how to have it deleted. Before filling in a form on any provider's site, including this one, look for the privacy link and check that the purpose is stated. A provider who cannot tell you how to delete your child's record is a provider to be cautious of on more than price.

sections.heading: Who may legally charge for private tuition in the UAE
paragraphs: Price and legality are connected in this market, because the cheapest quotes often come from people who are not permitted to charge at all. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and it is applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system under the service name 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time.

Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source and should not be relied on.

Two further points. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school - treat that as press-reported and verify against the current ADEK policy before relying on it. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no such permit and does not describe itself as having one, because it operates no UAE premises.

sections.heading: When paying for an Arabic B tutor is not the answer
paragraphs: The cheapest advice on this page is the advice to not spend. Several Arabic B situations in Dubai do not need paid support, and a provider who takes the booking anyway is selling something the family did not need. Saying so is more useful than another paragraph about quality, and it is the part of the conversation that distinguishes a service from a sales funnel.

If the school already runs a weekly Arabic B clinic and your child has not attended it, attend it first; it is included in fees you have already paid. If the problem is that the student has not read the two HL literary works, the fix is a reading schedule, not an hourly rate, and a parent can set one. If a single mock mark triggered the search, wait for the criterion breakdown before buying anything, because the language criterion and the conceptual-understanding criterion need completely different work. And if the student is in Arabic B when they should be in Arabic ab initio or Arabic A, no number of sessions corrects a placement error.

There is also a case where paid support is right and more of it is wrong. A student with one diagnosed gap needs a block of six, not a standing weekly commitment to July. The default commercial shape in this market is the open-ended weekly booking, because it is predictable revenue. The shape that serves the student is a diagnosis, a block, a review against marked scripts, and an honest decision about whether to continue. No tutor can promise a particular grade, and a provider who does is telling you something about their claims rather than about their teaching.

process.description: HL or SL, which of the written task, listening, reading or the oral is the concern, and the most recent mark with the criterion breakdown if the school gave one. With those three things a specialist can be matched without a paid diagnostic session, which is where families most often lose money first.

process.description: Each shows the components the tutor has taught most, the levels they take and their hours in Gulf Standard Time. You choose. We would rather tell you nobody suitable is free in your slot than put a general Arabic teacher in front of a Diploma component.

process.description: Forty-five minutes, one per family, no card details taken. The tutor sets a timed written task or runs a listening set, so the session produces evidence rather than impressions. You get a written note naming which of the three usual problems your child has.

process.description: Our rate is quoted after the trial, with the session length, what marking is included, the cancellation notice and whether the figure is inclusive of VAT all stated at the same time. An hourly number without those four things is not a price.

process.title: Review against marked scripts at session six
process.description: Six sessions is enough to see whether dialect interference has dropped or listening scores have moved. If they have not, the plan changes or the tutor does. We look at marked work rather than at reported confidence, because in a language subject the two often disagree.

whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names the provider page or rate table it came from, with the month it was read. Three of the most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which no UAE family transacts in.

whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, so you are not funding two journeys across Dubai per session. IB Gram makes no UAE home visits - that is a service we run only in India - and the published in-home band shows what that difference is worth.

whyPoints.title: Priced by component, not by subject
whyPoints.description: The written task, listening and the oral need different numbers of hours, and we will tell you which before you buy any. The default weekly open-ended booking is good for a provider's revenue and usually more than an Arabic B student needs.

whyPoints.description: If the school clinic covers it, if a reading schedule fixes it, or if the student is in the wrong course, we say so. A block of six after a real diagnosis beats a year of weekly sessions, and it is the recommendation that costs us the most to make.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay per hour for an IB Arabic B tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: On published market figures, a qualified subject tutor working online runs about AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and an IB specialist AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Below that, AED 45 to AED 150 buys a university-student tutor who will practise conversation but usually cannot mark against the Arabic B criteria. Above it, AED 500 to AED 650 reaches examiner-tier pricing that an Arabic B candidate seldom needs. In-home visits in Dubai are published at AED 180 to AED 500 because travel is priced in. Those are market rates, not ours.

faqs.question: Why does Arabic B HL cost more per hour than SL?
faqs.answer: Because HL adds two literary works in Arabic that the tutor also has to read, prepare and be able to discuss at extract level, and that preparation sits outside the paid session. The HL individual oral starts from an extract from one of those works rather than from a visual stimulus, so a tutor cannot improvise it. Across this market the HL premium is real and visible in published bands. If HL was chosen for prestige rather than for workload fit, the cheaper decision is often to revisit the level with the Diploma coordinator.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book a block of sessions or pay weekly for Arabic B?
faqs.answer: A block is usually cheaper in total and a weekly booking is usually cheaper per hour, which is why providers prefer the second. For Arabic B specifically, a block after a proper diagnosis tends to win, because the three things that hold Dubai students back each respond in six to eight sessions. The open-ended weekly commitment is the right shape only when a student is behind across all three components. Ask any provider how many hours they think the diagnosed problem needs before agreeing to a recurring charge.

faqs.question: Does the published hourly rate include marking my child's written work?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the provider, and in a language subject this is the question that decides value. The marked written task is the product: a response returned with criterion letters and marks attached is what shows a student whether they are losing marks on language or on conceptual understanding. Some providers treat marking as additional to the lesson rate. Ask directly, get the answer before the first invoice, and treat an hourly figure quoted without a marking position as incomplete rather than competitive.

faqs.question: Does the price of Arabic B tutoring in Dubai include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask every provider that question specifically, including us. We will not state how UAE value added tax applies to tuition fees as a general matter, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation we do not hold, and a tutoring page is the wrong place to interpret tax law. What a provider can tell you is whether the AED figure they quoted is inclusive or exclusive of VAT and whether they hold a tax registration number. A quote that does not say is a quote that may change.

faqs.question: Will rates go up if I book Arabic B support close to the exams?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, and lead time is the single largest variable in this market. Booked in September, a block of eight sessions draws on specialists with open timetables. Booked in March, the only tutors with capacity are those already carrying a full Year 13 load, and the effective rate reflects that scarcity. The cheapest Arabic B support a Dubai family can buy is bought before anything has gone wrong, and the most expensive is bought six weeks out. That ordering has nothing to do with any individual provider's price list.

faqs.question: Is a cheap Arabic conversation tutor enough for the Diploma course?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and this is where Dubai families most often spend money without result. Arabic B marks are lost on the conceptual-understanding criterion - text type, audience, register - and on trained listening. A conversation tutor at the bottom of the rate band has rarely read the criteria and cannot mark against them, so the sessions feel productive and the grade does not move. Conversation practice has a place in building fluency. It is not a substitute for criterion-referenced marking of the written task.

faqs.question: How many tutored hours does Arabic B usually need in total?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the student starts, and the honest ranges are wide. One diagnosed gap - text types, say - needs four to six hours. Listening alone needs eight to twelve hours spread over six to eight weeks because it cannot be compressed. A student weak across all three components from a low base needs something closer to twenty-five to forty hours across two or three terms. HL oral preparation adds eight to ten on top, spread across Year 12 and Year 13. Price the component, not the subject.

faqs.question: Why would online Arabic B tuition cost less than a tutor coming to our villa?
faqs.answer: Because an in-home visit prices two journeys, and in Dubai those journeys are long. A round trip to Arabian Ranches, Dubailand or Palm Jumeirah at 17:00 can exceed ninety minutes, and the published in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 reflects it. The teaching is the same teaching. IB Gram delivers one-to-one lessons over live video and makes no home visits in the UAE, so no part of what you pay is a car on Sheikh Zayed Road. Where a child genuinely needs someone in the room, online is the wrong choice.

faqs.question: Are tuition centres in Dubai better value than one-to-one for Arabic B?
faqs.answer: A centre group class costs less per student per hour and produces far less marked individual work, because a tutor cannot mark four or six students' written tasks against criteria inside one lesson. For content revision across the five themes a group can work. For diagnosing which criterion is leaking marks, or rehearsing a moderated individual oral, it cannot. The comparison worth making is cost per piece of criterion-referenced marked work rather than cost per hour of attendance, and on that measure the ranking frequently reverses.

faqs.question: What should I ask a Dubai tutor about the MoHRE permit before paying them?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold a private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and ask to see the reference. It is granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system, so there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you read online as unverified. School staff should also confirm their employer's position.

faqs.question: How do Dubai school fees and the 2026-27 freeze affect what I should budget for tutoring?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. That decision covers school fees, not tutoring rates, which are set by providers and have not followed it. For a household budget the useful framing is that the school fee is fixed and the tutoring line is the variable one. Six targeted sessions after a diagnosis costs a fraction of a weekly specialist commitment across two Diploma terms.

faqs.question: Can we cancel or pause Arabic B sessions during school trips and exam weeks?
faqs.answer: Ask before you commit, because this is where package money actually disappears. Dubai Diploma students lose sessions to residential trips, travel, sport fixtures and internal exam weeks, and an eight-session monthly package is poor value if four sessions are used. Get the notice period, the treatment of an unused session and the expiry date on any credit in writing at the point of booking. Most reasonable providers allow a pause with notice; the detail to check is whether paused credit expires at the end of the month or carries forward.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for Arabic B support in Year 11, before the Diploma starts?
faqs.answer: It is the lowest-cost route to the same end grade and almost nobody buys it. A fortnightly session in Year 11 or early Year 12, building Modern Standard Arabic reading and formal writing, costs less per hour than Year 13 specialist support and removes most of the need for it. The reason families do not is that nothing has gone wrong yet, so there is no trigger. If you are reading this page in Year 11 rather than in Year 13, the cheapest decision available to you is to start small now.

faqs.question: What happens if we cannot afford specialist Arabic B rates at all?
faqs.answer: Several things worth doing cost nothing. Use the school's own Arabic clinic if it runs one; it is inside fees already paid. Set a reading schedule for the HL literary works yourself, with dates, because the schedule rather than the tutor is what prevents the Year 13 problem. Get the criterion breakdown from the last mock so that any hours you do buy are aimed correctly. Then, if you buy anything, buy one text-type session and one listening diagnostic rather than a month of general conversation.

The trial lesson is free, one per family, with no card details taken, and it produces a timed piece of work rather than an impression. After it you get our figure with the session length, the marking position, the cancellation notice and the VAT position stated together. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with no travel priced into anything.

intro.heading: Higher Level Biology is a volume problem, and volume has a price
paragraphs: Ask a Dubai Diploma student which of their Higher Levels is hardest and Biology is rarely the answer. Ask which one they are most behind on and it often is. That gap is the whole story of this subject. Higher Level Biology is not conceptually brutal in the way that Higher Level Physics fields or Higher Level Chemistry thermodynamics can be. It is simply very large: 240 taught hours against 150 at Standard Level, organised into four themes, each examined across four levels of biological organisation from molecules up to ecosystems. A student who falls four weeks behind in Biology has not misunderstood something, they have missed content, and missed content does not come back on its own.

That changes what you are buying and therefore how to price it. In a conceptually difficult subject, the valuable hour is the one that makes an idea click, and three such hours can transform a grade. In a volume-heavy subject, the valuable hour is the one that compresses a theme into a usable structure and then tests whether it stuck. Those hours are not interchangeable, and a tutor who treats Biology like Physics will spend your money explaining things your child already follows.

So this page prices Biology by theme block rather than by hour. A theme block is the set of sessions needed to take one theme from patchy to examinable: a structuring session, two or three teaching sessions on the parts that are genuinely missing, and a marked-paper session to test it. At the published Dubai market band for an IB specialist of roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour, that is a knowable number per theme, and four themes is a knowable number for the course. The table further down sets it out so you can plan the whole two years instead of agreeing to a monthly figure and hoping.

The second thing that decides a Biology grade is not content at all. It is command terms. Biology examinations ask students to state, outline, describe, explain, distinguish, compare and contrast, suggest, deduce and evaluate, and each of those words has a defined expectation attached to it. A student who writes a beautiful paragraph of description in answer to an explain question loses marks while knowing the biology perfectly. Dubai students lose more marks to that single habit than to any gap in the syllabus, and it is the cheapest thing on this page to fix.

One point of honesty before the detail. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the Emirates, and no tutor from this platform will arrive at a UAE address; that service exists only in India. Biology here is taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with diagrams built on a shared whiteboard and saved for revision. For a subject where a student will need to revisit the same pathway diagram in October, February and May, a saved annotated file is worth more than a verbal explanation they will not recall.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-hl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Biology at Higher Level is a Diploma subject, and how many theme blocks a student needs depends almost entirely on what they studied before. The three stages below set the starting position.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Biology at Higher Level spans four themes across 240 taught hours, examined by two written papers and one internally marked scientific investigation. Of the three common Higher Level sciences it carries the largest volume of discrete content, which makes it the one most vulnerable to a term of absence, illness or a mid-year move.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Higher Level Biology is taken disproportionately by students targeting medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and biomedical courses, which raises the stakes on a grade and lowers the family's appetite for watching a 5 sit there for two terms. Dubai schools run August to June, so by the February of DP2 a Higher Level Biology student is carrying four themes of accumulated content and revising while new material is still being taught.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria, integrated sciences, no timed papers. Students arrive at Higher Level Biology able to design and evaluate an investigation, which is real preparation for the Diploma scientific investigation, and without experience of writing to a command term under time pressure. For a volume-heavy subject they also arrive without a note-taking system capable of handling four themes.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai school runs MYP straight into the Diploma, the Higher Level Biology class often contains both ex-MYP and ex-IGCSE students. The ex-MYP student's gap is not biological knowledge but information management, and the first useful session for them is structural: how to compress a theme into something retrievable, which is a transferable skill worth buying once.

programmes.name: IGCSE and the British route
programmes.description: Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE Biology, or Combined Science, to Year 11. Separate IGCSE Biology at grade 7 or above gives a genuinely strong Higher Level start, because much of the organism-level content is familiar in outline. Combined Science is the harder start, and the specific missing pieces tend to be molecular: enzyme kinetics, membrane transport detail and the genetics beyond simple inheritance.
programmes.countryNote: Because British-curriculum schools carry the largest share of Dubai enrolment, most of the emirate's Higher Level Biology cohort arrives via IGCSE. The useful diagnostic is to look at which IGCSE paper the marks were lost on rather than at the grade: a student strong on recall questions and weak on the longer structured answers has a command-term habit that will cost them far more in the Diploma than it did at 16.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-hl-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Few Dubai households buy Biology support alone. These are the subjects it most often sits beside, with what each one actually assesses, so you can judge where the money should go first.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Four themes across 240 taught hours: unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change, each examined at molecular, cellular, organism and ecosystem level, with Higher Level extensions throughout. Two written papers plus the scientific investigation.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The same four themes at 150 taught hours without the Higher Level extensions. A smaller volume rather than an easier subject, and a legitimate destination for a student whose Higher Level grade is not holding and whose intended courses do not require the higher level.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity strands, from the particulate model through to reaction mechanisms. The standard pairing for medicine applicants in Dubai. Shares the investigation format with Biology, so statistical and data-handling coaching applies to both internal assessments at once.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-weighted and modelling-led. Unusually relevant to Biology, because the scientific investigation expects real statistical treatment: means, standard deviation, error bars, and a correctly chosen significance test. A student fluent here needs far less investigation support.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus, functions and algebra. Less directly useful to Biology than Applications, with one exception: students who take it often handle rate and gradient questions in the data-based section more confidently, which shows up in Paper 1B.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics through to nuclear and quantum physics. Overlaps Biology at membrane potentials, gas exchange and thermoregulation more than students expect. Mentioned mainly because a student carrying Biology, Chemistry and Physics at Higher Level has a volume problem no amount of tutoring resolves.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Anatomy, physiology, energy systems, nutrition and training. Substantial overlap with Biology at the organism level, so content learned for one reinforces the other. A sensible second science for Dubai students who want physiology without a second laboratory-heavy course.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Ecosystems, biodiversity, pollution and resource management, counting for either the sciences or the individuals and societies group. The ecosystem-level content overlaps the interaction and interdependence theme in Biology directly, which makes the pairing efficient to revise.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, with research methods and ethics. The biological approach draws on the same neurophysiology as parts of Biology, and the research-methods training transfers usefully to the Biology investigation's design and sampling decisions.

sections.heading: The four themes, and where 240 taught hours actually go
paragraphs: The current Biology guide organises the course into four themes, each examined across four levels of biological organisation: molecules, cells, organisms and ecosystems. Higher Level adds extension content inside every theme rather than bolting on a separate unit, which is why Higher Level Biology feels less like a harder course than like the same course at greater density. Confirm the structure against the subject guide your child's school is teaching, because schools moved onto the current guides at different times, and a small number of Dubai cohorts sat transitional arrangements on the way through.

The table below maps the themes against the support they typically need. Two patterns show up consistently in Dubai. Continuity and change absorbs the most hours, because it carries the genetics, inheritance and evolution material where a single missing idea blocks everything after it. Interaction and interdependence absorbs fewer teaching hours but more marked-paper hours, because the ecology content is examined through data interpretation more than through recall, and students who have learned it can still answer badly.

Reading the table as a two-year plan is the point. Four theme blocks across DP1 and DP2, placed where the school is teaching each theme rather than months later, is a forecastable commitment: you know roughly how many sessions and roughly what they cost before you begin. That is a different proposition from a monthly retainer, which charges the same in a quiet August as in a frantic February and gives you no way to tell whether you are getting value.

sections.heading: Command terms: where Biology marks are actually decided
paragraphs: A Dubai parent looking at a Biology script that scored 5 usually sees correct biology and cannot work out where the marks went. They went to the command term. Biology examinations use a defined vocabulary of instructions, each carrying a specific expectation about what the answer must contain, and the mark scheme is written against that expectation rather than against general knowledge of the topic.

The failure is almost always in the same direction. Asked to explain, students describe. Description says what happens; explanation says why it happens, by what mechanism, with the causal link made explicit. Asked to distinguish, students write two separate paragraphs rather than a comparison with the point of difference named. Asked to suggest, students state a textbook fact instead of applying principles to an unfamiliar scenario, which is exactly what the term is testing. Asked to evaluate, they list advantages and stop before the judgement the term requires.

This is the cheapest fix available on a Higher Level Biology course and it is routinely overlooked because it does not feel like learning biology. Two or three sessions working through a student's own marked answers, identifying each command term, and rewriting the answer to meet it will usually move more marks than a month of content revision. It also transfers: the same discipline improves Chemistry and Physics extended responses and any essay subject on the timetable. If your child's marked papers show knowledge without marks, start here before buying anything else.

sections.heading: A memory-heavy subject and the case for a record you keep
paragraphs: In-home tuition is sold widely in Dubai and the figures are published: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, independent home tutors quote up to AED 500, and in-home monthly blocks of four two-hour sessions appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799. The premium over an online specialist band of AED 150 to 300 buys physical presence, and for a younger child that presence is worth paying for. For Higher Level Biology specifically, there is an argument the other way that has nothing to do with price.

Biology is revisited more than any other Diploma science. A student will meet the same protein synthesis sequence in DP1, again when the theme is revised, again before mocks and again in May. What they need is not a brilliant explanation once but a retrievable version of that explanation four times. A diagram built on a shared whiteboard, annotated during the session and saved, is exactly that. The same diagram drawn on paper at a kitchen table survives only as well as the notebook does, and in a two-year course with four themes, notebooks do not survive well.

The second argument is spacing. Retention in a volume subject depends on returning to material after it has partly faded, which means short sessions distributed across months rather than long sessions concentrated in a term. That pattern is only affordable when nobody is driving: a thirty-minute retrieval check is a sensible purchase over video and an absurd one if it involves a cross-city round trip. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE and does not send tutors to Dubai addresses; home visits are part of our India service only. If presence in the room is the requirement, a local in-home tutor is the right purchase and this is not the right page.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: sampling, statistics and the honesty line
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the Higher Level Biology grade comes from one piece of individual research marked by the school. Biology investigations fail differently from chemistry ones. The chemistry problem is usually a trivial research question; the biology problem is usually a design that cannot support statistical treatment: too few replicates, a sample chosen for convenience, an independent variable with three values where five were needed, or data that is obviously confounded by something nobody controlled.

That makes the first session the valuable one, and it is a statistics conversation as much as a biology one. How many replicates will make a mean meaningful. Whether the variation in the system is small enough for the planned sample size to detect an effect. Which significance test suits the data the student will actually get, and what the criteria expect to see: means with standard deviation, error bars that are explained rather than decorative, and a conclusion that respects the spread rather than reading a trend into noise. Students who get this right in week one write a strong report almost regardless of what the data shows.

Where the line sits is not negotiable. A tutor explains the criteria, pressure-tests the design, teaches the statistics, and reads a draft to say where the evaluation is thin or the conclusion has run past the evidence. A tutor does not supply sentences, rewrite paragraphs into better English, or hand over a method to copy. The report must be the student's own work in their own words, and the data must be theirs. Providers in this market sell finished reports at around AED 3,750; that is an academic-integrity breach and the consequence falls on the student's Diploma, not on the seller.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why a Dubai parent should know
paragraphs: Families move between emirates more than they expect, and the rules change when they do. Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That is the complete map, and it is worth noting that the Abu Dhabi regulator is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this market and Sharjah's by one.

The distinctions matter practically. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval sits with the emirate rather than only inspection. In Dubai, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai is also adding seven private schools for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 places.

Across all emirates one federal rule holds: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA requires those mandatory subjects in every private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For a Higher Level Biology family, the practical effect is simply that the school day is fuller than the curriculum brochure suggests, which is a scheduling fact worth planning around.

sections.heading: Ten weeks left and four themes to revise
paragraphs: This is the most common Higher Level Biology enquiry in Dubai, and it usually arrives in February. The student is in DP2, the four themes are all partly known and none is secure, mocks have come back in the fours and fives, and the family wants to know what is realistically achievable. The honest answer is that quite a lot is, but not by covering everything.

Ten weeks at one session a week is ten sessions. Spent trying to re-teach four themes, that is two and a half sessions per theme, which is enough to re-read content and not enough to secure it. Spent properly, the same ten sessions look different: one on command terms, because the fastest marks available are the ones the student is losing while knowing the answer. Then marked papers, every session, with the errors logged and sorted into content gaps and technique gaps. Then teaching aimed only at the content gaps the marked papers actually revealed, which is never four themes' worth and is usually six or seven specific topics.

The discipline that makes this work is refusing to teach anything the marked papers have not identified. A student who feels shaky about everything will ask for everything, and the instinct of a well-meaning tutor is to oblige. Resisting that is what makes ten sessions productive rather than reassuring. It also means the plan is visible: by week three you have a list of the six or seven specific gaps, and you can see it shrinking. If it is not shrinking, the problem is not the number of hours and buying more of them will not help.

sections.heading: When a Biology specialist is not free in your slot
paragraphs: Higher Level Biology demand in Dubai spikes twice: in the DP2 autumn when continuity and change is being taught, and in February when mocks come back. In those windows, a weekday evening slot on Gulf Standard Time with a Biology specialist is a genuinely scarce thing, and pretending otherwise produces bookings that disappoint.

What we do instead is tell you the real position. If no Biology specialist is free in your preferred slot, the options are a different time in the same week, a weekend morning, or a named date when a slot opens with nothing charged until it does. If no specialist whose working day overlaps Gulf Standard Time covers Higher Level Biology at the depth your child needs, we say so and state what is actually available, including any time difference, before you commit to anything. No competitor page researched for this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind a foreign phone number.

There is also a version of this where the right answer is not a tutor. A Higher Level Biology student whose marked papers show knowledge without marks needs a command-term intensive, which is two or three sessions and can be done at almost any time. A student who is behind on one theme needs that theme, not a weekly commitment. A student carrying three laboratory sciences at Higher Level may need a conversation with their coordinator about load rather than a fourth paid hour in the week. We would rather say that than sell a slot we cannot fill well.
