process.title: Send the school report and one recent assessment
process.description: A report tells us what the school sees. A recent assessment, ideally with the marks per question visible, tells us what a mark scheme saw. The gap between the two is usually where the first session starts, and it is why we ask for both.

process.title: Free first session on a mixed question set
process.description: The student answers a short set chosen to sample several question types, marked beforehand. The free session is spent on the pattern rather than on a single topic, and the note afterwards is the first entry in the question-type ledger.

process.title: Three weeks to a visible profile
process.description: Three marked questions per type make the profile clear. Until then we do not commit to a plan, because a single weak answer may be a bad evening rather than a weakness and designing a term around it wastes the term.

process.title: Practise the failing type on familiar content
process.description: If data interpretation is the gap, the questions used are on topics the student already knows well. Keeping the content constant means the skill is the only variable, and the improvement is attributable rather than guessed at.

process.title: Six-week review, written down
process.description: The review states continue, change focus, or stop, with the ledger attached. We do not predict a grade and we do not claim credit for a mock result. Where six weeks show no movement, stopping is the recommendation we make.

whyPoints.title: Marks are logged by question type
whyPoints.description: A topic list cannot explain why a student who knows the content scores two grades below it. A ledger recording type, topic, marks available and marks gained can, and it usually points at data interpretation or mechanism explanation rather than at a theme.

whyPoints.title: Data questions are practised on unfamiliar contexts
whyPoints.description: Paper 1B uses experiments a student has never performed, so practising on familiar topics trains recall with a graph attached. We choose stimuli from outside the taught sequence deliberately, which is harder and is the skill the paper tests.

whyPoints.title: Older material is sampled every week
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Biology is a large course and retrieval decays. Weekly questions drawn from material taught two terms earlier reveal decay cheaply, and a lower mark on old content is information rather than a setback.

whyPoints.title: The review can recommend stopping
whyPoints.description: Six weeks of ledger either shows the failing question type improving or it does not. Where it does not, adding sessions rarely changes that, and we write down the recommendation to stop rather than keeping a slot filled.

whyPoints.title: We will not claim what cannot be evidenced
whyPoints.description: No grade prediction, no attribution of a mock result to our sessions, no statistic without its source. Market rates here are published Dubai figures from October 2026, and IB session dates are absent because they could not be verified.

faqs.question: Which question types carry the most Higher Level Biology marks?
faqs.answer: Six groups cover nearly all of them. Recognition items in Paper 1A, which reward speed and elimination across forty questions. Data-based questions in Paper 1B, drawn from unfamiliar experiments. Short recall and definition items, which reward the examination's own wording. Mechanism explanations, which need a causal chain rather than a single statement. Comparison questions, where compare and contrast or distinguish demands paired statements. And extended evaluation, which requires a stated judgement. A student's performance across these six is almost never even, and the unevenness is the diagnosis a topic-based report cannot provide.

faqs.question: How do we find out which biology question type is costing marks?
faqs.answer: By marking questions against the published scheme and recording the result by type rather than by topic. A mixed set is chosen to sample all six types, each question is marked before the lesson, and the entry records type, topic, marks available and marks gained. Three entries per type make the pattern visible, which takes about three weeks. Until then we do not commit to a plan, because a single weak answer can be a bad evening. The output is a sheet a parent can take to a school meeting showing, for instance, 40 per cent on data interpretation against 85 per cent on recall.

faqs.question: Why does my son freeze on biology data questions about unfamiliar experiments?
faqs.answer: Because he is looking for the content in his notes and the question is not testing content. Paper 1B deliberately uses an organism, assay or habitat the student has never worked with, and what it assesses is the handling of evidence. The marks are specific: reading a value with units, describing a trend by direction and magnitude, calculating a rate, explaining the pattern biologically, and evaluating sample size, control or variability. Two faults dominate: describing where interpretation was asked for, and ignoring spread or error bars and then calling a difference real. Both respond to a short block of practice on deliberately unfamiliar stimuli.

faqs.question: Do biology diagrams need labels or sentences to earn marks?
faqs.answer: Labels, and prose beneath a drawing usually earns nothing. A labelled diagram wants ruled lines touching the structure, written horizontally outside the drawing, with correct spelling. An annotated diagram additionally wants a short functional note: not the structure named twice but what it does or why a feature matters. Proportions can carry a mark, so relative sizes should be roughly right, while shading and artistic detail earn nothing and consume time. Micrograph questions want a magnification calculation with units and working shown. Ten drawings practised properly against the scheme usually settles the habit for the rest of the course.

faqs.question: What does an explain command term require in Higher Level Biology?
faqs.answer: A causal chain, which in practice means at least two linked statements where the second follows from the first and reaches the consequence the question asked about. A single accurate statement is normally worth half the available marks. The commonest Higher Level failure is stopping one step short: naming the mechanism without saying what it produces, or naming the outcome without the mechanism. Counting the links in each answer makes this measurable, and it is one of the few faults a student can self-check once the habit exists. Describe, by contrast, wants observable features with no causal reasoning, and extra prose there earns nothing.

faqs.question: Why did a strong DP1 biology student stall in DP2?
faqs.answer: Because the assessment changed rather than the content. DP1 assessment usually samples recently taught material in familiar formats. DP2 assessment samples eighteen months at once, in unfamiliar contexts, with questions that combine themes taught separately. Three causes follow: retrieval decay on material not revisited, failure to connect topics that were learned in isolation, and heavier use of data and evaluation question types that unit tests may never have sampled. The response is weekly questions drawn from material taught at least two terms earlier, which reveals the decay quickly. Students resist it because the marks are lower, which is precisely why it is informative.

faqs.question: How is the Biology Higher Level investigation marked?
faqs.answer: Out of 24 marks across four criteria of six marks each, worth 20 per cent of the final grade, with a 3,000-word cap. Research design rewards a measurable question with stated range, increments and controlled variables, and in biology it requires replication sufficient for natural variability. Data analysis rewards processing that shows spread rather than means alone. Conclusion rewards an answer to the original question that acknowledges variability and compares with theory. Evaluation rewards specific biological sources of variation with realistic improvements, and human error as a named weakness earns nothing. The marking is identical at Standard and Higher Level.

faqs.question: What statistics does a Biology HL student need to know?
faqs.answer: Interpretation more than computation. The skills expected include measures of central tendency and spread, standard deviation and what error bars represent, recognising when a statistical test is appropriate and which one suits the data, and using a diversity measure in an ecological context. Confirm the exact expectations for your child's cohort with the school's Diploma coordinator, since guides are revised. Questions rarely ask for a test to be performed by hand; they ask what a result means, whether a difference between means is likely to be real given the spread, and why sample size changes confidence. Those marks appear in data questions and in the investigation.

faqs.question: What evidence should a parent see after a month of biology sessions?
faqs.answer: Four things. A question-type ledger with at least three entries per type, recording marks available against marks gained. A short written note after every session naming the next practice task. The marked questions themselves, with the scheme visible so a parent can see which specific link or label was missing. And a plain statement of what has moved and what has not. If the ledger shows no movement in the failing type after four weeks, the honest response is to change focus or to stop rather than to add sessions, and that recommendation should be in writing.

faqs.question: Can a predicted grade in Biology HL change?
faqs.answer: Yes, because a prediction is an estimate built from the evidence a teacher holds, and new evidence changes it. A student predicted below where they want to be should be producing marked work in the formats the school assesses least, since those are usually where the prediction is under-informed. What no tutor can do is promise a prediction will move, and any provider framing it as a purchase is selling something they do not control. The useful approach is to generate evidence, take it to the subject teacher, and ask specifically what would need to be demonstrated for the prediction to be revised.

faqs.question: Is Biology Higher Level required for medicine applications from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Many medical schools specify biology, frequently at Higher Level and usually with chemistry, but the requirements are set per programme and differ between institutions and between admissions cycles. Some faculties require chemistry at Higher Level and accept biology at Standard Level; others require both at Higher Level. The practical step is to read three named programme pages for the current cycle before the DP1 subject-change window closes, then confirm with each admissions office. A requirement published two years ago, or summarised on a tutoring site, is not evidence. No tutoring arrangement changes a published prerequisite.

faqs.question: How is a biology grade used in UAE certificate equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is a certificate-recognition process run by the Ministry of Education and is separate from university admission. Its published requirements are expressed per curriculum rather than per subject grade. For the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. For the American track, mathematics needs at least 450 in SAT Math, with English evidenced by IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing. No IB points figure should be quoted unless read on the Ministry's own site.

faqs.question: What is a fair hourly rate for a Biology HL tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour for budget online providers, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IB specialist, with premium named tutors advertised up to AED 650. Monthly packages of about AED 799 for eight online sessions appear in the same market. Those are market figures rather than our price list. The question that changes value most is whether marking and a written ledger are included, since without them there is no record of which question type is failing.

faqs.question: How many biology sessions a week should a DP2 student book?
faqs.answer: One 90-minute session a week with a marked question returned beforehand suits most students and produces a usable ledger within three weeks. Two shorter sessions suit a student working on a specific question type, because the practice benefits from frequency. In the final weeks before the written papers, families commonly move to two or three sessions built around full timed papers. Beyond three a week the limiting factor is sleep rather than teaching, particularly for students in communities with long bus routes, and we would rather say that than fill the slots.

faqs.question: What if no Biology Higher Level specialist is free in our time slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you before anything is booked and nothing is charged. Biology at Higher Level is widely taught, so an outright absence of availability is uncommon; the usual constraint is a specific recurring time, such as 4.30pm twice weekly in term time, which cannot be filled by a UAE-based tutor. The alternatives offered are the nearest workable slot, a weekend block, or a specialist in another time zone whose hours overlap Gulf Standard Time. What we will not do is accept the booking and allocate someone who has not taught this course at this level, which is how a family ends up paying for general science help.

Three weeks give a visible profile and six give an honest review, which may say continue, change focus, or stop. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the school timetable and mandatory subject periods.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: These specialists teach Biology at Standard Level across the four themes and the scientific investigation. Each card shows the levels taught, the Gulf Standard Time slots held, and the marking turnaround they work to, because a marked paper that arrives three weeks later is not evidence of anything.

intro.heading: How to tell whether you are buying teaching or buying company
paragraphs: There is a specific conversation that happens in Dubai households around week nine of a tutoring arrangement. The parent asks how it is going. The student says fine. The parent asks what they covered. The student says photosynthesis, or enzymes, or something. The parent pays the invoice, because the alternative is admitting they have no idea whether several thousand dirhams has achieved anything. This is the normal state of paid tutoring and it is entirely avoidable.

The fix is not a better tutor. It is a documentary trail. A Standard Level Biology arrangement that is working produces readable artefacts, on a schedule, whether or not anybody asks for them: a session note after each lesson saying what was covered and what the student got wrong, an annotated marked paper every few sessions with the reasoning visible rather than a number at the top, a running error log that sorts mistakes into categories, dated feedback on each investigation draft, and at six weeks a written verdict that is willing to say the arrangement should end. If none of that exists, there is nothing to evaluate, and an arrangement that cannot be evaluated will continue until somebody loses patience.

Biology at Standard Level is a good subject to run this way, because the evidence is unusually legible. The course is 150 taught hours across four themes, and the marks are decided largely by whether an answer meets the command term it was asked under. That means a marked script tells you something precise: this student knows the content and is describing when the question says explain, or this student does not know the content, or this student knows it and ran out of time. Those three diagnoses look nothing alike on paper and demand different responses, and any of them is more useful than a child saying fine.

The error log is the artefact Dubai parents find most immediately useful, and almost nobody in this market provides one. It is a short running document listing each mistake from each marked paper, sorted into categories: content not known, command term not met, time ran out, question misread, arithmetic. After three marked papers the pattern is visible on a single page. If forty per cent of the entries sit under command term, the fix is two sessions of answer rewriting and not a term of content revision. If they cluster in one theme, that theme is the brief. The log turns a vague worry into a list.

One thing is fixed before any of this begins. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the Emirates, and no tutor from this platform travels to a UAE address; home visits exist only in our India service. Standard Level Biology is taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That has a direct bearing on evidence, as it happens: when the teaching is on a shared screen, the annotated answer, the marked script and the diagram are already files, which is why the trail described above is routine here rather than an administrative favour.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Standard Level Biology sits in the Diploma, and the evidence a family should expect changes by programme, because the assessment changes. Here is what is measurable at each stage.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Biology at Standard Level runs 150 taught hours across four themes, assessed by two written papers and one internally marked scientific investigation. Evidence here is straightforward because past papers exist in quantity: a timed script marked against the real criteria is an honest measurement, and a sequence of them is a trend.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma students typically take Standard Level Biology alongside Higher Levels that matter more to their applications, which means the subject gets the least independent study time and the least parental attention until a report arrives. The practical consequence is that a documentary trail matters more here than on a Higher Level subject, because nobody in the household is watching the work closely enough to notice a drift without it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four assessment criteria rather than papers, so the evidence looks different: criterion-level marks on tasks rather than scripts against a mark scheme. A student can be scoring well on criteria and still be unprepared for a timed Diploma paper, which is why the first useful measurement for an ex-MYP student is a past paper under timed conditions.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run MYP straight into the Diploma. For those students the first marked past paper is often a shock that has nothing to do with biology: they have never written to a command term under a clock. Running that paper early, in DP1 rather than before mocks, converts a future crisis into an early data point, and it costs one session.

programmes.name: IGCSE and the British route
programmes.description: Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE Biology, or Combined Science, to Year 11. The useful evidence here already exists and is usually ignored: the component breakdown of the IGCSE result. A student strong on multiple-choice and weak on structured answers has a writing habit that will cost far more in the Diploma, and that is visible in the breakdown rather than in the grade.
programmes.countryNote: Because British-curriculum schools carry the largest share of Dubai enrolment, most Standard Level Biology students here come through IGCSE with a component breakdown sitting in a drawer. Asking the school for it before DP1 begins is free, takes one email, and frequently identifies the exact problem that would otherwise be discovered in a February mock two years later.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: A household usually has to choose where the money goes. These are the subjects that sit beside Standard Level Biology on a Dubai timetable, with the evidence that tells you which one has the real problem.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Four themes across 150 taught hours, examined from molecules to ecosystems, with two written papers and one scientific investigation. The evidence that matters is a timed script marked with annotation, because the gap between knowing biology and scoring in biology is wide and visible only there.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The same four themes at 240 taught hours with extension content throughout. Mentioned here because the evidence trail differs: a Higher Level student needs more marked papers to cover the content, and a plateau takes longer to interpret because there is simply more material in play.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity strands with the same two-paper and investigation architecture. Sits beside Biology for most Dubai science students. When both grades are stuck at 5, the error logs usually show the same cause, which means one intervention rather than two.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling with technology. Directly relevant evidence for Biology: if a student cannot process data into a mean with a measure of spread, the investigation and the data-based paper section will both show it, and no amount of biology teaching will move either.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Ecosystems, biodiversity, pollution and resource management, counting for either the sciences or the individuals and societies group. Overlaps the interaction and interdependence theme, so marked work in one subject is partial evidence about the other.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches with research methods and ethics. Shares the command-term problem with Biology almost exactly, and an error log from one subject frequently predicts the pattern in the other before any marked work exists for it.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Anatomy, physiology, energy systems and nutrition. Substantial overlap with the organism-level Biology content, which makes it one of the few pairings where evidence genuinely transfers: a secured physiology topic shows up in both sets of marked work.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis, oral and written components. On this list for one reason: a student who writes loose, unfocused answers in Biology usually writes them in English too, and the English teacher's written feedback is free evidence a Dubai parent already has.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Relevant here as timetable evidence: these lessons occupy real hours, so a claim that a student has spare study time usually needs checking against the actual week.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-home-tutor.regionsIntro: The local detail that matters for an evidence-led arrangement is when a session can realistically happen and whether the student is awake for it. These Dubai communities come up most often for Standard Level Biology.

sections.heading: What should land in your hands, and when
paragraphs: An arrangement you cannot evaluate is an arrangement you will keep paying for. The table below sets out the artefacts a Standard Level Biology arrangement should produce, when each one should arrive, and what it does and does not prove. The second half of that distinction is the part most providers skip: an annotated script proves what happened in one timed hour, it does not prove a final grade, and anyone implying otherwise is overselling.

Notice that none of these artefacts is a dashboard, a progress percentage or a star rating. Those are manufactured numbers, and this market is full of them. Several competitor pages researched for this project display a satisfaction figure with no sample size, no date and no method, and one displays a self-asserted star rating in its structured data that does not match the figure on the page. A rating a provider awards itself is not evidence. A script your child wrote, marked with the reasoning visible, is.

Ask for these before you agree to anything, because the answer is diagnostic in itself. A provider who says yes to all five has a working process. A provider who offers a monthly summary instead has one administrative touchpoint and no record. A provider who says the tutor will keep you updated verbally is offering you exactly the week-nine conversation described at the top of this page, which is the thing you are trying to avoid. Ask also how quickly a marked script comes back, because a paper annotated three weeks after it was written has stopped describing anything the student can still remember doing.

sections.heading: Reading a marked Biology script: the five error categories
paragraphs: A marked script with a number at the top is almost useless. A marked script with annotation is the single most informative document in this whole arrangement, because Standard Level Biology fails in a small number of distinct ways and they are distinguishable on paper. Sorting the errors is the work, and it is work a parent can do alongside a tutor rather than taking on trust.

The categories are these. Content not known: the student had nothing to write, and the fix is teaching. Command term not met: the student knew the biology and answered the wrong instruction, usually describing when the question said explain, and the fix is answer rewriting rather than content. Question misread: the student answered a related question accurately, which is a reading-under-pressure problem. Time ran out: the final questions are blank or thin while earlier ones are over-long, and the fix is pacing. Processing error: the biology and the structure were right and a calculation, a unit or a graph reading was wrong.

Each category has a different cost and a different timescale, and that is why sorting matters more than counting. A script losing twelve marks across four categories needs four small interventions. A script losing twelve marks entirely under command term needs two sessions and nothing else. Most Dubai families, shown their child's error log for the first time, are surprised by how few of the lost marks are content, and that surprise usually saves them money. It is also the evidence that settles the common argument in which the school says the student is fine and a mock says otherwise: both are describing different categories.

sections.heading: The first six weeks, week by week
paragraphs: Six weeks is the right first horizon. It is long enough for marked work to show movement and short enough that being wrong about the whole arrangement costs little. What follows is the sequence we actually run, so that the verdict at the end of it rests on comparable measurements rather than on everybody's impressions.

The logic is that week one and week six must be the same kind of event. A timed paper under exam conditions at the start and another at the end, both marked the same way, gives you two numbers that can honestly be compared. Everything in between is diagnosis and teaching aimed at whatever the first paper revealed. Without that bracketing, a six-week review becomes a conversation about whether things feel better, which is exactly the conversation that keeps unproductive arrangements alive.

The verdict at week six has three possible outcomes and we commit to all three in advance. Continue, because the marked work moved and the remaining pattern is clear. Change, because nothing moved and the same category dominates the log, which means the approach or the tutor is wrong rather than insufficient. Or stop, because the evidence says the problem is not one that tutoring addresses: a student not working between sessions, a mathematical limitation, or a student who is in fact fine and whose single bad mock was a bad day. Stopping is a normal outcome of an honest review. What makes it possible is having agreed the three outcomes before the first session, so that recommending the end of an arrangement is a step in the process rather than an awkward admission nobody wants to make.

sections.heading: What 150 taught hours contains, and what coverage evidence looks like
paragraphs: Standard Level Biology runs 150 taught hours across four themes: unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, and continuity and change, each examined at molecular, cellular, organism and ecosystem level. It does not carry the Higher Level extension content, which matters for evidence as much as for cost: a Standard Level student failing a question drawn from Higher Level material in a shared textbook has produced no useful information about their actual course.

The practical move at the start of an arrangement is to get the school's scheme of work and mark it against the subject guide your child is being taught. Two things fall out immediately. First, a list of what has genuinely been taught so far, which bounds what any marked paper can fairly test. Second, a list of Higher Level-only material to ignore, which stops a Standard Level student wasting revision hours and losing confidence on content that is not on their syllabus. Confirm the guide version with the subject teacher, since schools adopted the current guides on different timetables.

Coverage evidence then becomes simple to maintain. A single sheet listing the four themes and their sub-topics, with three states marked against each: taught at school, tested under timed conditions, and secured on re-test. Most students have far more in the first column than in the third, and the gap between those two columns is the real revision plan. It also stops the commonest waste in paid tutoring, which is re-teaching something already secured because nobody wrote down that it was.

sections.heading: The investigation draft trail, and the line that must not move
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the Standard Level Biology grade comes from one piece of individual research, marked by the school. It is also the component where an evidence trail protects the student rather than just informing the parent. Dated written feedback on each draft, kept on file, shows exactly what a tutor advised and when, and shows that what changed between drafts was the student's own work responding to comments.

What good feedback contains is specific and limited. Whether the research question can generate real analysis or merely confirms something already established. Whether the sampling and replication will support a mean with a defensible measure of spread. Whether the processed data is presented in a form the criteria reward, with error bars the student can explain. Where the evaluation is thin, where a limitation has been listed without being weighed, and where a conclusion has run past what the data supports. Each of those is a comment on the student's work, in writing, with a date.

What never appears is text. A tutor does not supply sentences, rewrite paragraphs into better English, or hand a method over to be copied. The report must be the student's own work in their own words, and the data must be theirs. The school awards the mark and a paid tutor has no part in that. Providers in this market sell finished investigation reports at around AED 3,750; that is an academic-integrity breach under IB rules and the consequence lands on the student's Diploma. A dated feedback trail is the cleanest possible demonstration that nothing of the sort happened here.

sections.heading: Why the grade does not move in a straight line
paragraphs: A parent watching marked scripts for the first time usually expects a line that climbs. What actually happens is lumpier, and knowing the normal shape prevents two expensive mistakes: abandoning something that is working and persisting with something that is not.

Three patterns are normal. A score can fall while the work improves, because the student has started attempting the harder extended-response questions they previously skipped, and attempting them badly scores lower than avoiding them. A score can sit flat for three papers and then jump, because command-term discipline is a habit that holds or does not, with little in between. And a score can rise on familiar content while the error log shows the same category unchanged, which means the paper was kinder rather than the student stronger. The log is what distinguishes these, and the raw mark on its own cannot.

What is not normal, and should end an arrangement, is an error log in which the same category dominates after six weeks of work aimed at it. That is not slow progress; it is the wrong approach, and buying more of it is the most expensive available response. The other signal worth acting on is an absence of evidence: if there are no marked scripts to look at after six weeks of weekly sessions, the question of whether the grade is moving cannot be answered, and the answer to an unanswerable question should be to stop paying for it.

sections.heading: The numbers we will not publish about ourselves
paragraphs: This market has a statistics problem, and a page about evidence has to address it. Competitor pages researched for this project publish satisfaction percentages with no sample size, no date and no method; self-awarded star ratings in structured data that differ from the figure visible on the page; and in one case a review count that contradicts a student count stated elsewhere on the same site. None of that is evidence. It is decoration, and in the UAE a fabricated commercial representation is a consumer-protection exposure as well as a structured-data violation.

So this page carries no satisfaction figure, no average grade improvement, no success rate and no star rating. Not because the arrangement does not work, but because we cannot produce the sample size, the date range and the method that would make such a number meaningful, and a number without those three things tells you nothing you should act on. The same applies to grade promises: nobody can guarantee an outcome in an externally assessed examination, and any provider offering one is either misunderstanding the assessment or hoping you will not notice.

What we will do instead is give you evidence about your own child, which is the only sample that matters to you. An annotated script is a fact. An error log across three papers is a trend. A dated feedback trail on an investigation draft is a record. Those are checkable, specific and yours, and if they do not show what we hoped they would show, the six-week verdict says so in writing. A provider willing to publish a bad verdict about one student is more trustworthy than one publishing a good percentage about everybody.

sections.heading: What the permit rules mean for the person marking your child's work
paragraphs: An evidence trail is only as good as the person producing it, so it is worth knowing who is permitted to do this work. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without the permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule, so any amount quoted should be treated as unverified.

One rule bears directly on evidence. Your child's own subject teacher should not be their paid tutor. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tuition of students at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond the regulatory position, there is an obvious conflict: the person who awards the internal mark on the scientific investigation cannot also be the paid reviewer of its drafts without compromising both roles.

Finally, a point of structure rather than law. A tutoring operation running from premises with staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That permit belongs to centres with premises. IB Gram is not a centre, does not hold that permit, has no office in the UAE, and should never be described as approved or accredited by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because it holds no such status. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is honest; implying its endorsement is not.

sections.heading: When the slot you need is taken
paragraphs: Standard Level Biology is easier to staff than Higher Level Chemistry, but the Dubai evening is still the Dubai evening. Between four and eight on Gulf Standard Time, in the weeks after February mocks, the slots a working family can actually use are the ones everybody wants. Here is what happens rather than what is advertised.

If no Biology specialist is free in your preferred slot, you get the real options: a different time in the same week, a weekend morning, or a named date when a slot opens with nothing charged until it does. For an evidence-led arrangement the weekend morning is often the better choice anyway, because the timed papers that anchor the whole plan give a truer reading from a rested student than from one who has been at school since seven. If no specialist whose day overlaps Gulf Standard Time can cover the brief, we say so and state what is available, including any time difference, before you decide. No competitor page examined for this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

And if the evidence says you do not need us, that is also an answer. A student whose error log is dominated by command terms needs two or three sessions and then nothing. A student with no marked papers at all needs to attempt one before anybody is paid. A student who is not working between sessions is not short of teaching. We would rather write that in a verdict and lose the booking than keep an arrangement running that the marked work cannot justify.

process.title: Send the evidence you already have
process.description: The last two marked Biology papers with annotations, the most recent report, and if it exists the IGCSE component breakdown. Most Dubai families already hold more evidence than they realise and have never lined it up. Doing so before the first session usually identifies the dominant error category straight away.

process.title: Run the baseline paper in week one
process.description: A timed past paper under exam conditions, marked with annotation, producing the first error log. This is the measurement everything afterwards is compared against, which is why it happens before any teaching rather than after a few comfortable sessions have shifted expectations.

process.title: Teach only what the log identifies
process.description: Sessions aim at the dominant category and nothing else, with a note after each one naming the specific errors addressed. Declining to teach topics the marked work has not flagged is what makes a short arrangement productive instead of merely reassuring.

process.title: Re-test under the same conditions
process.description: A second timed paper at week five, same length, same conditions, marked the same way, so the two scripts are genuinely comparable. The point is not the mark but whether the dominant category in the error log has shrunk, which is the question the whole plan is built to answer.

process.title: Read the six-week verdict together
process.description: A written document setting both scripts side by side, stating what moved, what did not, and which of continue, change or stop the evidence supports. We commit to all three outcomes in advance, including the one that ends the arrangement and the invoice with it.

whyPoints.title: Artefacts, not reassurance
whyPoints.description: A session note after every lesson, an annotated script roughly every third, a running error log and dated draft feedback. All readable, all yours, all challengeable. The week-nine conversation in which nobody can say what has been achieved does not happen when documents exist.

whyPoints.title: Errors sorted, not counted
whyPoints.description: Marks lost are sorted into content, command term, misread question, time and processing. A script losing twelve marks entirely under command term needs two sessions; the same twelve marks spread across categories needs four small interventions. The sorting is what tells you which.

whyPoints.title: Comparable measurements
whyPoints.description: A timed paper under exam conditions at the start of a block and another at the end, marked identically. Two numbers that can honestly be compared beat six weeks of impressions, and they make a plateau visible early rather than in a February mock.

whyPoints.title: A verdict that can be negative
whyPoints.description: At six weeks a written verdict says continue, change or stop, and stop is a real option we commit to in advance. A provider who has never recommended that a family stop paying has not been measuring anything.

whyPoints.title: No invented statistics
whyPoints.description: No satisfaction percentage, no average grade improvement, no success rate, no self-awarded star rating, no guaranteed outcome. We cannot publish the sample size, date range and method those would need, and a number without them is decoration rather than evidence.

whyPoints.title: A draft trail that protects the student
whyPoints.description: Dated written feedback on each investigation draft shows what was advised, when, and that the changes were the student's own work. We supply no text and no method. That record is the cleanest demonstration available that the honesty line was respected.

faqs.question: How will we know in writing whether the Biology sessions are working?
faqs.answer: By comparing two timed papers marked the same way, and by watching whether the dominant category in the error log shrinks. A paper under exam conditions in week one gives a baseline; another in week five gives a comparable measurement; the written verdict at week six sets them side by side and states what moved. Everything else, including how the sessions feel and what your child says about them, is weaker evidence. If no marked scripts exist after six weeks of weekly sessions, the question cannot be answered, and that absence is itself the finding.

faqs.question: What exactly do we receive after each session?
faqs.answer: A short written note naming what was covered and, more usefully, what the student got wrong during the session. The second part is the one that matters, because a note saying only the topic is a receipt rather than information. Roughly every third session you also receive an annotated marked script with the mark reasoning visible, and the running error log is updated each time. During the investigation period, each draft comes back with dated written feedback. All of it is kept on file so a pattern across weeks is readable rather than remembered.

faqs.question: Can we see a marked paper with the reasoning rather than just a score?
faqs.answer: That is the only form of marking worth paying for. A score tells you where a student stands and nothing about why, which means it cannot generate a next step. An annotated script shows the exact point where a mark was lost, whether the biology was absent or the instruction was missed, and which questions were rushed. Ask any prospective provider to annotate one paper before you commit, and ask how quickly it comes back. A marked script returned three weeks later has stopped being evidence and become a souvenir.

faqs.question: Our daughter's grade has not moved in six weeks. Does that mean it is failing?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and the error log settles it. Three innocent patterns exist: the score can fall while the work improves, because she has started attempting extended-response questions she previously skipped; it can sit flat and then jump, because command-term discipline is a habit that holds or does not; and it can rise on a kinder paper while the underlying category is unchanged. What is not innocent is the same category dominating the log after six weeks of work aimed at it. That means the approach is wrong rather than insufficient, and more of it will not help.

faqs.question: How many marked papers should a Standard Level Biology student have attempted before mocks?
faqs.answer: Enough that timed conditions are ordinary rather than an event, which in practice means several complete papers rather than one. The number matters less than the marking: three papers attempted and properly annotated are worth more than eight attempted and self-scored, because self-scoring cannot see a command-term failure, which is where most of the marks go. The other requirement is comparability. Papers attempted under different conditions, at different times of day, with different amounts of help, do not form a trend you can read.

faqs.question: What does an error log look like and who keeps it?
faqs.answer: One page, maintained by the tutor and shared with you, listing each mark lost from each marked script against five categories: content not known, command term not met, question misread, time ran out, and processing error. After three scripts the distribution is visible at a glance, and that distribution is the brief. Most Dubai parents seeing it for the first time are surprised how little of the loss is missing content. The student should also keep a copy, because reviewing their own pattern before a paper changes behaviour more reliably than being told about it does.

faqs.question: Do you publish a success rate or an average grade improvement?
faqs.answer: No, and we would be suspicious of anyone who does. A meaningful statistic needs a sample size, a date range and a stated method, and a figure lacking those three things carries no information whatever it looks like. Pages in this market display satisfaction percentages with none of them, and at least one carries a self-awarded star rating in its structured data that differs from the figure printed on the page. What we provide instead is evidence about your own child, which is the only sample relevant to your decision, including when it is unflattering.

faqs.question: How do we check the tutor actually read the investigation draft properly?
faqs.answer: Read the feedback. Genuine draft feedback is specific to that draft and that student: it names the research question's weakness, says whether the replication will support a mean with a defensible measure of spread, points at a particular paragraph where the evaluation is thin, and identifies a conclusion that has run past its data. Generic feedback that could be pasted onto any report is visible immediately. The feedback is dated and kept on file, so you can also see what changed between drafts, which tells you whether the comments were acted on.

faqs.question: Who keeps the record if we change tutors mid-term?
faqs.answer: You should, and that is an argument for insisting on documents from the start. If the session notes, the annotated scripts and the error log sit in your hands rather than in a departing tutor's head, a new tutor begins with the diagnosis already done and the first two sessions are not spent rediscovering it. This is the single most practical reason to require a written trail even when you are happy with the current arrangement. Tutors move, families relocate, and an undocumented six weeks has to be bought again.

faqs.question: Can the school see the session notes, and should they?
faqs.answer: They can if you share them, and often it helps. A subject teacher who knows that a student's lost marks are concentrated under explain questions can reinforce exactly that in class at no cost to you, and may well have noticed the same thing. What should not happen is anything resembling a negotiation about the internal mark on the scientific investigation; that mark is the school's and a paid tutor has no part in it. Share the diagnosis, not a request. Most Dubai teachers respond well to a parent arriving with specific evidence rather than a general worry.

faqs.question: What counts as evidence that the problem was never Biology?
faqs.answer: Three things show up clearly. If the error log is dominated by command term rather than content, the student knows the biology and is answering the wrong instruction, which is a writing problem. If the processing-error category dominates and the same student struggles with a bare algebraic rearrangement outside any biology context, the limitation is mathematical. And if performance is strong on untimed work and collapses under a clock, the issue is pacing and exam conditions. None of those three is solved by more biology teaching, and all are visible within two marked scripts.

faqs.question: Is a monthly progress report enough, or do we need notes every week?
faqs.answer: A monthly report is a summary of something, and if nothing was recorded weekly it is a summary of memory. Weekly notes cost the tutor a few minutes and give you the raw material: what was covered, what the student got wrong, what they should do before next time. The monthly or half-term document then has something to summarise and a verdict can rest on it. The practical test is whether a report names specific errors from specific sessions. If it describes effort and attitude in general terms, nothing was recorded along the way.

faqs.question: What does the evidence look like when we should stop paying?
faqs.answer: Three signatures. The named target has been hit and the marked scripts show it, in which case stopping is success rather than abandonment. The same error category dominates the log after six weeks of work aimed squarely at it, which means the approach is wrong and buying more is the costliest possible response. Or the student has begun doing the work independently and the marked papers hold up without sessions, which was the goal. The fourth case is an absence: no marked scripts after six weeks means there is nothing to justify the next invoice.

faqs.question: Is the evidence trail different for Standard Level Biology than for Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Same artefacts, different pacing. Standard Level is 150 taught hours against 240, so a smaller body of content has to be covered and a plateau becomes interpretable sooner: six weeks of marked work genuinely tells you something. At Higher Level there is more material in play, so a flat sequence of scripts can reflect breadth not yet covered rather than a technique problem. One Standard Level specific point matters: ignore any question drawn from Higher Level-only material, because a Standard Level student failing it has produced no information about their own course.

faqs.question: Our son says the sessions are going well but the marks say otherwise. Which do we trust?
faqs.answer: The marks, but read them before concluding anything. Sessions can genuinely go well while marks stay flat, because understanding in the presence of a tutor is not the same as retrieving under a clock, and that gap is the commonest finding in the whole of paid tutoring. The error log tells you which it is. If the log shows content being secured and time running out, the sessions are working and the pacing is not. If the log shows the same content gaps recurring, the sessions feel productive and are not landing, and the approach needs changing rather than extending.

faqs.question: Does a recorded session count as evidence of what was taught?
faqs.answer: Of what was taught, yes; of what was learned, no, and the distinction decides how useful it is. A recording is genuinely valuable to the student, who can revisit an explanation of membrane transport in February having met it in October. As evidence for a parent it is weak, because nobody will watch an hour of it and watching would not reveal whether anything stuck. The written note, the annotated script and the error log are compact and diagnostic. Keep recordings for the student's revision and judge the arrangement on the documents.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-home-tutor.closingHeading: Ask for the documents before you agree the first session
dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-home-tutor.closingBody: The difference between a Standard Level Biology arrangement that works and one that merely continues is usually not the tutor. It is whether anything was written down. Ask any provider, including this one, for five things: a session note every week naming the errors, an annotated script every third session, a running error log, dated feedback on each investigation draft, and a written verdict at six weeks that is permitted to recommend stopping. Start with the free diagnostic session, which produces a written finding from your child's existing marked work. You keep it either way, nothing is charged, and nobody travels to any UAE address.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Diploma Biology at Standard Level as its own course: themes A to D at common-core depth, the 40-hour practical scheme, biological drawing and data interpretation, and the investigation. Profiles name the papers each one works on most. Matching is done from a description of what goes wrong, not from a subject name.

intro.heading: Why a student who knows the biology still scores a 4
paragraphs: The most frequent description Dubai parents give of a Standard Level Biology problem is that their child knows the material. Quite often they are right. The student can define osmosis, name the stages of mitosis, and explain what an enzyme does. Then the paper arrives, and the questions are about an unfamiliar organism, a graph nobody has seen, and a method the student has to criticise. Knowledge is necessary and it is not sufficient, and a page that pretends otherwise is not going to help.

Diploma science papers are written against assessment objectives that go well beyond recall: knowing things, applying them to new situations, analysing and evaluating evidence, and demonstrating the skills of investigation. Paper 1 at Standard Level is ninety minutes and 36% of the grade, with a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 is also ninety minutes and 44%, built from short answers and extended responses. The investigation is 20% and is marked out of 24. Across all of it, the proportion of marks available for simply stating something is much smaller than students assume.

This is why defining everything correctly produces a 4. The definition marks are banked, the application marks are partly earned, and the analysis and evaluation marks are largely missed, because nobody has ever shown the student what an answer to one of those questions looks like. The content is not where the hours should go. The question types are.

There is a second, cheaper problem sitting alongside it, and Biology is unusual in having it: drawing marks. Labelled diagrams, annotated drawings, magnification and scale calculations, interpreting a micrograph. These are marks awarded for a technique nobody practises, routinely lost for things as small as drawing with a sketchy double line or writing a label where an annotation was required. Fixing that is one session, and it shows up on the next assessment.

Everything here runs online, one student at a time, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time slots arranged around your child's school week. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we provide only in India. A shared screen is the right surface for marking a drawing and for working a data question with the figure in front of both people, which is the bulk of what these sessions do.

The page also sets out the DP2 calendar by who controls each deadline, because most of the dates that govern a Dubai Biology student's year are set by their own school rather than by the IB. The first lesson is free, lasts 45 minutes, covers one subject and asks for no card details. Every AED figure quoted below is a market rate with its source and the month it was read.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Standard Level Biology turns up in three different International Baccalaureate contexts in Dubai, and the student's situation changes the advice more than the content does. The syllabus is the same in each; the amount of time available and the reason for taking it are not.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 16-19 · Three Standard Levels of six subjects
programmes.description: Most Standard Level Biology students in Dubai are full Diploma candidates taking it as their Group 4 subject, with their Higher Levels elsewhere. The Diploma is awarded on a points total across six subjects plus the core, with a published minimum and a set of additional conditions, so a Standard Level grade matters to the total without being the thing a university is looking at. That changes how many hours it deserves.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate candidates at 7% of enrolment, and seven more schools were approved for the 2026-27 intake. Standard Level Biology sets in these schools are often the largest science groups on the timetable, which is the practical reason an individual student's drawing technique has never been corrected.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 16-19 · Career pathway with DP courses
programmes.description: Career-related Programme students take at least two Diploma Programme courses alongside their career-related study, the reflective project and the personal and professional skills course. Standard Level Biology is a common choice for health and sports pathways. The examination is identical to the one a full Diploma candidate sits, including the investigation and its four criteria, which is not always obvious from the way the pathway is described.
programmes.countryNote: The number of Dubai schools running the Career-related Programme is small but increasing. Its students are the easiest in any school to under-serve, because revision sessions, mock timetables and study groups are built for the full Diploma cohort. A Career-related Biology candidate is frequently the only student in their band sitting that paper.

programmes.description: Middle Years Sciences is integrated and criterion-assessed, and its investigations reward process. A student arriving in Standard Level Biology has usually had more practice designing an experiment than answering a question about somebody else's. The two things to build before DP1 begins are reading a question for what it asks rather than what it is about, and producing precise definitions from memory rather than in context.
programmes.countryNote: Because Middle Years criterion grades look reassuring, Dubai families rarely test either skill before the Diploma starts. A short block in the final Middle Years term aimed at question analysis is more useful than content preview, and it costs less than the remediation it prevents in the first term of DP1.

sections.heading: What a Standard Level Biology paper is actually testing
paragraphs: The Diploma science guides set out assessment objectives that cover more than knowledge: demonstrating what you know, understanding and applying it in new situations, analysing and evaluating evidence, and demonstrating the skills needed to carry out an investigation. A student who treats the course as a body of facts to be memorised is preparing for one of those four and hoping the others look after themselves.

In practice the examination is built the other way round. A multiple-choice item usually requires a fact to be applied rather than merely recalled. A data-based question gives an unfamiliar figure and asks what it supports. A Paper 2 extended response asks for a mechanism in sequence, or for a comparison, or for a judgement on whether the evidence is good enough. Very few marks are available for the definition alone.

This is the single most useful thing a parent can understand before buying tutoring hours, because it determines what the hours should contain. If your child's school report says their knowledge is sound but their examination performance is weak, the answer is not revision in the usual sense. It is practice at the three objectives nobody has drilled: application, analysis, evaluation.

The table maps each objective to where it dominates and how it is practised, because the practice method differs for each. Application needs unfamiliar contexts. Analysis needs figures the student has not seen. Evaluation needs somebody else's flawed method to criticise. None of those can be generated by rereading a textbook, which is why the subject resists the revision style that works for a vocabulary list.

sections.heading: The question types in a Standard Level Biology paper, one by one
paragraphs: Students revise content and sit question types, and the mismatch is where a term of effort disappears. There are not many types. Once a student can name the type in front of them and say what form the answer takes, their mark rises without any new biology being learned. That is an uncomfortable fact for anyone selling content teaching, and it is consistently what marked Dubai scripts show.

The hardest type for Standard Level candidates is the comparison. Asked to distinguish between two structures or processes, students write a paragraph about the first and a paragraph about the second. Mark schemes award for linked differences, stated on the same axis: this one does X whereas that one does Y. The same content, reorganised, scores twice as much, and the reorganisation takes one session to teach.

The second hardest is evaluation. Asked whether a method supports a conclusion, students either accept it or list every limitation they can think of. Neither scores well. The mark scheme wants the limitations that actually matter for the conclusion drawn, ranked, with a statement about what could still be claimed. Students find this easier once they see that it is a judgement rather than a list, and it is the skill that most reliably separates a 5 from a 6.

The table below sets out the types, what each one needs, and the error that recurs. It is worth keeping beside a past paper: the student names the type before writing anything, which slows the first thirty seconds of each answer and saves several marks across the paper.

sections.heading: Drawings, labels and scale: the marks Standard Level candidates hand back
paragraphs: Biology is the only Group 4 subject where drawing technique carries marks in its own right, and it is the cheapest set of marks on the whole course to recover. Examiners expect clean single lines rather than sketchy double ones, proportions that match what was observed, and no shading. Students who have never been told this draw the way they draw in a notebook and lose marks for presentation alone, with the biology entirely correct.

The label and annotation distinction is worth more. A label names a structure. An annotation says something about it: a function, a property, a relationship to another structure. Mark schemes ask for one or the other, and a student who writes labels where annotations were required has answered a different question. Annotations are sentences, and teaching a student to write them as sentences takes about twenty minutes.

Magnification and scale are the third piece. Calculating magnification from a scale bar, or working an actual size from a stated magnification, appears regularly and is lost to unit confusion more than to method. Micrometres and millimetres, converted in the middle of a calculation, with the answer left without a unit. It is a procedure, and like all procedures it holds once practised four or five times.

This whole area is two or three sessions. Drawings are photographed and marked on screen, which works better than marking them in a classroom because the image can be enlarged and annotated live. Of everything on this page it has the shortest gap between the session and the visible result, which is why families with an assessment three weeks away are often pointed here first.

sections.heading: Biology as the sixth subject: what good enough looks like
paragraphs: A large share of Standard Level Biology students in Dubai are not going anywhere near biology after the Diploma. They took it to satisfy Group 4, or because it was the least unappealing science, and their Higher Levels are the subjects their university offer depends on. For these students the right question is not how to maximise the Biology grade. It is how few hours it takes to stop Biology costing them points they need elsewhere.

That is a legitimate question and it deserves a straight answer rather than an upsell. The Diploma total is built from six subject grades plus points from the core, with a published minimum and conditions attached, so a Standard Level subject contributes to the total without being the number a university reads closely. A student two marks short in Biology and five marks short in a Higher Level that matters should not be spending equal hours on each.

For that student the highest-yield work is almost entirely technique: the question types table above, the drawing marks, and enough data-question practice to stop losing Paper 1B. That is a block of six to eight sessions, not a term, and it can be done in DP1 and left alone. Content gaps in secure areas can be ignored deliberately. Saying so costs us hours and it is the honest advice.

The students who do need more are the ones whose degree target includes Biology, who are weighing a move up to Higher Level, or who have a genuine content deficit from a mid-cycle school change. Those three cases are visible in the first session, and they get a different recommendation. The first conversation should establish which of the four situations your child is in, because they do not share a plan.

sections.heading: The Standard Level investigation inside forty practical hours
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is 20% of the Standard Level grade, marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. The criteria are identical to Higher Level, which routinely surprises families. What is different is the practical budget: 40 hours across the whole Standard Level course rather than 60, and a school laboratory shared with every other set in the year.

The result is a predictable failure. A student designs a method that needs five concentrations, five replicates and three weeks of growth, gets two sessions of laboratory time, and ends up writing a conclusion from a data set that cannot support one. Research design and data analysis both suffer, and since each criterion is a quarter of the marks, one planning error can cost eight of the twenty-four.

The single most valuable session in this component happens before any data is collected, and it is mostly arithmetic rather than biology: how many laboratory periods are actually available, how many measurements fit in one, what range of the independent variable that permits, and whether a secondary-data or database investigation would produce better evidence than a thin wet-lab one. Database investigations are legitimate and well suited to a tight practical budget, provided the data source is properly identified and the processing is the student's own.

On support boundaries: a tutor teaches and gives feedback. Worked examples of error handling, an explanation of what an evaluation has to weigh rather than list, criterion-by-criterion comments so the student can see which marks are unearned. No sentence of the report comes from anyone but the student, and every checkpoint leaves a written record the school may inspect. Anyone selling a finished investigation is selling a risk that lands on the candidate's Diploma, not on theirs.

sections.heading: The DP2 year counted backwards, and who sets each deadline
paragraphs: Almost every date that governs a Dubai Diploma student's second year is set by their own school rather than by the IB, and families consistently discover this too late. The school sets the investigation draft deadline, the final internal submission date, the mock examination window, and the point at which predicted grades are issued. Those four dates shape the autumn entirely, and they can be obtained in writing from the Diploma coordinator in September.

The IB sets the examination session and the release of results. This page does not publish those dates. Automated access to the IB's own pages is blocked, which means no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and publishing an unverified examination date on a tutoring page would be worse than publishing none. Your school's coordinator has the confirmed calendar, and it should be read from there.

What a family can do with the school-set dates is work backwards. If the investigation draft is due in the second week of November, data collection has to finish in October, which means the method has to be fixed in late September, which means the research question needs to be settled before the autumn half term. Written out like that, the autumn is tight but manageable. Discovered in November, it is neither.

The table lists the milestones with who controls each one and what should be finished by then. It is deliberately silent on specific dates, because the whole point is that your school's version is the one that matters and a generic calendar would mislead. Filling in the middle column from the coordinator's reply takes ten minutes and is the most useful planning any Diploma parent does.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Dubai private schools teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to deliver, and KHDA's requirements for these subjects applied from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a Diploma student this is not a footnote. It is several fixed periods a week that sit outside the six Diploma subjects and outside the core, and it is the first thing that determines which evenings are actually free.

KHDA also sets how these classes are organised. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, while non-Arab students are taught in the language of the school's licensed curriculum.

Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and the guidance advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which is why a tutor supporting Arabic works within the school's own material rather than bringing a parallel syllabus.

The practical consequence for Biology is scheduling, and the table makes it concrete. Map the fixed mandatory periods first, then place the Biology slot. Families who do this in September keep the same slot all year; families who do not find themselves renegotiating in October when the timetable settles. No competitor page reviewed in this market mentions these subjects at all, which is strange given how much of a Dubai student's week they occupy.
