process.title: Send the theme, the feeder course and the timetable
process.description: Three facts shape the first session: which theme the class is on, whether the student came from IGCSE or MYP, and when the bus actually arrives. All three go on the booking form so the free lesson is spent diagnosing rather than asking.

process.title: Free first lesson on a marked Paper 2 answer
process.description: The student answers one timed extended-response question beforehand. The free session is spent on that script, separating chemistry gaps from command-term faults from precision faults. The written note afterwards names which is costing most marks.

process.title: A six-question gap diagnostic
process.description: One question each on energetics, equilibrium, bonding, measurement, organic recall and calculation speed, marked against the Diploma scheme rather than an IGCSE one. The profile is usually uneven, which makes the plan obvious rather than general.

process.title: Alternate Paper 1 and Paper 2 work
process.description: Sessions alternate between timed recognition with data-based questions and written explanation marked link by link. Blending the two inside one lesson feels efficient and produces a student who is mediocre at both, so we keep them apart.

process.title: Review at six weeks with three outcomes
process.description: After around six sessions we compare the mark log and the calculation timings with the first script. The outcomes are continue, change focus, or stop. We write down which one and why, in language a parent can take to a school meeting.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1 is treated as two examinations
whyPoints.description: Thirty multiple-choice items against a clock and data-based processing are different skills with different practice regimes. Preparing for them separately is the single structural change that most often moves a Standard Level Paper 1 mark.

whyPoints.title: Calculation speed is measured, not described
whyPoints.description: The four mole-calculation families are drilled with a timing record a parent can read. A student who moves from four minutes to ninety seconds on a concentration question has gained marks on questions they never previously reached.

whyPoints.title: Precision marks are enforced on every answer
whyPoints.description: State symbols, balancing, units and significant figures are marked in every session rather than mentioned occasionally. They accumulate to more marks across a paper than most topic gaps and cost nothing to keep once the habit exists.

whyPoints.title: The feeder-course gap is tested rather than assumed
whyPoints.description: An IGCSE leaver and an MYP leaver arrive at Standard Level chemistry short of different things. Six questions marked against the Diploma scheme settles which, and avoids a term spent re-teaching material the student already holds.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on the investigation
whyPoints.description: Feedback is criterion-referenced, on the student's own drafts, with a dated version history kept. No research question, data processing or text comes from the tutor, because the student certifies authorship and carries the consequence.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level chemistry content will my child never be examined on at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Both levels cover the same six themes across structure and reactivity, and Higher Level adds depth inside them rather than new themes. The extensions a Standard Level student does not meet include detailed organic reaction mechanisms, buffer calculations and pH curves, entropy and spontaneity treated quantitatively, electrode potentials, rate equations derived from experimental data, and the fuller spectroscopy work. Higher Level also runs to roughly 240 taught hours against 150, with longer papers. The scientific investigation is identical at both levels: 24 marks, four criteria, 20 per cent of the grade and a 3,000-word cap, which makes it proportionally heavier work for a Standard Level student.

faqs.question: Are Paper 1A and Paper 1B marked differently?
faqs.answer: They behave differently, which matters more than the mark scheme wording. Part A is thirty multiple-choice items where credit is binary: there is no partial mark for good reasoning that reaches the wrong option, and the distractors are written to catch specific misconceptions. Part B is data-based and carries partial credit across steps, so showing processing is worth doing even when the final answer is wrong. The practical consequence is that Part A rewards speed and elimination while Part B rewards careful unit and significant-figure work. Preparing for them with one revision method produces a student who is competent at one half of the paper.

faqs.question: Which mole calculations come up most often at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Four families cover most numerical marks. Mass and moles worked across a balanced equation, which brings in the limiting reagent. Solutions, including concentration, dilution and titration arithmetic. Gases, using molar volume at stated conditions or the ideal gas relationship. And yield work, including percentage yield and atom economy. Each has a characteristic lost mark: the wrong limiting reagent, a volume unit out by a factor of a thousand, molar volume applied at conditions the question did not give, and an inverted comparison. The fix is timed volume rather than re-teaching, because the understanding is usually already there.

faqs.question: How should a student use the chemistry data booklet under time pressure?
faqs.answer: As a navigation tool first and a reference second. Practise finding bond enthalpy values, ionisation energies and the relationships for energy change before the examination, so the search takes seconds rather than half a minute. When a question looks unanswerable, scanning the relevant page for a relationship containing the quantity asked about often converts a blank start into a method mark. What the booklet will not supply is definitions, the conditions under which a relationship holds, state symbols, or the reasons behind a trend, and those are the parts worth revising. Mapping that boundary theme by theme takes one session and produces a one-page revision plan.

faqs.question: How much organic chemistry is in the Standard Level course?
faqs.answer: Less than students fear and assessed more strictly than they expect. The material is a finite list: homologous series and functional groups, systematic naming including branched chains, combustion, substitution for alkanes, addition for alkenes with conditions, oxidation of alcohols with the partial and full distinction, and ester formation. Each carries a reagent, a condition and a product, and examinations ask for all three with little partial credit available. Students arriving from IGCSE usually know the reactions and not the conditions. Mechanistic arrow-pushing belongs to Higher Level, so a Standard Level student spending weeks on it is preparing for the wrong course.

faqs.question: What is the gap between IGCSE chemistry and IB Chemistry SL?
faqs.answer: Four measurable areas. Energetics, because most IGCSE specifications treat enthalpy change qualitatively while Standard Level expects calculation with sign conventions and bond enthalpy data. Equilibrium, where Le Chatelier is described rather than quantified at IGCSE. Bonding, since the Diploma pushes further into shape, polarity and intermolecular forces inside explanation questions. And measurement, because uncertainty is rarely propagated through a calculation before the Diploma. Examination style is the fifth difference: extended explanation marked link by link is new. Six questions, one per area, marked against the Diploma scheme rather than an IGCSE one, usually produces a very uneven profile and an obvious plan.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Paper 2 answer get half the marks?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the writing is one step short of the mark scheme rather than because the chemistry is wrong. A two-mark explanation receives one linked statement where two were wanted. A trend is restated instead of having its cause named. An equation appears without state symbols, and the mark goes with them. A definition is paraphrased where the examination's own wording was required. None of that shows up in homework, which is marked generously, and all of it shows up on a script marked against the published scheme. Once the repeated omission is named it is usually fixable in a few weeks.

faqs.question: How long should the Standard Level scientific investigation be?
faqs.answer: The cap is 3,000 words and the common error is treating that as a target. Markers are not required to read beyond the limit, and over-length reports typically pad research design and squeeze evaluation, which costs marks under the criterion that is hardest to recover. A well-structured Standard Level report usually sits comfortably under the cap, because processed data, graphs and tables do the heavy lifting rather than prose. The useful discipline is to draft the evaluation first and the introduction last, since the evaluation is where specificity earns marks and where students run out of words if it is written at the end.

faqs.question: What are the four criteria on the chemistry investigation worth?
faqs.answer: Six marks each, for a total of 24, with the component worth 20 per cent of the final grade. Research design rewards a measurable research question with defined and controlled variables and a method someone else could repeat. Data analysis rewards processing that is shown, with uncertainty carried through rather than mentioned. Conclusion rewards an answer to the original question, justified by the processed data and compared with theory or an accepted value. Evaluation rewards specific, prioritised weaknesses with realistic improvements. The marking is identical at Standard and Higher Level, which surprises most Standard Level students when they read the criteria for the first time.

faqs.question: Can a Standard Level chemistry student still apply for pharmacy?
faqs.answer: At some institutions yes, at others no, and the only reliable source is each programme page for the current admissions cycle. Pharmacy requirements commonly specify chemistry with a second science, and the level required varies: several universities accept chemistry at Standard Level alongside Higher Level biology or mathematics, while others specify chemistry at Higher Level. Medicine and dentistry more often require Higher Level chemistry. The practical step is to check three named programmes before the DP1 subject-change window closes, then confirm with each admissions office. Requirements move between cycles, so a two-year-old forum post is not evidence, and no tutoring arrangement changes a published prerequisite.

faqs.question: How many Chemistry SL sessions does a Dubai student need before the May session?
faqs.answer: A useful commitment is eight to twelve weekly sessions with a marked timed question before each, which is long enough to produce a mark log showing movement and short enough to stop without a long contract. Students rebuilding calculation speed often need a four-session drill block on top, usually best placed in a summer or half-term week. In the final weeks, families commonly move to two or three sessions built entirely around full timed papers. More than three a week is rarely about teaching; it is usually a sleep problem, and we will say so rather than sell the hours.

faqs.question: Does Chemistry SL count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is a certificate-recognition process run by the Ministry of Education with requirements documented per curriculum, and it is not the same thing as a university prerequisite. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. For the American track, mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math, with English evidenced by IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing. No IB points figure should be quoted unless read on the Ministry's own site. No tutoring is required for the process.

faqs.question: What does Chemistry SL tuition cost per hour for a Dubai family?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour for budget online providers, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit including the tutor's travel, and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IB specialist. Monthly packages of about AED 799 for eight online sessions appear in the same market. Those are market figures, not our price list. For Standard Level chemistry specifically, the variable that changes value most is whether a marked script is included, because the faults that limit a grade are only visible on one.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to post-Iftar slots in Ramadan for a chemistry student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most Dubai families that is the better arrangement rather than a concession. School hours shorten during Ramadan and afternoon concentration drops, so the pattern that works is shorter sessions held after Iftar, kept at the same frequency or slightly higher, with daytime reserved for light review of taught material rather than new content. Full timed papers are better moved to the weekend for the month. We plan the Ramadan schedule a few weeks ahead rather than week by week, because the evening slots fill quickly across the whole student group and a late request usually means an unusable time.

faqs.question: What happens if no Chemistry SL tutor is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you before anything is booked and nothing is charged. Standard Level chemistry is widely taught across the UAE, so a complete absence of availability is uncommon; the usual problem is a specific recurring slot, such as 4.30pm twice weekly in term time, which cannot be filled locally. The options we offer are the nearest workable time, a weekend block, or a specialist in another time zone whose working hours overlap Gulf Standard Time. What we will not do is take the booking and allocate a tutor who has not taught this course at this level, which is how families end up paying for general science help.

dubai/ib-dp-chemistry-sl-tutor.closingHeading: One marked script tells you more than a term of lessons
dubai/ib-dp-chemistry-sl-tutor.closingBody: Before committing to any arrangement, have one timed Paper 2 question marked against the published scheme. It will show whether the problem is chemistry, command terms, or precision, and those three need different lessons. The free first session with an IB DP chemistry SL tutor in Dubai is spent on exactly that script, followed by a written note you can take to the school. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the school timetable and mandatory subject periods. If the note says a four-session calculation block is all your child needs, that is what it will say.

intro.heading: The first question is not who to hire. It is which syllabus your child is on
paragraphs: Diploma Computer Science has been through a syllabus revision, and that single fact causes more wasted tutoring money in this subject than anything else. A cohort sitting one guide and a tutor teaching from another will spend weeks on topics that cannot appear, while the topics that will appear go untouched. Before you pay anybody, ask your school's DP coordinator one question in writing: which subject guide does my child's cohort sit, and what is the first assessment year for it. Then check the component structure for that guide on ibo.org rather than trusting any summary, including this one.

What follows on this page is the structure that has long governed the subject, described so a parent can recognise the shape of it, with an explicit instruction to verify every weighting and duration against the guide your child actually follows. Treating the page as authoritative on the current cohort's numbers would be exactly the mistake the previous paragraph warns about. Treating it as a map of what the subject assesses, and of how it goes wrong, is what it is for.

The second reason this subject goes wrong is a mismatch of competence. Computer Science looks like the most hireable subject on the Diploma because Dubai has a large technology workforce and a great many people who can program well. Very few of them have taught this course. Diploma Computer Science is mostly not a programming qualification: it examines system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks, and computational thinking, with abstract data structures, resource management and control added at Higher Level, plus an option topic the school selects. A capable software engineer with no knowledge of the guide will teach your child to write better code and will not move the grade.

The third reason is the internal assessment, which is unlike any other in the Diploma. The student develops a product for an identified client with a real need, and the marks are distributed across planning, a design overview, development, a video demonstrating functionality and extensibility, and an evaluation. Most of the available marks are not for the code working. They are for documenting decisions, justifying techniques and evidencing a process. Students who build an impressive application and document it thinly lose more marks than students who build something modest and document it properly.

On delivery: tutoring for Dubai families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or elsewhere in the UAE — sending a tutor to a residence is part of our India service only. For this subject in particular the online format is the natural one: the work happens in an editor on a screen, screen-sharing and a shared file are closer to how the subject is actually practised than two people looking at one laptop, and every version of a student's code and documentation is preserved rather than lost between sessions.

dubai/ib-dp-computer-science-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Students arrive at Diploma Computer Science from four different directions, and the direction predicts the first failure. These entries describe what each route leaves missing.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Computer Science is a group 4 subject at Standard or Higher Level. The core covers system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks, and computational thinking with problem-solving and programming. Higher Level adds abstract data structures, resource management and control, and extends the school's chosen option. Assessment combines written papers with a client-facing internal assessment. Verify current components and weightings in the guide your cohort sits.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Computer Science is often the smallest group 4 cohort in a school, sometimes fewer students than Physics has in a single class. A small cohort means less internal peer support, a teacher who may also cover another subject, and a real possibility that the option topic was chosen for timetable reasons rather than for the group's strengths.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Design is the usual feeder, and its design cycle — inquiry and analysis, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating — maps surprisingly well onto the Diploma internal assessment's structure. What MYP does not provide is the theory: students arriving from Design are comfortable documenting a build and unfamiliar with logic gates, addressing, protocols and operating-system concepts.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running MYP to the end of Year 11 send Computer Science students into DP1 with good project habits and no examination experience in the subject. The predictable outcome is a strong first draft of a product and a weak first theory test, which parents often misread as the opposite of what it is.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Computer Science works well inside the Career-related Programme, where a technology-related career study sits alongside DP courses and the four compulsory components. The DP course is assessed identically. The pressure point is that the reflective project and the client-facing internal assessment both require sustained independent documentation, and schools usually deadline them in the same term.
programmes.countryNote: A handful of Dubai schools offer CP with a technology pathway. Students sometimes assume their career-related work and their Computer Science product can share a client or a codebase. They cannot: each component must be independently produced, and overlap is an academic-honesty question rather than an efficiency.

programmes.name: IGCSE Computer Science or ICT into DP1
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 and Edexcel 4CP0 both give a genuine head start on data representation, logic and the basics of architecture. IGCSE ICT does not — it is an applications qualification and shares little with the Diploma beyond vocabulary. The gap from 0478 into DP1 is depth rather than content: the same topics are examined with more precision and more linkage between them.
programmes.countryNote: Because UK-curriculum schools account for 37% of Dubai private-school enrolment, the 0478 route is common here. A student who scored a grade 8 at 0478 and then struggles in DP1 is usually meeting two new things at once: the IB's own pseudocode notation, and questions that ask them to justify a choice rather than describe a feature.

dubai/ib-dp-computer-science-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Computer Science is the subject of this page. The rest of the list is what Dubai Diploma students most often take alongside it, described by the specific overlap or clash each creates.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Core topics covering system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks, and computational thinking with problem-solving and programming. Higher Level adds abstract data structures, resource management and control, plus extended option content. Assessment combines written papers — including a case-study paper at Higher Level — with a client-facing internal assessment. Confirm current structure in the guide your cohort sits.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The pairing most computer science degrees expect. The genuine overlaps are logic, sequences, recursion and proof, all of which support abstract data structures at Higher Level. Many UK and European computing programmes specify AA rather than AI, so the choice should be checked against the named degree before DP1 subject selection closes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A workable partner, with statistics and modelling that suit data-oriented work and the modelling and simulation option. The risk is a university prerequisite: a student intending to read computer science at a mathematically demanding department should verify whether AI satisfies it, because several departments state AA explicitly.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The most common group 4 companion for Computer Science students in Dubai. Circuits and digital logic genuinely overlap with computer organisation. The clash is workload: Physics carries its own internal assessment, and a student doing both faces two substantial independent investigations whose school deadlines frequently fall within the same fortnight.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Shares the client-and-brief logic that the Computer Science internal assessment depends on, and trains the habit of justifying a design decision against a user need. Students taking both usually write stronger planning and evaluation sections, because the discipline of writing for an identified client is already familiar.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: Covers the social and ethical ground that Computer Science examines only in passing — data, platforms, algorithms in society. Useful context for the evaluation sections of the internal assessment, but it is not a substitute for any part of the Computer Science course, and students sometimes assume otherwise when choosing options.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A frequent third choice for students heading towards technology management or finance. The transferable skill is evaluation under a command term, which Computer Science also demands in its extended-response questions. The habit that does not transfer is length: a Computer Science answer rewards precision over a developed essay.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: More relevant to this subject than students expect, because the internal assessment is a documentation task. The marks sit in writing that explains a decision clearly to a reader who was not present. Students who can write a precise paragraph score better on planning and evaluation without writing any more code.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: A common pairing for students building interfaces, and the one place where portfolio habits help: documenting iterations with evidence is exactly what the development criterion rewards. The caution is time, since both subjects assess a substantial independently produced body of work in the same year.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements. These take real timetable space, which is the practical reason a Computer Science plan has to be built around the week a student actually has.

sections.heading: What this search means, and the check to run before paying anybody
paragraphs: An IB DP Computer Science home tutor in Dubai, in the market's own language, is a specialist working one-to-one with a Diploma Computer Science student at a time the family chooses. The conventional version of that is a tutor who drives to a residence. IB Gram teaches the same course one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are part of our India service only and are not sold anywhere in the UAE.

Before format or price, run the syllabus check. Diploma Computer Science has been revised, which means two different component structures exist in circulation, and online material does not reliably say which one it describes. Ask your school's DP coordinator, in writing, which subject guide your child's cohort sits and what its first assessment year is. Then read that guide's assessment outline on ibo.org. Every weighting, duration and word limit should come from that document and not from a tutoring page, including this one.

The reason this matters so much here is that Computer Science has more apparent supply than real supply. Dubai has a substantial technology workforce, so a search for a tutor returns many people who can program professionally. Programming is one part of this course and not the part most students lose marks on. The core examines system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and computational thinking, with further topics at Higher Level and an option topic chosen by the school. A capable engineer who has never read the guide will improve your child's code and leave the grade where it was.

So the useful first conversation is diagnostic rather than commercial. What did the last theory test look like by topic. Which option is the school teaching. Has the internal assessment client been identified, and is the problem real. Which guide is the cohort on. Four answers, and they determine entirely what a plan should contain. The sections below set out what each component assesses and where marks actually go, so a parent can hold any tutor to the same questions.

sections.heading: What each component assesses, and what it rewards
paragraphs: Computer Science assessment combines written papers with an internal assessment that is a product made for a client. The written papers test the core topics and, at Higher Level, the further topics and extended option content, with a separate case-study paper at Higher Level based on material released in advance. The internal assessment is documentation-heavy and marked against published criteria.

The distinction that matters most for tutoring is what each component rewards. The papers reward precision and justification: naming the correct protocol layer, explaining why a particular data structure suits a particular operation, tracing an algorithm and stating its output exactly. They do not reward general technical fluency, and an answer that demonstrates wide knowledge while missing the specific demand of the command term scores poorly.

The Higher Level case-study paper rewards reading. The material is released in advance, so the preparation is research into a named scenario and its technical vocabulary, not revision of the syllabus in general. It is the component where a well-prepared student gains most relative to an able but unprepared one, and the component most often left until the term of the examination because it feels like something that can be read quickly.

The internal assessment rewards documented process. Marks are spread across planning, a design overview, the development work, a video demonstrating functionality and extensibility, and an evaluation. Most of them are not awarded for the product working. They are awarded for showing how decisions were reached and why techniques were chosen. Always confirm the current component list, weightings and durations against the guide your child's cohort sits, since the subject has been revised.

sections.heading: The core topics, and where marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Each core topic fails in a characteristic way, and a parent reading a theory test by topic can usually see which one is happening. System fundamentals loses marks to vagueness about stakeholders, change management and the difference between a requirement and a feature. Students who find this topic unexciting treat it as common sense, and it is examined as content with specific vocabulary.

Computer organisation loses marks in the detail of the fetch-execute cycle, the roles of specific registers, the purpose of cache levels and the difference between primary and secondary storage in operational terms. The recurring error is a student who can describe what a component is and cannot say what happens without it, which is the form the question usually takes.

Networks is where confident students are most often wrong with conviction. Layers get conflated, a protocol is named at the wrong level, and the difference between packet switching behaviour and application behaviour is blurred. Questions about transmission media, compression and the trade-offs of wireless in a specific scenario are answered with general observations instead of the named constraint the scenario supplied.

Computational thinking and programming is the topic families expect to be strongest and is frequently mid-band, because the examination tests it in the IB's own notation. A student who writes fluent Python but has not practised the pseudocode conventions used in the papers will lose marks on tracing tasks, array and collection handling, and on writing an algorithm in the expected form. That is a notation problem rather than a programming problem, and it is fixable in a handful of sessions once it is correctly identified.

sections.heading: The internal assessment is a client project, not a coding project
paragraphs: This is where Dubai families most often spend money in the wrong place. The internal assessment requires the student to identify a client with a genuine need, agree success criteria, design a solution, develop it with documented decisions, demonstrate its functionality and extensibility on video, and evaluate it honestly against the criteria agreed at the start. The marks are distributed across those stages, and the largest share sits in the development documentation rather than in the product.

The consequence is counter-intuitive and worth saying plainly: a modest product documented rigorously outscores an ambitious product documented thinly, every time. A student who builds an attendance system with three features, justifies each technique chosen, evidences the development with annotated extracts and evaluates it against the client's stated criteria will beat a student who builds something far more impressive and writes two pages about it.

The client is the other common failure. A client has to be real enough to state a need, agree criteria and respond to the finished product. A friend who agrees to be called the client, or a hypothetical business invented for the purpose, undermines the planning and evaluation sections because there is nothing genuine to plan against or evaluate with. The first session of any internal assessment work here tests the client and the problem before a single line of code is discussed.

On the boundary: a tutor may teach techniques, explain the criteria, test whether a client and problem will carry the assessment, read documentation the student wrote and score it, ask why a technique was chosen, and point out that a section asserts a decision without justifying it. A tutor may not write code into the assessed project, write or rewrite documentation, or produce the video. Under IB rules that is malpractice and the sanction falls on the candidate. Confirm the current criteria, mark allocations and video requirements in the guide your cohort sits.

sections.heading: The pseudocode problem, and why good programmers lose marks
paragraphs: This section exists because it accounts for a specific and recoverable loss that almost nothing written for parents mentions. Diploma Computer Science examines algorithms in a notation the IB defines for the purpose, not in Python, Java or JavaScript. Students are asked to trace given algorithms and state outputs exactly, and to construct algorithms in the expected form. A student fluent in a real language who has never practised that notation will make errors that have nothing to do with their understanding.

The errors are predictable. Loop boundaries are misread, so a trace is off by one iteration throughout. Array indexing conventions are assumed from the student's own language rather than read from the question. Collection handling methods are used in forms the notation does not define. Output is stated in a shape the question did not ask for, which costs the mark even when the logic is correct. And a constructed algorithm is written in the student's language of habit, which is not what was requested.

The fix is mechanical and quick. A student needs to practise tracing in the notation until the conventions are automatic, then practise constructing in it, keeping a table of their own recurring slips. Six to eight short exercises usually settle it. What makes this loss persistent is misdiagnosis: a parent sees a strong coder with a mediocre mark and concludes the child needs more programming, which is the one intervention that will not help.

There is a related and separate point about the subject's command terms. 'Trace', 'construct', 'outline', 'describe', 'explain', 'evaluate' and 'discuss' ask for different shapes of answer, and the marks follow the shape. A student who explains when asked to outline wastes time; one who describes when asked to explain loses marks. Practising against the mark allocation, rather than against the topic, is what converts knowledge into a grade in this subject.

sections.heading: Higher Level: further topics and the case study
paragraphs: Higher Level adds content that students consistently describe as the hardest part of the course, and it is also where a specialist tutor is most clearly worth the difference in rate. Abstract data structures covers stacks, queues, linked lists, trees and their traversals, with recursion running through the topic. The examination asks for traces, for the choice of structure to suit a named operation, and for a justification of that choice — not for an implementation.

Resource management covers how an operating system allocates processor time, memory and devices, including scheduling, paging and the consequences of contention. Control covers the use of computers to monitor and control physical systems, with sensors, feedback and the distinction between centralised and distributed control. Both topics lose marks to a general answer about computers where a specific mechanism in a specific scenario was required.

The Higher Level case-study paper is a different kind of preparation entirely. A scenario is released in advance and introduces technical vocabulary that the paper then examines. Preparing properly means researching the named technologies, building a glossary, and practising questions in the scenario's own language months before the examination. It is the single component where preparation most reliably converts into marks, and in Dubai it is also the one most often postponed, because reading a case study feels like something that can be done later.

Recursion deserves its own note, because it is where the largest Higher Level losses cluster. Students can usually recite the definition and cannot reliably trace a recursive call stack under examination conditions. The practice that works is physical: writing out each call, its parameters and its return value in a table, repeatedly, until the shape becomes familiar. Confirm the current Higher Level topic list and case-study arrangements in the guide your cohort sits.

sections.heading: The option topic, and why it changes everything about revision
paragraphs: The option is the part of this course parents are least aware of and that most affects what revision should contain. The school chooses one option topic for the group, it is examined, and at Higher Level it is extended. A tutor who does not know which option a school teaches cannot plan revision, because a quarter of the examinable content is determined by that choice.

The options differ substantially in character. A databases option is formal and vocabulary-heavy, with normalisation, transactions and data integrity. A modelling and simulation option is mathematical, suiting students on the Applications and Interpretation route. A web science option is conceptual, dealing with the architecture of the web, protocols, search and the social dimension. An object-oriented programming option is the one that most rewards students who already program, and the only one where coding fluency converts directly into marks.

Two practical consequences follow. The first is for subject choice: a student with a clear preference should find out which option their school teaches before confirming Computer Science, because that choice is not theirs to make afterwards. The second is for hiring: ask any tutor which option they have taught, and ask for a specific question from it in the trial session. A tutor who has taught the core but not your school's option is a partial fit, which is worth knowing before rather than after.

sections.heading: Why Computer Science specialists cost more in Dubai, and how to test one
paragraphs: Dubai's published tutoring rates are broad: market figures for 2026 run from roughly AED 33-65 an hour at the budget online end, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65, through a qualified-tutor band where Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200, to an IB specialist band that Bestimate's rate table puts at AED 200-450 and above, and premium figures such as BartyED's AED 650. Those are market rates published by those providers, not IB Gram's prices; our arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a plan quoted afterwards.

Computer Science sits at the scarce end of that market for a reason that is specific rather than general. The subject looks over-supplied because Dubai has many skilled programmers, and it is in fact under-supplied, because the examinable content is architecture, networks, computational thinking, the Higher Level further topics and a school-selected option. The overlap between people who can program professionally and people who have taught this guide is narrower than any other Diploma subject.

That gap is testable before any money is spent, and the table below is built as a hiring test rather than as a price list. Each row describes a profile a Dubai family will actually encounter in a search, what it can genuinely teach, and the specific question that exposes the gap. Put those questions in the free trial session; the answers are more informative than any credential list.

One caution on credentials. Do not accept 'IB examiner' as a qualification unless the status can be evidenced, and understand that examiner status would give no access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content in any case. Research for this project found competitor pages making examiner claims alongside self-asserted star ratings and inconsistent prices. A tutor who can answer a specific option question correctly has told you more than a profile page can.

sections.heading: Online or in the room, for a subject done on a screen
paragraphs: Most subjects make this a genuine trade-off. Computer Science makes it narrower, because the work already happens on a computer. A tutor in the room and a student share one laptop and one keyboard, which is a worse arrangement for code than two screens and a shared file. That is not a marketing claim; it is how the subject is practised professionally.

The advantages of an in-home tutor are still real and worth naming honestly. A person in the room reads disengagement faster, and for a student who closes down the moment a video call starts, presence matters more than any technical convenience. IB Gram does not sell that format in the UAE — a tutor travelling to a residence is part of our India operation only — so a family who concludes they need somebody present should hire locally and expect the in-home market band of roughly AED 180-350 and up to AED 500 independently, which absorbs a cross-city journey.

What online gives this subject specifically: a shared editor where the student types and the tutor questions, so no code is ever authored by the tutor in an assessed project. Version history that survives between sessions, which matters enormously for internal assessment documentation. Screen-sharing for tracing algorithms line by line. Recording with consent, which students use heavily when revising the Higher Level further topics. And a tutor selected for having taught the school's option rather than for living in the same community.

sections.heading: Academic honesty with code, libraries and AI assistants
paragraphs: This subject has an academic-honesty problem the others do not, because code can be obtained instantly and because generative tools will write it on request. The rules are not ambiguous even where the technology is new: work submitted for assessment must be the student's own, and any material from another source — a library, a tutorial, a forum answer, a generated suggestion — must be acknowledged in the documentation. Failure to do so is malpractice, and the sanction falls on the candidate.

The practical standard we work to is that the student types every line of their assessed project and can explain every line of it. Using a library is normally legitimate and sometimes necessary; using it without documenting what it does and why it was chosen is both an honesty problem and a direct loss of development marks, since the criterion rewards justified technique choices. Copying a block of code from a tutorial without attribution is the same failure in a worse form.

On generative assistants specifically: a student who cannot explain a function they submitted has a problem regardless of where it came from, because the development documentation requires justification and the evaluation requires honest judgement about the solution. Schools and the IB set their own policies on acknowledging such tools, and those policies change — ask the school's academic-honesty coordinator what the current requirement is for your child's cohort and follow it exactly, in writing, in the documentation.

What a tutor may do is wide and genuinely useful. Teach techniques using separate examples. Review code the student wrote and ask what a line does. Point out that a function is doing three things and ask whether it should. Score documentation against the criteria. Test whether the client and problem will carry the assessment. What a tutor may not do is type into the assessed project, supply code to be pasted, write or rewrite documentation, or produce the video. We also do not reproduce or distribute official past papers, mark schemes or subject guides; those are referenced and linked to the board's own site.

sections.heading: Universities, mathematics and UAE equivalency
paragraphs: Most Computer Science enquiries from Dubai have a destination attached, and the destination usually imposes a mathematics condition rather than a Computer Science one. Several computing departments in the UK and Europe specify Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, sometimes at Higher Level, and a number do not require Diploma Computer Science at all. A student choosing the subject to satisfy a prerequisite should read the named programme's own stated requirements before DP1 selection closes, because the assumption that Computer Science is the required subject is wrong as often as it is right.

Within the subject itself, the Higher Level further topics are the ones that most resemble early undergraduate work. Abstract data structures and recursion appear in first-year computing courses almost everywhere, so a student who secures them is buying more than a grade. That is a reasonable argument for prioritising those topics over option revision if time is short, though it is a judgement to make with the school rather than against it.

For families intending to use the Diploma inside the UAE, equivalency and attestation of secondary certificates is a Ministry of Education process. IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee it, and no tutoring is required for it. For the British track the published requirements are specific: five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade.

No IB points threshold for equivalency is published on this page, because none was read on the Ministry's own pages during research for this project. That is deliberate. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly, and treat any site stating an IB figure without citing the Ministry with caution — one competitor already publishes an incorrect subject count for the British track, which is the kind of error that propagates.

faqs.question: Which IB Computer Science syllabus is my child actually sitting?
faqs.answer: Ask the DP coordinator in writing, because Diploma Computer Science has been revised and two component structures circulate online without being clearly labelled. The question to ask is: which subject guide does this cohort sit, and what is its first assessment year. Then read that guide's assessment outline on ibo.org. This matters more in this subject than any other, because a tutor working from the wrong guide will teach topics that cannot appear while leaving examinable content untouched. No tutoring page, including this one, should be treated as authoritative on your cohort's weightings.

faqs.question: My child codes well but scores badly in Computer Science. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always one of two things. Either the losses are in the theory topics — system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks — which are examined as content with specific vocabulary and are not helped by programming ability. Or the losses are in notation: the examination tests algorithms in the IB's own pseudocode conventions rather than in Python or Java, and a fluent programmer who has not practised those conventions makes off-by-one trace errors and assumes indexing rules from their own language. Both are fixable, and neither is fixed by more programming practice.

faqs.question: Why does the option topic matter so much when choosing a tutor?
faqs.answer: Because the school selects one option, it is examined, it is extended at Higher Level, and a substantial share of the examinable content depends on which one was chosen. A tutor who knows the core but not your school's option is a partial fit. The options differ in character: databases is formal and vocabulary-heavy, modelling and simulation is mathematical, web science is conceptual, and object-oriented programming is the one where existing coding fluency converts directly into marks. Ask any tutor which option they have taught, and ask them a question from it in the trial.

faqs.question: Which parts of the internal assessment actually carry the marks?
faqs.answer: Documented process more than a working product. Marks are spread across planning with a real client and agreed success criteria, a design overview, development with justified technique choices, a video evidencing functionality and extensibility, and an honest evaluation against the original criteria. A modest product documented rigorously outscores an ambitious product documented thinly. Students routinely invert this, building something impressive and writing two pages about it. Confirm the current criteria and mark allocations in the subject guide your child's cohort sits.

faqs.question: How do we know the internal assessment client is good enough?
faqs.answer: A client has to be real enough to state a need, agree success criteria at the start and respond to the finished product. A friend who agrees to be labelled the client, or an invented business, undermines both the planning and the evaluation sections, because there is nothing genuine to plan against or measure afterwards. The first session of any internal assessment work should test the client and the problem before development is discussed at all. A weak client is the most expensive mistake available in this component, because it is discovered late.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's code without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach techniques on separate examples, review code the student wrote and ask what each part does, point out that a function is doing three jobs, and score documentation against the criteria. A tutor may not type into the assessed project, supply code to be pasted, write or rewrite documentation, or produce the video. Our sessions run in a shared editor where the student types throughout, which makes the boundary evidenceable through version history rather than merely stated. Malpractice sanctions fall on the candidate.

faqs.question: What are the rules about using AI tools on Computer Science coursework?
faqs.answer: Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own, and material from any other source — a library, a tutorial, a forum answer, a generated suggestion — must be acknowledged in the documentation. Policies on acknowledging generative tools are set by the IB and by schools and they change, so ask your school's academic-honesty coordinator what the current requirement is for your cohort and follow it exactly in writing. Practically, a student who cannot explain a submitted function has a problem whatever its origin, because the development criterion requires justification.

faqs.question: What is in the Higher Level content that Standard Level students do not sit?
faqs.answer: Higher Level adds further topic groups covering abstract data structures — stacks, queues, linked lists, trees and their traversals, with recursion throughout — plus resource management and control, and it extends the school's chosen option. There is also a case-study paper based on material released in advance. Students consistently report the further topics as the hardest part of the course, and recursion is where the largest losses cluster, because tracing a call stack under examination conditions is a practised skill rather than a known definition. Confirm the current Higher Level content in your cohort's guide.

faqs.question: How should a student prepare for the Higher Level case study?
faqs.answer: By researching it months in advance, not by reading it. The scenario is released ahead of the examination and introduces technical vocabulary the paper then examines, so useful preparation means investigating the named technologies, building a glossary, and practising questions inside the scenario's own language. It is the component where preparation converts into marks most reliably, and in Dubai it is also the one most often postponed, because reading a case study feels like a quick job that can wait. It is not a quick job.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to come to our home in Dubai for a Computer Science subject?
faqs.answer: No, and for this subject in particular there is little to gain from it. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; a tutor travelling to a residence is part of our India service only. Lessons for Dubai families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time with screen-sharing and a shared editor, which is closer to how the subject is actually practised than two people sharing one laptop. Version history survives between sessions, which matters for internal assessment documentation. Families who need a person in the room should hire locally.

faqs.question: What does Computer Science tutoring cost in Dubai, and why is it at the higher end?
faqs.answer: Published 2026 market figures run from AED 33-65 an hour at the budget online end, through a qualified-tutor band where Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200, to an IB specialist band of AED 200-450 and above in Bestimate's rate table, with premium figures such as BartyED's AED 650. Computer Science sits at the scarce end because the overlap between people who program professionally and people who have taught this guide, its Higher Level topics and a specific option is narrower than in any other Diploma subject. Those are market rates, not ours.

faqs.question: Is Computer Science a required subject for a computing degree?
faqs.answer: Often not. Many computing departments in the UK and Europe specify a mathematics route — frequently Analysis and Approaches, sometimes at Higher Level — and do not require Diploma Computer Science itself. Some do. The only reliable method is reading the named programme's own stated entry requirements before DP1 subject selection closes, rather than assuming the subject title answers the question. Students who take Computer Science because they enjoy it are making a good decision; students taking it solely to satisfy an unverified prerequisite sometimes are not.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Computer Science student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which of the three failures is happening, which is why the first conversation asks for a marked theory test. A notation problem is typically six to eight short exercises inside a few weeks. A core-theory gap across two topics is usually a block of eight to ten sessions. Option revision started late needs a term. Internal assessment supervision is three or four passes per section spread across DP1 and DP2. Mixing all of these into one weekly session produces slow progress, so a plan sequences them instead.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around Dubai school timings and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the pattern varies by area. Communities with schools inside them take 16:30 slots; Marina and JLT families with long northbound commutes usually want 18:30 or later. During Ramadan the UAE school day shortens and sessions move to post-Iftar timing rather than pausing, because a paused DP2 spring does not return the weeks it loses. Weekend mornings are popular for internal assessment work, which needs an uninterrupted block rather than an hour squeezed between other commitments.

faqs.question: What if the tutor turns out to know programming but not the course?
faqs.answer: That is the specific risk in this subject, and the free trial exists to catch it. Ask three questions in that session: which option does my child's school teach and what does it examine; explain the fetch-execute cycle to a mark allocation; and write this algorithm in the notation the examination uses. A tutor who hesitates on all three is a capable programmer rather than a Diploma specialist. Tell us and we will propose a different tutor; the trial is free, takes no card details and enrols you in nothing.

intro.heading: The work in this subject leaves a trail, and the trail is what to inspect
paragraphs: Computer Science is the Diploma subject where parents most often feel locked out. A student says the program works, the screen shows something moving, and there is no obvious way for a non-programmer to tell whether that represents a 3 or a 6. The useful response is not to learn to code. It is to realise that this subject generates more inspectable evidence than almost any other, and to ask for it.

There are four trails. The first is the record of tasks and the design documentation for the developed solution, which exists as a dated set of documents and which the assessment criteria reward directly. The second is the version history of the code itself, which shows when work happened and in what increments; a solution that appears in two commits the week before the deadline tells a story, and so does one that grows across forty. The third is the recording that demonstrates the solution's functionality against the criteria the student agreed with their client. The fourth is a stack of marked written-paper scripts, where pseudocode answers and trace tables are either right or wrong in a way anyone can see once the marking is annotated.

That is why this page is built around artefacts rather than around claims about teaching quality. A tutor who produces those four things across a half-term has given a family something to judge. A tutor who reports that the student is progressing nicely has given them nothing, and in a subject where the parent cannot independently verify the work, that gap matters more than it does in History or Economics.

The teaching reality in Dubai adds a second reason to care. Computer Science is offered by a minority of the emirate's IB schools, and where it is offered the cohort is often small, sometimes fewer than a dozen students across both levels. Small cohorts mean limited individual code review, and they mean a student with a particular architectural problem in their solution may be the only person in the building with that problem. Live-video one-to-one is a direct answer to that, because the tutor is chosen for Diploma Computer Science depth rather than for proximity to Al Barsha or Mirdif.

What follows sets out the assessment shape, what each documentation stage must evidence, why strong coders routinely lose marks that weak coders do not, how the Higher Level case study should be read, where academic honesty sits now that code generation tools are on every student's machine, and what the Dubai market charges with the sources for each figure. There is also a note on confirming the guide version, because the Computer Science course was revised recently and a student working from an older set of past papers can waste a term on content that has moved.

dubai/ib-dp-computer-science-online-tuto.programmesIntro: Computer Science arrives in the Diploma by three different routes in Dubai, and the route decides what the first block of tuition should repair. A student from IGCSE Computer Science has notation habits; a student from MYP Design has project habits; a student from neither has both to build.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Design assesses inquiry and analysis, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating, which maps unusually well onto the Diploma's developed solution. Students from this route tend to document instinctively and to under-estimate the algorithmic content of the written papers. Their first gap is almost always pseudocode notation and trace discipline rather than project management.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's continuum schools feed MYP Design students into Diploma Computer Science, and in several of them the MYP Design teacher is also the Diploma Computer Science teacher. That continuity is an advantage in the solution and a blind spot in the written papers, which is where outside marking tends to be most useful.

programmes.name: IGCSE Computer Science as the pre-Diploma route
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 covers data representation, networks, hardware, software, security, databases, algorithm design and programming. Students arriving from it have real notation fluency and a habit of short, closed questions. The Diploma asks for extended reasoning about system design and for a sustained independent project, which is a different discipline entirely.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools hold the largest share of Dubai's private enrolment, so 0478 is the commonest feeder into Diploma Computer Science in the emirate. The reliable early intervention for this group is extended-response practice, because the IGCSE habit of answering in three lines caps marks on Diploma questions worth considerably more.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Computer Science
programmes.description: Written papers covering system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks, computational thinking and abstract data structures, plus an internally assessed developed solution built for a real client with documented planning, design, development and evaluation. Higher Level extends the content and adds a paper based on a pre-released case study. The course was revised recently, so check which guide the cohort follows.
programmes.countryNote: Computer Science is offered by a minority of Dubai's IB Diploma schools, and cohorts are frequently small. That produces two effects a family should expect: fewer classmates to debug alongside, and a teacher splitting limited code-review time across students whose solutions share no common architecture.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and language development. Computer Science appears inside technology-oriented CP pathways, and the assessment demand for that single Diploma course is identical to the full Diploma version, developed solution included.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Dubai schools run CP with Computer Science inside it, so a student on that route may have no cohort at all for the subject. One-to-one over video is less a preference than a practical necessity there, and the solution supervision is the part that most needs an external second reader.

dubai/ib-dp-computer-science-online-tuto.subjectsIntro: Computer Science students in Dubai usually carry a mathematics commitment and often a science. The notes below say what each neighbouring subject assesses, because that determines whether one tutor can reasonably hold two of them.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Written papers on system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks, computational thinking and abstract data structures, plus a developed solution for a real client. Higher Level adds a case-study paper. Marks are lost in documentation and in pseudocode notation far more often than in programming ability.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most computer science degrees expect. Algebraic manipulation, sequences, calculus and proof. Higher Level Paper 3 rewards extended problem solving, which is the closest thing in the Diploma to the reasoning an abstract data structures question demands.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and matrices, with graph theory at Higher Level. Useful alongside Computer Science for data-oriented solutions, but worth checking against target university entry requirements, which frequently specify Analysis and Approaches for computing degrees.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity and fields, with an experimental internal assessment. Shares with Computer Science the discipline of quantitative reasoning under timed conditions, and competes with it directly for internal-deadline time in DP2.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Assessed partly through a design project with staged documentation, which is procedurally similar to the Computer Science solution. Students taking both meet two large documented projects in the same academic year, and the scheduling collision is predictable enough to plan around.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: Replaces the older information technology course, covering data, computing, networks and the social impact of technology through written papers and an inquiry project. Less programming, more argument. Some students switch into it from Computer Science in DP1, which is a decision worth taking early rather than late.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Written papers plus a scientific investigation. Appears alongside Computer Science in medicine-adjacent and engineering-adjacent subject combinations, and brings its own internal deadline into the same DP2 term.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Extended response and data response papers plus a portfolio of short commentaries. A common fourth subject for Computer Science students in Dubai; the transferable habit is quantitative reading of supplied data rather than answering from memory.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis, comparative essay and oral components. The relevant transfer for Computer Science is extended written structure, which is exactly what the longer written-paper questions reward and what IGCSE-trained students most often lack.

sections.heading: The four artefacts a Dubai parent can inspect without reading a line of code
paragraphs: Begin with the direct answer. A Diploma Computer Science student in Dubai should be accumulating four kinds of evidence, and a parent can interrogate all four without any technical knowledge: the dated documentation for the developed solution, the version history of the code, the recording that demonstrates functionality against agreed criteria, and a file of marked written-paper scripts. Each one answers a different question about whether the work is real and whether it is improving.

The documentation is the easiest to check and the most predictive. The developed solution is assessed across staged components, and a student who has a client, a written set of success criteria, a design record and a development log is on track procedurally even if the code is unfinished. A student with four hundred lines of code and no documentation is in trouble, because the marks are allocated to the documented process at least as much as to the artefact. Ask to see the documents, note the dates on them, and ask what changed between versions.

Version history carries information that nothing else does. A solution that grows across dozens of small commits over several months reflects sustained independent work. One that appears in two large commits in the final fortnight invites a question, and it is better for a family to ask that question in February than for a school to ask it at submission. This is not about suspicion of the student; it is about the fact that incremental development is also better practice and produces a better solution.

The functionality recording and the marked scripts complete the picture. The recording should show the solution doing the things the success criteria said it would do, in order, which is a test a parent can apply directly. The marked scripts show whether pseudocode notation and trace discipline are improving, and because those are mechanically right or wrong, a parent reading annotated marking can see movement without understanding the content. Delivery of all this work for UAE families is live video, one student at a time; nothing on this page involves a tutor travelling to an address in Dubai.

sections.heading: The written papers: pseudocode, traces, and the questions that are not about programming
paragraphs: A persistent misconception sinks capable Dubai students every year: that the written papers test programming. They do not test programming in any named language. They test computational thinking expressed in the examination's own pseudocode notation, alongside substantial content on system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and abstract data structures that involves no code at all. A student who has written games in Python since Year 8 can still sit in the middle bands on these papers, and usually knows it before anyone tells them.

Notation is the first mechanical loss. The examination uses a defined pseudocode with its own conventions for loops, conditionals, input, output and collection access. A student who answers in Java syntax, or in Python's indentation-based style, is relying on an examiner's goodwill rather than on the mark scheme. This is trivially fixable in two or three sessions and it is almost never fixed by a student working alone, because nothing in the self-taught programming world rewards learning a notation nobody runs.

Trace questions are the second. A trace table asks for the state of every relevant variable at every iteration, written out. Strong programmers hate them, because they can see the answer and resent showing the steps, and so they write the final value and lose most of the marks. The marks are in the intermediate rows. Practising traces by hand, slowly, with the tutor watching the student write each row, breaks that habit faster than any amount of explanation.

The third loss is structural. Extended-response questions on networks, system design or data structures reward organised argument: the concept named, the mechanism explained, the trade-off identified, the context applied. A student trained on IGCSE short-answer questions writes three sentences and stops. Marked practice with the mark allocation written beside each paragraph makes the shortfall visible, which is the point of returning annotated scripts rather than a score.

sections.heading: The developed solution: the documentation is the grade, not the program
paragraphs: This is the single most expensive misunderstanding in Diploma Computer Science. Students believe the internally assessed component is a programming task and that the documentation is paperwork wrapped around it. The assessment criteria say the opposite: marks are distributed across planning, design, the record of development, the demonstration of functionality and the evaluation. A technically impressive program with thin documentation scores poorly. A modest program with rigorous documentation scores well. Every experienced Computer Science teacher knows this and many students refuse to believe it until they see a marked example.

The planning stage requires a real client with a real problem, and success criteria agreed with that client in writing. Dubai students often choose a parent's business, a school club or a community organisation, which is a sound instinct provided the client interaction genuinely happens and is recorded. A fictional client is detectable and undermines the whole submission, because every later criterion refers back to the agreed criteria. Getting this stage right in the first fortnight prevents most of the problems that surface in the final month.

The design and development stages require evidence that decisions were made and recorded: structure diagrams, data flow, algorithm design, and a dated record of the tasks undertaken with the techniques used. The common failure is retrospective documentation, written in one sitting after the code is finished, which reads as retrospective and tends to be internally inconsistent. Building documents alongside the work is both easier and better rewarded, and it is the main thing a supervision session should enforce.

The evaluation stage requires honest assessment against the original success criteria, including the ones not met, plus recommendations for extension. Students systematically over-claim here, declaring every criterion satisfied. A criterion honestly reported as partially met with an explanation scores better than a criterion dishonestly reported as met and visibly not working in the functionality recording. The recording and the evaluation are read together, so inconsistency between them is the easiest deduction an examiner ever makes.

sections.heading: Why the strongest coder in the class is often not the highest scorer
paragraphs: This pattern repeats across Dubai cohorts with enough regularity to be worth naming directly. A student who codes confidently outside school arrives with real ability and three habits that cost marks. They skip notation, because nobody they have ever coded with uses examination pseudocode. They skip documentation, because in self-taught programming the working artefact is the whole point. And they skip the non-programming content, because system fundamentals and network theory feel like reading rather than doing.

None of those habits reflects weakness, which is why telling the student to work harder achieves nothing. The intervention is targeted: three sessions on notation with marked scripts, a documentation routine enforced weekly so it becomes part of development rather than an afterthought, and timed written practice on the theory content where the student can see the marks going missing. Capable students respond fast to this because the gap is procedural, and the evidence file makes the improvement visible within a half-term.

The mirror-image student also exists and needs the opposite plan. A careful, organised student with limited programming confidence usually documents beautifully and then under-builds, submitting a solution too simple to access the upper bands on the development criteria. For that student the paid time goes on technical ambition, scaffolded carefully: choosing a problem that genuinely requires a non-trivial technique, then building it in increments small enough not to stall. Those two students need completely different six weeks, which is why a diagnostic first session matters more here than in most subjects.

A third pattern, less discussed, is the student whose solution is architecturally wrong in a way that will cap their mark regardless of effort. Discovered in November of DP2 this is a serious problem; discovered in March of DP1 it is a conversation. An external reader looking at the plan early is cheap insurance, and it is a genuinely useful thing to buy from a specialist who has supervised a number of these projects and recognises an unrecoverable design when they see one.
